author: ryansiu-pplx
body:
Ownership validation currently discovers deep directories one ancestor at a time. In [a slow production evaluation](https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/trace/6ae3e4b70000000001e77ec0d2a9abdb), document discovery spent 5.7 seconds on ten sequential tree reads.

Extend `git/objects:batch` with optional `object_type: "tree"`, resolving directory SHAs through the existing bounded GraphQL batching. Callers can then fetch directory listings concurrently without losing file-mode information.

- Default/explicit `blob` behavior and existing cache keys are unchanged.
- Tree lookups use a separate cache namespace; cached non-blob results cannot hide directories.
- Missing paths and other object types return `null`; malformed upstream results fail without being cached as missing.

Deploy CacheW before enabling the ownership-service consumer. Older CacheW versions reject the new request field.

The exact 8- and 13-directory GraphQL queries from the sampled revision succeeded against GitHub in 0.59s and 0.78s including CLI overhead. This excludes CacheW/storage overhead. [Consumer PR and trace-based benchmark](https://github.com/ppl-ai/agi/pull/263735).

author: bccorb
body:
## What changed

Adds Amazon Cognito, Clerk, and Firebase Authentication (Identity Platform) to the Identity Cost Calculator at `compare/cost`, and lets a link prefill the calculator's inputs.

- `pricing.ts`: new sources (dated 2026-10-29), Cognito Lite/Essentials/Plus, Clerk Hobby/Pro/Business/Enterprise, and Firebase with Identity Platform. Per-user rates are applied graduated (each band's rate covers only the users in that band), which reproduces the vendors' own worked examples: Cognito at 950,000 MAU gives Lite $4,405, Essentials $14,100, Plus $19,000, and Identity Platform at 225,000 MAU gives $850.
- New `vendor` selector (Seamless Auth is always shown) and query parameter parsing.
- No-JavaScript tables for all three new vendors: Cognito per-MAU rates by band and plan, Clerk MRU and SSO connection rates, Identity Platform per-MAU rates.
- `cost.mdx`: how each vendor's numbers are read, a short section on prefilled links, and dated Sources entries.

List prices only. No price is estimated: anything the pages do not print is a note or "Contact sales".

## Query parameters (stable ids for `seamless migrate assess`, fells-code/seamless-cli#319)

| Parameter | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `mau` | whole number, 1 to 1,000,000,000 |
| `vendor` | `all`, `auth0`, `okta`, `cognito`, `clerk`, `firebase` (case-insensitive) |
| `useCase` | `b2c`, `b2b` |
| `enterpriseConnections` | whole number, 0 to 10,000 |
| `mfa` | `none`, `otp`, `enterprise` |

Missing or invalid values are ignored and the input keeps its default (for example `?mau=abc&vendor=nope&mfa=x&enterpriseConnections=-2` opens with the defaults).

## Prices read on 2026-10-29

**Amazon Cognito**, https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/pricing/ (tables are region-selectable; values are US East (N. Virginia), read from the page's own price feed because the tables render client-side)
- Lite: first 10,000 MAU free, 10,001 to 100,000 $0.0055, 100,001 to 1,000,000 $0.0046, 1,000,001 to 10,000,000 $0.00325, above $0.0025
- Essentials: first 10,000 free, then $0.015
- Plus: no free tier, $0.020
- SAML/OIDC federated users, any plan: 50 MAU free, then $0.015
- SMS and email via Amazon SNS and SES, no rate printed on the Cognito page

**Clerk**, https://clerk.com/pricing (sales: https://clerk.com/contact/sales)
- Hobby: free, 50,000 MRU limit per app, MFA and SSO connections not included, SMS not included
- Pro: $25/mo ($20 billed annually); Business: $300/mo ($250 billed annually); both include 50,000 MRU per app, then $0.02 (50,001 to 100,000), $0.018 (to 1,000,000), $0.015 (to 10,000,000), $0.012 (above)
- SSO connections (SAML, OIDC, EASIE): 1 included per app on Pro and Business, 2 to 15 at $75/mo each, 16 to 100 at $60/mo each, 101+ "Contact us"
- MFA included on Pro and Business; SMS $0.01 per SMS in the US and Canada, market rate elsewhere
- Enterprise: custom, annual only

**Firebase Authentication / Identity Platform**, https://firebase.google.com/pricing and https://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/pricing
- With Identity Platform: 50,000 MAU and 50 SAML/OIDC MAU at no cost on Spark and Blaze, Google Cloud pricing above (Blaze)
- Tier 1 (email, phone, anonymous, social): 0 to 50,000 free, to 100,000 $0.0055, to 1,000,000 $0.0046, to 10,000,000 $0.0032, above $0.0025
- Tier 2 (SAML, OIDC): 50 free, then $0.015
- SMS for phone and MFA: per country, $0.01 for the US and Canada, first ten SMS a day not billed

## Not verified or deliberately left out (please check on merge day)

- **Cognito region**: the page has a region selector. The calculator uses US East (N. Virginia); in the price feed, Essentials and Plus are the same in all 36 listed regions and the Lite rates are the same in the 34 regions that carry them.
- **Cognito extras not priced**: the legacy 50,000 MAU Lite free tier for pre-2024-11-22 accounts, the Advanced Security Features add-on, M2M token charges, multi-Region and quota add-ons.
- **Federated users (Cognito, Firebase)**: these vendors charge per federated MAU, while the calculator input is a count of enterprise connections. With any connection the price is shown as "From" the direct sign-in price, with a note giving the federated rate. No federated MAU count is guessed.
- **Clerk MRU vs MAU**: Clerk bills monthly retained users per application. The calculator treats your MAU as the MRU count for one application, which can overstate Clerk's bill; this is said on the page.
- **Clerk tier application**: the page lists MRU and SSO bands as "50,001 - 100,000: $0.02/mo each" with a "volume discounts" toggle and does not say outright whether a band's rate applies to all users or only those in the band. I applied it graduated (only users in the band), matching how the page lays out the bands. Worth confirming.
- **Clerk B2B**: organizations (100 MRO included per app, Enhanced add-on $100/mo or $85 annual, which is where "Link Enterprise connections with Organizations" is listed) are noted, not priced.
- **Firebase "Other Authentication services"**: firebase.google.com/pricing shows this row with a check mark on both Spark and Blaze and no price. It is ambiguous what it costs at scale, so the calculator prices only Firebase Authentication with Identity Platform and says so on the page.
- **Firebase Spark DAU limit** (3,000 DAU after the Identity Platform upgrade) is in Firebase's docs, not the pricing page, so it is not used.
- **MFA availability on Cognito and Firebase** is not printed on their pricing pages, so the calculator adds only per-message notes and never marks a plan unavailable for MFA on those vendors.

## Testing

- Production build served with `astro preview`, loaded in a browser at `/compare/cost/?mau=12000&vendor=cognito`: the form showed "Compare with: Amazon Cognito" and MAU 12000, and the results were Lite $11, Essentials $30, Plus $240, Seamless Auth $27.15. Loading `?mau=abc&vendor=nope&mfa=x&enterpriseConnections=-2` kept every default (5000 MAU, all vendors, 15 rows).
- No-JS static tables checked in the rendered HTML for all three new vendors.
- Pricing functions run under Node against the vendors' worked examples (numbers above).

## Checks

- `npx prettier -c .`: All matched files use Prettier code style!
- `npm run lint`: eslint, check-no-h1, check-sdk-results passed with no output
- `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints
- `npm run build`: 62 page(s) built, Complete (existing warnings only: `env` code-block language and the i18n collection)

Closes fells-code/seamless-auth-docs#141

body:
## What and Why

The job page every service will use, plus a way to reach it before any scoring form exists.

**OpenSpec change:** [`openspec/changes/add-job-page/`](openspec/changes/add-job-page/)
**Area:** frontend

- **`/jobs/:id`** polls `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` every second until the job is `succeeded` or `failed`, then stops. It shows:
  - **queued or running:** the status in a live region, and "This page updates by itself";
  - **succeeded:** the result (for `tools`, the tool table, where `null` reads "not available"), how long it ran (from the API's timestamps), and the versions the job ran with;
  - **failed:** the error's `detail`;
  - **not found or expired:** "Job not found", with a link home;
  - **API down:** "Job unavailable", with "Try again".
- **Home page:** a secondary "Check the scoring tools" button starts a `tools` job and opens its page. It's a placeholder until the service forms exist.
- **`src/app/api/wire.ts`:** the one module that converts the API's job (`created_at`, …) into the app's shape (`createdAt`, as epoch ms).

Riley's reply to a request for a slightly more romantic photo was accompanied by an almost identical ordinary outdoor selfie. - Keep actual character location/outfit continuity. Do not teleport or invent wardrobe changes from a "more flirty" request.
- Remove the category-blind "ordinary clothes" instruction from both Tess and non-Tess photo scene templates.

- Add regression tests for the shared guidance and the photo-history context label.

author: paulfidika
body:
A run's execution record now carries `reply_built_unix_ms` and `reply_sent_unix_ms`. With the stage stamps and TensorD's log phases, they split the time between a handler's return and `settled_at_ms` into the Runtime's share and the host's. Before this, a delay after a request could not be placed on either side.

## Proof

Pod-session 40983613751: one RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (24 GB, driver 595.91, EPYC 7352). A holder leaves 6 GiB free. SDXL int8, published packages, one cold request and six warm, both arms on the same pod. Times are ms after the handler's last stage.

| arm | request | reply sent | TensorD has it | output encoded | settled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR (0.35.5.dev4010, TensorFS 0.17.10) | cold | 522 | 559 | 860 | 1207 |
| | w1–w6 | 5–6 | 35–47 | 173–209 | 313–465 |
| Runtime 0.35.2 (prod2) | cold | n/a | 42 | 365 | 716 |
| | w1–w6 | n/a | 33–47 | 164–205 | 310–359 |

- **Warm requests:** the Runtime puts the reply on the seam 5 ms after the handler returns. The remaining 0.3–0.45 s is the host's: the seam, the frame-codec webp encode, then settle. It is the same in both builds.
- **Cold requests:** this build spends 0.52 s in the Runtime before its reply is built, inside the request's close and before its confessions. 0.35.2 spends 3 ms there. That is the host tier's share and has a separate follow-up.
- Execution times match: warm 5.54–6.67 s here against 5.66–8.07 s on 0.35.2. Peaks are within 30 MiB.

author: mark-torres10
body:
Refs https://github.com/METResearchGroup/lab_data_integrations_interface/issues/280

## Findings

These come from reading the code and runbook. Nothing was checked against live Cloudflare, AWS, or Grafana, so each one is a hypothesis to confirm.

**1. Most likely: no run has been started.**
- Since #258 the backfill Worker is on demand. `cloudflare/backfill/src/index.ts` launches the container only on `POST /start`.
- There is no cron supervisor, unlike Jetstream, which restarts its process every minute.
- A run stops 6 hours after the latest `/start`, or when the process exits, and stays down until the next `/start`.
- Railway ran the loop continuously, so the cutover changed "always on" to "off unless triggered". Queueing the 220k users does not start anything.
- No process means no metrics or logs, which matches an empty last-24-hours view and visible data at 30 days.
- Check: `GET https://ldi-backfill-preview.mind-technology-lab.workers.dev/status`. `{"running": false}` confirms it. Then follow the runbook to `/start`.

**2. Possible: the rotated AWS credentials.**
- The container only gets the Worker's `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` secrets.
- If those are stale, the OTLP header read from Secrets Manager fails. That was logged at INFO, so telemetry went off silently.
- `queue.receive()` would also raise. That ended the loop and the container exited, with nothing to restart it.
- Check: container logs after a `/start`, and whether the Worker's key matches the current IAM user.

**3. Weaker.**
- The Workers observability destinations (`ldi-preview-grafana-*`) are separate from the in-process OTLP exporter, so Worker logs reaching Grafana does not show that app metrics are exporting.
- Dashboard panels do not filter on `deployment.environment`, so the new label alone should not hide data.

Open question for triage: should a supervisor restart the run while the main queue is non-empty? That reverses the on-demand choice in #258, so it is not part of this PR.

Throughput for 250k and 500k cannot be estimated from the repo. It needs a real run or the dashboard's `repos_landed` and `rows_written` rates. About 3B rows for 130k users is roughly 23k rows per user.

## Changes

- `fetch_repos/main.py`: a failed `queue.receive()` now logs the exception, waits 30 seconds, and continues, so a bad credential or SQS outage does not end the run.
- `lib/aws/secrets_env.py`: the two "telemetry secret not loaded" messages are now warnings, not INFO.

## Validation

`py_compile` passes on both files. pytest could not run here because the dependencies would not install. Per the issue, no unit tests were added. A smoke run still needs credentials: `/start`, then confirm the receive-error path and the Grafana panels.

author: natedawg888
body:
KAN-121, part of KAN-107. **Stacked on #179 (KAN-120 sales): merge that first.** Until then this diff includes #179's commit.

**Bills and wages count as expenses, on the date paid** (payments basis, like invoices, sales and the GST return)
- `businessMoney` adds paid supplier bills and wages paid. They appear in the business totals, the P&L ("Stock purchases", "Delivery", "Wages"), and the accountant export. Unpaid bills don't count yet.
- A tagged bank payment linked to a bill or wage shows `countedVia: 'bill' | 'wage'` and isn't counted again. A payment can be linked to only one bill or wage, and only money out can be linked; this is now checked for bills too.
- GST return: paid bills are purchases, claimable (`standard`) when the supplier has a GST number, otherwise `exempt`. Wages carry no GST.

**Wages**
- `GET/POST /:id/wages` and `PUT/DELETE /wages/:wageId`.
- A wage has an employee (or just a name), a date paid (today or earlier), an amount, an optional bank payment and notes.
- Deleting an employee keeps their wages under their name.

**Budget**
- `GET /:id/budget?taxYear=`.
- Categories and plans:
  - `POST /:id/budget/categories`
  - `PUT/DELETE /budget/categories/:categoryId`
  - `PUT /budget/categories/:categoryId/plans`
  - `PUT /:id/money/category` puts a tagged transaction in a category.
- Default categories: Sales, Other income, Stock, Delivery, Wages, Rent, Marketing.
  - The first five fill in automatically. They can be renamed but not deleted.
  - Deleting another category moves its transactions to uncategorised.
- Plans are per month (`YYYY-MM`) or per tax year (`2027`). Changing a category's cadence drops its plans.
- Where actuals come from:
  - Sales: recorded sales and invoice payments.
  - Other income: tagged income rows, and tagged deposits not in a category.
  - Stock: paid stock bills, less their freight.
  - Delivery: freight on stock bills, and paid delivery bills.
  - Wages: wages paid.
  - Any category: tagged bank transactions put in it. Payments left out of a category show as uncategorised.
- Profit:
  - Gross profit = sales − cost of goods sold.
  - Net profit = gross profit + other income − operating expenses.
  - Stock purchases are shown in the budget but not counted as an operating expense, because their cost comes through cost of goods sold.
  - Both profits are null while a sold item has no cost yet.

**Also:** accountants and viewers (KAN-129) reach wages, budget categories and plans only for the business they were let into.

**Tests**
- New `server/business/budget.test.ts`, added to `test:business`. It covers the default categories, every actual source, gross and net profit, plans, category rules, payment-link rules, totals, P&L and GST matching, keeping wages after an employee is deleted, and isolation.
- Turning off the bill double-count guard makes it fail.
- `members.test.ts` now covers wage and budget scoping.
- All CI suites and the build pass locally. `test:crypto` failed once ("DeFi in net worth") and then passed 3/3; it doesn't touch business code.

author: esetera
body:
Pure3D scenes looked like toy blocks. Every scene was unit primitives with flat colours, under one fixed rig of three lights, with no shadows, sky, reflections, fog or finishing. This PR changes how scenes look and gives agents (and people) the tools to build natural scenes.

## The look (`settings.look`)
- **Sky or studio**: a physical sky with clouds and a sun (three's `Sky`), or soft studio light (`RoomEnvironment`) on the background colour. Either way the environment also lights and reflects every material (PMREM).
- **Sun**: height, direction, strength and colour (warm by default near the horizon), with soft or sharp shadows.
  - The shadow is fitted to what the camera sees, so it stays crisp on a table and in a forest.
  - Bias is scaled to the shadow texel size, so there's no acne.
- **Fog** sized to the scene and coloured like the horizon.
- **Finishing**:
  - Neutral tone mapping
  - ambient occlusion (GTAO) as contact shadows
  - bloom
  - depth of field
  - 4× MSAA through `EffectComposer`
- **Defaults**: a scene with no look still gets studio light, a sun with soft shadows and contact shadows.
- **Inspector**: a "Light and finish" section.

## Generated shapes (saved as small, seeded params, not triangles)
- **`terrain`**: noise hills coloured by height and slope (grass, soil, rock, snow), with an optional flat clearing. Its centre is at y 0, so things in the clearing stand at y 0.
- **`scatter`**: an instanced mesh of pines, firs, broadleaf trees, birches, bushes, rocks, grass, flowers or ferns over an area, or over a terrain (`on`). Each instance varies in size, turn and colour, with clumping, a maximum slope and an `avoid` radius.
- **`tree`**, **`rock`** (displaced, mossy), **`water`** (waves, reflects the sky) and **`roundedBox`**.
- **Foliage**: leaf cards on a leaf atlas drawn on a canvas, so nothing is downloaded. Ambient occlusion leaves the cut-out cards out of its depth pass.
- **Materials**: also take `emissive`, `clearcoat`, `transmission` and `sheen`.
- **UI and agent guidance**:
  - add menu, outline icons and an Inspector for each generator
  - the tool descriptions and `agents.md` teach agents the look and the generators

## Captures
`captureViewport` and PNG export now render a finished still **off screen**, at 2× and scaled down, with finer shadows. They work while Pure3D is hidden (this fixes the blank captures), and the gizmos and selection box are left out.

## Tested
- `tsc` is clean.
- `vitest`: 133 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `useSceneDocument` › close handshake (`expected 44 to be less than 42`), and it fails the same way on main without this change.
- New tests: `generators.test.ts` (params validation and merge, seeds, clearing, scatter on terrain, rebuild on terrain change, shadow flags, look merge, sun direction). Viewport tests now use a fake rig for stills.
- Live: the PureDesktop 3D artist built a golden-hour forest clearing with the new tools in the dev desktop. Its captures worked with the app off-screen.

Not in this PR: a path-traced "Render" (three-gpu-pathtracer) is a possible follow-up. It needs a new dependency and a ps-suite lockfile change.

body:
## What

A hands-free call on mobile waits on several slow steps before it records: loading the audio module, the microphone permission prompt and the recorder setup. This PR makes sure a call that was hung up during one of those steps stops there and leaves the next call alone.

## Why

The old turn kept running after hang-up. It could start recording after the call had ended. When it finished, it switched recording off under the next call's recorder, so the new call stopped hearing the user. Device dictation had the same gap: a cancelled request that arrived late stopped the newer dictation session.

## Changes

- After each awaited step, the turn checks whether its call has ended and stops without recording.
- Only the turn that owns the shared audio mode switches recording off.
- A dictation request that is already cancelled returns before it touches the current session.

## Tested

Unit tests hold each awaited step open, end the call and start the next one, and check that the late step neither records nor stops the next call. I ran the mobile unit suite, biome and the mobile typecheck. Not tested on a device.

author: wfgp12
body:
Clave de idempotencia en el registro paso a paso, para que reintentar un guardado no cree un movimiento duplicado (contrato del backend 2.2.7).

- `crearTransaccion(datos, clave)` envía la clave en el header `Idempotency-Key` y no en el cuerpo.
- El flujo de registro genera un UUID por acción y lo reutiliza al reintentar con los mismos datos; si el usuario cambia un dato tras un fallo, genera una clave nueva.
- El 409 (todavía se está guardando) muestra un aviso propio.
- Dependencia nueva: `expo-crypto` 57.0.4 (versión exacta) para generar el UUID en el celular, donde Hermes no trae `crypto.randomUUID`.
- `__mocks__/expo-crypto.js`: soporte de jest, porque el módulo nativo no genera UUID bajo `jest-expo`.

Criterios CA-RF06-15 a 22 y pruebas del tester en `6a03df9`. Con este cambio el backend ya puede activar `IDEMPOTENCIA_OBLIGATORIA`.

author: niteshbalusu11
body:
Closes #1270.

Core's `getmininginfo` now returns `bestblockhash` (bitcoin/bitcoin#36081), so a miner gets the tip hash and the next block's `nBits` from one call. Ours had no `bestblockhash`. Its `next` also copied the tip's bits instead of the work the next block must meet, so the pairing would have been wrong at a retarget.

- `bestblockhash`, `blocks`, `bits`, and `target` come from one tip header read. `next` and `networkhashps` are computed for that tip. `next` uses Core's `NextEmptyBlockIndex` rule through a helper shared with `getblocktemplate`, so GBT is unchanged.
- `next` and `networkhashps` read the chain by height at or below that tip, so a connect above it keeps the sample and a syncing node answers from its first one. A disconnect during the reads (the sampled slot changed, or `Query::disconnect_gen` moved, which also catches a reorg away and back) or a failed read waits for the running tip job and starts the sample over. After 8 samples the call returns an error.
- `currentblockweight` / `currentblocktx` were a fixed 8000/0 once any template was built. They now report Core's last assembly: the reserved 8000 plus the selected transactions, recorded by `getblocktemplate` and by each block of `generate`. `generateblock` records Core's empty assembly before it mines and does not record the transactions it was given.
- `difficulty`, `next.difficulty`, and `networkhashps` print at Core's 16 significant digits, like `getblockheader` and `getblockchaininfo`.

Not in this PR: the Stratum v2 template provider does not record assemblies (noted in `docs/rpc.md`). The `getnetworkhashps` RPC itself still prints a raw `f64`.

Proof: each new rpc test fails on the code before its fix and passes after. That covers the retarget `next`, the reorg-mid-sample and away-and-back cases (a debug-only hook reorgs inside the call), a disconnect below the sample, a connect during a sample, giving up after 8 samples, the per-block and failed-`generate` counters, and `generateblock`. On a live regtest node, 4 readers made 64,466 `getmininginfo` calls during 776 generate/invalidate/reconsider cycles with 0 errors, and the slowest took 13 ms. A live `rbitcoin-node` on regtest and Core 32.1 `bitcoind` gave the same `currentblockweight`/`currentblocktx` sequence (8268/1 after a template with one tx, 8000/0 after `generate 2`, 8268/1 after a one-tx `generate 1`, 8000/0 after `generateblock`) and the same 16-digit difficulty. Core 32.1 predates #36081, so `bestblockhash` was checked against `getbestblockhash` instead. Local fmt, clippy, deny, ast-grep, ratchets, doc, `ci-os-smoke.sh`, and the workspace tests pass. The exceptions are `outbound_refill_journey`, which needs sudo for a netns locally, and two tests that fail intermittently under workspace load (`tip_accept::two_full_senders_both_enqueue`, `tip_accept::full_lane_parks_instead_of_spinning`, `cross_surface::sv2_tp_bootstrap`, `array_table::fd_only_truncate_then_get_is_absent`), which passed 3/3 when run alone.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 4 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved on `d7647c5c7`. The later `f36ef1896`, which drops the retry sleep after a rearden-grok nit, was not reviewed by Sol because the round budget was spent.

author: denn-gubsky
body:
## Why
A fresh review found that keyed re-import of a new edition could lose the work or misattribute its text:
- **Lost work key.** Under a confirmed ontology, an ordinary `update_chunk` on the work's root cleared or overwrote the work key, which lived in the column the class rules recompute. The next edition then created a second document.
- **Misread insert.** Inserting an article and renumbering the rest was read as "every later article changed". The old text lost its stable id and its citations moved onto the inserted text.
- **Statements.** A statement between two changed parts was copied twice. A `[[link]]` the new edition removed survived as a permanent edge.
- **Older editions.** An older edition imported after a newer one replaced the current text.
- **Concurrency.** Concurrent re-imports left two parts in force under one anchor.
- **Root.** The edition's root (title, preamble) never changed.
- **Leaks.** `resolve_anchor` and `documents/ingested` revealed works a confined caller may not read.

## What
- **`chunks.work_key`.** A new column, unique per scope, migrated on both tiers with a backfill of recognisable claims.
  - Lookup is by `work_key`, then by a root's class identity.
  - The ontology's `identityCollision` also meets a held work key, so creating a work directly still collides with its placeholder. That is a one-query change, made with the ontology line's agreement, in its own commit.
- **Reconciliation in passes:** exact anchor+body, then body moves, then same-anchor supersession, then new parts. New parts get fresh stable ids.
  - This corrects the earlier ordering, which put supersession first.
  - Caveat: identical boilerplate text in two articles can now read as a move.
- **Statement carry.**
  - One old→new id map; each statement is copied once with both ends remapped, and wikilink statements are not carried.
  - The carry happens before the old part closes, and copies are transactional.
  - A rerun finishes an interrupted supersession.
- **Edition dates.** An `edition_date` older than the edition in force is refused.
- **Serialisation.** An in-process lock per work and per document. Across replicas, the unique index refuses the second claim and the loser deletes its keyless copy.
- **Root.** Title and preamble follow the edition through `update_chunk`, updated in place; history keeps the old preamble. A filled placeholder takes the real title.
- **Leaks closed.**
  - `resolve_anchor` answers an unreadable holder as not found.
  - `documents/ingested` is published only when the caller's rules do not partition reading; otherwise the response says `not_announced`.
- **Faults.** A body-read fault stops the reimport before any write.
- **Help.** import_md, resolve_anchor and create_document are updated, including which inputs a reimport ignores: the `loom-edges` block, `valid_at`/`invalid_at` in `loom:` lines, and images.

## Tests
Each failed on the unfixed code. The ones marked "both tiers" run on sqlite and postgres.
- `TestReimport_RootEditUnderAnOntologyKeepsTheWorkKey`
- `TestMigrateAnchors_CarriesClaimedWorkKeysIntoTheirColumn` (both tiers)
- `TestClassRules_CollisionWithAPlaceholderSaysToFillIt` (extended)
- `TestReimport_InsertedPartRenumbersTheRestAsMoves`
- `TestReimport_StatementBetweenTwoChangedPartsIsCopiedOnce`
- `TestReimport_WikilinkTheEditionDroppedDoesNotSurvive`
- `TestReimport_RerunCompletesAnInterruptedSupersession`
- `TestReimport_BackdatedEditionIsRefused`
- `TestReimport_ConcurrentReimportsOfOneWorkSerialise` (`-race -count=5`, both tiers)
- `TestReimport_EditionRootIsReconciled`
- `TestResolveAnchor_UnreadableWorkIsNotFound`
- `TestPublishIngested_OnlyWhenReadingIsNotPartitioned`
- `TestReimport_BodyReadFaultChangesNothing`

The full builtin, mcp and help packages pass.

Known gaps, left as follow-ups:
- A run that dies between `createChunk` and its anchor transaction leaves a closed stray.
- Two replicas re-importing an existing work at the same moment can still interleave.
- Concurrent first ops on a fresh scope race schema provisioning. This was already the case on main.

author: whilo
body:
An embedding host that retains Git merge bases needs to exclude managed collection while establishing durable snapshot roots. Default-off deleting GC is insufficient: a dry run or timed-out/background collection can already have been admitted, and another home can enable collection later.

Add `prohibit-storage-gc!`, an irreversible process-wide boot policy. Installation, enabling and collection admission share one monitor. Installation refuses enabled homes or any earlier managed admission; once installed, both collector entrypoints (including dry runs) and later enabling refuse before constructing work. Repeated installation with the same namespaced reason is idempotent.

This is native HOST configuration, not copied world state, retention evidence or a settlement authority. Use a fresh JVM instrumented from startup. Direct operator collectors and other processes sharing storage remain outside this operating profile. No Simmis deployment or broader Spindel/Dvergr lifetime changes are included.

Validation: independent implementation review approved; `clj -M:ffix` and diff checks pass; 8 policy tests/61 assertions plus 3 focused real-SCI sandbox/existing GC tests/15 assertions pass in the reused local REPL. Coverage includes both entrypoints, empty/failed/timed-out/background admissions, process-wide homes, and installation races against enable/collect.

author: knight-ai-av
body:
Phones can now say a wish, as the web already could. Until now the microphone button only showed on the web, because phones had no recorder.

What changed
- components/voice/use-recorder.ts (phones) uses expo-audio's microphone stream, asked for at 16 kHz mono. It keeps the web's rules: it stops after a pause once the wish is said, after a stretch of nothing, or at one minute, and it sends the same 16 kHz WAV to the same transcription.
- A phone has no browser gain control, so the line between speech and the room follows the room (three times the quietest moment so far, between a floor and the web's line), the listening bars are drawn against that line, and the clip is brought up to a clear level before it goes. When nothing crosses the line but something was louder than the room, the clip still goes to transcription instead of being thrown away.
- The stream sets the phone's audio up for recording; afterwards the app puts it back the way its sounds play (lib/sound.ts resumeSounds).
- app.json adds expo-audio's plugin for the microphone permission, with background audio off. The iOS text reads: "Dandelist listens only while you say a wish, to write it down." The image picker had removed that key (its microphonePermission was false), so it now carries the same text. Checked with expo config --type introspect: the text is in Info.plist, there are no background modes, the entitlements are unchanged (Sign in with Apple only), and Android asks for RECORD_AUDIO.
- A refused microphone says: "Allow the microphone in Settings to say your wish, or type it."

Native: this needs the next TestFlight build (the microphone permission and the stream are native).

Tests: lib/wav.test.ts covers the room line, the channel average and the level boost. The app's tsc, check-type and vitest pass (34 files, 273 tests).

body:
## Summary

Adds a full round-trip for storyboards: the board (with edits) can be exported as `dionysus.storyboard/1` JSON, revised by an AI, and re-imported by merging by id. It also adds two Send modes.

### Re-import: merge by id (item 13)
- On an existing board, **Import revised JSON…** validates the JSON and shows a preview of **New**, **Changed** (with the changed fields) and **Removed** shots and assets. Meta, order, connection and audio changes appear under "Also updated".
- **Apply changes** keeps the following for every id that still exists: uploads (versions), the picked version, trims, production step order, timeline links and QA. A check whose text is unchanged keeps its id and result. New ids are added.
- If anything would be removed, a confirm step comes first. Uploads of removed items stay in the media library.
- **Replace instead…** (behind a confirm) still imports the JSON as a fresh board.
- Each action is a single undo step.

### Export (item 19)
- **Export** (in the desktop header, or the ⋯ menu on phones) offers **Download .json** and **Copy JSON**, plus a read-only preview.
- `storyboardToDoc` folds asset states, keyframes, still/HTML clip slots, references and dialogue back into source form. Importing the export gives the same board.
- Round-trip tests cover the fixture, the guide example, the rich fixture and boards with edits.

### Send modes (item 10)
- The first send works as before. Once board clips are on the timeline, **Send** opens a dialog with two options:
  - **Update timeline** applies only changes since the last send. It appends new ready shots and audio, swaps clips whose picked version changed (in place), refreshes shots whose layers, effects or params changed, and re-places edited cues. The dialog shows a summary of what will change.
  - **Replace timeline…** clears the timeline and rebuilds it in story order, after a confirm. Undo restores the previous timeline.
- The board records a per-shot and per-cue signature (`storyboard.sent`). Boards sent before this change are back-filled without a rebuild.
- All targets are at least 44 px, on desktop as well.

### Docs and AI guide
- `STORYBOARD_FORMAT.md` §4.6 (export and re-import) and §4.7 (send modes) are new. The rules list is updated.
- New **RULE 30** (`stable-ids-reimport`) is appended to `RULE_LIST`. It tells the AI that users may re-import its revised JSON and that ids must stay stable. `aiGuide.test.ts` pins it.
- `npm run gen:ai` has been re-run.

author: deffenda
body:
## Summary

The Rust and Node SSH-config `Include` glob matchers already disagreed, so the
same `~/.ssh/config` produced a different host set per backend: the Node
matcher consumed one UTF-16 code unit per `?` and never matched a newline,
while the Rust matcher — the shipping transport — works in Unicode scalar
values. This pins the Node matcher to the Rust behaviour and puts the matcher
into the shared cross-backend corpus so the two cannot drift apart again.

## Linked issue

Closes #480

## Changes

- `apps/desktop/server/backend-glob.mjs` (new): the Node matcher, lifted out of
  `backend.mjs` so it can be asserted without booting the server, and built
  with the `u` and `s` flags — `u` makes `.` consume one code point, `s` lets
  it match a newline. A pattern that cannot be expressed as a Unicode regex is
  skipped rather than thrown.
- `apps/desktop/server/backend.mjs`: use the extracted matcher, and skip a
  pattern the matcher cannot build instead of failing the request.
- `tests/fixtures/security-helper-conformance.json`: a new `globMatches` group
  — eleven hand-authored cases (an astral character, a newline, `?` vs `*`, a
  literal `[`, prefix matching) with the Rust answer as the expectation.
- `tests/integration/security-helper-conformance.integration.test.ts`: assert
  the new group against the Node matcher.
- `src-tauri/src/native_transport_conformance_tests.rs`: assert the same group
  against the Rust matcher, so each side is checked against the other.
- `src-tauri/src/main.rs`: a Rust unit test for `glob_match` over the same
  cases.

## Acceptance criteria mirror

- [x] The corpus carries a `globMatches` group covering an astral character, a
      newline, `?` vs `*` and a literal `[`, with the Rust values as the
      expectations.
- [x] Both harnesses assert that group — `native_transport_conformance_tests.rs`
      and `security-helper-conformance.integration.test.ts`.
- [x] The Node matcher consumes one Unicode code point per `?` and matches a
      newline with `*` and `?`, like the Rust matcher.
- [x] A pattern that cannot be built as a Unicode regex is detected and
      skipped explicitly, with a comment saying why — no crash path is
      introduced.
- [x] A Rust unit test covers the same cases as the corpus.
- [x] The `nosemgrep` suppression keeps its original justification, which the
      `u`/`s` flags do not change.
- [x] Neither matcher's wildcard semantics changed, and no third glob
      implementation was added.

## Test plan

- `TERMSNIP_RUN_BACKEND_FIXTURE=1 npm run validate` — **pass**: eslint, the
  full vitest suite, the desktop build, `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `test`
  (143 passed, 0 failed), the real backend transport fixture against a
  throwaway sshd (including its SSH-config glob boundary checks), and
  changed-file Semgrep through Docker.
- `bash ./scripts/backend-transport-test.sh` — **pass** on its own.
- `cargo test glob` — **pass**: 6 glob tests, including the new conformance and
  unit tests.
- Not run, and why: `TERMSNIP_RUN_SSH_FIXTURE=1` (this change touches neither
  the PTY readers, the session loops nor the native_transport capture loops),
  `TERMSNIP_RUN_E2E=1` (no UI change), `TERMSNIP_RUN_NATIVE_TRUST=1` and
  `TERMSNIP_RUN_RUST_AUDIT=1` (this is not a dependency change). CI runs the
  Rust advisory audit on every pull request regardless.

## Changelog entry

- [FIX] one-line description matching the changelog.d fragment

## Confirmed defect (on merged main)
After PR #472 successfully minimized analytics route names and parameter values, `public/analytics.js::track()` still validated the **event name** only with `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`. author: griffinwork40
body:
## Summary

Refs #1415 — **partial proposal; do not close the issue**.

Expose the existing registry through read-only `artifact_get`, `artifact_list`, and `artifact_read` builtins. No replacement registry, new persistence backend, producer auto-registration, or retention changes.

- Metadata is bounded and omits arbitrary tags/lineage. Lists filter by producing session/subagent/tool, MIME type, and date range.
- Small text reads default to 4 KiB and cap at 16 KiB. Binary and >64 KiB artifacts return metadata plus a read path, not inline content.
- IDs do not grant filesystem access: existing credential/read-root policy and canonical hash-derived blob checks apply, including metadata/list visibility.
- Model-facing index reads reject >8 MiB before parsing, including concurrent growth; list responses cap at 32 KiB and 100 records. Existing internal registry API callers retain their default behavior.
- Wire schemas/handlers/category/child allowlists and document limitations. No baseline growth or oversized source files.

## Original proposal verification (687024c)

- Proposal HEAD: `687024ccac35aa27c8b56e97ef2b88c5f0edeccb`.
- Starting worktree HEAD/base: `d97a3747d320eb3d927ca22ab9bad9ba4c8554d1`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor d97a3747d320eb3d927ca22ab9bad9ba4c8554d1 HEAD` passed before edits (and again before commit).
- Read external selection/check artifacts, issue body/comments/timeline, linked merged #3629 and open PR references; issue was open/unassigned with no competing open #1415/registry proposal at the final pre-commit recheck.
- Independently confirmed source risk: base `store.ts:229-280,289-342` already implemented put/get/list/read; repository search found no production consumers outside the registry. #3629 explicitly left model tool exposure and integration as followups. `workspace-tools.ts:63-98,203-218` had no structured artifact references and `witness-sweep.ts:1-20` swept whole witness sessions, not registry policies. The registry is reused, not recreated.
- Repro/verification: 18 new deterministic handler tests cover lookup persistence, byte bounds, large/binary omission, filters, response cap, missing/invalid IDs, cancellation, oversized indexes, malformed producers, factory cwd/read roots, malicious URIs, symlink redirection, size mismatch, and read-only behavior. An independent review found the initially unbounded index read; the cap and regression test now address it, and a second inspection confirmed the repair.

### Tests and gates

- `test_run` / `pnpm test src/agent/tools/handlers/artifact.test.ts`: **18 passed** (rerun on committed HEAD).
- `test_run` / `pnpm test src/agent/artifact-registry/store.test.ts`: **33 passed** (rerun on committed HEAD).
- `test_run`: `schemas.test.ts` **55**, `schema-classification.test.ts` **13**, `nesting.test.ts` **50** passed. **169 relevant tests total**.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check:audits`: **16/16** passed, including security/env/SDK/module-state/clone/pin checks; reran via pre-push hook on committed HEAD without bypass.
- `pnpm audit:filesize:check --changed-vs <base>`, `pnpm audit:funcsize:check --changed-vs <base>`, `pnpm audit:posix:check`, `pnpm lint:tests:check`, `git diff --check`: passed. Test typecheck ratchet remains **2688**, unchanged; full test typecheck is not clean.
- `pnpm audit:deps`: exit 0 under existing critical-only policy; reported **6 existing advisories (2 low, 3 moderate, 1 high)**. No dependency/lockfile changes.
- Full repository suite was not run during original proposal preparation; it was run during the CI repair below. Live model/provider calls not run. Build emitted existing Vite/chunk-size warnings.

## Remaining acceptance / limitations

1. Add safe bounded `artifact_publish` exposure (path/content authorization, metadata/lineage validation, and quota admission) without recreating the registry.
2. Integrate real output producers: screenshots, reports/patches/captures; return artifact IDs and bounded metadata from those producers.
3. Structured workspace artifact-ID persistence/query/preamble delivery and witness trace artifact IDs; task/daemon/DAG result links remain unwired.
4. Enforce session/TTL cleanup and permanent-retention/quota policies; add witness-sweep integration coverage. Merely storing a retention field is not enforcement.
5. Broader lifecycle/producer integration tests and complete acceptance evidence before closing #1415.

This slice deliberately does not enable automatic persistent screenshot copies before quota enforcement. Lists consider at most the first 1,000 matching records (no pagination); oversize indexes require maintenance compaction. Byte slices may split UTF-8 characters (documented/tested); large-blob integrity rehashing and atomic protection against adversarial filesystem replacement between authorization/open are not claimed.

## CI repair — `5680f50f50edf803182b9eb940c49bbd08ce1996`

All five failed jobs in run [40999622967](https://github.com/griffinwork40/agent-afk/actions/runs/40999622967) (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Ubuntu Node 24 and Node 26) had exactly the same three failures: `createBuiltinHandlers` count assertions expected 42 but registration correctly returned 45. Reproduced all three on unchanged proposal HEAD before editing.

Repair changes **only `src/agent/tools/handlers/index.test.ts`**: update those three counts and assert callable registrations for `artifact_get`, `artifact_list`, and `artifact_read`. No production changes: bounded 8 MiB index IO, canonical blob checks, read grants and credential floor are unchanged. Independent read-only scope/review: APPROVE. Refs #1415 remains partial; no merge performed.

Verification on repaired tree (macOS, Node 26.11.0):
- `test_run`: 176 focused tests passed across factory (7), artifact (18), registry (33), schema (55), classification (13), and nesting (50).
- Full `test_run`: **34,639 passed, 0 failed** in 92.149s. Runner emitted worker-termination timeout warnings for `concurrent-emitter.bench.test.ts` and `trace-completeness.bench.test.ts`; preexisting status not established, no warning fix claimed. Captured tool output is head/tail-capped, not an uncapped process log.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:audits` **16/16**, `pnpm lint:tests:check` (unchanged baseline 2688), `pnpm audit:posix:check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Pre-push audits also passed **16/16** on committed HEAD, without bypass.
- Normal fast-forward push to original PR branch only. Remote rerun [41003342393](https://github.com/griffinwork40/agent-afk/actions/runs/41003342393): all five originally failing jobs now **SUCCESS** (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Node24 and Node26). Dashboard is **CANCELLED**, not green; its log ends “The operation was canceled” without a failed assertion (job123892548797, log line409). No dashboard code change or cancellation fix is claimed. All other reported checks succeeded or were neutral.

Local repair evidence: `.afk/pr4551-repair-5680f50/` contains scope manifest, all three comment-store harvests, exact failed-job logs and normalized failure summary, red reproduction, focused/full-suite captures, independent review receipt and gate/push logs. These are local receipts, not committed source files.

author: vasiliibabkin
body:
Records and bounded collections now work directly in `.sdr` and generate an offline task manager for Web and Android/Jetpack Compose from one source. This is an unreleased experimental 0.10 increment; no release, deployment or merge is performed.

## Реализовано

- Зафиксирована нормативная грамматика записей и ограниченных списков: именованные поля `int/bool/text`, обязательные аргументы конструктора, статические типы и доступ к скалярным полям.
- Парсер, AST, проверка типов, интерпретатор, выражения, действия и CLI поддерживают `append/update/remove/get/has/count/next_id` и `require`.
- Упорядоченные неизменяемые списки выдают монотонные положительные int32 ID независимо от индекса. Изменение сохраняет ID, удаление сохраняет порядок, отклонённое действие не меняет принятое состояние.
- Ограничения вместимости, int32, Unicode и ресурсов проверяются без неявных преобразований или усечения. Чрезмерный начальный снимок отклоняется до генерации.
- Сохранение использует строгий schema-1 envelope с отпечатком объявлений. Повторяющиеся JSON-ключи, неверные типы/поля/ID/вместимость, несовместимая схема и повреждённый JSON отклоняются целиком. Scalar-only программы сохраняют прежнюю семантику восстановления.
- `run --state-file` восстанавливает снимок и атомарно заменяет файл только после успешного выполнения; при ошибке существующий файл сохраняется.
- Генераторы создают выбор строки, ввод, действия CRUD, перерисовку и локальное сохранение. Web сообщает ошибки вместимости и отсутствующих ID; Compose сохраняет принятое полное состояние при пересоздании Activity.
- [examples/task_manager.sdr](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/blob/feature/010-records-collections-spec/examples/task_manager.sdr) — рабочий офлайн-список задач: создание, список, переключение выполнения, переименование, удаление, пустое состояние и восстановление. Ручная правка сгенерированного приложения не требуется.
- Общий внутренний компонент `sedrava_records.py` используется ядром языка. Совместимый API `sedrava_collections.py` сохранён и делегирует изменения общему механизму.
- Обновлены спецификация, README, roadmap, changelog, CLI/Build и руководства начинающего разработчика на русском и английском.

## Фактические результаты

Проверен финальный HEAD **38c3ea932c33224c0dd3a816f1a9f4f84577f90c**. Все 8 workflow PR и все запуски push этого HEAD завершились успешно. Рабочее дерево чистое; PR остаётся draft.

| Уровень | Что действительно проверено |
| --- | --- |
| Python | **121 тест**, включая сохранённые регрессии 0.9 и текстового ядра; CI на Python **3.10, 3.12, 3.13** |
| Python ↔ Web | Общая последовательность из **22 шагов**, состояния, принятие/отказ и канонический JSON; дополнительно два типа записей, int32-поля, вложенная вместимость и граница размера состояния |
| Повреждённые снимки | **20 случаев** в общем наборе: schema, поля, типы, дубликаты ключей/ID, Unicode, размер и вместимость; дополнительные проверки полного отката |
| Chromium | **17 реальных браузерных сценариев**, включая CRUD задач, устойчивые ID, перезагрузку, повреждённое хранилище, переполнение и неверный ввод |
| Android JVM | **3 теста task manager + 1 тест обобщённых записей**, с Python-эталоном, точным JSON, Unicode, int32, вместимостью и отказами |
| Android build | Успешные APK для task manager и generic fixture, Lint, компиляция instrumentation, проверка подписи и allowlist разрешений |
| Android emulator | **Android 15 x86_64**: реальный Compose CRUD, выбор, перерисовка, недопустимый ввод, поворот, пересоздание Activity и сохранение выбранного ID |
| Холодный запуск | После `am force-stop` проверен настоящий SharedPreferences-файл: элемент **id=2**, **next_id=3**; новый процесс показывает сохранённую задачу через UIAutomator |
| Дистрибутивы | wheel/sdist, Twine, аудит состава и чистая установка вне репозитория; CLI check/test/run/persistence/build web/build android |
| Физическое устройство | **Недоступно; не проверено** для этого изменения |

Проверка холодного запуска первоначально выявила, что Gradle удаляет инструментируемое приложение после теста. Исправлена настройка сохранения APK/данных; обязательные проверки SharedPreferences и интерфейса сохранены и прошли повторно. Тесты не отключались.

## CI финального HEAD

- [Основная CI](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349421)
- [Python matrix, Chromium, package audit](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349388)
- [Records: APK, JVM, generic fixture, Compose и холодный запуск](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349392)
- [Регрессия текста Android 0.10](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349841)
- [Регрессия Android 0.9](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349454)
- [Android Compose build](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349368)
- [Совместимый collection core](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349369)
- [Distribution verification](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349397)

## Артефакты

- [APK task manager и generic fixture, Web, JVM/Lint/instrumentation отчёты, SharedPreferences, XML интерфейса и скриншот после холодного запуска](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349392/artifacts/12954059319)
- [Все Web-примеры](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349388/artifacts/12954044363)
- [Трассы Chromium](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349388/artifacts/12954074414)
- [Проверенные wheel/sdist](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/actions/runs/41003349388/artifacts/12954078914)

В архиве основной APK: `tasks-android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`; автономный Web: `tasks-web/index.html`. Это артефакты CI, а не публичное развёртывание.

## Ограничения

- Нет вложенных записей/списков, равенства записей/списков, индексации, сортировки, миграций и многоэкранной навигации.
- Записи являются элементами коллекций или выражениями derive; отдельные record-state объявления не входят в этот шаг.
- До 16 скалярных полей, 16 типов записей, 16 коллекций, 100 элементов в списке; текст — 1024 Unicode scalar values; полный принятый envelope — до 200000 UTF-16 code units.
- Android-примеры пока используют общий application ID; хранилище локальное и без шифрования. Неверные черновики не обязаны переживать пересоздание.
- Успех эмулятора не является проверкой физического устройства или сертификацией доступности.
- Sedrava 0.10 не объявляется выпущенной; PR не объединён, новый релиз и публикация не созданы.

Документация: [спецификация](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/blob/feature/010-records-collections-spec/docs/RECORDS_COLLECTIONS_010.md), [engineering report](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/blob/feature/010-records-collections-spec/docs/COLLECTIONS_010_REPORT.md), [русское руководство](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/blob/feature/010-records-collections-spec/docs/RECORDS_QUICKSTART.ru.md), [English guide](https://github.com/VasiliiBabkin/sedrava/blob/feature/010-records-collections-spec/docs/RECORDS_QUICKSTART.en.md).

body: Owner requirement: every generated artifact must receive an explicit Git/DLE vs private Google Drive vs disposable placement and rights/custody decision. Public source-neutral policy in `docs/artifact-routing-aar-cdr.md`, preserving AAR/CDR as canonical direct resumable transfer mechanism. No new uploader; no private Drive IDs/machine names in this PR. Codes, schemas and small public synthetic receipts → Git/DLE; models, animations, images, audio/video, editable Blender/GLB and large original logs → private Drive, with private Git manifest and independent SHA256 remote readback. author: xerhab
body:
**Summary:** A host with one free slot no longer gets an operator's resume and a queued ticket in the same moment, and a leftover idle terminal session from the retired sleeper pause is cleaned up when an agent upgrades.

Fixes XERK-2453

## Why
- The hub works out how many slots a host has left by counting commands it has already sent that will start a session. Resumes and starts were not counted. On a one-slot host, a resume and a ticket from the hub queue could go out together, so the agent had to queue or refuse one of them. Found by QA during XERK-2441.
- XERK-2441 removed the sleeper pause. If an older agent was still shutting a paused session down when it self-updated, that session's terminal process (an `agent-<id>` tmux session) stayed running with nothing tracking it.

## What changed
- The hub counts queued `resume`, `resumeTranscript` and `start` commands as taken slots, the same way it counts spawns. This is the one set `SLOT_TAKING_COMMANDS` in `turma/server.js`.
- When the agent turns an old paused record into an ordinary ended one, it remembers that record's tmux name. At boot (`resume_on_boot`) it kills that tmux if it is still alive. This runs once and never raises. It skips any name a live session record uses, and it uses the strict alive check, so a Windows process id that has been reused is not mistaken for the leftover.

## Risk
Low.
- Resuming or starting a session that is already in error is now counted, even though that session still holds its own slot. This can delay a queued ticket by one beat. It never sends one too many.
- The boot reap only targets the exact tmux names of records that were paused. Roll back by reverting the PR.

## Testing
**QA result:** PASS. Both fixes were run for real:
- the hub gate through its HTTP routes on a one-slot host (resume, resumeTranscript, error-session resume);
- the boot reap against a real tmux server, with names that share a prefix and with hostile names.

The QA agent's low findings are handled under Follow-ups.

**Not tested:** the Windows terminal-host (pty-host) path, because there is no Windows host available. A real self-update from an agent older than XERK-2441 with a teardown in flight was simulated with seeded state rather than reproduced.

<details><summary>Test evidence</summary>

- `node --test tests/server.test.js`: 1151 pass, 0 fail. The new `XERK-2453:` case checks resume, resumeTranscript and start each fill the slot, and kill does not.
- `TestResumeCarry.test_a_dropped_pause_reaps_the_idle_tmux_it_left` covers:
  - the tmux named on the record;
  - the `agent-<id>` fallback when a record names no tmux;
  - a tmux that is already gone;
  - a kill that fails, which is swallowed;
  - a name a live session owns, which is skipped;
  - the strict alive check;
  - the reap running only once.
- QA (first pass, before the follow-up fixes): full agent suite 3569 tests passed, 6 skipped. Hub HTTP rigs QA2453-A, B, C and D. Real-tmux reap rig on `-L qa2453`. Mutations: 3 of 6 caught. The 3 that escaped are now covered by the expanded test above.
- No second QA pass after those fixes. They are a strict-flag change, adding `start` to the counted set, and test cases, each covered by the tests listed.

</details>

## Follow-ups
- QA found `start` of a stopped session uncounted (this existed before the change). Fixed here.
- QA found the boot reap's alive check was not strict on Windows. Fixed here.
- QA found three test gaps: the fallback name, the already-gone tmux, and the swallowed failure. Fixed here.
- QA found the boot reap does not stop the leftover session's web terminal (ttyd). Accepted: the closed record keeps no ttyd process id, so it cannot be found safely. The cost is at most one leaked port per affected session, once per upgrade, and new launches skip ports that are in use.

author: yumo666666
body:
This adds the one-database, multiple-finger implementation for the FPC1264 sensor, together with the design notes.

**Code included**
- `libfprint-tod/fpc1264-oem.c`: remembers the stored finger when a database is extended and rewrites the returned finger ID with `fp_print_set_finger()`, so fprintd replaces the same template instead of creating a second print.
- `oem/native_enrol.py`: when a template exists, copies it to a private path, extracts the raw `fpi-data` database, runs the existing-database enrollment pipeline and reports `native_enrol=OK database=extended canonical_finger=N`. It refuses an unexpected multi-file state instead of merging or deleting it.
- `libfprint-tod/fpc-oem-extract.c`: new root-only tool that deserializes the FP3 container, validates driver/username/finger and the database header, and writes the raw database with `O_EXCL` and mode 0600.
- `tools/build-tod.sh` and `tools/package_fingerprint.py`: build and package the extractor, install it mode 0700, and ship its source.
- `docs/FINGERPRINT-MULTI.md` / `.zh-CN.md`: the design, the measured two-finger result and the limits (five slots, one Settings row, delete-all).

**Testing**
The driver and extractor compile on the tablet against the installed libfprint TOD ABI (`fpc-oem-extract` 72,088 bytes, `libfprint-tod-fpc1264-oem.so` 76,384 bytes); the provider passes `py_compile`. The two-finger result comes from the installed round2 binaries: both fingers unlock, template grows from 772,578 B to 1,162,014 B. A fresh native acceptance on the packaged candidate has not been run, so the release scope stays one finger and the docs say so.

**Risk**
This touches the TEE enrollment path. The provider preserves the live template and only writes a new private output; a failed extract or enrollment leaves the stored database untouched. Review of the security properties is the main reason to keep it experimental until the acceptance flow is repeated.

**Goal:** site search (Phase 2d, first part): Ctrl/Cmd+K anywhere, and a /search page.

Look locally: search needs the built index, so use the workers.dev preview after this merges, or `npm run build && npx astro preview`. In `astro dev` the modal says plainly that search works on the built site.

- **Ctrl/Cmd+K or `/`** opens a search dialog from any page; the header's Search link does the same. It's a native `<dialog>`, so focus is trapped inside and returned to where you were, and Esc closes it.

- **Empty state:** "No match for '…'. Try a broader term, or browse the sections."

author: akkarit
body:
On the pilot, `hyperstorctl audit list --since 30d` showed 5 records, but the stored days held more. Without `--since`, 22 records listed as 1970-01-01, and every one came from `hyperstor-mgmt`: people's logins, role changes, and drains through the UI.

## Cause

`hyperstor-mgmt` wrote `time` as a JSON string (`"1793311482.737"`). The map service's `append` accepted either form, so these records were stored under the right key. The read side read only a number, so they had time 0:
- `matches`, which applies `--since` and `--until`;
- the API's `time_ms`.

## Fix

- `audit_log::time_of` reads a number or a string, and appending, filtering and the API all use it. The stored records keep their strings and list with their real times; no data is rewritten.
- mgmt now writes `time` as a number, as the map service does. Anything outside hyperstor that parses mgmt's audit lines from journald will see a number instead of a string.

## Tests

- `audit_log::tests::a_time_written_as_a_string_is_read` (new, tracked): a string time is read, filtered by `since` like a number, and appended. Fails without the fix.
- `audit::every_change_lands_in_the_audit_log` now lists mgmt's records with `--since 1h` and checks that none is dated 1970. With the read side and mgmt's string format restored, it fails with "No audit records", as the pilot does.

The note is I189, and the audit section of `19-administration.md` (§23.9.4) says both forms are read. Locally, fmt, clippy, the release build, the workspace tests, spec-check and `board.py check` pass.

body:
## Summary

Clicking a matrix bracket or just after a scripted symbol can put the cursor inside its contents. Correct those outer-edge hits in the shared math-field setup, covering inline math beside prose, display math, and the expanded editor.

```text
matrix left bracket  → cursor before matrix
matrix right bracket → cursor after matrix
right edge of script → cursor after complete scripted symbol
cell/base/script hit → MathLive's existing hit testing
```

The correction runs after MathLive's pointer handler, uses public element bounds and offsets, and applies only to unmodified left mouse clicks. A corrected boundary click also focuses the math field for typing.

## Evidence

- Updated against MathLive 2.5.2 (`7966724`), retaining its mobile layout, keyboard focus handling, and Quick Latex shorthands.
- **Before:** clicking the left bracket of an inline 2×2 matrix beside normal text produced offset 7 inside the matrix instead of offset 2 before it.
  **After:** real mouse clicks on both sides of square and round matrices place the cursor at the expected outer offsets; typing `z` confirms insertion outside the matrix and persistence in the note while surrounding prose remains intact.
- Additional tests verify complete subscript/superscript boundaries and normal editing inside cells, scripts, and bases.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass.
- All 30 tests in `compound-cursor.spec.mjs` pass across inline, display, and expanded editors.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored-note migration or dependency changes.

**Blast Radius:** cursor. Only matrix-bracket and script-edge mouse hits are corrected; modified clicks and other input types retain MathLive's behavior.

author: dbtlr
body:
An exclusive option group counted a fill from the environment or the configuration source as a supplied member, the same as a typed token. ADR-0085 stated that no cross-option source precedence suppresses an exclusive conflict. So with `exclusive('json', 'yaml')`, `json = true` in a configuration file and a typed `--yaml` failed with exit 2. Every later run that typed `--yaml` failed the same way until someone edited the file. That contradicts Loom's own precedence, where argv wins over the environment and the environment wins over the configuration source.

Now the highest input tier that supplies a member of an exclusive group wins. Right after the input-source stage fills, and before validation, core withdraws each member a lower tier filled beside a sibling a higher tier supplied.

- A withdrawn member reads as unfilled by every tier. Its declared default applies, or it is omitted. Nothing validates its lower tier's value, it is absent from the `supplied` record, and it activates nothing.
- `json = true` in the file with a typed `--yaml` runs with `yaml`. An environment member wins over a configured one, and the named values of an `invoke()` call are the argv tier.
- Members one tier supplied still conflict, such as `--json --yaml`, two bound variables, or two configured keys. The diagnostic still names each member's source.
- A bound variable outside its grammar beside a sibling typed in argv is the member's lower tier, so the run reports no failure for it.
- `oneRequired` and `requiredTogether` count every tier's fills, a withdrawn member included. Their problem's `supplied` list names what they counted, and a `requiredTogether` diagnostic names the source that filled a withdrawn member.
- A member in two exclusive groups withdraws when either group holds a member a higher tier supplied, whatever the declaration order.
- Decision record: ADR-0123 (proposed) narrows ADR-0085's clause that no cross-option source precedence suppresses an exclusive conflict. ADR-0085 and ADR-0032 carry dated entries.

**Checks**

- Tests written first in `packages/core/tests/option-groups.test.ts`:
  - a typed member wins over a configured sibling, which reads at its default and unsupplied
  - a typed member wins over a sibling's bound variable
  - an environment member wins over a configured sibling
  - members one tier supplied still conflict, and the diagnostic names each source
  - a withdrawn member is never validated
  - `oneRequired` is satisfied by a configured member
  - `requiredTogether` counts a withdrawn member
  - a member in two exclusive groups gives the same outcome whatever the declaration order
  - a variable outside its grammar beside a typed sibling is not reported
  - named `invoke()` values are the argv tier
- Tests added in the review round:
  - a `requiredTogether` failure over a withdrawn member names the source that filled it
  - `oneRequired` is satisfied by a withdrawn member
  - a rejected variable beside a typed sibling satisfies no other group
  - a group problem's `supplied` list names a withdrawn member it counted (through `invoke()`)
  - a withdrawn configured member's omission reads the run's working directory
- Each of the five surviving mutants was applied one at a time with core rebuilt, and each failed one of these tests.
- `pnpm verify`: pass, 292 test files, 6376 tests passed and 192 skipped.
- `pnpm check:packed`: pass.

**Review**

Review seats returned ten findings. The controller judged each against the two tests.

- Broken link to the exclusive option group in `docs/core/validation.md`, reported twice: fixed.
- A `requiredTogether` diagnostic over a withdrawn member dropped that member's source label, reported twice: fixed. The withdrawn member's label is kept for group reports, and a failing test came first.
- A test name stated the opposite of the order-independence it checks: renamed.
- The `Tier` doc comment misstated the rank order: corrected.
- Surviving mutants in `oneRequired` counting and in the problem's `supplied` list: killed by new tests.
- Surviving mutants in the `isSupplied` guard and `fills.delete` in `withdrawLosers`: killed by new tests.
- `requiredTogether` still counted a withdrawn member, so `exclusive('token','user')` plus `requiredTogether('user','password')` with a configured `user` failed every typed `--token` run. The owner ruled that a `requiredTogether` group holding a withdrawn member is not checked: fixed in 7d1800ef, with tests for `user` configured alone and beside `password`.
- A false higher-tier fill, such as `--no-yaml`, withdrew a configured true sibling, so neither member applied. The owner ruled that a Boolean member at its absent value neither claims the group nor conflicts, so `--json --no-yaml` runs, while a typed `negative` member still claims its group: fixed in 7d1800ef and f54cee65, with completion and the MCP schema aligned and ADR-0085's every-spelling rule loosened by a dated entry.

Verifier (Opus, fresh context): PASS on the first fix round. A second delta Verifier passed the owner-ruling round, reverting each ruling's code to see its tests fail and probing every tier, completion, the MCP schema, and help; its two notes (a stale sentence in `docs/core/options.md` and a stale test name) are fixed in 7cbc7404.

Kody reviewed the PR and found no issues.

**Decisions for the owner**

- A losing member is decided right after the input-source stage fills and before validation, so its lower tier's value is never validated.
- A losing member takes its declared default or is omitted, and it is absent from the `supplied` record.
- The named values of an `invoke()` call are the argv tier.
- `oneRequired` counts every tier's raw fills, a withdrawn member included; a `requiredTogether` group holding a withdrawn member is not checked (owner ruling).
- A rejected variable of a member beside a sibling typed in argv is not reported.

**Changelog:** .changes/exclusive-group-highest-tier.md (fix) and .changes/feature.locate-booleans.md (feature, `locate()` reports `booleans`)

body:
🤖 Research for the spec's "the play button sails the voyage on its own calendar" (`docs/spec/design.md`, the voyage row's Feature). It proposes; it settles nothing. Docs and images only: no app code, no voyage data.

Head: 48ba1a8f3c2a573e0cc7d74538b8feae2803d862

## What changed
- **`docs/voyage-play/README.md`**: the play transition in six key frames, three ways to carry the controls, three shapes for a leg's dates, and a census of how today's free-text dates parse.
- **Images**: each one is the real renderer at map size (1600 × 1000) with Magellan's track cut at the pen's date, and the controls painted over it as mockups. The pen's calendar comes from today's `dates` strings, parsed, so it is what a play button could do with the data as it stands.

## The play transition: Magellan, 1,082 days in nine seconds
Before, pressed, the San Julián winter (pen still, date running), mid-Pacific, the months at Tidore, home.

![key frames](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mark-brannan/portolani/48ba1a8f3c2a573e0cc7d74538b8feae2803d862/docs/voyage-play/play-frames.jpg)

## Three ways to carry the controls (same moment, 20 Jun 1520)
A: the button alone, the date beside the pen. B: the row grows a calendar strip. C: a log-book band at the foot of the map, with pause, stop, the date, the leg and the strip as scrubber. **Pick: C**, the only one that keeps the date and the leg in view when the drawer is shut or is a phone's bottom sheet.

| A | B | C |
|---|---|---|
| ![A](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mark-brannan/portolani/48ba1a8f3c2a573e0cc7d74538b8feae2803d862/docs/voyage-play/variant-a.jpg) | ![B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mark-brannan/portolani/48ba1a8f3c2a573e0cc7d74538b8feae2803d862/docs/voyage-play/variant-b.jpg) | ![C](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mark-brannan/portolani/48ba1a8f3c2a573e0cc7d74538b8feae2803d862/docs/voyage-play/play-3-winter.jpg) |

## The shape of a leg's dates
Shown on Magellan's third leg, today `"dates": "Nov – 29 Nov 1519"`:

| shape | the leg |
|---|---|
| 1. two dates, each as precise as the source | `"start": "1519-11", "end": "1519-11-29"` |
| 2. one EDTF interval | `"when": "1519-11/1519-11-29"` |
| 3. days from the voyage's start | voyage `"start": "1519-09-20"`, leg `"days": [42, 70]` |

**Pick: shape 1.** Each end reads alone and checks with one regular expression; its length is its precision, which the player needs where a month-wide end overlaps the next leg (Magellan's `Nov 1520`, measured); it is the plainest subset of EDTF, so shape 2 can be made from it; `dates` stays as the tile's wording.

Census of today's strings, measured: **9 of 36 voyages** parse to the month or day on every leg and could play on their calendar now; 16 parse but only to the year on some leg; 11 have a leg that does not parse (28 legs: seasons, `early`, `late`, `after 1513`, `1502 or 1503`, centuries).

## Goldens
None: no drawing changed, so `npm run golden` was not run.

## Pencil:
- The mockups use Magellan at a world view (lon 15, lat -6, zoom 1.45), the line at 4.5 px (the Heavy weight item 4 proposes) rather than the shipped 2.2.
- Where a month-wide leg end overlaps the next leg, the mockup puts the boundary at the precise side, else mid-month.
- The mockup and census scripts are not committed (a research PR, no code); the census table is in the README.
- The census counts a `sameAs` leg once in each voyage that has it.

Tests: `node --test test/decisions-verbs.test.mjs test/voyages.test.mjs test/assets.test.mjs`: 70 pass, 0 fail. The full suite was not run: docs only.

## Scope: opener-0573 — §9.1 Shared extension project

Define conservative, transport-independent **browser capability flags** for Chromium, Firefox, and Safari WebExtensions without granting or inferring permissions.

### Changes
- Add `extensions/webextension/src/browser-capabilities.js` with a stable, frozen six-flag catalog and opt-in `getBrowserCapabilityFlags(selectedNamespace)`.
- Report only explicitly observed API shapes for runtime metadata, runtime messaging, and the complete downloads event interface. Unknown, incomplete, inherited, getter-based, or hostile API members default to `false`; the detector never calls browser API methods.
- Keep `nativeMessagingEnabled`, `pdfOpeningEnabled`, and `scannerVerificationEnabled` hard-disabled. API presence does **not** mean effective permission, authenticated sender, PDF safety verdict, or authority to scan/open a file.
- Add eight Node regression tests for shape detection, fail-closed behavior, no getter execution, immutable snapshots, and absence of browser side effects.
- Document contract, security limitations and relationship to the separately scoped browser compatibility adapter.

### Coordination and preservation
- Rechecked live `origin/main`, open and merged task PRs, and the recursive repository tree; there are no applicable `AGENTS.md` files or existing opener-0573 implementation.
- Open PR #367 (opener-0572) implements Promise/callback API compatibility; this PR **does not modify that adapter or its files**. It also leaves the shared background, Firefox/Safari manifests, messaging and download modules intact.
- Exactly three isolated new files; no scanner, quarantine, native helper, installed extension, Xcode project, permissions, user customizations or CI workflow changes.
- The current `npm test` wildcard already discovers `tests/browser-capabilities.test.mjs`, and required `scanner-tests` runs it with Node 22, so no duplicate CI job is needed.

### Verification
- Node 22 in a fresh isolated workdir: `node --test tests/browser-capabilities.test.mjs`: **8 passed**.
- Direct git clone was unavailable because the execution container could not resolve github.com; GitHub connector was used for an isolated branch from verified live main and to commit changes.
- Gate the squash merge on all GitHub checks for the final head SHA; verify `merged=true` and the full merge commit SHA independently.

body:
Azure Blob stores declared presigned URLs whatever their credentials, although the SDK signs a SAS with an account key only. A store opened with a SAS token, the default credential chain, anonymous access or a connection string without an account key reported the capability, then failed in presignGet and presignPut with a NullPointerException from the SDK. Such stores report no presigned URL support and refuse to presign with an UnsupportedCapabilityException.

Fixes #150

author: deandret
body:
Keeps every occurrence of an element that an XSD `xs:any` wildcard also matches, so values are neither dropped nor duplicated.

- **Reading:** a declared single-occurrence field takes the first matching element. Later occurrences go through the lax wildcard's checks and become generic items, keeping their position in ordered content. Before, they were dropped, or read back as copies of the first value.
- **XSD import:** wildcard ports that duplicate a declared sibling are resolved at import, including referenced globals, extensions of either side, and ports covering several namespaces. A strict wildcard has no generic fallback, so import refuses it with a typed error wherever extras couldn't be represented.
- **Writing:** a generic item may reuse a declared name only after that field's own element has been written, so read→write→read round-trips. No-namespace declarations are matched by name, as the reader matches them.
- **Typed refusals:** extras outside the wildcard's namespaces, too many extras, and unrepresentable orderings are refused rather than silently changed.
- **Docs:** `docs/design/xml-wildcard-exclusions.md` and the formats reference describe the rules and the check order.

Related problems found along the way: #1183 (unqualified declarations match any namespace) and #1184 (generic elements pick up indentation as text).

Closes #1142.

author: fotedev
body:
## What

Adds a new string field `dotnet.mvid` with the module version identifier (MVID) of the
.NET module. The MVID is the first GUID in the `#GUID` metadata stream, which YARA has
always exposed as `dotnet.guids[0]`. Tooling built on the module typically dumps that
value as a generic "guid", which is easily confused with the COM typelib GUID exposed
by `dotnet.typelib` (that one comes from the `GuidAttribute` custom attribute). This is
the confusion reported in #2057, where ildasm/dnlib label the value "MVID".

## Why no rename

`guids`/`number_of_guids` keep their exact meaning and values, so existing rules keep
working unchanged - the declared field surface is treated as frozen for compatibility.
The docs now state explicitly that `guids[0]` is the MVID.

## Docs & tests

- `docs/modules/dotnet.rst`: new `mvid` entry (`.. versionadded:: 4.7.0`) plus a
  clarification in the `guids` entry.
