Builds #62 (spec #51 "Office Contact plugin" and "Public reads" (Contact), `01` §10, `03` §12). Targets `003-public-website`.

## Summary

Staff keep **Office Contact** on one Admin settings form. Citizens see it on `/contact`, and every page's footer shows the official channels.

```text
Admin → Plugins → songhealth-office-contact → Settings          (Administrator only: plugins:manage)
  ที่อยู่สำนักงาน · โทรศัพท์ · อีเมล · เวลาทำการ · ละติจูด · ลองจิจูด · ลิงก์ LINE

/contact
  H1 ติดต่อเรา + lead, breadcrumb หน้าแรก › ติดต่อเรา, canonical /contact
  ที่ตั้ง        address + "เปิดแผนที่" (map link from the coordinates, new tab, rel=noopener; nothing embedded)
  โทรศัพท์      tel: link while it is one number, else text
  อีเมล         mailto: link while it is one plain address, else text
  เวลาทำการ
  ช่องทางทางการ  Facebook · LINE · YouTube · X · Instagram · LinkedIn · GitHub, only those set
  ร้องเรียนและเสนอแนะ        → ดูบริการประชาชน (/services)
  ติดต่อหน่วยบริการสุขภาพ    → ดูหน่วยบริการสุขภาพที่เกี่ยวข้อง (/health-services)
  An empty value leaves its line out; with nothing set the page still answers.

footer (every page)
  ช่องทางทางการ: Facebook ↗ · LINE ↗ · …   (only those set; "(เว็บไซต์ภายนอก) (เปิดในแท็บใหม่)" for screen readers)
  นโยบายความเป็นส่วนตัว · การเข้าถึงเว็บไซต์ · ติดต่อเรา
```

```diff
 astro.config.mjs                     # + plugins: [{ id, version, entrypoint: src/plugins/office-contact.ts }]
 src/
+├── plugins/office-contact.ts        # createPlugin(): definePlugin({ admin: { settingsSchema } }), nothing else
 ├── lib/
+│   ├── office-contact-settings.ts   # plugin identity, the settings form, officeContactFrom()  (no runtime import)
+│   ├── contact-links.ts             # telephoneHref, emailHref, officialChannels               (no runtime import)
+│   └── office-contact.ts            # readOfficeContact(): getPluginSettings + getSiteSettings().social
 ├── components/
+│   ├── ActionLink.astro             # pill call to action, now shared by /contact and the 404 page
 │   └── ContentLink.astro            # + compact: the "leaves the site" note for screen readers only
 ├── layouts/SiteLayout.astro         # + footer channel list
 └── pages/
+    └── contact.astro
 scripts/
 ├── dev-runtime-verify.sh            # + "the Office Contact plugin is registered and enabled, with its settings form"
 ├── dev-runtime-common.sh            # pat_get, shared by pat_identity and the new check
 ├── fixture-kit.ts                   # + officeContact(): show values for a screenshot run, restore after
+└── screenshot-fixtures/contact.ts
```

**Channels:** the native `social` settings hold usernames, not addresses; the Admin asks for "Your Facebook page or profile username" and so on. So `officialChannels` builds the profile address:
- a handle in any script, such as `@สาธารณสุขอำเภอสอง`, becomes the profile address;
- a pasted address is kept, and `https://` is added when it is missing;
- a value that is neither, or an address that is not http(s), is left out.

**Extension gate (`10` §22):** EmDash's site settings accept only a fixed key set. A plugin's `settingsSchema` is the platform's own way to add a settings form. The plugin has no hooks, routes, storage or capabilities.

**Version facts relied on** (emdash 1.1.0, recorded with source paths in `docs/agents/emdash-1.1.0.md` "Plugins and plugin settings"):
- **Registration:** a native plugin is a `plugins: []` descriptor whose entrypoint exports `createPlugin()`. A configured plugin with no stored state is active.
- **Settings form:** the Admin generates it at `/_emdash/admin/plugins-manager/{id}/settings`. It saves an emptied field as `null`, which deletes the value. `getPluginSettings` returns stored values only.
- **Permission:** the settings API needs `plugins:manage` (Administrator only, `@emdash-cms/auth` `src/rbac.ts`), and a token also needs the `admin` scope. Recorded on #51 (comment 6516981671).
- **`social` writes:** the settings API patches `social` key by key and accepts only strings, so a handle can be emptied but never deleted.

## Evidence

- **Before** (tests first, runtime at the base `3a7f5b9`):
  - `cms-office-contact.spec.ts` and `public-contact.spec.ts`: 10/10 failed. The plugin settings API answered 404, and `/contact` answered 404.
  - node: `src/lib/contact*.ts` missing.
- **After:**
  - **Full browser suite at `b1e0d16`** (served by the runtime, VERIFY PASS): **244 passed, 14 skipped** (the coordinator-only `cms-public-reads`). T021 coordinator: 14/14, no owned-fixture residue. `dev-runtime-residue.sh`: RESIDUE NONE.
  - `f9e8e64` (this head) changes only a comment. The runtime is promoted to it (VERIFY PASS, 17 checks including the new plugin check), and the two contact suites pass 10/10 there.
  - `npm run test:node` 166/166 (13 new). Typecheck, `build:check`, `format:check`, knip and `lint:shell` are clean. The pre-commit hook passed on every commit.

```text
plugin       listed enabled + hasSettings; schema = the 7 fields with their Thai labels
             Admin form at /_emdash/admin/plugins-manager/songhealth-office-contact/settings shows every label (dev-bypass session)
permission   role fixture switched to Editor: GET settings 403, PUT settings 403; restored to Author
/contact     address lines; เปิดแผนที่ → https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=18.4686%2C100.1834, target=_blank,
             rel=noopener; no iframe/embed/object; tel:054591234; mailto:…; opening hours; canonical; breadcrumb
channels     /contact and footer: Facebook → facebook.com/songhealth.{x}, LINE → lin.ee/{x}, YouTube → youtube.com/@…,
             each new tab + noopener, accessible name "… (เว็บไซต์ภายนอก) (เปิดในแท็บใหม่)"; Homepage footer too
empty        "054 591 234 ต่อ 12" + latitude only → one row โทรศัพท์ as text, no map link
             nothing set → 200, no details, no channel heading or list, both calls to action still there
CTA          ดูบริการประชาชน → /services (clicked); ดูหน่วยบริการสุขภาพที่เกี่ยวข้อง → /health-services
axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) + visible focus at 1440 and 320 px, with Office Contact set and with nothing set;
no sideways scroll at 320 px with a long email; third-party request guard on every page load
settings     saved first and restored in finally (Office Contact exactly; social handles see Notes)
```

Screenshots: `scripts/screenshot-fixtures/contact.ts`, taken at `b1e0d16`. `f9e8e64` changes no captured page.

| | Desktop | Mobile 375 | Mobile 320 |
|---|---|---|---|
| /contact | ![](https://github.com/9GotStory/songhealth/blob/b2c45bf485c7a5ee33be4d450261129f5caa5822/contact-desktop.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/9GotStory/songhealth/blob/b2c45bf485c7a5ee33be4d450261129f5caa5822/contact-375.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/9GotStory/songhealth/blob/b2c45bf485c7a5ee33be4d450261129f5caa5822/contact-320.png?raw=true) |
| menu open | | ![](https://github.com/9GotStory/songhealth/blob/b2c45bf485c7a5ee33be4d450261129f5caa5822/contact-375-menu.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/9GotStory/songhealth/blob/b2c45bf485c7a5ee33be4d450261129f5caa5822/contact-320-menu.png?raw=true) |

**Product Owner decisions** (#62 comment 6516956505, "ตามที่แนะนำ"):
1. Telephone and email links: accepted as built.
2. **Footer channels: changed.** The links are compact ("Facebook ↗"), and `/contact` keeps "(เว็บไซต์ภายนอก)" in view. Done in `b1e0d16`.
3. Channel order and handle rules: accepted. #67's staff guidance gains the Office Contact items, including "paste the page's full address".
4. `/contact` copy: accepted. Revisit the complaints button once a complaints Service exists.

**Built on precedent:**
- **Detail card:** the `ที่ตั้ง` label with the map link and the `เวลาทำการ` label come from the Health Service page.

body: Deck, match, and cloud game writes each wired the same durable queue by hand: repository classes re-exposing the engine, a hand-mapped connected drain, copied backoff and lifecycle code, and callers passing their in-memory lists in so dedupe and failure budgets worked. Cleaning up a finished game deleted the queue's keys from outside the queue. `createOutbox` (`src/features/sync/outbox.ts`) now owns persist, dedupe, order, the drain loop, backoff, failure capacity, and `clear()` for one queue. The four queues shrink to a codec, `send`, `rejectReason`, and their own rules. The cloud game controller reads pending and failed writes from the outbox instead of keeping a second copy, so `mergeDrainSnapshot`, `drainingIds`, `dismissedFailureIds`, and `inFlight` are gone. Terminal-game cleanup calls `outbox.clear()`. Stored keys and record shapes are unchanged. `test/storedOutboxes.test.ts` holds strings that main's own writers stored for all four queues (run before any code changed: 2a5c6572 for decks and games, b0757e9f for matches), copied byte for byte. It loads them under this branch, then drains, dismisses, and clears them. A separate orchestrator run generated fresh records with main's writers for all four queues; they loaded, sent once, dismissed, and cleared here too. Small behavior differences: - A cloud game paused at failure capacity retries when the queue changes (new tap, folded tap, confirmed write, dismissed failure), on each server projection, and on reconnect. Main retried on every publish. - An environment change no longer aborts an in-flight pass; the drain checks it can still sync before each send. - A write queued while a pass runs goes out in the same pass. - On web, a tab sees another tab's queued writes after its own next drain instead of on every publish. Also in scope: the manual match queue (landed in #791 during this work) and one call site in `src/features/stats/deckChoices.ts`. `src/features/sync/drainOutbox.ts` stays as a one-line type re-export because `src/features/lan` imports from that path. ### Proof - `pnpm compile`, lint on changed files, `pnpm deps:check`: clean. - Jest over sync, connected, decks, stats, matches, lan, the compatibility test, ShippingIndexRoute, and the connected, deck, and record-match screen tests: 100 suites, 1065 tests pass. The 5 failure-capacity recovery tests in `OutboxSyncController.test.ts` fail on e8d7cee7 and pass on 95744096. - Web on the dev backend (Playwright, Convex socket blocked to go offline): renamed a synced deck and changed a card count offline, tapped life in a cloud game offline, reloaded while offline, then reconnected without reloading. Everything drained once: john's board showed jane at exactly 14 (20, −2 online, −4 offline), and a fresh jane session read the deck edits from the server. Afterward I reverted the deck and abandoned the game; the game's local keys were cleared. | Deck after offline reload | Deck back online | | --- | --- | | | | | Jane after offline reload (3 queued) | John after reconnect | | --- | --- | | | | ### Review - Refactor (e8d7cee7, same patch as reviewed 7d88936c): Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) and `codex review` both failed with 429. A fresh read-only Claude Opus 5.5 (high) reviewer: **APPROVE**, 6 nits, none changed. Follow-ups: a stale `drainAgain` after stop can cost one extra pass; skip republishing when `dismiss` removes nothing; `deckChoices` could read pending card writes without loading failures. - Orchestrator differential run (main vs a513f77a, scripted fake Convex): no P0/P1; found the failure-capacity recovery regression, fixed in 95744096. - Fix (95744096): Sol and `codex review` were rate-limited (429) again. A fresh Claude Opus 5.5 reviewer on that commit: no P0/P1; recovery covers every trigger main had, retries no faster than main, and the 5 tests fail without it. One P2 (an offline projection or tap hid the "need review" message until reconnect) is fixed in the next commit, with a test that fails without it. - Offline fix (orchestrator): the pause lifts only when the outbox can drain. 712 tests across sync, connected, decks, matches and storedOutboxes pass; compile and lint clean. `codex review` still rate-limited. author: poli0981
body:
## Summary

winget-pkgs deprecated manifest version 1.12.0 on 2026-10-30, and a moderator sweep flagged the 1.0.1 pull request, microsoft/winget-pkgs#439835. That one was raised to 1.28.0 by hand on its branch the same morning (poli0981/winget-pkgs@b1d934e), and the bot dropped `Needs-Author-Feedback`. Every released Komac still writes 1.12.0, so `submit.ps1 -Version 1.0.2` would have been flagged the same way.

Raising the version after `komac update` is not enough by itself. From Komac's source:

| Komac | `komac update` | `komac submit` |
|---|---|---|
| 2.16.0 (pinned) | writes `ManifestVersion: 1.12.0` | keeps the field, but rewrites every `$schema` comment from a per-type constant: the 1.12.0 schema |
| 2.17.0, 2.17.1 | the same | also resets `ManifestVersion` to 1.12.0 in every manifest but the installer |

So Komac now only generates, and the script submits the bytes it checked:

- `Set-ManifestVersion` raises Komac's output to `$ManifestVersion` (`1.28.0`, a new row in doc 11's table).
- Step 5 reads each file once, as bytes, and checks both the field and the schema comment. A hand-written `-ManifestDir` set at another version is refused.
- Step 6 sends those bytes: a branch on the fork (`createRef`), one commit GitHub signs (`createCommitOnBranch`), then the pull request over REST, with Komac's branch and title format. The body is winget-pkgs' checklist, ticking only what the script checked. "Tested manifest locally" is left for a person to tick after a Sandbox run. A dry run writes the title and body to `build/winget/x.y.z/` as well.
- Komac sees the token only while `komac update` runs.

## Docs

The procedure changed, so doc 11 changes with it. Per-release steps 1 and 3 now say the script raises the version and opens the pull request itself, and "Komac, and why it is pinned" says why `komac submit` is gone. Doc 15's WinGet row records the 1.0.1 bump.

## Verified

- `Set-ManifestVersion`, taken from the script through its AST, turns the five 1.12.0 files Komac 2.16.0 wrote for microsoft/winget-pkgs#439835 into exactly the bytes now on that pull request's branch, which `winget validate` passes.
- A dry run against the hand-written 1.0.1 set passes every check and `winget validate`. Its title comes out as `New package: poli0981.MarkLens version 1.0.1`, and the body reads as intended. The same run on the old 1.12.0 set fails exactly the five manifest-version checks.
- `winget_test.dart` has four new or rewritten tests. Removing the raise and bringing back `komac submit` turned three of them red.
- `flutter test test/repo` (88) passes; `flutter analyze` and `dart format` are clean.

## Not verified

Step 6 cannot run without opening a real pull request on microsoft/winget-pkgs, so its first run will be v1.0.2's submission. Its calls are the one that fixed microsoft/winget-pkgs#439835 this morning (`createCommitOnBranch`) and the one Komac makes to create the branch (`createRef`, whose input type was checked by introspection); the pull request itself is a plain REST `POST /pulls`.

body:
This PR defines the completed enveloping algebra `Û = lim_N U / I_N` of a residue central extension at a fixed level, where `U = U(ĝ) / (ι K - a)` and `I_N` are the left ideals generated by high-order currents. It is built as the limit of the tower of quotients `U / I_0 ← U / I_1 ← ⋯`, using the existing `TauCeti.ModuleTower` limit API. It carries the inverse limit topology, which is linear, Hausdorff and complete. The canonical map `U → Û` has dense range, induces the `I`-topology on `U`, and has kernel `⨅ N, I_N`. The orbit maps of `U` on `Û` are continuous: for each `x` and `N` there is `M` with `I_M x` contained in the kernel of the projection to `U / I_N`.

Roadmap target: [AffineLieAlgebras/README.md, A4 "Central-level UEA and left-ideal completion"](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/AffineLieAlgebras/README.md#a4-central-level-uea-and-left-ideal-completion), specifically "Define Ûκ as the compatible-family inverse limit of these discrete modules. Prove its linear complete/Hausdorff structure, coordinate topology, canonical dense Uκ map". This builds on `orderLeftIdeal` and the right-shift estimate `exists_forall_mul_mem_orderLeftIdeal` from #22084. After this PR, A4 still needs the PBW separation `⋂ I_N = 0` (equivalently, injectivity of `U → Û`), the ring structure on `Û` obtained by extending the `U`-action on the smooth `Q_N`, with its closed left-ideal kernels and continuity estimates, and the polynomial/formal comparison.

New files:

- `TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Tower/Topology.lean` (184 lines). The inverse limit topology on `lim A` for any tower of modules over any ring. The kernels of the projections form a basis of neighbourhoods of zero. It provides `IsTopologicalAddGroup`, `IsUniformAddGroup`, `IsLinearTopology`, `T2Space` and `CompleteSpace` instances, local constancy of the projections, and a dense-range criterion.
- `TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Tower/Quotient.lean` (178 lines). The tower `ModuleTower.quotients J hJ` of quotients `M ⧸ Jₙ` for a decreasing family of submodules over a possibly noncommutative ring. It comes with the canonical map `toLimQuotients`, its kernel `⨅ n, Jₙ`, the pullback of projection kernels to `Jₙ`, dense range, and surjective projections. The existing `ModuleTower.reduction` is the dedicated commutative ideal-power case and is left unchanged.
- `TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Current/Completion.lean` (118 lines). The tower `orderQuotientTower`, the type `CompletedEnveloping`, the kernel of `U → Û`, and the orbit-continuity estimate.

The tower is indexed by `n : ℕ`, which is cofinal among the integer orders, so it gives the same topology as the positive-order system in the roadmap (`iInf_orderLeftIdeal_natCast`). No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored. The topology construction follows the existing filter-basis pattern of `TauCeti.Algebra.Lie.Current.Topology`. The modules cite Frenkel, *Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups*, §2.1.2 and §3.2.1, and Bourbaki (*General Topology* III §7, *Commutative Algebra* III §2).

Roadmap: AffineLieAlgebras

author: axtimpoka
body:
## What this changes

Adds `.github/CODEOWNERS` naming `@dennisjhao` as the owner of two paths:

```
/.github/workflows/   — CI can check everything except itself
/.github/CODEOWNERS   — the file that assigns ownership has to be owned
```

`require_code_owner_reviews` was turned on before this PR (repo settings, not a file). `required_approving_review_count` stays **0**, so ordinary PRs still need no approval. Only owned paths should need one.

This is Step 5's last rule from the article: any CI workflow file needs a person. A one-person repo cannot say that with an approval count, because GitHub blocks self-approval.

Why CODEOWNERS owns itself: otherwise a PR deletes it and changes a workflow in the same diff. Same shape as the `CLAUDE.md` problem — the thing that governs review must not be editable by what is being reviewed.

## How it was tested

**Not yet, and that is why this PR is on its own.** Two things are unverified:

1. Whether GitHub enforces owner review when `required_approving_review_count` is 0. The API accepted the combination; accepting is not enforcing.
2. Whether an ordinary PR touching no owned path still needs no approval.

Both get a throwaway PR after this merges, and the result goes in `PIPELINE.md` then — not before. Writing "this works" ahead of measuring it is a mistake this repo has already made twice in this step.

Note the bootstrap gap: this PR adds the file, so the file does not govern this PR. `@dennisjhao` is not required here. Every later change to those paths should need them.

## How to undo it

`git revert`, plus turning `require_code_owner_reviews` back off — that part is repo settings and is not in git:

```
gh api -X PATCH repos/AxtimPoka/claude-review/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews \
  -F require_code_owner_reviews=false -F dismiss_stale_reviews=true -F required_approving_review_count=0
```

author: waylandyang
body:
Lets an operator pick a node's backend from the console instead of editing its systemd unit.

## Design

**Add node.** Auto, gVisor or Firecracker, plus optional kernel path and work dir, carried into the install command. The master validates paths before they reach a root shell.

**Installer.** `SANDSTORM_BACKEND` is `auto`, `gvisor` or `firecracker`; unset stays gVisor, so existing scripts keep working. It checks `/dev/kvm`, the guest kernel and a real reflink probe, then runs the new `sandstormd preflight`, which makes the same checks a node makes at startup. A refusal says what is missing and installs nothing. Auto prints what it picked and why. Firecracker comes from `SANDSTORM_FIRECRACKER`, the PATH, or the release and sha256 pinned in `setup-host.sh`.

**Switching.** The choice lives in a file (`--backend-file`), not the unit's command line, because `ProtectSystem=strict` keeps the node out of `/etc`. `POST /v1/nodes/:id/backend` sends a `SetBackend` command; the node preflights, rewrites the file and exits 75 for `Restart=on-failure`. Refused while the master records any sandbox or snapshot on the node, and again by the node if anything is in `bundles/`, warm seeds included. Snapshots count too: a tag on a dial-in node is forked on that node, so it would be restored on the wrong engine. The node is out of placement from acceptance until it reports the new engine, or 120 s. The dialog says it will change host group.

**Templates.** Nodes report which templates they can start on their backend. The master places a template only on those; if none can, the create is a 409 naming both forms. Nodes that have not reported are placed on as before.

**Create dialogs.** "Where" lists each backend with its pools, and each node with its backend. This needed a new optional `backend` on `POST /v1/sandboxes`: a pool name also matches its `#fingerprint` groups, so it cannot pin a backend.

## Behaviour changes

- gVisor install now **refuses** when runsc is missing; it used to warn.
- Nodes installed before this have no backend file, and must be reinstalled to switch. The console says so.

Also fixes an existing installer bug: backticked words in the unit's comments ran as root during install (`ip netns add`, `runsc start`) and were lost from the unit.

## Verified

On the bare-metal KVM host, with a real master, `install.sh`, systemd unit, runsc and Firecracker v1.17.0, on an XFS loop mount:

- Auto on an ext4 work dir: picked Firecracker, refused, nothing installed.
- gVisor install, then a sandbox ran; the switch got a 409 and the file was unchanged.
- Empty node: switched to Firecracker, NRestarts 0 to 1, fingerprint changed, and a real microVM answered exec (guest kernel 6.1.141) under the hardened unit.
- Template with no ext4 form: 409 naming both forms.
- Switched back to gVisor; a sandbox ran.

Tests: `cargo test --all` on Linux, 316 passed. `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean. Console 12 passed, plus `packaging/tests/install_backend.sh`; both are added to CI.

## Not verified

- The Firecracker download path in the installer: the test host already had a binary on its PATH.
- A switch on a node in a mixed pool on real machines: the node was alone, so its pool name stayed `default`. Moving groups is covered by the existing `refingerprint_node` test.
- Listen-mode nodes on real machines.
- The new dialogs in a browser: only type-checked, built and unit-tested.

## What and why

This is C3 of `docs/tech-plan.md`. It serves DESIGN.md "Designed for drop-in, drop-out": friends get onto the island sooner, and returning players re-download less after each deploy. Gameplay is unchanged.

- **The caves load after start, in their own chunk.** Their ground shape (`site.js`) stays eager, so terrain and lockstep inputs are unchanged.
- **The Boogler's conversations** (`talk.js` and the 1,100-line `lines.js`) load right after start. If you talk to him before they arrive, the box opens once they do. His short lines (pats, rides, fleeing) move to a new eager `barks.js`.
- **The netdebug overlay and the debug camera** load only with `?netdebug=1` or `?debugcam=1`. Their code is now in `src/debug/`.
- **Vendor chunks:** three.js, cannon-es and PeerJS are split out, so they stay cached across deploys.
- **`onStart(fn)`** now runs right away if start has already happened, so a lazily loaded module can register hooks the same way an eager one does.
- **The "Lazy parts" rule** is documented in `src/loop.js` and in one line of AGENTS.md. It never applies to sync ops or state, `src/world/rules/`, or anything visible in the first seconds.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Initial download, gzipped | 384.9 kB | 359.4 kB (−6.6%) |
| What a game-code-only deploy re-downloads, gzipped | ~385 kB | ~107 kB |

Draw calls are the same: they cluster around 135 on both builds, and shadow calls stay at 55–56.

`npm run check` passes (152 tests). The `smoke` scenario passes all 9 checks. CI runs `world-inputs`, which pins that lockstep order and inputs are unchanged, plus `smoke` and `two-player-dig`.

author: tihero87
body:
## CHIRP-4301: upgrade ui-kit dependencies and close known vulnerabilities

Jira: https://chirpiot.atlassian.net/browse/CHIRP-4301

Base: `build/release-v3.12.0`, cut from `build/release-v3.9.0` (the line chirp-frontend consumes). Each group is a separate commit, so any group can be reverted on its own.

### Result
- `yarn audit`: 3 critical / 152 high / 82 moderate / 27 low → **0**. All of them were in build, lint and Storybook tooling; none reached the browser bundle.
- No package in `yarn.lock` is younger than 7 days (checked against npm registry publish times; to be re-checked on merge day).
- Public API and emitted `.d.ts` are unchanged except that type declarations no longer reference broken `../../../node_modules/@mui/...` paths.

### Commits
1. **Lock peer libraries.** They were installed by `install-peers` outside `yarn.lock`, so every build pulled whatever was latest and audit never saw them. Now they are pinned as devDependencies; `install-peers` removed.
2. **Build toolchain:** Vite 8 (rolldown), @vitejs/plugin-react 6, vite-plugin-dts 5, vite-plugin-svgr 5, TypeScript 6, Node 24 (`.nvmrc`). `build.lib.cssFileName: 'style'` keeps `dist/style.css` (Vite 6+ renamed it to the package name).
3. **Storybook 10:** essentials/interactions folded into core, `@storybook/blocks` → `@storybook/addon-docs/blocks`, globals via `initialGlobals`, backgrounds via `options`.
4. **Lint toolchain:** eslint 9.39, typescript-eslint 8.72, react-hooks 7 (same two rules as before), stylelint 17, prettier 3.9. `tsconfig` moves to `moduleResolution: bundler` (Storybook 10 ships types only via `exports`); the `@mui/material/*` paths override and deprecated `baseUrl` are removed. Story `render` functions that use hooks become `function Render()`.
5. **Peer majors** aligned with chirp-frontend (CHIRP-4188): react-router-dom 7, date-fns 4, i18next 26, react-i18next 17, react-dropzone 20, react-date-range 2, react-toastify 11. Peers that ui-kit never imports are no longer required from consumers (nivo, echarts, react-datepicker, MUI tree view, react-colorful, react-hook-form, emotion server, styled-engine-sc, sass-embedded).
6. **Lockfile refresh:** stale transitive versions re-resolved.
7. **Remove the committed `.env`; age the lock.** This line never reads the Mapbox token; the map style owner and ids (public, already inlined in every build) move into `map-utils.ts`. `.env` is ignored again. Versions younger than 7 days pinned back to the newest older release.
8. **Stop requiring bundled peers** (@mapbox plugins, @turf, mapbox-gl-draw-geodesic, moment are bundled into dist); i18next / react-i18next floors match chirp-frontend; CLAUDE.md stack line.
9. **Build fixes found in review:** declare `buffer` (imported by `helpers/base64.ts` but never declared; it used to arrive transitively, and without it Vite 8 replaced it with an empty module, so `encodeBase64`/`decodeBase64` threw). Keep `react/*` and `react-dom/*` external: Rolldown left `require("react")` inside the bundled JSX runtime, which throws in the consumer's development mode. Both reproduced on the build before the fix and verified after it.
10. **Rebuilt `dist/`** (no bundled JSX runtime anymore).

### Not on the latest major, with reason
- `@tanstack/react-table` stays 8: v9 changes the column definition types that ui-kit exports, so every table in the consumers would need rewriting. No known vulnerabilities in 8.
- `typescript` 6 (typescript-eslint supports < 6.1), `eslint` 9 (eslint-plugin-import does not support 10), `react-router-dom` 7 (chirp-frontend is on 7; react-router 8 is a consumer migration).

### Verification
- `yarn build`, `yarn build-storybook`, `yarn lint` (eslint + stylelint) green; `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` green.
- All 83 Storybook stories render in a browser with no errors or console errors.
- Components from `dist` render in both `NODE_ENV=development` and `production`; base64 helpers round-trip UTF-8 identically to `Buffer` in ESM and CJS builds.
- chirp-frontend (PR #1173 branch) with this build in place: peer ranges all satisfied, `tsc` green after two small fixes in chirp-frontend (separate PR), 340 jest suites green, production and development builds green, all bundle modules link and the app boots to the login redirect.
- Pre-existing, not changed: one type error in `PromoBanner.tsx` (polymorphic `href` on Button) and type errors in some stories; `tsc -p tsconfig.json` still stops on TS6305 because `vite.config.ts` is in both projects.

### Rollout
ui-kit is not deployed on its own: chirp-frontend#1176 picks up this build and is merged after chirp-frontend#1173. Order: this PR → move the chirp-frontend#1176 ref to `build/release-v3.12.0` → #1173 → #1176. Registry: architecture-plans `docs/releases/3.12.0/CHIRP-4301.md`.

author: skoropadas
body:
## What and why

The workspace moves from npm to **pnpm 12.16.1**, run through Corepack (`packageManager` in `package.json`). This is the first of the three 22.2 PRs. Nx Release, [ng-doc/ng-doc#345](https://github.com/ng-doc/ng-doc/pull/345), is stacked on it.

**Lockfile**
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` comes from `pnpm import` of `package-lock.json`, which is deleted. The import adds no new package version. It lines up about 50 indirect dependencies on versions that were already in the lockfile, among them the dev dependency `autoprefixer` 10.6.0 → 10.6.1.
- pnpm 12 writes the lockfile as two YAML documents. The first locks pnpm itself, and the second locks the project. Nx reads it as-is (2108 entries).
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only holds settings. `allowBuilds` lets five packages run their install scripts (`@parcel/watcher`, `esbuild`, `lmdb`, `msgpackr-extract`, `nx`). pnpm 12 fails the install on any other.

**Dependencies npm's hoisting used to provide**
- They are declared at the versions the lockfile already had: `hast-util-is-element`, `jsonc-parser`, `rehype-stringify`, `unist-util-visit-parents`, `parse5`, `sass`, `yaml`, the istanbul libraries and `@shikijs/langs`. There's no `shamefully-hoist` or `public-hoist-pattern`.
- The unused `@stackblitz/sdk` is dropped, and so is the npm-only `nunjucks` override: pnpm doesn't install that optional peer, and no template loader watches files.

**CI**
- `.github/actions/nodejs` enables pnpm through Corepack and caches the pnpm store by OS, architecture and lockfile hash. Every job runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`.
- `seed-caches.yml` fills the store once per OS (the store is the same for every Node version).
- Every `npx`/`npm` step now uses `pnpm exec`, and the browser action installs Playwright with `pnpm add`.

**Tooling**
- The generator build hashes `pnpm-lock.yaml` and reads the dependency tuple from its project document (`pnpmLockfileProject`).
- The Analog compatibility plugin compares paths by their real path, so it still finds Analog's files through pnpm's symlinks.
- The Husky hooks use `pnpm exec`.

**Acceptance runners**
- `vite-packed` installs its consumer with pnpm (the workspace's version). pnpm's strict layout fails on a dependency a packed package uses without declaring it.
- `package-consumer`, `package-optional`, `packed-b-optional` and `ng-add-e2e` stay on npm on purpose, to cover npm consumers. Each runner says which package manager it uses and why.

**Product bugs the strict layout exposed** (separate commits):
- `fix(utils)`: `@ng-doc/utils` imported `hast-util-is-element` and `unist-util-visit-parents` without declaring them, so it couldn't load in a pnpm application.
- `fix(builder)`: `kernel/runtime-identity.ts` resolved packages without following symlinks. Under pnpm, Shiki's packages therefore resolved to no version, and upgrading them didn't change the highlight-cache or fast-start keys. They now resolve as Node does.
- `feat(builder)`: on Windows, `ng-doc dev -- pnpm …` starts Corepack's pnpm through Node with an argument array, as `ng`, `npm` and `npx` already are.

**Docs**
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the developer skill describe the pnpm setup, the strict layout rule and the CI cache.

**Note for 22.2 docs:** a pnpm 12 application that installs NgDoc will be asked to approve the install scripts of `@parcel/watcher`, `lmdb` and `msgpackr-extract`. The installation guide should say so.

### Verification (Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.16.1)

- **Install, build, lint:** a clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the full `type:lib` build, `ng-doc:link-libs`, and `nx run-many -t lint` on 8 projects all pass.
- **Specs:** every `nx test` target passes with `--configuration=ci`: `app` (+ zoneless and search-index), `ui-kit` (+ zoneless), `ng-doc`, `add`, `builder`, `keywords-loaders`, `utils` and `core`.
- **Tool scripts:** `node --test tools/scripts/testing/*.test.mjs` passes 114/114, and `check-ci-jobs.mjs` passes.
- **Generator runner** (the full posix lane earlier, on pnpm 10; the light groups and `bootstrap` again on pnpm 12): every group passes, and the coverage gates hold where measured. `compiler` ran as 4 shards and `vite-adapter` as 3, both with merged coverage. Two failures come from the test container, not from this change:
  - In `semantic`, one test expects a `chmod 000` file to be unreadable, which isn't true as root. It passes 20/20 as an unprivileged user.
  - In `compiler`, one test exceeds its 20 s timeout on that machine. It also exceeds it on `main` with npm.
- **Acceptance:** `vite-packed` passes with a pnpm 12 consumer: tarballs, 232 entry points under NodeNext, an Analog AOT build and an SSR render.
- **Site:** `ng-doc:build` and `ng-doc:build-legacy` pass.
- **Not run locally:** parity, because the container can't reach `angular.dev` or `rxjs.dev` for keywords. The npm-consumer acceptance runners and the Windows/macOS jobs weren't run either. CI covers all of these.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests are added or updated for the change.
- [ ] Author-facing changes are documented in `apps/ng-doc/docs`. *(No author-facing change. The pnpm install note above goes with the 22.2 docs.)*
- [x] The title follows Conventional Commits with a scope, for example `fix(builder): …`. A breaking change has a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer with a migration path, never `!` in the title.

author: chrislemke
body:
## Summary

```diff
+.github/workflows/
+├── ci.yml                  # every PR and push to main: pre-commit hooks, go test -race, Docker tests, govulncheck
+└── main-build.yml          # every push to main: publish binaries in the prerelease main-latest
+.pre-commit-config.yaml     # golangci-lint, go mod tidy, file hygiene, actionlint, zizmor; testdata/ excluded
+.golangci.yml              # standard linters + gofmt
+assets/images/icon.png     # 512 px, 51 KB, top of the README
 .gitignore                 # js-prueffactory → /js-prueffactory
+cmd/js-prueffactory/main.go   # was hidden by .gitignore, so a clone could not build
 go.mod                     # + toolchain go1.27.3, golang.org/x/text v0.43.0
```

`main-build.yml`:

```text
on push to main
  go test ./...
  build linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64 + SHA256SUMS   (outside the work tree, so vcs.modified stays false)
  if release main-latest exists
    move tag main-latest to the pushed commit
    replace the assets
  else
    create prerelease main-latest
```

Download URL, stable across pushes: `https://github.com/invia-flights/js-prueffactory/releases/download/main-latest/js-prueffactory-linux-amd64`. Every Report names the commit in `producer.vcs_revision`.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `go test ./...` in a fresh clone fails: `TestTheShippedBinaryDoesNotContainTheUpdateCommand`: `lstat ./cmd/: no such file or directory`
  **After:** passes
- **Before:** govulncheck: `Your code is affected by 10 vulnerabilities from the Go standard library` (go1.27.1)
  **After:** `No vulnerabilities found.`
- **Before:** golangci-lint: 64 issues (dead code, `reflect.Ptr`, a loop instead of `append(...)`, unchecked `Close`/`Fprint*`)
  **After:** `0 issues.` Stylistic checks that are left out are explained in `.golangci.yml`.
- In a `golang:1.27.3` container as an unprivileged user on a fresh clone: pre-commit via pipx, `go test -race`, govulncheck and the build steps of `main-build.yml` pass. actionlint and zizmor (pedantic) report nothing for both workflows.
- `go test -tags docker` passed on macOS (internal/cli 1344 s) before the lint fixes. This PR's run is the first one on a GitHub runner.
- The Publish step of `main-build.yml` runs only after the merge.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting removes the workflows. The prerelease `main-latest` and its tag stay until deleted by hand. Anyone who starts downloading from its URL breaks when it goes.

**Blast Radius:** CI

- Every push to main publishes public binaries.
- Every PR waits for the Docker job, about 25 min.
- With Go 1.27.1 and the default `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, local builds download go1.27.3.
- The `main` ruleset requires CodeQL results, but CodeQL is not set up, so this PR can be merged only by an admin bypass until it is.

body:
Closes #172

Decisions: https://github.com/trungle1612/hueni-api/issues/172#issuecomment-6517495891

## What
**Public `/v1`** (the page itself lives in hue-ni). New `V1::BaseController` handles CORS for hueni's origins and answers the `OPTIONS` preflight; `VacancyController` now inherits from it.
- `GET /v1/places/:slug/booking_site?from=&to=` returns the room types shown, rooms left, and the cheapest stay for those nights. When the page is paused it returns only `{ name, open: false }`.
- `POST /v1/places/:slug/bookings` (5 requests / 10 min per IP, honeypot field `website`). `Place#book_online` checks open, room type shown, past day, same-day cutoff, ≤ 30 nights, name / phone / guest count, then takes the first free room of that type by name.
  - Errors never come from the room checks, because those name the booking in the way, which belongs to another guest. Instead the guest sees "Hết phòng loại này…".
  - The answer never echoes the guest's name or phone.
- `GET /v1/bookings/:token` (a `signed_id`, 90 days) returns the status: held / confirmed / cancelled, the amounts, and while held the bank details plus the transfer content (`DP0142`).

**Holds:** `bookings.online` and `hold_expires_at`, set to the owner's hold time when the page asks for a deposit.
- A payment (Payment `after_create`) or a check-in ends the hold.
- `Booking.expire_holds` runs every minute and cancels the rest with reason *Hết hạn giữ chỗ*.
- Deposits are recorded by hand; there is no bank webhook.

**Activity log:** online bookings show "Khách đặt online" as the actor.

**Mini App:**
- `PATCH /api/v1/places/:id/booking_site` (owners): `open`, `deposit_percent` 0/30/50/100, `hidden_room_types`, `hold_minutes` 15/30/120, `cutoff_hour` 18/20/22.
- Opening the page needs a room type shown and, when a deposit is asked, a bank account.
- Place detail has a `booking_site` field (owners only); Booking JSON has `online` and `hold_expires_at`.

## Ceilings / not done
- Rooms without a `room_type` are never offered online.
- Two guests asking for the last room in the same instant: the second one's save could pass validation before the first commits. SQLite serializes the writes, so the window is small; I didn't add a lock.
- Rate limits are untested, because the test env uses `:null_store` like elsewhere.
- No guest messages (waiting on #171) and no Telegram ping to owners (the existing chat is the admin's). New online bookings show up in the Mini App with `online` / `hold_expires_at`.
- `deposit` is computed from the homestay's current %, so if the owner changes it mid-hold, the guest's link shows the new amount.
- The cheapest stay picks up season prices once #163 is merged.

## Docs
- hueni-api wiki Home: public booking-page API. Mini-App-API: `booking_site` settings and the Booking fields.
- Bruno: `Booking site (public)` folder and `Homestay/update booking site`.
- hueni-zalo wiki Booking-Site.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/rails test` (0 failures), `bin/rubocop`, `bin/brakeman`
- [ ] After deploy: confirm the `expire_holds` recurring task runs (`config/recurring.yml`)

body:
TL;DR: main green after font packs

Summary:
- #2010 added a test that pins `resolveLightVariantFace('Calibri Light')` to `Carlito-Regular.ttf`. #1972 renamed the bundled Latin faces to packed `.ttf.zst` files in `@betteroffice/fonts-latin` in parallel, so main fails `packages/fonts/src/index.test.ts` ("light variants resolve only for families we bundle"). The two expectations now name the packed files, like the neighbouring last-resort assertions already do.

author: suzuki-shunsuke
body:
Close #1828

## Background

#1826 made pinact leave actions locked by the workflow lockfile `.github/workflows/actions.lock` to the lockfile. #1828 refines the spec:

- Actions in onboarded workflows shouldn't be changed at all. An action the lockfile doesn't record makes GitHub Actions reject the workflow anyway, so it's an error, but pinning it wouldn't help either.
- Self repository actions `$/<path>` have to be handled: gh actions-lock follows them recursively and locks the actions they use as dependencies of the calling workflow (`ScanSelfRepositoryActions` in github/gh-actions-lock), so pinning them breaks the lockfile.
- An unreadable lockfile should stop pinact, because pinact can't tell which workflows are onboarded.

## Behavior

A workflow is onboarded if the lockfile's `workflows` lists it. If the lockfile exists:

| Target | pinact |
| --- | --- |
| Steps of an onboarded workflow | Doesn't change them (no pinning, no `--update`, no version comment verification). Fails with exit code 2 for actions the lockfile doesn't record |
| Steps of a workflow that isn't onboarded | Pins them as usual and warns |
| Steps of an action file used as `$/<path>` by an onboarded workflow | Doesn't change them |
| Steps of other action files | Pins them as usual |
| Reusable workflows (`jobs.<job_id>.uses`) | Pins them as usual |

- If the lockfile doesn't record an action of an onboarded workflow (or of an action file it uses via `$/<path>`), pinact fails with exit code 2 on the action's line: `action cannot be auto-fixed: the lockfile doesn't record actions/setup-go@v6 for .github/workflows/ci.yml, so GitHub Actions rejects the workflow. Run gh actions-lock to regenerate the lockfile`. For an action file used by several onboarded workflows, all the workflows missing it are listed. Other actions and files are processed as usual.
- A workflow that isn't onboarded gets a warning once: `the workflow isn't in the lockfile. Run gh actions-lock to add it`. This also covers a workflow that isn't onboarded but uses an action file via `$/<path>` together with an onboarded workflow; the action file isn't changed because pinning it would break the onboarded workflow's lockfile.
- Action files used as local actions `./<path>`, published for other repositories, or used by no workflow are pinned, because the lockfile doesn't lock them. Excluding them by configuration is proposed in #1829.
- If the lockfile can't be read (invalid, or a schema version newer than the parser supports), pinact fails with exit code 3 without processing any file.

## Changes from #1826

- An action missing from the lockfile in an onboarded workflow: still an error (exit code 2). Actions in action files used via `$/<path>` are checked too, and the message names the workflows.
- A workflow that isn't onboarded: a warning is added.
- An unreadable lockfile: per-action handling (SHA-pinned left, others exit code 2) -> exit code 3 without processing any file.
- Self repository actions `$/<path>` are supported.

## Implementation

All lockfile logic is in `pkg/controller/run/lockfile.go`.

- `readLockfiles` groups targets by repository root (`lockfileRoots`) and reads each lockfile once (`readTargets`). It returns an error if a lockfile can't be read, and `Run` returns it with exit code 3 (`ExitCodeAPIError`) before processing files.
  - Workflow file: the root is derived from its path (`<root>/.github/workflows/<file>`), as in #1826.
  - Action file (`action.yml` / `action.yaml`): the root is the nearest ancestor directory having `.github/workflows/actions.lock` (`findLockfileRoot`).
- `scanSelfRepositoryActions` scans the workflows in `<root>/.github/workflows` for step-level `uses: $/<path>` and follows `$/<path>` in the referenced action files recursively. It runs only for repositories with target action files. References with `@` (invalid), paths outside the root, and `$/<path>` without `action.y(a)ml` (e.g. a job-level reusable workflow) are ignored.
- A target (`lockfileTarget`) keeps only the onboarded workflows concerning the file. Workflows that aren't onboarded get the warning (`warnNotOnboarded`, once per workflow).
- `checkLockfile` returns whether to leave the action to the lockfile and an `ErrUnfixable` error listing the onboarded workflows that don't record it. `ParseActionRef` returns nil for reusable workflows, so they are pinned as usual.
- The lockfile is parsed with the keys of the concerned workflows, so required fields are validated only for entries they reference.
- `Run` and `readTargets` are split into helpers to keep cyclomatic complexity under the limit.

## Docs

`docs/workflow_lockfile.md` is rewritten for the spec (table, warnings, self repository actions, unreadable lockfile). README, `docs/exit_codes.md` (exit code 3), and `docs/why_pinact_not_pin.md` are updated.

## Verification

- `cmdx v`, `cmdx t`, and `golangci-lint run` pass.
- Tests cover `readLockfile` (missing, no workflow, valid, invalid, future schema version, broken unused entry), `readLockfiles` (onboarded and non-onboarded workflows with the warning, action files not used via `$/`, no lockfile next to the file, an invalid lockfile returning an error, an unrelated invalid lockfile not read), self repository actions (nested `$/`, a job-level `$/` reusable workflow not followed, an action file shared with a non-onboarded workflow warning once), `checkLockfile` (recorded, sub-action path and casing, not recorded, SHA not recorded, missing for one or all of several workflows), and `processLines` not changing onboarded workflows and exiting with 2 for an unrecorded action. Ignoring the read error or dropping the warning makes the tests fail.
- Ran the built binary on a sample repository: onboarded `ci.yml` (`actions/checkout@v6` recorded, `$/.github/actions/setup`), `setup/action.yaml` (`actions/cache@v4.2.0` recorded, `actions/setup-go@v6` not recorded), non-onboarded `release.yml` (`$/.github/actions/setup`, `actions/setup-go@v6`), and a root `action.yaml`:
  - Valid lockfile: a warning for `release.yml`, which is pinned; `ci.yml` and `setup/action.yaml` unchanged, with an error on the `setup-go` line of `setup/action.yaml`; the root `action.yaml` pinned. Exit code 2.
  - Lockfile with schema v0.0.4: `pinact failed` with the parse error and exit code 3, no file processed.

author: pocha
body:
## What
- **`createCheckoutSession`** (HTTPS, asia-south1): prices the plan on the server and returns a Stripe Checkout URL. First 10 users free, then $12 per user per year, capped at $199 for a first payment and $399 on renewal. One-time payment, no auto-renewal. Self-serve is 11 to 100 users; above 100 it answers with a custom-quote message and takes no payment.
- **`stripeWebhook`**: verifies Stripe's signature, processes each event id once (`StripeEvents`), raises `Codes/{code}.totalUserCount` (never lowers it), sets `paidUntil`, and records `Payments/{sessionId}`.
- **Website**: pay box in the pricing section (`assets/js/checkout.js`) with a live quote, success and cancelled pages (noindex), and a new refund policy page at `/refund/` (full refund within 15 days, then pro-rata by the day less Stripe's processing fee).
- `functions/STRIPE.md` documents setup. Keys are Firebase secrets (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`); nothing secret is in the repo.

## Deploy order
1. Set the secrets (placeholder webhook secret first) and deploy `createCheckoutSession` and `stripeWebhook`.
2. Add the webhook endpoint in Stripe (`checkout.session.completed`), set the real `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, redeploy `stripeWebhook`.
3. Merge so `/payment/success.html` and `/refund/` are live, then test with card `4242 4242 4242 4242`.
4. Repeat with live keys when ready.

## Tested
Offline with a mocked Firestore, a dummy key and a locally signed event: quotes (first year $199 at 30 users, $240 on renewal, 101 users refused, 10 users refused), signed webhook raises the limit and records the payment, duplicate delivery ignored, bad signature gets 400. Not tested against Stripe itself (needs your keys).

## Notes
- Refunds are issued by hand in the Stripe dashboard; set the code's `totalUserCount` back to 10 by hand.
- `paidUntil` is a record for the manual renewal invoice; it is not enforced.
- Anyone can pay for any existing organisation code (intended).

body:
Refs #630. Design: docs/decisions/2026-10-28-target-client-server-architecture.md (Latency rule 4), docs/peer-link.md.

## Change
- The link names each accepted QUIC connection (random 128 bit) and sends it as `X-Studio-Link-Connection` with `X-Studio-Link-Token`. The backend makes the token at start and gives it to the link in its config (`linkToken`). The link strips every `X-Studio-Link-*` header from the peer's own request.
- The backend uses the name only when the token matches (constant time). The owner check (`tailscale status` + `whois`) runs on the first request of a connection. Later requests with the same connection and address reuse it.
- Always checked: requests without the token (Serve/HTTPS), with a `Tailscale-User-Login`, or with an auto-pair probe. Signatures stay per request on every path.
- Result dropped after 60 s without a request (link idle timeout). A closed connection cannot send, and its name is never reused. Cache cap 256. Revoked key still closes its connections (existing `replace_keys`).
- Code: `multi_server_pairing.rs` (`lookup`, `LINK_CONNECTION`), `incoming_multi_server.rs` (`link_connection`), `peer-link/src/inbound.rs`, config plumbing.

## Measurement (this Mac, read-only, 20 runs, median)
- Only per-request whois site: `TailscaleOwnerLookup::observe` (`multi_server_owner.rs`), two processes per call, called from `MultiServerBoundary` (prepare/handle/authorize/discovery).
- `tailscale status --json`: 67 ms. `tailscale whois --json`: 126 ms (max 270). About 190 ms per request, before the 10 ms poll loop.
- The federation routes use a local whoami, not a per-request peer whois.

## Tests
- `owner_is_checked_once_per_link_connection` (services): failed first (5 checks for 5 requests), now 1. Also covers a new connection, no connection, and the login header.
- `owner_is_checked_once_per_link_connection_and_only_for_the_link` (HTTP): right token 4 requests = 1 check; wrong or missing token = checked each time.
- `the_link_owns_the_forwarding_headers` extended.
- Run and passed: runtime-services `multi_server` (35), runtime-http `multi_server_incoming` (7), peer-link (5), runtime-server `peer_link` (8), clippy on four crates.

## Not done / not verified
- `just test-fast`: started, but killed by SIGTERM by another agent's `pkill` at 395/2519 tests (18 SIGTERM aborts, no real failure seen). Not rerun (owner rule 2026-10-30, machine overloaded). Gate runs later.
- Not done: "a restored connection sends the pending outbox at once". The federation outbox uses HTTPS only, and the backend gets no connection-open event from the link (listed under "Not yet" in docs/peer-link.md). It needs a new event channel; asking the owner first (AGENTS.md Simplicity).
- No live two-server run. No test of the revoke close path beyond existing code.
- Staleness: a connection keeps its owner result while it is used (no hard age limit).

author: drummondj
body:
Fixes #228.

## Problem
`update_placement $p -layout $l2 -name q` reported a name clash but left `p` moved into `l2`. Nothing bumped the version, logged a change or recorded undo. Separately, the reparent check used the *old* name, so `-layout $l2 -name fresh` was wrongly refused when `l2` already had a placement with `p`'s old name.

## Fix
- **Two-phase `Root::update_<type>`** (codegen `update_root_body`):
  1. Validate everything without writing: the singular parent slot, the resulting name under the resulting parent, and each global unique field.
  2. Apply the changes; this phase can't fail.

  A refused update changes nothing and logs no change.
- **Edit op** (`update_op_body`) pre-checks the resulting name, so the error names it (`a sibling Placement with this name ('q2') already exists`). A Root refusal after that is reported as an internal error.
- **Setters:** the 90 generated `set_<klass>_<field>` setters are deleted; only tests called them. `set_<klass>_owner` stays as the way to move an owned object.
- **Docs:** the generated `update_` doc and the docstring are rewritten.
- **Small change:** plain fields are now moved in rather than copied.

## Tests
- `edit_ops_test.cpp` (new):
  - the repro: refused, nothing changed, version unchanged, and undo undoes the previous command;
  - reparent plus rename to a fresh name succeeds;
  - a refused reference update changes nothing.
- `database_test.cpp`:
  - Root-level reparent and rename cases, including no change-log entry on refusal;
  - a global-name clash leaves the update's other fields unchanged;
  - the setter tests become `update_` tests.
- codegen unit tests: the clash check comes before the writes.

Full Debug ctest passes: 1236/1236. `le_tcl_shell_gui_exit` failed once in a parallel run and passed when rerun alone.

author: chemaclass
body:
## 🤔 Background

`rand-int` includes its upper bound, so `(rand-int 1)` can return `1`. `rand-nth` compensates for that behavior and forwards an invalid range to PHP for an empty collection.

## 💡 Goal

Use an exclusive positive integer bound and report empty selection clearly.

## 🔖 Changes

Return `0` for non-positive integer bounds and choose within `[0, n)` otherwise. Pass the full collection size from `rand-nth` and reject empty collections with an error at the Phel caller. Preserve existing nil and integer-argument behavior.

Verified with 505 focused Phel checks, an isolated last-element selection check, caller-location CLI checks and formatting. Review found no further issues. Callers that need an inclusive bound can use `(rand-int (inc n))`.

Closes #3679

body:
Adds to `docs/journal/2026-10-30-bz2-threads-teams.md` the efficiency reading of the A/B registered in #214, which passed narrowly (merged as #215).

**The reading:** the split spent +16.9% CPU for −4.2% wall, about 39 CPU-s per second saved. That is the contention signature this programme learned to read. The cap's own A/B showed the mirror image: −31% CPU for −7% wall.

**The cause isn't established.** The candidates are oversubscription, L3 sharing with the parsers, or helpers spinning before they park.

**The decision:** the cap stays at 4, and no PR proposes changing it. `WIKIDATA_BZ2_THREADS=8` remains available on a machine with idle cores. The measure for decoder work becomes CPU per byte as well as speed.

This PR changes the journal only.

author: mthines
body:
REAPER's web server never frees a socket whose client closed the connection first (curl, or Chrome dropping an idle connection): it stays in `CLOSE_WAIT`/`CLOSED`, and at about 100 the server stops answering until REAPER restarts. Measured: each `curl` request leaked one socket; Chrome leaked one when it dropped its connection on its own.

- The bridge counts those sockets every 30 s with `lsof` in the background (macOS and Linux; ~50 ms, never on the defer loop) and publishes `status.web = { stuck, limit }`. A count left by an earlier REAPER run is dropped at start.
- The page shows a notice from 50% (urgent from 80%) telling you to restart REAPER; the bridge prints one console line at 90%, since the page can't load once it's full.
- `find_web_port` now skips an HTTP entry past `csurf_cnt`, the same rule as setup's fix in #35.

Tests: three wasmoon bridge tests (count published and console warning, stale count ignored, inactive entry ignored) and `webSocketLevel` thresholds. bridge-ui 159/159, server 658 passed (REAPER-dependent suites excluded); the real `lsof` command matched a direct count on a live REAPER.

author: jt-mchorse
body:
`atomic_write_text` writes a sibling temp file and renames it over the target. A rename swaps the directory entry, so the kernel checks only the directory's write bit and never the target's own. As a result, a `chmod 444` output file was silently rewritten, while `Path.write_text` (the call this helper replaced) raises `PermissionError`. The `--out` write seams in `bench_savings` and `tune_threshold` say an unwritable output becomes an `::error::` line and exit 2. A read-only file was the one case that did neither.

This change ports prompt-regression-suite#318. A new helper, `_refuse_unwritable_target`, runs after the symlink resolve and before the temp file is created. It calls `os.stat` (a missing target is the create case, and a link loop keeps its own ELOOP), then `os.access(W_OK)`, and raises `PermissionError(EACCES)`. Root still writes, as it does with `write_text`. Nothing is left behind on refusal.

**Sibling sweep:** `atomic_write_text` is the only rename-based writer in the repo. There is no `atomic_write_bytes`, `*_many`, or `check_writable` pre-flight. The library `dump_stats_json` / `dump_aggregate_json` writers all route through it. `scripts/capture_demo.py`'s stable-artifact copy uses `shutil.copy2`, which already refuses an existing-but-unwritable target with exit 2 (#180, the comment at ~line 415). That path is unchanged, and the bench writer now agrees with it.

**Measured (macOS, uid 502, Python 3.11)**
- Before (origin/main 096a929): `atomic_write_text` on a 0444 file gave no error, the contents became `new`, and the mode stayed 0444. `Path.write_text` on the same file raised `PermissionError` errno 13.
- After: both writers raise EACCES, the file is unchanged, and no `.tmp` file is left. `bench_savings --out` and `tune_threshold --out` on a read-only `.json` print `::error::` and exit 2, and the file is untouched.

**Revert probe** (`io_utils.py` back to origin/main, `__pycache__` cleared, new tests kept): 5 red, 4 green. The green ones are the controls: 2 `Path.write_text` parity arms and 2 writable/missing-target arms.

**Gates:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` are clean. `pytest --cov=cost_optimizer --cov-report=term-missing --durations=10` exits 0 with 2539 collected, 2453 passed and 86 skipped (3.11 venv with `[dev,dashboard]`). The new tests skip on Windows and as root. GitHub's ubuntu runners are non-root, so CI runs them.

Closes #377

受講者の「ステージ一覧」と別ページの「スキルツリー」を廃止。`/stages` (受講者) と `/skill-tree` はホームへ送る。**staff の `/stages` (ステージ管理) とダッシュボードは変えていない** - 提出・添削履歴、学習時間、学習のペース、お知らせ、期限は新しい「学習の記録」(`/records`) へ移した。AI のカードは右下のボタンと重複するので置かない - サイドバー (受講者) は スキルツリー / 現在のレッスン / 学習の記録 / 面談対策 / 修了証 / 個人の本棚 / 殿堂 の 7 項目 - 使わなくなった `LearnerDashboard`・`StageList`・`SkillTreePage`・`StagePath`・`home-path`・`TodayPlan`・`PlacementWizard` を削除 ### 直したこと - サーバが「進行中なし」(`active_stage_id: null`) と返したとき、受講中の先頭を当て推量していたため、ツリーではまだ鍵の掛かった星 (島の AWS 講座など) を「続きから」と出していた。サーバの値だけを使うようにした (当て推量はデモと地図の取得失敗時だけ) ### ドキュメント - 画面内ヘルプ (`helpContent.ts`)、`AGENTS.md`、`docs/learning-pace.md` を新しい画面に合わせた ## 確認 - `bun run typecheck` / `bun run lint` (警告は main と同じ 36 件のまま) / `bun run test` (256 ファイル / 3,439 件) が通る - ローカルの実データ (`db:seed` + `dev:api` + `dev`) で、受講中 (`seed-learner`) と未受講 (`seed-learner2`)、PC / タブレット / スマホ幅、ダークテーマ、星の詳細のボタン、「続きから」「レッスン一覧」の遷移と戻り、`/stages`・`/skill-tree` の転送、ガイドの開閉、staff (`seed-admin` のダッシュボード、`seed-instructor` の `/stages`) を確認した ## レビューで見てほしい点 - 「学習のペース」をホームから「学習の記録」へ移した (設定画面にも引き続きある) - 初回案内の「あとで選ぶ」は無くした (ツリーが常に見えているため) - ステージを切り替える確認ダイアログは、ガイドと次にやるリストから始めるときだけ出す (星の詳細からは従来どおり確認なし) --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01QjZbnvmYCzN2nimw4PjXvW)_ ---

author: mstomar125
body:
Fixes #4066

Adds `applicationShouldTerminate:` to the running delegate's class on `RunEvent::Ready` (macOS), returning `NSTerminateLater` and calling `initiate_app_quit` so Dock/Cmd+Tab/logout quits take the same window-close, flush, destroy path as the Quit menu. The process ends through that path (or the existing quit watchdog), which satisfies the deferred terminate. The delegate is reassigned once so AppKit notices the new method.

Tests (unit level): a runtime test registers a dummy ObjC class, installs the method, sends `applicationShouldTerminate:` and asserts the hook runs and the reply is NSTerminateLater (and an existing implementation is not replaced); a source-wiring test pins the Ready arm to `initiate_app_quit`. Both mutation-checked. clippy workspace all-targets, fmt, guard tests pass; app-lib suite passes except 7 skill_setup tests that need a built skill installer not present in the worktree.

Not verified (no GUI): that AppKit actually dispatches `terminate:` to the added method after the delegate reassignment, that logout behaves with NSTerminateLater, and the end-to-end flush on a Dock quit. Needs a manual check: type, quit from the Dock, relaunch.

Hardening: the reply is NSTerminateLater only when the hook ran and started a quit (no hook, poisoned slot, or no open window answer NSTerminateNow); the hook is stored before the method is added; the slot lock is not held while the hook runs. Each has a mutation-checked unit test.

## Needs physical-Mac check
- [ ] Type text, quit from the Dock, relaunch: the text is there
- [ ] Cmd+Tab then Q
- [ ] Cmd+Q
- [ ] Quit with no window open (exits promptly, no 8s wait)

author: jayzed80
body:
## What and why

Outline Stroke could crash (a panic inside the `linesweeper` geometry library) when a path had an absurdly wide stroke (about 1e200 points or more) with round joins. `normalize_bez` was the one path-merging step without the panic guard that `Sweep::new` already has. It now wraps the sweep in `catch_unwind` and returns `PathOpsError::Degenerate`, so the command reports that it cannot do this and leaves the art unchanged.

Reach is low: the Outline Stroke command clamps its weight to 0..1000, so a file with a huge stroke width (for example an imported SVG) would be needed. I did not test the import path end to end. Found by probing the path functions with extreme numbers; no issue exists. Round joins only; 1e150 is fine, 1e200 panics.

## How it was tested

- New `crates/pathops/tests/it/hostile_params.rs`: edit, stroke and offset functions fed junk numbers.
- `cargo test -p vectorcraft-pathops -j 2`: 79 unit tests and 82 integration tests pass.
- With the fix reverted, `stroke_and_offset_survive_hostile_numbers` fails (linesweeper panics with `Left == Ish`); with it, it passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-pathops --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- Not run: the full `cargo xtask ci` (wasm, layers, brands); CI does that.

## Checklist

- [ ] `cargo xtask ci` passes (not run locally; scoped to the crate as above)
- [x] No panics in shipped code: the change removes one reachable panic; no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing added
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code
- [x] No new assets

Possible overlap: open PR #4345 touches the same crate (offset path complexity); I did not find it changing these lines.

body:
Vercel Web Analytics Installation Complete
==========================================

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for this static HTML portfolio website.

Project Analysis
----------------
- Framework: Static HTML/CSS with vanilla JavaScript
- Structure: Multi-page site (main index.html + portfolio/index.html)
- No package manager or build system detected

Installation Approach
--------------------
Since this is a static HTML website without a package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn) or JavaScript framework, I used the official Vercel documentation's recommended approach for vanilla HTML sites:

1. Fetched latest documentation from https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart
2. Consulted Vercel Community guidance for static HTML implementation
3. Used the script-based approach rather than npm package installation

Files Modified
--------------
1. index.html - Added Vercel Web Analytics script tags to <head>
2. portfolio/index.html - Added Vercel Web Analytics script tags to <head>

Implementation Details
---------------------
Added two script tags to the <head> section of both HTML files:

1. Analytics initialization script:
   - Creates window.va function with queue (window.vaq) pattern
   - Enables analytics tracking to work immediately on page load

2. Deferred analytics loader:
   - Loads /_vercel/insights/script.js with defer attribute
   - Vercel automatically serves this script when site is deployed

The scripts were placed just before the closing </head> tag, after all stylesheets, following best practices for analytics implementation.

How It Works
------------
- The first script creates a queue system (window.vaq) that buffers analytics calls
- The second script loads the actual Vercel analytics code asynchronously
- When deployed to Vercel, the /_vercel/insights/script.js endpoint is automatically available
- Analytics data will appear in the Vercel dashboard after deployment

Next Steps
----------
1. Deploy the site to Vercel
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard (Project Settings > Analytics)
3. Visit the site to generate initial page view events
4. Check browser Network tab for requests to /_vercel/insights/view
5. View analytics data in the Vercel dashboard (may take a few hours to appear)

Notes
-----
- No package.json changes needed (static HTML approach)
- No dependencies to install or build steps required
- No lock files to update
- Implementation follows official Vercel documentation for static sites
- Analytics will only work when deployed to Vercel (local testing won't show data)

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
[XLA:GPU] Pass free_visitors to DeviceAddressVmmAllocator.

`GpuAllocatorConfig::sub_allocator_free_visitors` was previously only wired into `CreateBFCAllocator`, leaving `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`) without free callbacks when virtual address ranges are unmapped.

Add `FreeVisitor` support to `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (and its CUDA and ROCm subclasses and factories) so registered callbacks are invoked in reverse order immediately before mapped virtual address ranges are unmapped during pending deallocation completion or allocator teardown, and forward `allocator_config.sub_allocator_free_visitors` from `GetStreamExecutorGpuDeviceAllocator`.

body:
## Why

Several live pages on docs.fereai.xyz describe how the app used to work. The biggest gap: the docs say "there's no separate personal wallet" and that each agent shows its own deposit address. In the app, every user has a **Fere Wallet**, which is the only address they ever send to, and agents are funded from it. Button names, Stop, fees and minimums had drifted too, and nothing explained crypto basics to a first-time user.

Every product fact in this PR was checked against the current webapp and wallet_service code.

## What changed

**Wallet & Security (`wallet.mdx`)**
- Rebuilt around the Fere Wallet: deposit → **Add money** → **Take money out** → **Withdraw**.
- Where to find it: **Portfolio → Fere Wallet → Deposit / Withdraw**.
- Table of the 7 deposit networks with the coin to send and typical arrival time; Base recommended.
- Deposits on networks other than Base are converted to Cash at a small cost; amounts under $5 aren't converted.
- Wrong coin / wrong network warning.
- Withdrawals go out as USDC on Base, after the first/last-4 address check.
- Agents can only pay back to the Fere Wallet. Hyperliquid money comes back to the Fere Wallet ($1 fee, $6 minimum), replacing the old "sent straight to your address" text.

**Agents (`agents.mdx`)**
- Button names match the app: Add money, Take money out, Add money to start again.
- Stop now says plainly that it never sells; Fere offers to take the agent's Cash back to the Fere Wallet.
- New **How Much You Need** section: spot agents need their amount per trade (often $20, never below $5); Hyperliquid perps agents need at least $50; the Add money screen always shows the exact figure.
- Fees: Fere's 0.5% / 0.1% is unchanged, plus a list of costs that come from networks and markets (non-Base conversion, slippage, Hyperliquid's $1).
- Backtests: replaced the "+190% a year" example with a warning that annualizing short tests inflates the number.
- Leverage: added a liquidation warning.
- Welcome email: rewritten for users; the internal note ("primary button is Fund, not Deploy") and the raw `/agents/{slug}?fund=1#fund` URL are removed.

**FAQ (`faq.mdx`)**
- Updated answers for: where money is held, what Cash is, how to add money, how to withdraw, how to stop an agent, what it costs, and the minimum to start.
- New questions: What is the Fere Wallet? / I don't own crypto, how do I start? / Which network should I send on? / How long does a deposit take? / I sent the wrong coin / Do I have to pay tax?
- Privacy answer no longer says data is "never shared with third parties" (the app uses analytics and email providers); it points to the Privacy Policy instead.

**New page: New to Crypto (`new-to-crypto.mdx`)**
- What USDC and networks are, a six-step first deposit, how to get money back, and a glossary (perps, leverage, liquidation, slippage, dust, backtest and more).

**MCP (`mcp.mdx`)** — "Revoke access anytime from your Fere account settings" pointed to a screen that doesn't exist. It now says to remove the connector in your AI client, or contact support to cut off access everywhere.

- **Research / Agent Builder.** The FAQ still says Research runs through the MCP, while `/research` in the app is the Agent Builder waitlist. Left for a separate decision.
- **Refer & Earn.** Text left as is. The app's profile menu still shows the old credits-based referral screen (200 credits + 5 points, needs credit packs that can no longer be bought), so the product side needs a decision first.

author: cmmrox
body:
## What this is

The architecture rework (CR-021, CR-022) as one refactor. It also includes the fixes for the bugs the F01–F03 regression found, the owner's interface-first services, and a faster delivery process. Nothing a salon, a staff member or the operator sees changes, apart from the bug fixes below.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/DECISION_LOG.md`, entries 055–068:
- 066: architecture work is a refactor, not a feature, so F23's records are removed.
- 067: services are written interface first, then implementation.
- 068: QA has three kinds of run, and delivery gets faster.

## Architecture

- **Modules and boundaries.** Each API module has a root-package API and a conventional internal layout: `controller/ dto/ mapper/ service/ service/impl/ entity/ domain/ repository/ adapter/ job/ config/ event/ local/`.
  - Spring Modulith verification enforces the module boundaries.
  - ArchUnit rules enforce the layout, and each rule has a fixture that proves it fails.
- **Interface-first services (decision 067).** Every business service is `service/FooService`, implemented by `service/impl/FooServiceImpl`.
  - Callers inject the interface.
  - No interface exposes an entity.
  - In shared, the outbox and audit internals are hidden in `impl/`.
- **Persistence and generated code.**
  - Spring Data JPA is the default, with `JdbcClient` limited to five named exceptions.
  - Lombok is used under an allow-list, and MapStruct generates the response mappers.
  - Hibernate `@TenantId` works together with row-level security, and each guard is tested alone.
- **Ownership and events.**
  - Every table and every `/api/v1` path has a declared owning module.
  - The OpenAPI client is exported per module.
  - Durable, versioned events go between modules through the outbox, with idempotent subscribers.
- **Web.**
  - `apps/web/src` is organised by the same modules: `features/<module>` and `surfaces/`.
  - Lint enforces the import boundaries, and server code is marked `server-only`.
  - Shared formatting is in `@salon/format`.
  - Prettier and knip run as gates.
  - Next.js is upgraded to 16.4.1, past GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r, GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw and GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr.

## Bugs fixed (found by the 2026-10-30 regression; all verified by QA)

| Bug | Severity | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BUG-F01-007 | major | No stack API instance could start since F03: it read the migration user's name at start-up. Now read only where migrations run. |
| BUG-F01-008 | major | Critical CVE-2026-111497 (brotli): a `brotli-libs>=1.2.1-r0` floor in the API image, and the web image moved to Node 24.22.2. |
| BUG-F02-015 | major | Introduced by the refactor: a silent database answered 500 instead of 503. A commit or rollback on a lost connection now answers 503 in both transaction managers. This also fixes the same latent fault on the platform side. |
| BUG-F02-014 | minor | `/salon-site` looped through the proxy under a 127.0.0.1-bound standalone server. |
| BUG-F03-007 | minor | `operator-bootstrap.sh` stopped on an unbound `RESOLVED_JAVA_HOME`. |

## Process (decision 068)

- **Three kinds of QA run:**
  - feature QA;
  - smoke: 7 checks, about 2.5 minutes;
  - regression: 47 checks, about 36 minutes;
  - plus a `release` suite for the slow load, stack and image checks.
- **Lighter test records.** Test titles carry each case and its acceptance criterion, so `cases.md` and the yaml case lists go for new features. There is one evidence rule and no separate QA branch.
- **Smaller skills and tooling.** The skills are about 25% shorter, and the evidence tooling is removed.
- **Bugs found after a merge** carry `found_after_merge` and don't reopen the merged feature.

## Verification

- **API:** `./mvnw -q verify` passes on the combined tree, 928 tests with 0 failures. Spotless and `-Werror` are clean.
- **Contract:** `pnpm contracts:check` passes; the OpenAPI document and client are unchanged by the refactor.
- **Web:** lint, typecheck, test (700 web tests), build, `format:check` and knip all pass.
- **Images:** `images-build` and `images-scan` are clean for both images.
- **QA, on a quiet machine:**
  - smoke passes 7/7;
  - regression passes 47/47;
  - all five bugs are verified;
  - eight stale test checks from F03 are repaired, with their meaning unchanged.
- **Review.** The lead reviewed each part. An independent read-only review covered tenant isolation, transactions, the outbox, the service refactor and the web BFF/proxy, and found no defects.

## Known, not fixed here

- **BUG-F01-009 (major, open).** Under the deploy check's 50 virtual users on a laptop, a rolling deploy, its rollback and an instance loss fail some requests. The cause is the window in which one instance carries all the traffic. `origin/main`'s own API and web fail the same check, worse, so this predates the refactor. Nobody had run this check since F03, because no stack API could start. It needs a fix (capacity or readiness during replacement) before any deploy.
- **Regression is over its 20-minute budget** (36 minutes). The next step is per-worker test salons with a serial clock project, so it can run in parallel.
- **A sign-in race test is load-sensitive.** `OperatorAccessIntegrationTest.simultaneousAttemptsOnOneEmailCountEveryAttempt` sends 16 parallel requests over 4 pool connections, and fails only at a high machine load.
- **The owner's retained local database** holds a leftover V17 from abandoned work. It needs a reset or a repair before the API runs on it.
