author: artificial-friend
body:
Two bugs reported from play: salvage floated in the air above hulks, and a cut fuel cell shot off into space.

**Gaps.** The core placed parts on invisible collision spheres (~0.92 r out), while the renderer drew much flatter hulls (a TCN top sits at ~0.6 r), so parts floated metres above the deck. The laser and collisions used the same spheres, so sparks and bumps happened in empty space.
- The core now owns the hull shape. Each section is a rounded-box prism (superellipse |x/a|⁴+|y/b|⁴=1) with per-faction proportions, mirrored in `client/shipkit.js` (`HULL_SECTION`) and the tests.
- Parts are bolted flush to that surface along its normal, never inside a neighbouring section, and clear of other fittings.
- Laser, harpoon, line of sight, ship collision, drone avoidance and loose-part bumps all use the hull distance and a sphere-traced ray instead of spheres.
- Wrecks are drawn with exactly that cross-section.

**Fuel cell launched into space.** Holding the laser on a part after cutting it free pushed it with ~40 kN; on a 400 kg jump cell that is 100 m/s². The push is now ablation recoil: 60 N at full beam, about 3·10⁻⁵ N per watt. A cell in the beam only drifts.

**Tests** (16 pass):
- every bolted part in both zones is within 5 cm of the hull;
- a cut jump cell held in the beam leaves at under 3 m/s;
- a ship dropped onto a hulk makes contact at its collision radius from the drawn hull.

The salvage test now lines up along the part's normal, since the old line grazed another section on the true hull.

author: mi897
body:
## Summary

Two commits, the second builds on the first (so `feat/live-stance-height` is contained here and needs no PR of its own).

**1. The stance height changes while the robot walks** (`c0e3115`). The stand height used to be a model-rebuild parameter: changing it reset the simulation, and the standalone page had no slider for it. It is now eased like the other commands (0.3 s) and the feet are placed that far below the hips on every step, so the body rises or sinks over planted feet while the gait carries on. Trot and crawl can run at custom heights. `live_sim` and the browser port (`browsersim.js`) change together; a **Stand height** slider is on the standalone page and the playground's Live physics tab.

**2. Raise and lower it from the controls** (`69113fe`). In walk mode X and Z (right stick up and down, right thumb on the touch pad) move the stance height at `live_sim.DRIVE[...]["height_rate"]` (0.04 m/s) while held, from the height the page reports, clamped to the slider range; the height stays where it was left. Nothing is sent while idle, so the slider is left alone. Works on the standalone page, the playground Live physics tab and the Kinematic lab (where it moves the lab's own stand-height slider). The view shows the stand height. Pose mode is unchanged (X and Z there still move the body offset over planted feet).

## What was measured (`live_sim.LiveSim`, placeholder model, 150 mm leg segments)

Walking each preset for 2 s at its own height, then setting the height, then 2 s more, then watched for 3 s:
- Trot (0.2 m/s commanded): 0.174 to 0.177 m/s measured at 0.16, 0.19, 0.2125, 0.24 and 0.26 m with no servo saturation (torque peak 0.74 to 0.85 of stall). At 0.13 m it saturates and slows to 0.109 m/s; 0.28 m saturates (0.150 m/s); at 0.10 and 0.30 m the stance is out of reach.
- Crawl (0.05 m/s commanded, measures 0.03 to 0.04 m/s at every height, as before): no saturation from 0.13 to 0.26 m, saturates at 0.28 m, out of reach at 0.10 and 0.30 m.
- Nothing fell at any height. The default trot height of 0.16 m is near the low end of its clean range; other leg lengths move these ranges.
- Controls, in headless Chromium: holding X for 2 s while trotting on the standalone page took the height from 0.160 to 0.239 m (0.04 m/s predicts 0.240) with the robot still trotting at 0.232 m/s; 1 s of Z then gave 0.200 m. Kinematic lab: 1.5 s of X took 0.212 to 0.273 m. Emulated phone: right thumb held 2 s raised it from 0.160 to 0.250 m.

## Tests

- `tests/sim/test_live_sim.py`: the body reaches the new height with feet planted and no rebuild; trot and crawl keep walking at a lower and a higher height; an unreachable height is reported; `height_rate` crosses the slider range in a few seconds.
- `tests/website/test_browsersim.py`: the browser port against the Python through a height change while walking (needs `npm install --no-save @mujoco/mujoco@3.16.0`; runs in the `browser-sim` CI job).
- `tests/website/test_drive_js.py`: signs, rate, clamp, continuing from where it was left, pose mode sends no stance height.
- `python -m unittest discover tests`: 197 tests, 1 error: `tests/sim/test_actuators.py` cannot import `scipy` in this cloud container (it was so before). CI not yet checked.

## What this does not show

- Placeholder dimensions, masses and servo figures: nothing about the real robot; below about 0.16 m or above about 0.26 m (trot) the servos start to saturate and held input will take you past that.
- Only the keyboard and an emulated phone were tried; no real gamepad or phone.
- The Kinematic lab is geometry and static torque: it says nothing about balance or grip.

author: tiagovilasboas
body:
Follow-up to the scorecard on #622.

## Problem

The `universal-skill` playbook had three defects:

1. It named models (`flash_lite`, `haiku-5-5`). Models must come only from the live `providers` tool.
2. It named MCP tools that do not exist (`downshift_providers`, `downshift_playbook`, `downshift_status`). The server registers `providers`, `playbook`, `status`, `apply`, `delegate`, `collect` and `cancel` (`internal/mcp/tools`, joined in `cmd/downshift/cmd_mcp.go`).
3. It shipped as a worker playbook, so a delegation could hand orchestrator strategy text to a worker. Workers receive the output of the `playbook` tool; guidance for the orchestrator belongs in the `downshift-orchestrator` skill.

Its remaining claims (a session ceiling of five, named strategies such as economy and rescue) are not Downshift behaviour either.

## Change

- Remove the `universal-skill` asset and its entry in `shipped()`. The accurate parts (compactor wrapping, fail-open) are already in the orchestrator skill, so nothing moves.
- Update the expected set lists in `playbook_test.go` and `cmd_playbook_test.go`, and the README playbook line.
- Add `skills/shipped_text_test.go`. It scans the installed skills and the shipped worker playbooks and checks that:
  - no token is a catalog model id, or a versioned family name such as `haiku-5-5`;
  - every `mcp__downshift__x` and "MCP tool `x`" mention is a tool the server registers, and no `downshift_x` form appears.
- The test also checks its own matchers against the removed text. With the old asset restored, both content tests fail, naming `flash_lite`, `haiku-5-5` and the three `downshift_*` names.

## Compatibility

A user who had edited `universal-skill.md` keeps the file; it now loads as a custom playbook. A user who had not has no file and simply no longer sees the set.

## Verification

`downshift compactor -- make check` exits 0 (gofmt, vet on host, windows and linux, `go test -count=1 ./...`).

Not touched, out of scope: the README MCP bullet still says `delegate`, `steer`, `result` and `cancel` are specified and not built, while the server registers `delegate`, `collect` and `cancel`.

author: siddsachar
body:
What the owner's real Growth workflows ran into today, fixed before 5.3.1 ships (the release commit isn't tagged yet).

- **Each scene says its own line when the title has a version number.** `output_name` took everything after the last dot as a file type, so "Row-Bot 5.3.1 beta | …" named every scene's voice `Row-Bot 5.3.wav`. Each scene then played the last scene's 3-second line, followed by about 15 s of silence. Now only a real file type comes off the end, and a long title is shortened so the scene or version that tells files apart stays.
- **Turning a video's own sound off works.** At volume 0 the original sound was left out of the mix, which broke ffmpeg in two ways: a made stream nothing read ("Error binding filtergraph inputs/outputs"), or a mix with no inputs ("Result too large"). It now stays in the mix at volume 0. Checked against real ffmpeg 7.1: muted gives a silent track, muted plus a voice gives only the voice.
- **The Video panel's Download works in the desktop app.** It used the browser-only download, which the desktop window refuses, and the notice landed in the panel's foot, out of sight. It now uses `platform.save`, like other exports: the Save dialog, Exports while reconnecting, or a browser download.
- **Checks catch long pauses.**
  - An edit that lays a voice is checked when it's made.
  - A narrated video with 6 s or more without the voice needs attention.
  - So does any picture held still for 10 s or more.
  - The video guide says "needs attention" isn't done.
  - Run on the real video, the new checks flag both the narration gaps and the 13–15 s stills.
- **Narration as part of the project.** A version can carry one narration file said over the whole video, in place of each scene's line. The timeline shows it as a Narration track. Before, a workflow dubbed it onto a picture-only version outside the project, so the panel showed a silent video. Tool schema snapshot re-recorded (+202 characters).
- Release notes: two lines under "New Since The Beta".

## Tests
- New behaviour tests for each fix (Python: video projects, video editing; vitest: the panel's Download and the narration track). Each one fails on the code before its fix.
- Focused runs: video Python tests 51 passed; `src/features/video` vitest 10 passed; prettier, eslint and tsc clean.
- `uv run python scripts/run_test_matrix.py pr` (Windows): exit 0. Client checks with vitest 3413 passed; pytest 12391 passed, 52 skipped; strict app smoke passed.

author: nuk3s
body:
## Description and Motivation

On main, the Zig engine refuses every structured-output request with HTTP 400. That's `response_format` `json_object` and `json_schema`, `guided_json`, `guided_choice`, `structured_outputs` and Anthropic `output_config.format`. So a client has to put the schema in the prompt and check every reply itself. #22 runs into this for document extraction. I ran into it with a pydantic schema that has a `confidence` field between 0 and 1.

`zig/patches/0039-structured-output.patch` makes all of them work, with DSpark drafts on.

Terms I use below. The engine turns the schema into a grammar, the rules for which bytes can come next. DSpark drafts are guesses from a small draft model, and a verify is the full model checking them in one pass. Rank 0 is the process that serves HTTP.

What's in it:

- Rank 0 keeps each reply inside its request's grammar. Rank 1 never sees the grammar.
- Schemas follow xgrammar 0.2.8 (the grammar library vLLM uses) and get the usual structure keywords, six `format`s, and numeric bounds (`minimum`, `maximum` and the exclusive ones).
- After each verify, rank 0 runs the accepted tokens through the matcher, the new code that checks them byte by byte against the grammar. If the grammar refuses a token, rank 0 picks a new one at that position with the refused tokens masked out. So a reply comes out the same whether it's drafted, run with `"draft": false`, or sitting next to other requests.
- Anything it can't enforce gets a 400 before the first token, and the error names the keyword (`regex`, EBNF `grammar`, `pattern`, `multipleOf` and more, full list in `docs/api.md`).
- There's no switch. A request without a grammar runs the same code as before.

The patch is 21,222 lines, but only 3,166 of them are engine code. Two saved corpora (test strings with xgrammar's verdict on each) take 13,447, and tests and fixtures take 2,833.

## Related Issues

- #22. This covers everything there except regex and EBNF, so I left off a closing keyword.
- #81 also uses the number 0039. The two patches apply in either order (I checked both), so whichever lands second needs a new number in its file name and README row. If something else lands first, I'll renumber and rebase.
- The same change is open on the engine side as bertholomus/TensorFold#48, #49 and #50. Once `TF_REF` includes them, this patch can go.

---

## Testing

- It applies with the Dockerfile's loop on a clean `fbbc971` checkout.
- Host tests (main `0e7d421` + this patch, x86_64, Zig 0.17.0): `zig build test` 589/591 (main is 527/529 with the same two spill failures), `zig_test.sh` 97/97 and 98/98, `test_lanes.sh` 50/50, grammar module 46/46, `port_test.sh` 148/148.
- The matcher agrees with xgrammar 0.2.8 on every string in the corpora: 3,000 `json_object`, 5,400 schema and choice, 4,950 with bounds.
- On my two DGX Sparks at temperature 0, `tools/exact.py` (31 cases, no grammar) gives `IDENTICAL` against my image without this patch (setup below). For `json_object` and `json_schema`, the drafted, `"draft": false` and 4 concurrent replies all have the same `token_sha` (a sha256 of the reply's token ids).
- Speed without a grammar, one run each: 32K prefill 2,151.4 tok/s with the patch vs 2,162.1 without, and one-stream decode 82.1 vs 82.2 tok/s.

Not tested on the Sparks: drafted vs `"draft": false` for sampled replies and for `guided_choice`, and #22's long extraction replies and pictures (the reporter offered to test a branch).

<details>
<summary>Test details and edge cases</summary>

Host tests:

| | main | main + 0039 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zig build test` | 527/529 | 589/591 |
| `zig/tests/server/zig_test.sh` | 91/91 and 95/95 | 97/97 and 98/98 |
| `tools/zig/test_lanes.sh` | 44/44 | 50/50 |
| `zig test zig/src/core/grammar/grammar.zig` | (no module) | 46/46 |

The two `zig build test` failures are the spill store's "write faults" check and fsio's `a partial direct write off the 4 KiB grid finishes buffered`. Both do short `O_DIRECT` writes in a test folder on XFS, and this patch doesn't touch spill code. `test_lanes.sh` skips its recorded fixtures (4 and 5 tests) on both sides because `TF_LANES_FIXTURES` isn't set.

With xgrammar 0.2.8 installed, `tools/zig/xgrammar_json_corpus.py --check` and `xgrammar_schema_corpus.py --check` label the corpora again and find 0 differences. The Zig tests check the matcher's verdict on each string, down to the index of the byte it refuses. On the fake target (the lane core's test backend), new tests check that `json_object`, `json_schema` and choice replies come out the same drafted, with `"draft": false` and sharing a round with other requests, both greedy and sampled. A schema reply that decodes while the engine reads another prompt in pieces equals the same reply run alone.

Why drafted replies stay exact: in the verify pass each position has a row of logits. At temperature 0, a row keeps its token if the grammar allows it. Every other row gets drawn again from the logits rank 0 already holds, with the refused tokens set to -inf (a new optional `Backend.VTable.redraw`). That masked draw is bit for bit the plain draw on a copy of the row with the refused tokens at -inf, and a refused draft can never equal the masked pick.

Setup on the Sparks: kernel 7.0.0-1019-nvidia, driver 580.178.04, the EAQ v1 pack @45ee5d0f, `CONTEXT=1048576`, `PARALLEL=6`, `POOL=2101248`, drafts on, `GRAPH_CAP=128`, `SPILL_GIB=256`, `KV_SHARD=0`, `TF_DS_ENGRAM_LEAD=1`, `TF_FILL_CHUNKS=1`, `TF_FILL_CUT_IN=8192`. The image also has other patches and script changes of mine that I'm still testing. The image I compared against had the same ones, minus this patch and two more of mine (the restore-room patch, which is my next PR, and one that only changes tests).

Results there:

- My structured-output check script passes 15 of 15. The shared `token_sha` is `b85c5effc473` for `json_object` and `9e3c566430ac` for `json_schema`. A plain reply next to 3 structured ones equals its solo reply. The other checks look for valid JSON (thinking off and on, a nested schema, both `guided_choice` spellings, streaming, Anthropic `output_config.format`) and for the 400s on `pattern`, `guided_regex` and `ignore_eos`.
- The pydantic schema I mentioned at the top is 170 lines with `$defs`. The `triage_report.json` fixture in this patch is that schema with shorter descriptions. I sent it 3 s into a 43,707-token prompt that the engine was reading in pieces. It came back HTTP 200 with every required key and `finish_reason` `stop`.
- One-stream decode used two 512-token prompts, twice each, 256 tokens out. The 32K prefill reply has `token_sha` `2222e35c1fbc` on both images.
- With a grammar, a 40-item JSON list decoded at 122.4 tok/s under `json_schema` and 122.3 under `json_object` (streamed, thinking off, best of two).
- Sampled replies: only the Anthropic request ran sampled on the Sparks (server default temperature), and its JSON was valid. A sampled stream draws every accepted row again, and I haven't measured that cost on GB10.

Edge cases:

- Numeric bounds copy xgrammar 0.2.8, which turns them into a range regex: no exponent, no leading zero, at most 6 decimals. A bound off the 6-decimal grid moves to the nearest grid point inside, and whole parts cap at int64 like in xgrammar.
- These also get a 400: `ignore_eos` with a grammar, a grammar next to `tool_choice` `"required"` or a named function, `uniqueItems`, and an `anyOf` whose branches can start with the same byte. The message names the keyword and its path, like `#/properties/s: pattern: it is not enforced by this engine`.
- If the engine must commit a token the grammar refuses (a forced `</think>` from the thinking budget, or a row where nothing is allowed), only that request ends, with HTTP 500, or an error event when streaming.
- Where it differs from xgrammar 0.2.8: the matcher refuses an encoded surrogate in a string, nesting past 128 levels, and every added token. With DeepSeek-V4.1's tokenizer, xgramm

author: tpurtell
body:
Runner extension for the kernel-route audit (tpurtell/cuteafd#912 follow-up). Benchmarks plus one opt-in compile option; no export changes.

## Changes
- `benchmark_mixed_trellis.py` coordinator mode:
  - `--no-coop`: the first `--coordinator-arm` (WS) is the bit-exact oracle, with no cooperative injection.
  - `prerotate=0/1` arm key: hoisted token-major FC1 rotation vs in-tile rotation.
  - `revision=SHA` arm key: compiles that arm from a frozen fork revision's K4 sibling modules (existing `materialize_k4_arm`/`load_k4_arm` bundles; `--arm-source-dir` for staged runs without Git).
  - `--live-rows`: times each compiled capacity at partial planner units. Each count is checked against the oracle at that count and against the capacity batch's prefix.
  - Receipts record the oracle name, arm revisions and the enforced board power limit (NVML; `null` on GB10).
- `compile_mixed_trellis(..., ws_prerotate=None)` and `W4A16MixedTrellisWSKernel(prerotate=None)`: `None` keeps the existing `not wire and a16` predicate, so every current export is byte-identical. Explicit `True` with wire or A8 is rejected.

author: bensheridanedwards
body:
## Why

`captureText: false` is the documented way to keep page copy out of maps, but overlay capture ignored it. Overlay subtree text reached published maps, and popup keys and trigger labels built from text appeared in the leaked-overlay warning. Closes #1142.

## What changed

- `src/capture.ts`, `src/capture/browser.ts`: with `captureText: false`, overlay text is never read and the `text` property is omitted from the map.
- `src/runner/browser.ts`: in privacy mode, popup trigger labels and the text part of popup keys are replaced in the page by an 8-character FNV-1a hash of the text, instead of the raw text.
  - Review round 2: round 1 dropped the text entirely, which weakened popup tracking. With hashes, privacy mode keeps the same guards as text mode. A shifted same-tag sibling with different text is still caught by the `missing` guard. An overlay whose only change is its text still counts as opened. Leftovers that differ only in text are still reported as leaked, and the warning shows hashes, not copy.
- With text capture on (the default), keys, labels and overlay text are unchanged.
- Tests:
  - New `test/overlay-text-privacy.e2e.spec.ts`: a map captured with `captureText: false` contains neither the dialog's email address nor the toast's payment text. The toast is asserted to be a detected overlay, so that check can fail.
  - New `test/overlay-text-privacy.test.mjs`: overlay text omission, hashed popup identities, and the three popup guards in privacy mode.
- CHANGELOG `### Fixed` line.

## Reviewer view

```
captureText: false
  overlay subtree   -> no text read, no text property in the map
  popup key / label -> text replaced by an in-page 8-char hash (e.g. "3f1a9c2e"); guards unchanged
captureText: true   -> unchanged
```

## Proof

Before (`origin/main` b50a6440 source, new tests kept; Linux Cua Space on the Mac mini):
```
e2e:  Error: expect(received).not.toContain(expected)
      Expected substring: not "alice@example.com"
  1 failed
  1 passed
✖ overlay capture omits the text property without reading copy when disabled
✖ popup privacy identities hash copy and change when copy changes
✖ privacy mode reports text-only leftovers as leaked without logging raw copy
ℹ tests 7
ℹ pass 4
ℹ fail 3
```
After (fix applied):
```
  2 passed (2.4s)
✔ overlay capture omits the text property without reading copy when disabled
✔ popup privacy identities hash copy and change when copy changes
✔ privacy mode skips a shifted same-tag sibling with different text as missing
✔ privacy mode counts an overlay text-only change as opened
✔ privacy mode reports text-only leftovers as leaked without logging raw copy
ℹ tests 7
ℹ pass 7
ℹ fail 0
```
- Proof Law (what would falsify this PR): a map captured with `captureText: false` that contains overlay copy, or raw copy in a popup key, label or warning in that mode.
- Screenshots: Not applicable (no rendered surface changes).

## Behaviour changes

- Behaviour change: Given `captureText: false`, when a page has overlays, then no overlay text is stored in the map.
- Behaviour change: Given `captureText: false`, when a popup cannot be cleared, then the leaked-overlay warning names it by a text hash instead of its copy.

## Not asked for

- Extra change: None. (The reviewer noted that `src/variant-crawler.ts` builds variant keys from button text regardless of `captureText`; that is out of scope here.)

## Review guide

- Start here: the `captureText` check in `detectOverlayCandidates` (`src/capture/browser.ts`), then `privateText`, `labelOf` and `popupKey` in `src/runner/browser.ts`.

## Verification summary

- Commands run: the e2e and unit tests, before and after, in the Cua Space; the runner/popup/capture unit suites (Codex: 199 selected tests); the pre-commit hook; the full pre-push hook on push (anti-slop lint, `pnpm test`, browser e2e `--workers=4`).
- Results: before e2e 1 failed and units 4/7; after e2e 2 passed and units 7/7.
- Unrelated failures: None.
- Known risks or skipped checks: the hash is non-cryptographic (32-bit FNV-1a) and only appears in memory and CI warnings; short, guessable copy could be matched by brute force.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [jdx/mise-action](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action) | action | patch | `v5.2.3` → `v5.2.4` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/mise-action</summary>

### [`v5.2.4`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v5.2.4): : Reuse cached signed checksums when restoring mise

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.3...v5.2.4)

Jobs that restore mise from the cache no longer have to download its signed checksums from GitHub on every run, so a network failure at that step no longer fails a job that otherwise restored correctly.

#### Fixed

- **Restoring a cached mise no longer needs a network download of the checksums.** The action checks the cached mise binary against the signed `SHASUMS256.txt` and its `.minisig`. Before this release it downloaded both files from GitHub on every run, even when the cache restored correctly. When that download failed, for example after repeated curl errors, the job failed. Now, once the signature checks out, the action saves both files as `SHASUMS256-<version>.txt` and `.minisig` in `<mise_dir>/bin`, which is part of the mise cache. On later runs it reads them from the restored cache and checks the minisign signature again before using them. If the files are missing, corrupt or tampered with, the action downloads them as it did before. There are no new inputs. ([#​708](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/708) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))
  - Caches saved by earlier versions don't contain these files. The main cache is only saved on a cache miss, so runs keep downloading the checksums until the cache is saved again or its key changes.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.3...v5.2.4>

</details>

body:
Suite des pull requests #18 et #19 (déjà fusionnées) : les notes annexes du module « États financiers annuels — FABS-CI ».

## Ce que contient cette pull request

**27 notes annexes calculées depuis la comptabilité**, affichées à l'écran, dans le dossier PDF et dans l'export Excel :
- **Notes 3A, 3C, 3C BIS, 3D** (immobilisations) : tableaux de mouvements (ouverture, acquisitions, cessions, dotations, sorties, clôture, plus- et moins-values) calculés depuis les comptes 2x, 28x, 29x, 81x et 82x.
- **Notes 4 à 11, 14, 15A, 16A, 17 à 27A, 29** : détail par sous-compte, en N et N-1.

**Export Excel** : les notes sont écrites dans les feuilles « NOTE n » du modèle. Les totaux du modèle restent des formules. Les lignes que l'ERP ne calcule pas sont vidées au lieu de garder les chiffres d'une autre année.

**Fiches R1, R2 et R4** (`fiches-modele.ts`) :
- **R1** : dates de l'exercice et de l'exercice précédent, et identification saisie dans l'ERP (RCCM, codes, désignation, coordonnées, activité, expert-comptable, signataire). Si un champ est vide dans l'ERP, la valeur du modèle est conservée et signalée « à vérifier ». La date d'arrêté des comptes, l'approbation par l'assemblée et la date de signature sont vidées, à compléter.
- **R2** : chiffre d'affaires de l'exercice reporté sur l'activité principale, avec une hypothèse signalée s'il y a plusieurs activités.
- **R4** : chaque note calculée est cochée A si elle a au moins un montant en N ou N-1, N/A sinon. Les autres notes gardent les marques du modèle.
- **R3** (dirigeants) n'est pas modifiée.

## Garde-fous
- **Chaque note est recoupée par un test** avec le poste du bilan ou du compte de résultat qu'elle détaille (AQ, BA, BB, BJ, BQ, BR, CD, CF, CG, CL, CM, DA, DB, DC, DM, DQ, DR, RK, RM, TK).
- **Aucun rapprochement approximatif** : libellés identiques au modèle, sinon correspondance écrite ligne par ligne (`notes-modele.ts`). Un test échoue si une correspondance devient orpheline.
- **Un compte n'est ventilé que si son rattachement est certain.** Sinon, il apparaît en « non ventilé » et l'export le signale.
- **Ce que la comptabilité ne distingue pas** (répartition des ventes par zone, opérations de groupe, virements de poste à poste, reprises d'amortissements, immeubles de placement) fait l'objet d'une **hypothèse affichée** à l'écran, dans le PDF et dans la feuille « ERP - LISEZ-MOI ».
- Montant inconnu : case vide, jamais zéro.

## Correction du bilan
La dépréciation **591** (titres et valeurs à encaisser) diminue désormais le poste **BR**, et non plus la trésorerie BS.

## Vérifications
- Sur le classeur DGI 2025 réel (fichier confidentiel, hors dépôt) : les 27 notes trouvent toutes leurs lignes. Dans Excel, aucun écart avec la liasse sur les notes 3A, 3C, 3C BIS, 3D et sur 12 des 13 autres nouvelles notes. Pour la 27A, le total est exact ; sa ventilation est limitée par le jeu d'essai, qui regroupe la paie sur un compte.
- Les totaux des notes recalculés par Excel égalent ceux de l'ERP.
- Fiches, vérifiées dans Excel : les dates, l'identification, le total de R2 et les marques de R4 sont corrects, sans aucune rubrique introuvable.
- Le PDF a été rendu et relu page par page : notes 3 en paysage, sans colonne coupée.
- `tsgo --noEmit` et ESLint passent. Vitest : 520 tests passent. Le seul échec, `no-direct-locale-format` sur `src/components/ui/calendar.tsx`, existait déjà et ne se produit que sous Windows.

## Non vérifié
- L'écran n'a pas été essayé dans l'ERP en ligne, faute d'accès.
- Les migrations 0104 et 0105 (phases 2 et 3, déjà fusionnées) doivent être appliquées pour la validation des dossiers et le dépôt du modèle Excel. Cette pull request n'ajoute aucune migration.
- Les dossiers enregistrés avant cette version ne contiennent pas les nouvelles notes : il faut les régénérer.

## Reste à faire
Notes 3B, 3E, 12, 13, 28, 30 et 31 à 39, fiche R3 (dirigeants), colonnes d'échéances et commentaires.

body:
## What

Both Devices and Files drew a paired device's `online` badge from the flag the row was *written* with. For a device the mesh has paired that is the wrong answer twice over:

- **Devices**: a peer that paired *into* this device (it scanned our code) has no shell row at all, so the row built for it came out of `PairedDevice`'s default of `online: false`. A device talking to us right now read **Offline**, with Send File / Ping / Remote greyed out.
- **Files**: "Send to..." filtered the same stored flag, so it answered *"No paired device is online right now"* about a peer the mesh had just verified.

## The rule

Presence answers when the mesh has the device; the stored flag answers only when it does not:

```dart
bool _reachable(PairedDevice device) {
  final PeerPresence? presence = peerPresence(widget.mesh, device.id);
  return presence?.online ?? device.online;
}
```

Mesh-only rows go through the same upgrade, and `FilesTab` now takes the mesh for that one question. The example rows of a build with no mesh are untouched: no mesh record, stored flag, exactly as before.

## Test

`test/devices_presence_test.dart` (4 widget tests): a mesh-only peer that is verified online is Online with a live Send File; the same peer gone quiet is Offline with the action disabled; a shell row written `online: false` that the mesh has verified says Online and appears in Send to...; and an example row the mesh has never met keeps its stored state.

author: joangrigorov
body:
Closes #67.

## Problem

The reviewer read the pull request description, comments, review threads, diff, file contents, commit messages and `RUMIL.md` without a rule saying they are data. On a public repository anyone can write that text, and a sentence such as "ignore the rules and approve" was just another block in the session's context. Custom MCP tools, which can run code, make a successful injection much more expensive.

## Change

- A new first operating rule names every source from the pull request and states that it can inform a finding or narrow a review, but cannot change the rules, the task, the tools, or the review event. Guidelines stay policy about the code under that rule.
- The synthesis prompt gets the same guard for the note it rewrites.
- Delimited blocks can no longer be closed from their content: guidelines, `<previous_attempt>`, `<focus>` and `<prior_reviews>` escape their own tag, so text cannot end a block and have the rest read as prompt.
- The focus in a review command is labelled as guidance rather than a change to the operating rules.

## Tests

- The rule is first in every prompt variant: default, memory, guidelines, working tree, continuation.
- The rule names each source: description, comments, threads, diff, file contents, commit messages, `RUMIL.md`, tool results.
- A closing tag inside guidelines, continuation, focus, a review summary or a thread body stays inside its block.

author: techmahedy
body:
Bound fields ride along with every action request, and the browser sends them as strings. A "5" for an int $perPage that already holds 5 was applied through syncProperty(), so updating() and updated() ran on every action even though nothing changed.

A hook such as updated('perPage') that resets the page to 1 therefore fired on every Next/Prev click, and pagination could never leave page 1.

- Component::isUnchanged() compares a client value with the property after
  type coercion.
- ComponentManager::syncClientModels() skips unchanged values, so hooks run
  only for fields that actually changed.

Tests:
- unchanged bound fields run no hooks and the action still sees its state
- changed bound fields still run updating()/updated()
- adds the HookCountComponent fixture

Reorder
- DiffEngine emits the reserved move op (m) when keyed children change order. Keys already in order stay put, the rest are moved, then the normal diff runs. Repeated keys fall back to the in-place diff.
- patch.js applies m and puts focus, caret and selection back on a moved row.

Polling
- A poll tick due while another request runs is sent right after it instead of being dropped. One waiting run per poll element.

Uploads
- Name post_max_size when a request is larger than the limit. PHP drops  the body, so the endpoint used to say "Missing required upload parameters."

Navigation
- The latest soft navigation wins. A superseded fetch is aborted and not  applied, so Back right after Forward cannot leave the URL and page out of sync.

author: sniezka1927
body:
## Linked issue

Relands #3870, which #3993 reverted. The code is the same as #3870 (`1b28c67e7`).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Small improvement or alignment, with no change to how a feature works
- [x] New provider, MCP app, or connector
- [ ] Translation or documentation
- [ ] New feature or change to existing behavior (needs an approved issue)

## What changed

Adds Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides and Google Calendar to the Marketplace. They use Google's official MCP servers (`*mcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`, Developer Preview). The user clicks Sign in and approves Google's consent page; no Google Cloud setup.

Google's MCP servers do not support dynamic client registration, and Google's token endpoint needs a client secret. So:

- **Signal (`remote/api`)**: new `POST /v1/google/oauth/token`. Signal holds the secret of the OpenBot Google sign-in app (`GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENTS`, encrypted in `remote/.env.production`) and does only the code exchange and the token refresh. It checks the host's remote ticket, accepts only known client IDs and a loopback `/mcp-auth` redirect, allows 30 requests a minute for each host, and stores and logs nothing. Contract: `packages/contracts/src/signal-protocol/google-oauth.ts`.
- **Host**: `src/backend/google-mcp-sign-in.ts` maps each Google MCP URL to its scopes (read and write). `McpOAuth` gives a Google URL the OpenBot app when the user saved none, and sends its two token requests to Signal (`src/main/google-token-broker.ts`, public client ID of project `openbot-a3328`). The tokens stay on the host and the MCP traffic goes to Google directly. A sign-in app that the user saved still wins. The stored record shape does not change; the built-in app always reads the current scopes.
- **Catalog**: 6 listings, guides on openbot.run, 13 locales. `test:mcp-catalog` skips these URLs.
- **Limits from Google's servers, stated in the listings**: Gmail has no send or permanent delete tool; Drive has no move, rename or delete tool; Slides has no create or delete presentation tool. Tasks has no Google MCP server and is not included.

Surfaces: desktop renderer (Marketplace data only, no component change), mobile (generated catalog; sign-in runs on the host through the existing relay), `apps/auth-api` (plugin pages), Signal, IPC contracts unchanged, no migration, docs (`PRIVACY.md`, `docs/architecture/integrations.md`, `remote/README.md`, `remote/api/AGENTS.md`). Reverse action: disconnect or sign-out revokes the token at Google directly.

## Verification

- [x] Narrow checks for what changed: Biome on changed files, `typecheck:node` (also with `--exactOptionalPropertyTypes` on the changed files), `typecheck:renderer`, `remote/api` and `apps/auth-api` typecheck, `marketplace:build:plugins -- --check`, `i18n:check`, release-note fragment check, `knip` exports
- [x] Surfaces touched are named under "What changed"
- [x] Relevant manual smoke test completed (table below); the real Google consent is not checked
- [x] No credentials, private data, generated output, or real user files are included (the client secret is only encrypted in `remote/.env.production`)

E2E:
- `bun run test:signal`: 28/28, with 9 Google broker checks (no ticket, foreign key, unknown client, non-loopback redirect, extra keys, exchange with secret, refresh and refusal pass-through, rate limit, no secret/code/token in logs).
- `bun run test:mcp-google-broker` (new): 11/11. Real Google discovery and consent page for Calendar; code exchange and refresh through a local Signal against a fake token endpoint; `removeSignInApp` keeps an OpenBot-app sign-in; an older scope and an earlier client ID on file are replaced; a host with no OpenBot account gets no OpenBot app; a Signal refusal shows `error.backend.googleSignInUnavailable`; a saved sign-in app wins; a host with no ticket gets the account sentence.

Smoke (`bun run dev`, worktree profile, desktop):

| # | Feature | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Marketplace lists the 6 Google apps | pass | Apps tab: `Open Gmail`, `Open Google Drive`, `Open Google Docs`, `Open Google Sheets`, `Open Google Slides`, `Open Google Calendar`, each with `Connect` |
| 2 | Listing text | pass | Gmail page: "…write drafts, add and remove labels… Agents cannot send email…"; Slides page: "…add, change and delete slides…", 3 prompts |
| 3 | Connect Google Calendar starts the Google sign-in | pass | Dialog "Connect Google Calendar" with `Waiting for the browser…`; no "does not accept OpenBot" error; no MCP sign-in error in the stack log |
| 4 | Built-in sign-in app hidden in the server row | not checked in the app | Covered by `test:mcp-google-broker` (`signInApp` is `null` for the OpenBot app) |
| 5 | Cancel (reverse) | pass | Dialog closes; Calendar shows `Connect Google Calendar` again |
| 6 | Google consent and token exchange | not checked | Needs a test user's Google consent and production Signal with `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENTS` |

## Risk and security impact

- **Network**: the host sends the Google authorization code, PKCE verifier and refresh token to Signal over TLS, with its remote ticket. Signal adds the secret, forwards to Google and returns Google's answer. Nothing is stored or logged (`test:signal` checks the logs). Documented in `PRIVACY.md`.
- **Scopes**: restricted (`gmail.*`, `drive`, `drive.readonly`) and sensitive scopes. The consent screen is in Testing (max 100 test users, 7-day refresh tokens) until Google verification and CASA.
- **Deploy order**: Signal must be deployed with `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENTS` before a release with this change; without it the route answers 503 and Google sign-in fails with Google's error.
- **No OpenBot account**: a host with no host ID gets no OpenBot app, so Google servers behave as before (the user's own sign-in app). A Signal refusal shows `error.backend.googleSignInUnavailable` instead of an empty error.
- **Not confirmed**: The `openbot://mcp-auth` fallback (no free loopback port) does not work with a Google Desktop client.

author: lvaoliveira
body:
First of the five remaining web screens, built in the agreed order (Projects → Analysis → Component → Security → Gates) and from real data only: parts of the design nothing records are left out and listed in the roadmap.

## Projects (`/projects`)

**Columns**, as of each project's main branch's latest analysis:
- gate, score and ratings (Rel · Sec · Mnt pips);
- coverage, duplication, open issues and size;
- when it was analyzed.

**Controls:**
- **Filters:** gate (All / Blocking / Passing, with counts), language chips and name search.
- **Sort:** lowest score, most issues, lowest coverage, recently analyzed, or name.
- **URL:** filters and sort are kept in the URL, so a filtered view can be shared.

The empty state tells you to upload a project when there are none.

## Project page (`/projects/:key?branch=`)

- **Header:** a branch picker (each branch's gate and age), languages, lines, the analysis commit and tool version.
- **Measures:** score, ratings and six tiles (bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells, coverage, duplication, debt), switchable between overall and new code. Tiles link to the project's issues on that branch.
- **Gate:** each condition from the repository's `sonda.toml`, with its actual value and pass, fail or no-data status.
- **History:** the branch's last 12 analyses, as issue, coverage, duplication and debt sparklines plus the gate result per analysis.
- **Components:** top-level directories with languages, owner (from the uploaded CODEOWNERS), files, lines, issues and debt.

Overview project names now link to their pages.

## Server

- **`GET /api/projects` and `GET /api/projects/{key}`**, documented in docs/server.md.
  - An unknown project is a 404.
  - A branch without analyses is a 400 that names the analyzed branches.
- **New `health` module:** the ratings, gate states, condition labels and formats the Overview already computed move into it, so the Overview and Projects use one implementation instead of copies. This is behavior-neutral: the existing overview and drill tests pass unchanged.
- **Integration test:** `tests/projects.rs` runs against Postgres and covers ratings from tracked issues, branches, components and the error cases.

## Web

- **Issue links:** `IssueQuery` gains `project` and `branch`. The server already supported them. The Issues page reads `?project=&branch=` from links and names the project in its summary.
- **Mock:** projects consistent with the mock Overview and issues.
- **Tests:** four app tests for filtering, the page, branch switching and the issue links. Screens were also checked at desktop width.

## Not in this PR

Recorded in the roadmap:
- Monorepo detection, saved views and a grid view: nothing records the data, and saved views need teams.
- The app shell keeps its sidebar at phone widths. Every page scrolls sideways there; this isn't new.
- Stale roadmap rows (CODEOWNERS owners, branch protection, the Overview layout gap) are removed.

author: varshith-kali
body:
## What it does

Screens a tool result before any agent sees it. A non-agent task produces the tool result first, a screening task inspects it for credential material and instruction-override language, and only the screened (redacted or cleared) output is passed into the AIAgent task's prompt. The agent never sees the raw result. Credential matches are redacted and the agent works from the safe copy. Instruction-override matches, or an empty result the screen cannot judge, fail the run before any agent call, so no token is spent on a poisoned or unseen input.

## Prerequisites

A Kestra instance with the AI plugin and a GEMINI_API_KEY secret in the flow namespace. A real tool result to screen: paste it into tool_result_text for a standalone run, or pass a real tool task output into that input when running as a subflow. In production, replace produce_tool_result with the real tool task and keep the screen task as the only bridge to the agent prompt.

## How it works

1. produce_tool_result (python Script, not an agent task) hands the supplied tool result forward unchanged.
2. screen_tool_output (python Script) scans it twice: credential patterns (AWS keys, private key headers, GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI, Slack tokens, bearer tokens, assigned secrets) and instruction-override phrases. Credentials become [REDACTED] in the screened copy; instruction matches, or an empty result, yield BLOCKED with an empty screened copy.
3. triage (If) fails the execution itself (Fail) on BLOCKED, naming only finding counts and categories, never matched secret values. On CLEAR or REDACTED it only logs the counts.
4. run_agent (AIAgent, no tools configured) runs only after the screen passes, with a prompt built from the screened output alone.
5. deliver (Return) reports the verdict and the agent answer together.

## How to adapt it

Add credential patterns for the token formats your tools actually return, keeping the redaction rule for every new pattern, and extend the instruction-override phrase list for your domain. Never pass the raw tool output into any agent prompt, system message, or memory store: the screen task stays the only bridge. If an agent legitimately needs a credential-bearing result, route that case to a separate, human-approved flow instead of loosening this gate.

## Verification

Scripts were extracted from the committed YAML and run against stub cases, all passing: clean output passes unchanged (CLEAR), AWS key redacted (REDACTED, key absent from screened copy), GitHub token redacted (REDACTED), instruction-override output blocked (BLOCKED, empty screened copy), secret plus instruction blocked (BLOCKED), empty output fails closed (BLOCKED). YAML parses. No live Kestra run is claimed: the agent call itself requires a Kestra instance with a GEMINI_API_KEY secret, and the Validate check on this PR covers the flow definition.

## Distinctness

This is the exact inversion of closed #4941, where the agent had already read the raw result before the scan ran: here the screen sits strictly before the agent call, and the agent prompt is built from the screened output alone. It differs from open #4926 (config change watchdog) and open #4946 (daily spend gate), which judge neither tool result content nor pre-agent screening, and from closed #4927 (post-hoc token check), #4934 (failure-loop watchdog), #4939 (live-call loop guard), and #4942 (tool-privilege gate), none of which screen a tool result before the agent sees it.

author: tuxxy
body:
Fixes tuxxy/keep-core#28

Remediation batch 5, keep-core half. The FROST proof producers now size their SPV proofs from the Bridge's `txProofDifficultyFactor` and the relay's epoch difficulties, using the base `getProofInfo`, as the legacy maintainer does. They no longer use the operator's `Confirmations` as the depth.

## Change
- `pkg/chain/ethereum`: `FrostRedemptionChain` reports `TxProofDifficultyFactor` and `GetCurrentAndPrevEpochDifficulty`. It reads the second through the relay that the Bridge names in `contractReferences`, using the same two functions the Bridge calls.
- `pkg/frost/redemption`: the C-04 `Reader` gains these two methods. The deposit and movement readers embed it, so every producer's existing `Chain` field carries them, as base `spv.Chain` carries the factor. No producer gained a field.
- `pkg/maintainer/spv`:
  - the movement, incoming-sweep, deposit-sweep and redemption producers derive the depth with `frostProofDepth`;
  - `Confirmations` is only a floor;
  - with fewer confirmations than the Bridge needs, they submit nothing;
  - `getProofInfo` now takes the two narrow interfaces it reads, instead of the whole legacy `Chain`.
- `pkg/frost/redemption/fake_test.go`: the unit-test fake gains the two methods as stubs that return an error. It never sizes proofs. This is the only test-file edit; it is not a frozen file.

**Why interface methods rather than a type assertion:** a first version asserted the binding's type. That broke the existing K-06/K-07 integration tests, because their lost-reply wrappers embed the `Chain` interface and hide any method the interface does not declare. With the methods on the interface, those wrappers (which batch 2 also touches) work unchanged.

## Frozen tests (byte-identical, from tuxxy/keep-core#99 `d2f1c93855addde74ba8a04e4760790b5956eeb4`)
```

604c0893ca9e07739fec83e8025a1e3ac2a61446 test/spvdepth/README.md

39780a088debac6f08e0b87fd529488a6b34298d test/spvdepth/run.sh
```

## Acceptance
`test/spvdepth/run.sh` at head `2f6f80b31` (clean):
- result: **`accepted: true`**, 16/16 passed (8 at factor 6 and 8 at factor 2), 0 skipped, none missing or extra;
- run time: about 11 s;

## Controls
The frozen wrong patches are written against the `28-derive-depth.fix` file shapes, so they do not apply to this code. I applied the same two mutations to this code instead, in a scratch worktree at `2f6f80b31`:

| Control | Mutation | Result |

| ignores-factor | `TxProofDifficultyFactor` returns 6 instead of reading the Bridge | the 8 factor-6 cases pass; the 8 factor-2 cases fail at `derived a 37-header proof; the Bridge at factor 2 needs exactly 7` (×4) and `derived a 35-header proof; … needs exactly 11` (×4) |

author: grubba27
body:
Change Streams take the start point of each collection stream and each new observer's "caught up" floor from `ping`'s `operationTime`. When the server leaves it out, a write that lands after an observer starts listening but before its stream is open never produces an event, and `_waitUntilCaughtUp` waits for an unrelated later write with no limit, logging `catching up took too long` every 10 s. The method's `updated` is never sent, which is the login spinner in [#14872](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/issues/14872); the `snapshot read concern: command not found` line in that report is a separate, harmless symptom.

- **Server check**: the one-time Change Streams eligibility check now also requires `ping` to return `operationTime`; otherwise Meteor uses the next configured driver (polling on Atlas Flex, as on 3.4), like the existing standalone fallback. Local replica sets, `mongos` and authenticated replica sets return it (verified on 8.0.29), so normal deployments are unaffected. Refs #14872
- **Log the reason once per connection** when the server check rejects Change Streams, so a silent move to polling is visible; the standalone and version fallbacks were silent before. Concurrent first observers now share one support check instead of each running it.
- **Tests**: `changestream - fence does not hang when ping omits operationTime` emulates the Flex replies; before the fix it reproduces the reporter's exact diagnostic state (`lastProcessedOperationTime: null, isReady: true, changeStreamOpen: true`) and fails, after it passes, with about 270 ms of timing headroom. The full `mongo` suite passes with `changeStreams,oplog,polling`.
- **Changelog** entry under Fixes, reporter credited; `disable-oplog.md` and the Change Streams guide now state the `operationTime` requirement.

Flex omitting `operationTime` from `ping` is inferred from the reporter's diagnostic state and consistent with Atlas's proxy behaviour, not confirmed on a Flex cluster; `await MongoInternals.defaultRemoteCollectionDriver().mongo.db.command({ ping: 1 })` in `meteor shell` on Flex would settle it. Keeping Change Streams on Flex by taking the floor from a write's own `operationTime` is a feasible follow-up, too invasive for the RC. Applies cleanly to release-3.5.4 for a backport.

author: lanesawyer
body:
When `CoreTracker::tasks` skips a task because its `factory` metadata won't deserialize into `RunUpdate`, it now posts a Note on that task. The note names the bad field(s) and the parse error, and says the factory will pick the task up again once the field is fixed or removed. The posting is in `flag_bad_metadata`.

- **Once per problem:** the tracker keeps a map of the task key to the note body it has posted. Later run-loop passes find the same note there, so they neither comment nor log.
- **Restarts:** before posting, it checks the task's existing comments for an identical note. A restarted factory doesn't repeat it.
- **Changed problem:** if the metadata is still malformed but the error or fields differ, a new note is posted and logged.
- **Failed note:** if the note can't be posted, it logs a warning and tries again on the next pass.
- **Field names:** serde's error doesn't name the field (it says `expected u32`). `bad_fields` finds the offending keys by deserializing each metadata key on its own.

I extended `a_task_with_malformed_factory_metadata_is_skipped_not_fatal`. After repeated `ready` and `in_flight` passes it asserts exactly one comment on the task, and that it names `attempt_base`. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test -p trailhead-control` all pass.

Follow-ups:
- The note is a plain Note, not a question, so the task isn't parked. I chose that so a bad value doesn't also change the task's status. A `needs_input` question would make Lane's attention explicit; say if you want that.
- A skipped in-flight task still drops out of reconcile. The note makes that visible, but it doesn't change the behaviour.

author: dhilst
body:
The xnba loader cannot netboot a node over IPv6. The node reaches xNBA and stops at
"No configuration methods succeeded" without ever sending a DHCPv6 solicit, so its firmware
releases the address and gives up.

The cause is that the package ships a loader its own spec does not build. `binary/xnba.efi`
reports `xNBA 1.20.1+` while `xnba-undi.spec` builds 1.21.1, and 1.20.1 carries no
`NET_PROTO_IPV6` in `config/defaults/efi.h`. 1.21.1 does, so rebuilding the binary from the
source the spec already names is the whole fix.

Both loaders are rebuilt from `xnba-1.21.1.tar.bz2` with the six patches the spec applies. The
EFI loader grows from 155520 to 187904 bytes and gains IPv6. The BIOS loader grows from 66899
to 67789, which is the release difference and not the protocol: built with and without an
explicit `NET_PROTO_IPV6` override, `undionly.kkpxe` is byte identical at 67789, because
`config/defaults/efi.h` reaches only the EFI build.

Measured on an IPv6-only AlmaLinux 10.1 node with the DHCPv6 boot file pointed at `xnba.efi`.
The shipped loader logged only the firmware DUID and stopped. The rebuilt loader reports
`Configuring (net0 ...) ok` and `net0: 2001:db8:149::1002/64 gw fe80::4054:ff:fec9:95d3`, and
the DHCPv6 server logs a solicit from xNBA's own DUID beside the firmware's.

The branch carries a first attempt and its revert. That attempt added a
`config/local/general.h` override, which the byte identical builds above show does nothing

author: tokg-venv
body:
### What

Adds regression tests for how a MathType equation reaches the screen.

Word stores a MathType equation as an OLE embed (`ProgID="Equation.DSMT4"`) whose appearance comes from the metafile the package carries next to it (`v:imagedata` → `word/media/imageN.emf` or `.wmf`). The parse has to turn that metafile into a picture; if it does not, the equation has nothing to draw.

### Why

For #2316 ("MathType equations appear blank") I walked the equation paths in the current `main` and they all resolve — the metafile becomes a picture, the picture survives a save, and an equation without a preview degrades to a visible "Embedded object" label rather than an empty slot. Nothing in the code I could reach reproduces the report, so the suite now pins the paths down: a regression in any of them turns red instead of shipping a blank equation.

### Covered

- an EMF preview → the equation block carries a rendered picture and the size Word declares
- a WMF preview → the same
- an equation sharing its paragraph with text (the run-image path, the common shape for an inline formula) → the run carries the picture
- a save → the embed (`ProgID`, the `v:shape`, the `v:imagedata` relationship) and its preview survive

`packages/docx-engine/tests/helpers/fake-canvas.ts` stubs `OffscreenCanvas` / `ImageData` / `FileReader` so the vendored metafile converter can replay in Node, the same way `metafile-render.test.ts` already does.

### Tests

- `packages/docx-engine/tests/ole-embed-preview.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `npm run typecheck` (all packages) passes
- The docx-engine suite passes (1975 passed). `tests/deep-nested-table.test.ts` fails under the full parallel run on this machine and passes on its own; it fails the same way on `main` without this change.

### One question

Since the paths above work, #2316 must be something the test suite does not model. If the reporter can attach a de-identified `.docx` — only the affected paragraph(s), saved by the program that created the file, so the original equation XML is kept — I can turn it into a fixture and pin the real shape.

author: narasaka
body:
Encrypted dotenvx values (`HELLO="encrypted:BG8M…"`) need the crypto that dotenvx uses: ECIES over secp256k1, configured as in eciesjs and ecies-rs. This adds it, together with dotenvx's error codes. The next PR wires decryption into parsing and loading, with a keyring.

- **Dependency:** `github.com/decred/dcrd/dcrec/secp256k1/v4` v4.4.1, the module's first. Go's standard library has no secp256k1. decred is tagged, maintained and widely used (btcd, lnd), and adds one module to `go.mod`. Its field and scalar arithmetic is constant-time. Its scalar multiplication (`ScalarMultNonConst`, used for ECDH and for deriving public keys) is not. That matters little here, because decryption runs a few times at process start; exploiting it would need local timing of repeated decryptions with the same key.
- **Everything else is the standard library:** HKDF-SHA256 from `crypto/hkdf` (hence `go 1.24`), with no salt or info, over the uncompressed ephemeral public key followed by the uncompressed shared point. AES-256-GCM with eciesjs's 16-byte nonce, and `crypto/rand`.
- **Payload:** `encrypted:` + base64 of ephemeral public key (65 bytes) ‖ nonce (16) ‖ tag (16) ‖ ciphertext. That is what eciesjs produces, and Go's `Seal` output is rearranged to match.

API:
- `Decrypt(privateKey, value)`: values without the prefix pass through, as in dotenvx.
- `Encrypt(publicKey, value)`: takes a compressed or uncompressed public key.
- `PublicKey(privateKey)`: compressed, which is what `DOTENV_PUBLIC_KEY` holds.
- `GenerateKeypair()`.

Errors are `*Error` values in dotenvx's `[CODE] message` form, with an optional cause (`Unwrap`). `errors.Is` matches them by code against `ErrMissingPrivateKey`, `ErrInvalidPrivateKey`, `ErrWrongPrivateKey`, `ErrDecryptionFailed`, `ErrInvalidPublicKey` and `ErrEncryptionFailed`. Each call returns a fresh value, so changing a returned error can't change the sentinels.

The mapping is the one Node 4.3.0 actually produces, checked case by case with the oracle:
- **`WRONG_PRIVATE_KEY`:** a failed GCM tag check.
- **`DECRYPTION_FAILED`:** a payload that is empty, isn't base64, is too short, isn't a valid point, or is a hybrid point (`0x06`/`0x07`, which decred would accept but eciesjs rejects). dotenvx's decrypt has a `MALFORMED_ENCRYPTED_DATA` branch, but it matches an error message the bundled eciesjs never produces, so Node never returns that code, and neither does this.
- **`INVALID_PRIVATE_KEY`:** a private key that isn't 32 bytes of hex, or isn't a valid scalar (zero, or not below the curve order).
- **FIPS 140-only mode:** under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, Go refuses GCM with the scheme's 16-byte nonces. Decrypt and Encrypt then return `DECRYPTION_FAILED`/`ENCRYPTION_FAILED` wrapping that error, instead of panicking. `internal/fipstest` checks this with `//go:debug fips140=only`, which applies to a whole test binary and so needs a package of its own. `make test` now uses `-coverpkg=./...`, and the coverage gate already sums each block's counts across test binaries.

Base64 is read as Node's `Buffer` reads ASCII and Latin-1 text: both alphabets, other characters skipped, decoding stops at the first `=`, and a dangling final character is dropped. A differential fuzz of 200,000 random strings against `Buffer.from(s, "base64")` gave no mismatches. So a value like `"encrypted:… "`, with a stray space, decrypts as it does in dotenvx. One documented deviation: characters from U+0100 up are skipped, where Node reads each UTF-16 code unit by its low byte, so it takes `Ł` for `A`. Encrypt accepts a `0x` or `0X` prefix on the public key, as eciesjs does. Errors with a cause include it in their message, as Node's do.

Compatibility, checked both ways:
- `testdata/ecies/vectors.json` holds values that Node's `@dotenvx/primitives` 4.3.0 encrypted: the empty string, ASCII, multibyte text (including astral characters), 1000 bytes, and newlines. Go decrypts all of them, and also the dotenvx fixture `testdata/encrypted`.
- `testdata/ecies/go_vectors.json` holds values this port encrypted (`go run encrypt.go`), with both compressed and uncompressed public keys. `generate.js` checks that Node decrypts all of them, and it does (12 of 12). CI has no Node, so that check runs when the vectors are regenerated.

Deliberate differences from Node, documented on `Decrypt` and `PublicKey`:
- Private keys are parsed strictly as 64 hex digits. Node's `Buffer.from` reads hex up to the first character that isn't hex.
- Non-ASCII characters in the base64 are skipped. Node reads them by the low byte of their UTF-16 code units.
- Plaintext that isn't valid UTF-8 is returned as is, rather than with U+FFFD.

Examples cover `Decrypt` (including matching an error with `errors.Is`), `Encrypt`, `PublicKey` and `GenerateKeypair`.

`crypto/rand.Read` can't fail since Go 1.24, and the AES and HKDF constructors can't fail for these fixed sizes. Their errors are ignored, with a comment saying why. The GCM constructor's error is handled, as above.

author: chris0jeky
body:
## What changed

Reclaim rules v4 (follows the #1023 template): names-only recognisers for the Windows leftovers a nearly full `C:` points at first. Nothing executes; owner steps are display text.

- `crates/loomward-catalog/src/machine-stores-root.sql`: root-relative rules (direct children of the granted root). One materialised pass over the root's children feeds every arm, and the new arms use `CROSS JOIN` so the planner cannot scan the whole `dir` table. The root query now costs about 0.78M VM steps on a 30,000-child root, against 1.26M before.
- `crates/loomward-catalog/src/machine-stores.sql`: parent-chain rules for `AppData\Local` stores (wherever `AppData` sits under the grant) plus walk shields for every new root-level store. Walk cost rose about 9% per directory (361 to 392 VM steps, measured with Python's sqlite3 on a synthetic catalogue).
- `crates/loomward-catalog/src/machine_stores.rs`: `candidate()` metadata for the new rules; the report's `rules_version` is 4.
- `crates/loomward-engine/src/reclaim.rs`: `windows_leftover` maps to `GroupKind::ToolOwnedCleanup`; `RULES_VERSION` is 4. The usual verified-relief rule applies, so unobserved sizes stay unknown.
- `contracts/v3/examples/commands/reclaim.plan.result.json` (`rules_version: 4`), `docs/52-reclaim-planner.md` section 3, `crates/loomward-catalog/README.md`.

## Rules and owner steps

Class `windows_leftover` (provider `windows`), plans under Tool-owned cleanup, except `crash-dumps` and `driver-extract`, which have only manual owner steps: class `windows_manual_leftover`, planned under Archive candidates (review fix, docs/52 section 5):

| Rule | Names (parent chain) | Owner step |
|---|---|---|
| `windows-old` | `Windows.old`, `$WINDOWS.~BT`, `$WINDOWS.~WS` directly under the root | Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files ("Previous Windows installation(s)") or Disk Cleanup |
| `memory-dump` | `Windows\MEMORY.DMP` (file), `Windows\Minidump`, `Windows\LiveKernelReports` | Disk Cleanup, "System error memory dump files" |
| `error-reports` | `ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive` and `ReportQueue` | Disk Cleanup, "Windows Error Reports and Feedback Diagnostics" |
| `temp` | `Windows\Temp`; `AppData\Local\Temp` | Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files (Storage Sense) |
| `crash-dumps` | `AppData\Local\CrashDumps` | review by hand |
| `shader-cache` | `AppData\Local\D3DSCache`, `NVIDIA\DXCache`, `NVIDIA\GLCache`, `AMD\DxCache` | Disk Cleanup, "DirectX Shader Cache", or the vendor control panel |
| `driver-extract` | `AMD` or `NVIDIA` directly under the root with an installer payload | delete by hand after the driver is installed |
| `delivery-optimization` | `Windows\SoftwareDistribution\DeliveryOptimization`; `NetworkService\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization\Cache` | Disk Cleanup, "Delivery Optimization Files" |

Class `system_managed` (informational, never counted): `installer-cache` for `ProgramData\Package Cache` and `Windows\Installer`; the owner step says never to remove them by hand because they back repair and uninstall.

Decisions to check:
- **Volume root cannot be told from the SQL**, so `driver-extract` requires an installer payload instead: a direct `Setup.exe` file, a `Packages`, `Display.Driver` or `DisplayDriver` child directory, or a child directory holding `Setup.exe`. Pinned by `driver_extracts_need_an_installer_payload_directly_under_the_root` (empty `AMD`, `Docs`-only `NVIDIA`, payload two levels down, wrong vendor, `NVIDIA Corporation`, `Program Files\NVIDIA` are all not candidates; a stale vendor listing proves nothing).
- **Case.** New Windows names compare ASCII case-insensitively (`COLLATE NOCASE`). The v3 names (`Windows`, `WinSxS`, `$Recycle.Bin`) keep their exact comparison, unchanged.
- **Disk Cleanup labels** use Windows' own category names (for example "Windows Error Reports and Feedback Diagnostics"), not the shorter wording in the issue table.
- **Delivery Optimization** also sits inside the already-listed informational `SoftwareDistribution`. That parent is never counted as reclaimable, so there is no double count.
- The NetworkService Delivery Optimization rule requires the `NetworkService` and `AppData` names in the chain, not a longer `ServiceProfiles` prefix.
- Every recognised root-level store shields its subtree from the walk, so nothing inside `Windows.old`, `Windows\Temp` or a payload driver extract is reported twice.
- All new rules keep the shared safety filters (flags mask, reparse attribute 1024, `listing_state` and `listing_outcome` exclusions, same-run file observation).

## Tests run (Windows, own target dir `E:/loomward-build/target-rules-v4`)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p loomward-catalog -p loomward-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p loomward-catalog --test machine_stores`: 33 passed (27 existing, 6 new), including the unchanged budget tests
- `cargo test -p loomward-engine --test reclaim`: 20 passed (19 existing, 1 new)
- `cargo test -p loomward-catalog --lib`: 106 passed, 2 ignored
- Also run: `cargo test -p loomward-protocol` (13, 22, 10, 30, 3 passed, the contract example validates) and `cargo test -p loomward-service reclaim` (51 passed)
- `git diff --check`: clean
- Mutation checks: six deliberate SQL breakages (drop the `AppData` chain test, disable each walk shield, drop the payload test, drop the `SoftwareDistribution` name test, drop the `AppData` check on vendor caches) each fail at least one new test.

New tests: positives for every rule with class, provider, owner-step text, bounded text lengths and recorded sizes; ASCII case-insensitivity; about 45 wrong-place negatives (a `Temp` outside `AppData\Local`, `Windows.old` not directly under the root, nested `Windows`, files in place of directories, wrong vendor or cache child, wrong Delivery Optimization chain); driver payload positives and negatives; shielding of nested stores; the shared safety filters and unknown sizes staying null. Engine test: leftovers plan as Tool-owned cleanup with observed relief `Some` and unobserved relief `None`, installer caches stay informational.

## Not verified

- No real Windows tree was walked: only synthetic catalog rows. Real `Windows.old`, `WER` or driver-extract layouts, and the real cost of the walk on a multi-million-row catalogue, are unmeasured here. The walk is still bounded by the existing 2,000,000-step budget.
- Not run: `py -3 scripts/verify.py`, the Svelte app checks and the Tauri shell build (outside this change's seams).
- Two checks in my own mutation list (the walk shield for `WER` and the `Windows` child shield) were not mutated individually; the shield test covers them by construction.

Closes #1067

author: think-in-universe
body:
## Summary
The original main lockfile had 37 RustSec vulnerability findings, 14 unsoundness warnings, 5 unmaintained-crate warnings, and 2 yanked versions. The updated lockfile passes cargo-audit with warnings denied and the stricter cargo-deny policy from #416: **zero vulnerabilities, warnings, or yanked packages; no advisory ignores**.

- Use the latest published near-api and near-api-types **0.8.7 from crates.io**, without a Git pin or fork. Upgrade direct zstd to 0.14.3; both paths now use patched zstd-safe 8.2.0 and zstd-sys 2.1.2. Updating near-api also removes the old Hickory dependency path.
- Upgrade Swagger UI to 10.0.2 and Utoipa to 6, resolving ZIP to patched 9.1.3.
- Reuse cloud-api's client-only dstack-sdk 0.1.3 patch, removing unused Alloy and crypto-bigint dependencies. The two client source files are unchanged from the published SDK, with provenance and hashes in vendor/dstack-sdk/README.md. Include vendor/ in the Docker build. Remove the unused services-level dstack-sdk declaration.
- Remove unused rmcp and serde_yaml dependencies. Replace unmaintained rustls-pemfile with rustls-pki-types and cover custom CA bundle acceptance plus empty/malformed rejection.
- Upgrade compatible HTTP, TLS, Postgres, Tokio, and other affected transitive dependencies. Replace the yanked spin version; the near-api upgrade removes slipped10 entirely.
- Keep AWS SDKs on their current HTTPS client without enabling the redundant legacy Rustls 0.21 / Hyper 0.14 feature. The explicit AWS-LC client remains in use.

Compared against freshly fetched cloud-api main at 65679081. Security workflow enforcement and manual triggering are isolated in **#416**, stacked on this PR.

Staking view calls explicitly use one total RPC attempt so near-api 0.8.7's default retries do not bypass application reconciliation backoff. The existing 15-second timeout is retained; regression coverage checks HTTP 429/500/503 and failed/partial subscription probes.

## Risk & impact
Runtime changes affect TLS, HTTP, Postgres, async execution, NEAR RPC/authentication, and compression. Swagger/OpenAPI moves to a new major release. No schema migration; Rust remains pinned at 1.91.1. The dstack patch is limited to the clients already used by chat-api, and should be removed when upstream allows excluding the affected Ethereum tree.

## Testing
- Complete local `cargo test --features test --locked -- --test-threads=1`: 850 passed, 1 ignored. Serial execution avoids local shared-state interference observed in parallel completion tests.
- Complete subscription integration suite: 93 passed, including both failed/partial-probe backoff regressions. Staking RPC unit suite: 10 passed.
- Workspace all-target/all-feature compilation and strict Clippy (-D warnings) passed on Rust 1.91.1.
- Full workspace library/binary suite: **457 passed**, including database failover tests against isolated PostgreSQL.
- Additional custom CA regressions: 3 passed; all 7 pool tests passed.
- NEAR authentication and OAuth/Swagger/OpenAPI integration suites: **12 passed** against isolated PostgreSQL.
- cargo fmt --check and git diff --check passed; changed Rust code and manifests reviewed for readability.
- Vendored client SHA-256 hashes match the published 0.1.3 sources and cloud-api patch.
- cargo-audit 0.22.2 with --deny warnings passed against RustSec checkout 2295466c (2026-10-30), including registry/yanked checks.
- cargo-deny 0.20.2 with #416's strict policy and --locked --all-features passed advisories, bans, and sources.
- Production Docker build and live NEAR wallet login were not run locally. Required CI must pass before merge.

## Rollback plan
Revert this PR and rebuild the previous dependency graph.

## Review
- [ ] Reviewed by a non-author

## Deploy path
Merge through the existing main branch build/deploy pipeline; this PR does not deploy directly. Merge #416 afterward to enforce the clean security baseline.

author: lincicomb
body:
## Summary

Adds `uint64_t JS_GetProgramBranchCount(JSContext *ctx)` to count backward and conditional bytecode branch safepoints executed in `ctx`, independent of how many times a host suspends, snapshots, and restores the runtime.

## Why behind it

When a host coordinator meters or time-slices guest TypeScript/JavaScript executions across `JS_RequestSuspend()` -> `JS_WriteSnapshot()` -> `JS_ReadSnapshot()` -> `JS_Resume()`, it needs a deterministic work counter that answers: **how much actual guest program work ran in this slice?**

If the host counts invocations of `JSInterruptHandler` (`__js_poll_interrupts()`), two things skew the count whenever an execution is paused and resumed:
1. `ctx->interrupt_counter` is decremented not only at bytecode branch safepoints (`SAFEPOINT()`), but also on function-call entry and during job/suspension housekeeping.
2. When an execution is suspended, written to a snapshot, and restored in a fresh runtime, `ctx->interrupt_counter` resets to `JS_INTERRUPT_COUNTER_INIT` (`10000` by default) while the engine performs pause/resume checks of its own.

As a result, pausing and resuming an identical deterministic workload changes its total interrupt-poll count — charging the engine's pause/resume housekeeping against the guest program's work budget:

| Metric | Uninterrupted run (`plain`) | Suspended & resumed across 4 snapshot slices | Delta | Pause-invariant? |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| `JSInterruptHandler` poll counter (`JS_INTERRUPT_COUNTER_INIT=1`) | `15,317,723` | `15,318,011` | **`+288` extra polls** | **No** — pause/resume housekeeping inflates the count |
| **`JS_GetProgramBranchCount(ctx)`** | **`9,317,699`** | **`9,317,699`** (`2,329,425 + 2,329,425 + 2,329,425 + 2,329,424`) | **`0` drift** | **Yes** — exact match across 1 to `455,049` hibernations |

## Design (`16` lines across `quickjs.h` + `quickjs.c`)

- **Unconditional increment in `SAFEPOINT()`:** Because `SAFEPOINT()` is already the exact bytecode boundary where synchronous execution can suspend (backward and conditional branches in `JS_CallInternal`), incrementing `ctx->program_branch_count++` unconditionally inside `SAFEPOINT()` gives a zero-overhead, pause-invariant measure of guest program branches.
- **Process- and context-local (not serialized):** A fresh context (`JS_NewContext` / `JS_NewContextRaw`) and a context restored by `JS_ReadSnapshot()` both start at `0`. Summing `JS_GetProgramBranchCount(ctx)` across every process slice of a hibernated execution equals the count of an uninterrupted run on the same input.
- **Orthogonal to interrupt polling:** `ctx->interrupt_counter` and `JS_SetInterruptHandler()` behavior are completely unchanged.

## Verification

- `make -j8 CONFIG_WERROR=y && make test`: `test_program_branch_count` in `tests/test_api.c` verifies initial zero state, per-context isolation (`ctx` vs `ctx2`), `JS_NewContextRaw` zero initialization, and in-process `JS_RequestSuspend()` / `JS_Resume()` branch-count invariance.
- `make test-snapshot && make -C tests/snapshot stress`: `tests/snapshot/test_hibernate.c` verifies `plain.branches == st.branches` (uninterrupted run vs. sum across all hibernated slices) across all 19 snapshot test scripts in both full and `-d` delta mode, including `js/hibernate-sync.js` across **`455,049` hibernations** (`705,662` interrupts) under `-DJS_INTERRUPT_COUNTER_INIT=97`.
- `cargo check --manifest-path rquickjs/sys/Cargo.toml --features update-bindings`: all 18 target bindings updated and verified.

([#​13068](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13068), [#​14056](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14056), [#​13926](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13926), [#​13120](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13120), [#​14046](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14046), [#​13825](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13825), [#​14092](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14092))
- **Server data and search:** MudAutocomplete, MudTable and MudDataGrid now keep the results of the newest search or load. Before, they kept whichever finished last. An autocomplete stays closed after you close it, select or clear while a search is running. A grid or table that lands past the last page goes back to the first page and keeps its loading bar until the data arrives. Popovers removed before their first render no longer leak in Interactive Server, so grouped grids with a pager stop collecting orphaned tooltips. ([#​13944](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13944), [#​14053](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14053), [#​14069](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14069), [#​14070](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14070), [#​14064](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14064), [#​14065](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14065), [#​14068](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14068), [#​13949](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13949), [#​14057](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14057), [#​14063](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14063), [#​14049](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14049), [#​14050](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14050))
- **Date range picker:**

  - `MinDays` and `MaxDays` now apply on both sides of the first clicked date.
  - Hovering an earlier date previews the range.
  - Changing the limits before the second click takes effect right away.
  - Opening an editable picker no longer marks a valid range invalid.
  - `ResetAsync` returns the calendar to its starting month.

  ([#​14052](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14052), [#​14054](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14054), [#​14058](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14058), [#​14059](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14059), [#​13945](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13945), [#​13936](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13936))

#### Upgrading

- **The "is any of" operator appears on every enum column.** Its `Value` is a collection of enum values. If your `ServerData` code doesn't handle that operator yet, hide it with `Column.FilterOperators`. ([#​14056](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14056))
- **More parameters raise MUD0012 when read through a component reference.** This now applies to `Title` and `SecondaryText` on MudStep, and to `MinDays`, `MaxDays`, `MinDate` and `MaxDate` on the date pickers. If you treat warnings as errors, read the step values through `IStepContext` (for example `MudStepper.Steps`), or keep the values in your own fields. Setting these parameters in markup is unchanged. ([#​13939](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/13939), [#​14058](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14058))
- **Date range pickers with `MinDays` set allow earlier dates.** A date before the first click can become the range start when the span is within `MinDays` and `MaxDays`. A `MinDays` of 0 or less now behaves like 1. ([#​14054](https://redirect.github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/pull/14054))
