author: juanfrank
body:
## Summary

Extends the bi-report-spec skill and adds tooling for Power BI semantic models (`Model.bim`).

- **Bookmark scenarios.** `extract_report` reads each page's bookmarks. `annotate_captures` treats the saved state and each bookmark as a scenario, declared per capture with `--scenario`. Numbering is stable across captures, and the markdown gains a section 4 (scenarios, shows/hides vs. the saved state, covered badges).
- **Overlap checks.** Badges covered by a higher-z visual are reported per scenario, and a `- contornos.png` outline image is written for visual comparison.
- **Hidden visuals.** Visibility resolves up the whole parent-group chain; absolute positions sum the full chain.
- **Redaction by default.** `scripts/redact.py` redacts hosts, IPs, credentials and connection strings in every JSON and markdown output, and in copied source text files. `--raw` opts out for local use. `Model.bim` is no longer copied into the repo.
- **Model origins.** Appendix C lists, per table, the source database, schema and table/view. Query text (M or SQL) is not published; it is kept only with `--raw`.
- **Relationship appendix.** Narrowed to relations between page tables, or activated by a page measure (`USERELATIONSHIP`/`CROSSFILTER`, matched on both table and column).
- **Measure hygiene.** DAX comments (`//`, `--`, `/* */`) are removed from measures and calculated columns; string, table-name and column-name contents are preserved. Block comments nest.
- **`scripts/bim_core.py`, `scripts/bim_search.py`.** Read a `.bim` and search it through a cached SQLite FTS5 index (cache lives outside the repo).
- **`scripts/dax_check.py`.** Local structural validator for DAX, plus a check that comment cleaning does not change live tokens. Runs over all 516 measures/calculated columns in Model4 with 0 problems.

## Examples

`processed/SGC_Civil/` is regenerated with the current code (two captures, scenarios, and the SGC `Model4.bim` appendices). `processed/SJO-Notificaciones/` is unchanged.

## Notes for review

- Commit `e77876d` briefly put two internal server IPs into test fixtures. Later commits (`e8dd597`, `ae2b4b7`) replace them with RFC 5737 documentation addresses. History was not rewritten, so the original addresses remain in that commit.
- Two measures (`Juez Estado Fallo`, `Juez En Mora Prueba`) comment a block that contains its own `/* */` comments. Cleaning treats block comments as nested, which matches the visible intent. If Power BI does not accept nested block comments, those two measures already fail in the original text. Worth checking in Power BI Desktop.
- Captures (images) are not redacted; review them before committing.

## Tests

Unit tests (stdlib `unittest`, run from the repo root):

```
python -m unittest scripts/test_redact.py scripts/test_bim_core.py scripts/test_build_markdown.py scripts/test_dax_check.py
```

author: exponential-agent[bot]
body:
This is step 1 of the end-to-end design (#EXP-1457). It adds the server-only registry where every install records its eNet identity: desktop, CLI daemon, iOS, Android and web browser. The contract is on #VAPP-37.

- **Table:** `installs` (migration `0218_exp1457_installs`), with no Electric shape. It stores the user, kind, an optional `devices` row, label, platform, `endpoint_id` (unique hex ed25519), `x25519_public` and `last_seen_at` / `revoked_at`.
- **`installs.register`:**
  - The request is signed with the install's ed25519 identity over `exp-install-v1\n<userId>\n<endpointId>\n<x25519Public>\n<signedAt>`; `signedAt` may be at most ±10 minutes off.
  - It is an idempotent upsert behind a per-user advisory lock.
  - It answers CONFLICT when another user owns the endpoint and FORBIDDEN when the endpoint is revoked.
  - A user can have at most 50 installs that aren't revoked.
- **`installs.list {teamId}`:** the installs of the team's members, team-scoped through `resolveTeamAccess`. It is the eNet access allowlist.
- **`installs.mine`** returns the caller's own installs, and **`installs.revoke`** revokes one of them.

**Tests:** 12 router tests with real ed25519 keys plus the migration journal tests pass, and `tsc` is clean. The child sessions building the desktop/daemon, iOS, Android and web nodes code against this contract.

body:
## Issue / Fase

Closes #450

F3-52 · Fase 3 — Mantenimiento de seguridad: `pg_temp` al final del `search_path` de las funciones SQL. Hallado en la revisión independiente de #449.

## Objetivo

Cerrar, por defensa en profundidad, el sombreado por tabla temporal: PostgreSQL busca `pg_temp` primero para relaciones y tipos si el `search_path` de la función no lo nombra, y `crm_app` puede crear tablas temporales.

## Cambios

- **Auditoría de todas las funciones SQL del repositorio** (cuerpo leído una por una): ninguna era explotable por `pg_temp`, porque cada relación que leen ya va cualificada con `public.` y las funciones y operadores no se resuelven por `pg_temp`.
- **Tres migraciones** (`core/0004`, `audit/0005`, `pricing/0005`) con `ALTER FUNCTION ... SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp` para `outbox_pending_organizations` (SECURITY DEFINER), `audit_ensure_partitions`, `platform_audit_ensure_partitions` y `product_prices_immutable`. `ALTER` y no `CREATE OR REPLACE`: solo cambia el ajuste, no el cuerpo, el propietario ni los permisos; la inversa restaura el valor anterior. Las funciones de promociones ya lo tenían desde #449.
- **`app_current_tenant` y `app_current_user` no se tocan**: un `SET` impediría que se expandan dentro de las políticas RLS y `crm_app` controla esos ajustes en su propia sesión, así que no son un límite.
- **Decisión sobre `REVOKE TEMPORARY`**: no se aplica ahora. Rompería los tests que crean tablas temporales como `crm_app` a propósito y quitaría la posibilidad de probar el ataque; queda como endurecimiento posterior junto con mover esos tests al rol migrador.

## No incluye

- Cambios de comportamiento de las funciones; `REVOKE TEMPORARY`.

## Cómo se verificó

- `make check` en el árbol exacto del HEAD: exit 0 (`git write-tree` igual antes y después). Backend: 1640 tests. Frontend: 864 tests, lint, tipos, build. Auditorías y gitleaks limpios.
- `tests/test_pg_temp_shadowing.py`: la configuración (`proconfig`) de las siete funciones; una tabla temporal `outbox_events` como `crm_app` no cambia el resultado; tablas temporales que sombrean el padre de las particiones no desvían las funciones de partición. Solo el test de configuración falla antes del cambio (los de comportamiento pasan antes y después porque las funciones ya cualificaban).

## Definition of Done

- [x] Tenant context respetado (`organization_id` desde el contexto; nada del payload)
- [x] RLS en tablas tenant-owned nuevas (una política PERMISSIVE por comando) — sin tablas nuevas; triggers y permisos de columna nuevos

- [x] Slice de producción (AGENTS.md §11): servicio oficial; nada en `/demo`

## 概要

イシュー #37 の整合性レビュー4件と、同日の資料・実装チェックで見つかった資料側の矛盾をまとめて修正しました。`origin/main`（fa4c2c0）から分岐し、修正1コミットと操作履歴2コミットに分けています。

## イシュー #37 の4件

- **[P2] 匿名モードでサンプルの案件保存が有効なまま** — Commonへ `CommonOptions.HasIdentifiedUser`（単独開発でも匿名モードでもない）を追加し、サンプルの保存・案件一覧を画面とサーバーの双方で拒否します。`ToolController` の保存分岐、`RecordsController.OnActionExecuting` での404、保存ラジオボタンと一覧リンクの無効化が対象です。固定共通ユーザーを本人向けデータの所有者にしない契約は設計書10・12と機能追加ガイドへ明記しました。
- **[P2] 問い合わせIDの採番がテスト用業務日付に影響される** — `InquiryService` の依存を `IBusinessDateProvider` から `IApplicationClock` へ変更し、実UTC時刻から求めたJST日付で採番します。
- **[P2] 共通エラー画面が例外処理の応答に使われない** — `CommonErrorResponse` を追加し、`/api` はProblemDetails、それ以外のHTML要求は `CommonError` View を描画します。描画に失敗した場合はProblemDetailsへ退避します。障害時にDBを再参照しないよう、エラー画面では共通メニューを表示しません。
- **[P3] 入口資料に匿名・HTTP運用の例外が反映されていない** — 要件定義へ段階リリース第1段の匿名モードを例外として追記し、PortalのREADMEの設定表へ `Site:AuthenticationMode` / `Site:TransportMode` を追加、`Portal:BaseUrl` を通信方式に合わせる記述へ、SMTPの行へ匿名モードでの無効化を補いました。

## 資料の矛盾の修正

- 設計書03：通信方式の節から「ツールの起動URLのスキーム」を削除（同一サイト内パスのため切替で変更しない）、`access-implementation` アンカー直後にあった01・02からの複製10行を参照1行へ置換、外部設定の一覧へサイト名・認証モード・通信方式を追加。
- 設計書02：通知許可4行の重複を7節への参照へ統合、問い合わせメール件名の「システム名」を「サイト名」＋設定キーへ、一覧のWeb起動も別タブと明記、バージョン列幅の記述を正しい節へ移動。
- 設計書11：経路表へ `POST /admin/tools/{toolId}/content/url`、構成図へ `Mail/`。
- AGENTS.md へ13を追加、SKILL.md のSQL READMEのパス修正と10〜13の追加、config/README へ匿名モードで本人向けデータを扱えない旨。
- 実装：ツール一覧のWeb起動リンクを詳細画面と同じ別タブ指定へ、サンプルの `/records` から `WebOpenLoggingFilter` を外して `WEB_OPEN` を入口1件に戻しました。

## 検証

- 4ソリューションとも `dotnet build` が警告0・エラー0（.NET SDK 10.0.401）。
- `dotnet test --no-build`：Common 172件 / Portal 119件 / テンプレート 25件 / サンプル 27件、失敗0・スキップ0（330→343件、13件追加）。
- Markdownの相対リンクと見出しアンカーを全27ファイルで確認し、未到達なし。

- 共通エラー画面の描画は、テンプレートの `ToolPipelineTests` で実際の `Program.cs` を起動し、`text/html`・問い合わせ番号あり・例外名なしで返ることを確認しています。
- 実DB・実SMTP・IIS配置・共有Cookieの複数アプリ往復は未検証です。匿名モードで `/records` が404になること、一覧のWeb起動が別タブで開くことはブラウザーで未確認です。
- 資料が前提にする運用用の「所定SQL」（新規ツール登録、サイト公開状態の変更、FAQ・CodeMaster更新、アップロードポリシー変更、ログの定期削除、ツール固有ErrorCodeの登録）は今回も未作成で、残件です。
- イシュー #37 のチェックリスト4件はすべて対応済みですが、イシューのクローズと返信は行っていません。

author: lhjnilsson-bot
body:
Stacked on lhjnilsson/foreverbull#233 (`fix/marketdata-sync-lock-ctx` @ 2d7bbce), which sits on lhjnilsson/foreverbull#230 and lhjnilsson/foreverbull#231. Merge order: lhjnilsson/foreverbull#231, lhjnilsson/foreverbull#230, lhjnilsson/foreverbull#233, then this. It doesn't depend on lhjnilsson/foreverbull#234. The base stays `main` because those branches live on the lhjnilsson-bot fork. Review only the commits after 2d7bbce.

Provider rate limit and task time limit for large downloads (lhjnilsson/foreverbull-internal#115).

## Changes

**Shared per-provider rate limit.** Every Yahoo, Stooq and Alpaca request waits for a slot from one limiter per provider. The limiter is shared across the whole broker process, so it covers every concurrent `DownloadHistoricalData` and ingest, and every client instance, since Stooq and Alpaca clients are built per request.
- The limiter is `golang.org/x/time/rate` with a burst of 1, plus a shared `pausedUntil`. This is a server-side Go dependency. Client runtime deps are untouched.
- Rates: Yahoo 5 requests/s, Stooq 2/s, Alpaca 3/s. Alpaca's free market-data plan allows 200 a minute. At these rates a 10,000-symbol download takes about an hour on Yahoo or Alpaca and about 85 minutes on Stooq.
- The ISIN lookup on markets.businessinsider.com doesn't count against Yahoo's budget.
- A 429 pauses the provider for every caller, including callers already waiting for a slot. When a caller's timer fires it checks the pause again, waits it out, and takes a new slot.
- The pause is `Retry-After` when that is 1–30 s, otherwise 2 s doubling up to 30 s. The seconds are checked before they become a duration, so `Retry-After: 18446744074` can't overflow into a short wait. Yahoo and Stooq resend the request up to 3 times. Alpaca's SDK already retries 429s itself, so its transport only pauses the shared limiter.
- A cancelled or timed-out wait gives its slot back (`Reserve` + `Cancel`).
- A wait whose slot, or the end of a pause, comes after the ctx deadline is refused at once with `WaitRefusedError`, which is a `DeadlineExceeded`. That error text is only logged and never reaches users (see Copy).
- The wait uses the request ctx, so the HTTP client timeout (30 s on Yahoo and Stooq) and Alpaca's 60 s fetch budget still bound a fetch made under the symbol lock. Both stay below the 90 s idle-in-transaction timeout.
- Yahoo `GetIndex` runs at most 4 asset lookups at a time (`errgroup.SetLimit`). It used to start one goroutine per component and append results without synchronisation. It now also refuses an empty index result instead of panicking.

**Task time limit.**
- `FINANCE_TASK_TIME_LIMIT` (Go duration, default `2h`) bounds one `DownloadHistoricalData` and one finance ingest. It replaces the `downloadTimeLimit`/`ingestTimeLimit` package vars. The broker refuses to start when the value isn't a duration or isn't above zero, and the error names the variable. It's documented with the broker env in `deploy/README.md`.
- Symbols stored before the limit stay stored. A symbol still in flight rolls back. If that symbol is mid split-refetch, the old-scale rows stay as they were.
- The RPC ends with `DeadlineExceeded` and `the download hit its time limit of 2h0m0s at SYM`, naming the first symbol it hadn't answered for. This text is separate from the provider-timeout sentence. A ctx cause separates the limit from the client's own deadline or cancel.
- These also get the limit copy rather than the provider-timeout copy:
  - a symbol waiting on its DB lock when the limit fires;
  - a provider wait refused because its slot comes at or after the limit (`marketdata.AtTaskLimit`).
- A refusal under a shorter deadline, such as the HTTP client's, is a provider timeout.
- A provider call that times out while there's still time left fails that symbol with `<provider> took too long to respond for SYM` (`STATUS_ERROR` on the RPC) instead of the generic download failure. This covers:
  - an HTTP timeout;
  - Alpaca's fetch budget;
  - a refetch in `Sync`, including one under the lock.
- A database error is never read as a provider timeout.

**Copy.** The provider name goes through the `ShownProvider` allowlist. The limit is named with `numfmt.LimitSpan`. Whole hours read in hours ("2-hour", "1-hour"). Anything else reads in whole minutes ("90-minute", never "1h30m"). A limit that isn't a whole number of minutes rounds up, with a minimum of 1, so `30s` reads "1-minute" and `90m30s` reads "91-minute".

| Where | Cause | Text |
|---|---|---|
| create | provider timeout for a symbol | `Couldn't load data for backtest 'oef-2024q1': alpaca took too long to respond for AAPL. The backtest wasn't saved. Try again later, or use another provider with --provider.` |
| create | time limit | ``Couldn't load data for backtest 'oef-2024q1': the download hit the 2-hour limit after 6,212 of 10,000 symbols. The backtest wasn't saved. Split the symbols across several backtests, then run `fbull backtest create` again.`` The counts are symbols done of the total, counted and formatted like the progress line (`numfmt.Thousands`). |
| ingest | provider timeout | `<provider> took too long to respond for SYM, so the price import stopped. Prices imported before SYM were kept. Try again later.` Ingest has no `--provider` flag, so there's no clause for it. |
| ingest | time limit | `The price import hit the 2-hour limit at SYM. Prices imported before SYM were kept. Import fewer symbols at a time, or try again later.` |

Create shows the provider-timeout text only when it has that exact shape and names the response's own symbol. It shows the limit text only on `DeadlineExceeded` with the exact limit text and a positive limit. The client's own deadline keeps the generic sentence. A raw `rate: Wait(n=1) would exceed context deadline` is never read as the limit. Finance never sends it anyway, because the limiter reserves and never calls `Wait`. If the backtest can't be removed, both create texts end with the usual `fbull backtest delete` step instead.

**Progress in place.** No proto changes.
- `internal/stream` gains `ReportProgress(ctx, text)`. The subscriber publishes the text on core NATS subject `foreverbull-progress.<module>.<component>.<method>.<id>`. That subject is outside `foreverbull.>`, so progress isn't stored on the unlimited `foreverbull` JetStream stream and gets no `message_states` row.
- Core NATS fits the CLI path because the CLI only sees progress through the broker's `RunOrchestration` stream, which follows the task live. A dedicated `foreverbull-progress` stream isn't needed, and the shared stream's config is unchanged.
- If a waiter's progress buffer (64) fills, NATS drops the new texts for that waiter and flags it as a slow consumer. The next report has the current count again.
- `WaitForCompletion` subscribes before the task is published. Before it returns the final state it flushes and drains any pending progress, so reports arrive in order ahead of the completed step. `RunOrchestration` emits each one as a RUNNING step with the text as its message.
- `UpdateOrchestration` now replaces the step message on every update, so a progress text never stays on a completed step.
- Backtest `DownloadFinancialData` reports `Downloading prices: 1,240 of 10,000 symbols`, starting at 0, at most every 2 s.
- `fbull backtest create` shows that text in place of the Downloading row and puts the label back when the step ends.
- Not in this PR: a "(yahoo is limiting requests, waiting 30 s)" suffix on the progress line. It would need the limiter's wait to reach the backtest service, which only sees the finance gRPC stream. That's a follow-up.

## Test-only fix for a flake in #233's tests

`waitForLockWaiters` (repository tests from #233) counted advisory lock waiters across the whole Postgres server. The test container is shared by every package, each in its own database, so a waiter from another package (including this PR's lock-at-the-limit tests) could satisfy the wait early. That m

author: lalalune
body:
Notes-only PR for lane `w12b01-hop-gep` (target 0x5b3b0 `multi_hop_curve::swap_hop`, pinned 18,584 B). It changes no program source.

swap_hop is already a normalized and raw match on main via #2766 (w12b09, `(allowed, global)` tuple spelling). This lane reached the same binary in parallel with two helper spellings. It records the mechanism, the oracles and a more ordinary alternative spelling.

## Metrics

| build | bytes | ratio | slots | normalized / raw | losses | candidate sha |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| main 20a1ae9c0 (before) | 18,584 | 0.99913 | 18 | 1033 / 1033 | - | 4eb9dc9e542e9b9a |
| `v3cc` on 20a1ae9c0 | 18,584 | 1.0 | 0 | 1034 / 1034 | none | cbd9bf08d09967f7 |
| `wlok` on 20a1ae9c0 | 18,584 | 1.0 | 0 | 1034 / 1034 | none | cbd9bf08d09967f7 |
| `v3cc` in place of the tuple on main 70f27048e | 18,584 | 1.0 | 0 | 1034 / 1034 | none, no gains | cc795ce731592a48 (= main) |

- `v3cc`: line 599 `let allowed = crate::trade::v3_can_cross(&a.global,c,&a.user.key());` plus `pub(crate)` on trade_v3's existing `v3_can_cross`.
- `wlok`: a plain module-level `fn whitelist_ok(global:&Global,user:Pubkey,curve:&BondingCurve)->bool`.

On current main, `v3cc` is binary-identical to the tuple spelling. A steward can apply `edits/v3cc_on_tuple.py` with `land.py --allow-neutral` if they prefer it. It reuses the helper that trade_v3's buy already calls for the same can-cross check.

## Mechanism

1. **llc.** MachineSink moves an ADD defined in bb57 (over-reserves block) or bb58 (memcmp block) to the top of the complete_fill block. That matches the original's `ldxdw r2,[r10-0xb28]; add64 r2,8` at +0x29f8. Post-opt oracle: 1.0 / 0 slots.
2. **opt.** InstCombine sinks a single-use instruction only into a user block whose unique predecessor is the def block. In rustc's pre-opt IR, the call block's only predecessor is already bb58. So a bb58 GEP is sunk, giving 18 slots, while a bb57 GEP survives, giving 0 slots. Pre-opt oracle: `opt -O3` + llc.
3. **MIR.** `complete_fill(global, ..)` gets a coercion reborrow `&*global`. ReferencePropagation rewrites it into a fresh `&((*box_ptr).0)` in the call block, which is why hoisted `&Global` bindings are byte-identical.
4. **What works.** A plain, non-`#[inline]` helper whose optimized MIR still contains a call (the `raw_eq` of the Pubkey compare) is not cross-crate-inlinable, so the MIR inliner skips it. Its `&a.global` argument is materialized in bb57, LLVM inlines the helper, and EarlyCSE folds the call-site GEP into the bb57 one.

Tools in `reconstruction/pump-main/lanes/w12b01-hop-gep/tools`:
- `capir.py`: IR/MIR capture build.
- `orc.py`: llc oracle, with `--opt` for pre-opt modules.
- `gepwhere.py`: where complete_fill's `&Global` argument is defined.
- `trial.sh`

Ledger keys are in NOTES.md and SUMMARY.json.

## Problem

The `.proto` files are the API's reference documentation, but `buf lint` only checks their style. Most messages and fields have no comment, so a reader has to guess what they mean.

## Change

`buf lint` now also runs buf's `COMMENTS` rules, so every service, method, message, field and enum needs a comment. This adds the ten that were missing and regenerates `gen/`, which carries the comments into the Go code.

## Not done or not tested

- Nothing.

## Docs

`docs/content/development.md` says that the `.proto` files are the API's reference and need a comment on every part.

body:
## RT-984 — production compose drops API env settings

Jira: [RT-984](https://rahmaqanater.atlassian.net/browse/RT-984) (W7, Implementation, production configuration; owner-approved scope 2026-10-30). Follows RT-983 / #148.

`services/backend-core/docker-compose.prod.yml` lists the `api` environment explicitly with no `env_file`, so any setting missing from that list never reaches `dp2-api` from `backend.env`. RT-983 fixed this for the tender gates only. This PR passes the rest through and adds a guard so the bug class cannot return.

### Changes
- **Compose `api.environment`** — 21 settings:
  - gates, default `false`: `POS_RETURNS_ENABLED`, `POS_REFUND_SETTLE_BEFORE_POST_ENABLED`, `POS_LEGACY_REFUND_ENABLED`, `DEVICE_TOKEN_EXPIRY_ENFORCED`, `AI_GATEWAY_ENABLED`;
  - default empty: `OUTBOX_AUDIT_ENABLED` (**not** `false`: unset means ON in production, RT-124), `TRUST_PROXY_REQUIRED` (inert while `TRUST_PROXY` is fixed);
  - tuning, default empty so the code default applies: AI reservation TTL, public-auth limiter, console and pre-auth rate limits, cashier admission/takeover.
- **Deliberately unmapped**, each with its reason in the spec:
  - `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`: `caddy-same-origin.spec.ts` (RT-336) requires it absent, which keeps CORS off. This is a deviation from the approved scope, recorded on RT-984.
  - `ERPNEXT_FEED_RESPONSIBILITIES_ENABLED`: until the RT-419 hold lift.
  - `VERIFY_DATABASE_POOL_BOUNDARY`: test-only.
- **`deploy/prod.env.example`** documents each setting with its default and range.
- **New `apps/api/test/deploy/compose-api-env.spec.ts`:**
  - collects every env name read in `apps/api/src` (literal keys, `isEnvFlagOn("X")`, `name: "X"`, `*_ENV = "X"`);
  - fails on an unmapped or unexcluded name, on a mapping that does not pass the host variable of the same name, or on an env read it cannot resolve (indirect key, `env.X` on a parameter, destructuring);
  - runs every `''`/`false` default through the real parser and checks the result equals the variable being unset.
- **`changelog.d/RT-984-fixed.md`.**

Behaviour is unchanged until an environment sets one of these.

### Test plan
- [x] `compose-api-env.spec.ts`: 31/31 pass locally.
- [x] Mutation checks: removing a mapping, setting `OUTBOX_AUDIT_ENABLED:-false`, and misspelling a passthrough each fail the spec.
- [x] Other deploy, tooling and compose-health specs green locally, including `caddy-same-origin`. `redis-restart.spec.ts` needs Docker (not available locally; runs in db-integration).
- [x] `tsc` (build + typecheck) and `eslint` clean; `node tools/changelog/assemble.cjs` OK.
- [x] `pr-review` in a fresh subagent: 0 Critical, 0 Major. Both Minor findings and the trivial ones are fixed.
- [ ] Required CI green.

### Before deploying
The live `deploy/prod.env` may already hold some of these names. Until now they had no effect; after this ships they will. Check it for a stale `OUTBOX_AUDIT_ENABLED=false`/`0`, which would turn the production audit outbox off, and for `DEVICE_TOKEN_EXPIRY_ENFORCED`.

### Not covered
`DP2_OTEL_DISABLED` / `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` are read in `@data-pulse-2/shared`, not in `apps/api/src`, and are still not passed through. They need a separate decision.

author: alexis-marcel
body:
After an update was asked from one card, the other cards (their "→ version" and button, waiting for eriphe-core first) and "Update all" stayed as they were until a reload.

- The answer to a request, and the poll answer that sees a followed request end, carry an `updates-changed` event (HX-Trigger).
- Every part of the updates that follows no request of its own (each device card's foot, eriphe-core's row, and "Update all", now its own fragment at `GET /settings/updates/all`) asks again on that event. Cards that are following a request keep their own polling, so their outcome stays shown.
- eriphe-core's own update ending used to reload the whole grid; the event does it now, card by card, with "Update all" too.

Tests: the event on request and on done (not on a plain re-ask), the followers in the page, and a two-node run where eriphe-core's update frees the nodes' buttons and one card's request removes "Update all".

author: k2b-cloud-agents[bot]
body:
## Outcome

Reactive extensions added with `editor.use(() => …)` no longer dispatch in the middle of a CodeMirror update. A factory may read signals that change while the editor updates, such as a document store written by the Yjs binding, without crashing a plugin.

## Root cause

`use()` dispatched each new factory value synchronously from a Solid effect. In the k2b notes SPA the note's store is rewritten synchronously in the chain CodeMirror update → yCollab → Y.Doc → store, so the effect ran inside the update. CodeMirror refused the dispatch ("Calls to EditorView.update are not allowed while an update is in progress") and switched off the plugin that triggered it, the Yjs sync. Further typing no longer reached the shared text until the next reconnect: silent data loss in a shared note. Reported by the notes SPA lane, which removed its trigger in #2151.

## Change

- `packages/editor/src/editor-state.ts`: a slot stores its new value at once; all pending slots reach the view in one dispatch one microtask later, after the update finished. Late-added places (`appendConfig`) and removals use the same path. Values that change before the view exists reach it after `attach`.
- Docs: `frontend/editor` says changes reach the view one microtask later.

## How do we prevent this next time?

- Test: `building-blocks.behavior.test.tsx` › "a factory that reads a signal written during an editor update leaves the writing plugin running" (a view plugin writes a signal a factory reads; no crash, the plugin keeps seeing updates, the facet has the latest value). It fails without the fix.
- Lesson: `2026-10-30-editor-use-dispatched-during-update.md`.

## Verification

- `packages/editor` and `packages/notebooks` typechecks
- Package `building-blocks` (10)
- Notebooks, whose `NoteEditor` uses `use()` for all reactive extensions: `sync-ended` (61), `EditorToolbar` (10), `NoteEditor` (4), `tab-key-preference` (3), `linked-heading` (5), `lib/yjs/history` (14), `shared-editor` (3), `shared-text-editor.browser.test.ts` (49, Chromium; an earlier run at VM load 27 timed out on page loads, passed at normal load)
- Rules `biome`, `help-writing`, `boundaries`, `test-clock`; docs `check:docs`; `git diff --check`

author: abb65
body:
Every seed entry in `.contentrain/meta/` was `status: "draft"`: 10 entries in 8 meta files.

Why it matters:
- Studio's CDN delivery serves published entries only.
- An `@contentrain/query` build with `publishedOnly`/`requireStatus` drops drafts.
- So a project started from this template got empty pages on those paths, and Studio listed every entry as a draft.

**Changes**
- `.contentrain/meta/**/*.json`: `"status": "draft"` → `"status": "published"`, 10 lines.

**Kept as is**
- `source` and `updated_by`.
- Key order, 2-space indent and trailing newline: the edit is a plain text replacement of that one value, with no JSON re-serialisation.
- `.contentrain/config.json` (incl. `workflow: review`), the models and the content.
- No Contentrain CLI or MCP write was used.

**Supersedes / removes:** nothing.

**Verification** (clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, Node 22.17, pnpm 10.17.0)
| | after |
|---|---|
| `git diff` | 8 files, 10 lines; every changed line is the `status` value |
| `contentrain validate` (repo CLI) | 0 errors, 2 warnings (the existing `footer`/`navigation` title_field notes, unchanged by this PR) |
| `npx contentrain@0.18.12 validate` (Studio's reader) | 0 errors, 2 warnings (the existing `footer`/`navigation` title_field notes, unchanged by this PR) |
| Build output, before vs after | `build/` differs only by build noise: SvelteKit's `version.json` timestamp, the `__sveltekit_*` global and the chunk hashes that follow from them. The visible text and image sources of all 4 HTML pages are identical. |

The default build doesn't filter on status, so the site is unchanged. The change is visible in Studio and in published-only builds.

author: xingkaixin
body:
## Why

RD-984 (milestone v0.17.0). `packages/reader-ui` renders the reader shell for every source and still kept local UI state in `useState`. It also used effects for timers, keyboard shortcuts, measurement, and a copy request counter. `docs/renderer-state.md` moves these to reducers, ref callbacks, and the allowlisted primitives. This PR finishes the package and removes it from the lint exemption list.

Stacked on #994.

## What Changed

* Annotation cards, the comment composer, the floating composer, and avatar stacks use event-named reducers and measure through ref callbacks.
* The annotation rail ends its exit animation with `useInterval` on a fixed 190ms period instead of an effect-driven timer.
* The reader shell state, toolbar, TOC panel, chat panel, composer, and surface view use reducers and ref callbacks.
  * Keyboard shortcuts attach through `useEventListener`; a `null` target turns them off while the shell is not interactive.
  * Viewport size is read through `useSyncExternalStore`.
  * Unmount cleanup for pending frames goes through `useMountEffect`.
* The selection menu exposes copy through a `SelectionMenuHandle` ref instead of a `copyRequestKey` counter prop. The handle is internal to reader-ui.

## Impact

* [x] Reader
* [x] Annotation
* [x] AI Chat
* [ ] Memory
* [ ] Sync
* [x] Search
* [ ] Settings
* [ ] API
* [x] Infrastructure

## Notes for Reviewer

* Behavior changes:
  * The rail exit animation ends on the fixed 190ms interval tick rather than a timeout started in an effect.

author: jon890
body:
## 변경점

`nhncloud volume` 에 조회와 생성만 있어, 쓰지 않는 볼륨을 지우려면 콘솔에서 연결 해제와 삭제를 해야 했다. 같은 일을 CLI 로 할 수 있게 세 명령을 더한다.

- `volume attach <volume-id> --server <server-id>`: Compute 의 서버 볼륨 연결 API 를 쓴다. 이미 그 서버에 붙어 있으면 요청하지 않고 `unchanged` 로 끝낸다.
- `volume detach <volume-id> [--server <server-id>]`: 연결이 하나면 그 서버에서 뗀다. 여러 서버에 붙어 있으면 `--server` 를 요구한다.
- `volume delete <volume-id>`: 연결된 볼륨은 거절하고 `volume detach` 를 안내한다.
- `BlockStorageClient` 에 `delete`, `waitForVolume`, `waitForDeleted` 를 더한다.

## 안전장치

- `detach`, `delete` 는 실행 전에 볼륨 이름, 크기, 상태, 연결 서버를 stderr 에 보여 준다.
- 터미널에서는 확인을 묻는다. 비대화형 환경에서 `--yes` 가 없으면 API 호출 전에 거절한다(기존 `instance delete` 와 같은 방식).
- `--dry-run` 은 조회만 하고 요청을 보내지 않는다.
- `--wait` 는 연결은 `in-use`, 해제는 서버 연결 목록에서 빠질 때, 삭제는 조회가 404 가 될 때까지 기다린다. `error*` 상태가 되면 바로 실패한다. `--timeout <sec>` 는 `--wait` 와 함께만 쓸 수 있다(기본 300초).

## 결정

- 연결과 해제는 기존 `InstanceClient.attachVolume`, `detachVolume` 을 재사용했다. 새 엔드포인트가 없고 Keystone 토큰을 공유한다.
- `--yes` 는 TTY 에서 생략하면 확인 프롬프트를 띄운다. ADR-038 의 「TTY 무관 `--yes` 필수」 가 아니라 `instance delete` 선례와 지시서의 「확인을 받는다」 를 따랐다.
- `attach` 는 되돌리기 쉬워 확인과 `--dry-run` 을 두지 않았다.
- ADR 은 만들지 않았다. 새 결정이 기존 선례의 적용이라 코드만 봐도 같은 결론이 나온다.
- 버전 올리기는 별도 릴리스 커밋이 맡는다. 이 저장소에 CHANGELOG 는 없다.

## 검증

- `pnpm run build`, `pnpm verify:package`, `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm test`(1482건), `node dist/index.js commands --json`, `node scripts/check-pii.mjs`, `git diff --check` 모두 통과
- API 는 가짜 응답으로만 테스트했다. 실제 클라우드에는 요청하지 않았다.

author: nischalravi
body:
Fixes #666

## What changed
LP-10: evidence per revocation and metrics for the least-privilege loop. No new table and no migration.

- **Evidence record** (`internal/lp/evidence.go`, schema `tessera.lp-evidence/1`), computed from `lp_revocations`, its events, `lp_false_positives` and `lp_denials`: usage window, confidence and reasons, evaluator verification (used calls kept, none broken), simulated diff, approval path (auto policy or staged person), verified re-read, any restore (trigger, latency, denial events), false-positive label, timeline, and its SHA-256.
- **Audit chain**: the `lp.revocation.revoked`, `.finalized` and `.restored` events carry `evidence_sha256`. For a finalized or restored revocation the exported record's digest equals the one in the chain.
- **Export**: `GET /api/lp/evidence?from=&to=&limit=` and `GET /api/lp/revocations/{id}/evidence` (both `audit.read`); evidence packs get `least_privilege_revocations.csv` (mapped to SOC 2 CC6.3, ISO A.5.18, PCI 7.2.2).
- **Metrics**: `GET /api/lp/metrics?days=` (`graph.read`) and a card on Insights > Least privilege (`LpMetricsCard`, via `src/api.ts`): unused permissions removed, false-positive and restore rate per confidence level, median restore time, auto against staged.
- README section added.

## Tests
- `internal/lp/evidence_test.go`: finalized and restored records, digest equals the audit event's, `audit.Verify` chain intact, metrics, tenant isolation, golden export `testdata/golden/lp_evidence_v1.json` (`-update` to regenerate).
- `internal/evidence/leastprivilege_test.go`: pack file, period filter, control mapping.
- `internal/api/lp_evidence_test.go`, `lp_test.go` (cross-tenant), `rbac_routes_test.go` rows for the three routes.
- `internal/store/isolation_lp_test.go`: `TestIsolation_LPEvidenceReads`.
- Results: gofmt and vet clean; race: lp, evidence, audit, archtest, api (`LP|Evidence|RBAC|Route|Parity`) pass; store passes without `-race` (its race run exceeds 40 min on this loaded box) and its LP, classification and parity tests pass under race; Postgres (store, lp, evidence, api) pass; frontend `npm run build` and `npm test` (362) pass.

## Reviewer should check
- **Behaviour change**: in `lp.Run`, a verified restore now writes the false-positive label *before* moving to `restored` (it was after), so the digest in the audit event covers the label. No outcome change.
- The design (section 7) names an `lp_evidence` table and copies of per-source usage coverage and gaps; the brief said to prefer existing rows, so this computes the record instead. Per-source coverage/gaps are not kept with the candidate today and so are not in the record (used calls, confidence reasons and snapshot id are). Say if you want a table or a follow-up to store them.
- Digest is reproducible for terminal revocations; for a `revoked` one it is a snapshot as of that transition.
- Export is capped at 5000 records per call (metrics notes truncation).
- No parity fixtures changed; no admin change type added; no `.github/` change.

author: optimey
body:
## What

Upgrades Pillow from 12.3.0 to 13.0.0 in `requirements.txt` and names the new version in `LICENSES.txt`.

## Why

All 41 open Dependabot alerts (5 critical, 23 high, 13 moderate) are for the same package, Pillow 12.3.0 in `requirements.txt` (runtime scope). Every advisory lists 13.0.0 as the first patched version; none is fixed on the 12.x line, so 13.0.0 is also the smallest upgrade. No other package has an alert.

Pillow decodes the user's photos in the shipped app, so this reaches users with the next release; it is not build-only tooling.

## What else the bump touches

- `LICENSES.txt` (ships with the installer) listed "Pillow 12.3.0"; now 13.0.0. The MIT-CMU text in appendix H and the list of bundled native libraries are the same in the 13.0.0 wheel (only the versions of harfbuzz and libjpeg-turbo moved), so nothing else changes there.
- `tools/third_party_sources.json` has no Pillow entry (only pillow-heif), so `build.ps1`'s pin check is unaffected. pillow-heif 1.8.0 installs and works with Pillow 13.0.0 (HEIC test image decodes).
- The 13.0.0 wheel is still linked with MSVC 14.51, so the VC++ runtime minimum in the installers stays at 14.51.
- Pillow 13 drops Python 3.10; the project builds on 3.14.

## Tested

Fresh venv on Python 3.14 from the new `requirements.txt`, `pip check` clean:

- `tests\test_imaging.py`: 41 passed
- `tests\test_engine.py`: 26 passed
- `tools\test_build_tools.py`: 10 passed
- `tests\test_app_updates.py`: 25 passed, 18 skipped (they need a built `dist\` folder; no build was made)
- the imaging and engine tests also pass with `-W error::DeprecationWarning -X dev`

No release was built or signed, and the updater pins and release assets are untouched.

## Dependabot PR #5

#5 makes the same bump in `requirements.txt` only. This PR adds the `LICENSES.txt` change; after it is merged, #5 has nothing left to do and Dependabot closes it by itself.

author: dmstern
body:
## Zusammenfassung

• **Datensicherung in Admin-Oberfläche integriert (`AdminBackupCard.vue`, `SettingsAdminTab.vue`, `SettingsDataTab.vue`, `useSettingsTabs.ts`, `SettingsView.vue`):**
  • **Konsolidierung der Admin-Werkzeuge:** Der bisherige separate Tab „Daten“ in den Einstellungen wurde aufgelöst und die Datensicherungs-Card als modularer Baustein (`AdminBackupCard.vue`) harmonisch in die Admin-Oberfläche integriert.
  • **Einheitliches Card-Design:** Nutzt nun `SettingsCardHeader` mit Datenbank-Icon (`IconDatabase`), konsistenten Button-Styles mit Lade-Spinner (`:loading="exporting"`) und standardisierten Hinweistexten.
  • **URL- & Abwärtskompatibilität:** URLs mit `?tab=data` werden in `useSettingsTabs.ts` automatisch auf `admin` gemappt; `SettingsDataTab.vue` dient als transparenter Wrapper.
  • **Bereinigung von Altlasten:** Nicht mehr benötigte Screenshots (`settings-data-*`) und veraltete E2E-Spec-Einträge entfernt.

• **Konto sperren / entsperren (`AdminUserManagementCard.vue`, `useUserManagement.ts`, `users.ts`, `auth.ts`, `db/index.ts`):**
  • **Lebenszyklus-Aktion statt Löschzwang:** Admins können Benutzerkonten per Klick sperren und entsperren, um inaktive oder ausgeschiedene Accounts lahmzulegen, ohne verknüpfte Reisedaten, Packlisten und Ausgaben zerstörerisch löschen zu müssen.
  • **Sicherheits- & Selbstschutzregeln:** Admins können ihren eigenen Account nicht sperren; Administrator-Accounts können nicht gesperrt werden; Nicht-Admins wird der Zugriff verwehrt.
  • **Login- & Session-Gating:** Gesperrte Nutzer werden beim Login (`POST /api/auth/login`) mit 403 abgewiesen („Dieses Benutzerkonto ist gesperrt“); bei bestehenden Sessions wird der Aufruf von `/api/auth/me` abgebrochen und die Session zerstört; Selbstservice-Passwortresets (`POST /api/auth/forgot-password`) sind für gesperrte Accounts unterbunden.
  • **UI-Status:** Rotes Status-Badge „Gesperrt“ in der Tabelle und Aktionsbutton „Sperren“ / „Entsperren“ mit Tabler-Icons (`lock` / `lock-open`) und Bestätigungsdialog.
  • **Demo-Client-Parität:** `PUT /users/:id/lock` im Demo-Client unterstützt.

• **Anzeige des letzten Logins in der Nutzerverwaltung (`AdminUserManagementCard.vue`, `users.ts`, `auth.ts`, `db/index.ts`):**
  • **Letzter Login (`last_login_at`):** Admins sehen jetzt auf einen Blick in der Benutzertabelle, wann ein Nutzer zuletzt eingeloggt war („vor 2 Std.“, „Gestern“, „vor 3 Wochen“, „vor 5 Monaten“, „Nie“ bzw. voller Zeitstempel als Hover-Tooltip).
  • **Datenbank-Migration:** Additive Spalte `last_login_at` (TEXT, nullable) und `is_locked` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) in `users` via `ensureColumn` mit Unit- & Migrationstest.
  • **Backend-Login & Registrierung:** Bei erfolgreichem Login (`POST /api/auth/login`) und automatischer Erstanmeldung bei Registrierung wird `last_login_at` auf den aktuellen ISO-Timestamp gesetzt.
  • **Privatsphäre & Berechtigung:** `last_login_at` wird in `GET /api/users` ausschließlich an Administrator:innen ausgeliefert; für normale Nutzer:innen bleibt die Information unzugänglich.
  • **Frontend-Helper:** `formatLastLogin(dateStr, now)` in `dateFormat.ts` für relative, prägnante Zeitangaben mit umfassender Testabdeckung.
  • **Demo-Modus:** Beispielhafte `last_login_at`-Werte in `demoData.ts` für realistische Demo-Instanzen.

• **Klarstellung Sponsor-Prinzip in Rollen- und Stufen-Modals (`UserRolesModal.vue`, `SettingsUsersTab.vue`):**
  • Erläutert das Sponsor-Prinzip (Sobald ein Mitglied im Urlaub Plus oder Admin ist, gilt der Urlaub als gesponsert und der 3-Personen-Deckel entfällt).

• **Double-Opt-In-Checkbox bei deaktivierter Registrierung (`SettingsAdminTab.vue`):**
  • Wird deaktiviert (`:disabled="regForm.registrationMode === 'off'"`), wenn die Registrierung gesperrt ist.
  • Zeigt einen transparenten Hilfetext (`Erfordert einen konfigurierten SMTP-Mailserver. (Nur verfügbar, wenn die Selbstregistrierung aktiv ist.)`).
  • Behält den gespeicherten Wert im Zustand bei, sodass eine spätere Aktivierung der Registrierung die Voreinstellung nicht überschreibt.
  • Unterdrückt den Mailserver-Fehlalarm, wenn Registrierungen ohnehin gesperrt sind.

• **Rollenvergabe bei manueller Neuanlage durch Admin (`CreateUserDialog.vue` & `users.ts`):**
  • Ersetzt die alte Admin-Checkbox durch ein klares Rollen-Dropdown (`Select`): Basis-Konto, Reisotor Plus, Administrator:in.
  • Standardmäßig defensiv auf Basis-Konto voreingestellt.
  • Dynamischer Hilfetext erläutert den Rechteumfang der jeweils gewählten Rolle.
  • Checkbox „Gewählte Rolle für nächste Neuanlage merken“ speichert die Auswahl auf Wunsch im `localStorage` (`reisotor_admin_last_created_user_role`) für Serienanlagen.
  • Backend (`POST /users`) unterstützt `role: 'restricted' | 'plus' | 'admin'` abwärtskompatibel zu `is_admin` und `is_restricted`.

• **Bugfix Passwort-Reset & Zwischenablage (`AdminResetPasswordModal.vue`, `useUserManagement.ts`, `offline.ts`, `users.ts`):**
  • **Kein Hänger mehr bei SMTP:** SMTP-Versand beim Admin-Reset per `Promise.race` auf max. 2.5s begrenzt.
  • **Admin- & Nutzer-Routen niemals offline queuen:** `/users`, `/admin` und `/backup` in `isQueueablePath` (`offline.ts`) sowie explizit `noQueue: true` in `performResetPassword`.
  • **Automatisches Kopieren & Schutz vor `undefined`:** Bei Vorliegen des Reset-Ergebnisses wird das temporäre Passwort automatisch in die Zwischenablage kopiert; `copyToClipboard` prüft defensiv auf Text; Buttons sind bei leerem Wert deaktiviert.
  • **Demo-Client-Parität:** `demoClient.ts` um Mock-Handler für `POST /users/:id/reset-password`, `PUT /users/:id/role` und `POST /users/:id/verify-email` ergänzt.

## Verifikation

• Unit-Tests im Backend (`backend/test/routes/usersAdmin.test.ts`, `backend/test/routes/auth.test.ts`, `backend/test/unit/dbMigration.test.ts`) für Rollen-Zuweisung, Validierung, Admin-Passwort-Reset, `last_login_at`, Kontosperrung und DB-Migration erfolgreich.
• Unit-Tests im Frontend (`AdminBackupCard.test.ts`, `useSettingsTabs.test.ts`, `SettingsView.test.ts`, `CreateUserDialog.test.ts`, `AdminResetPasswordModal.test.ts`, `dateFormat.test.ts`, `useUserManagement.test.ts`, `demoClient.test.ts`) für Datensicherung, Tab-Mapping, Rollen-Auswahl, Auto-Copy, Undefined-Schutz, `formatLastLogin` und `toggleLockUser`.
• `npm run typecheck` und `eslint` fehlerfrei ausgeführt.

body:
## Zusammenfassung

Umfassender unabhängiger Sicherheits-, Logik- und Infrastruktur-Tiefencheck über Python-Module, JavaScript-/Worker-/Browser-Code, Docker-Konfigurationen und alle 97 CI-Definitionen mittels **Zizmor**, **Bandit**, **Ruff**, **ESLint (`eslint-plugin-security`)**, **`pip-audit`** und **`npm audit`** – inklusive direkter Dauerheilung aller realen Befunde im unversiegelten Bestand.

Alle **50 SHA-256-versiegelten Kerndateien** (`data/integrity_lock.json`) blieben unangetastet (`integrity_guard.py --gate` grün).

## Zentrale Reparaturen & Härtungen

1. **Laufzeit- & Logikfehler behoben**
   - **`engine_generate` (`F823` / `UnboundLocalError`):** Lokales `import glob, re` überschattete das globale `re` und löste bei gesetzter `pin_description` vor Zeile 248 deterministisch `UnboundLocalError` aus; auf Top-Level-Import bereinigt.
   - **`keyword_optimizer`:** Raw-String `r"[,\\n;]"` schnitt KI-Vorschläge bisher am Buchstaben `n` statt am Zeilenumbruch `\n`; korrigiert auf `r"[,\n;]"`, `.strip(...)` bereinigt und Schleifenvariable gebunden.
   - **`tools/seo-cockpit/app.js` & `app.test.cjs`:** Doppelten Schlüssel `'description-length'` entfernt, der das konkrete 155-Zeichen-SERP-Limit überschrieb (+ Regressionstest).
   - **`static/premium/ff-voice.js` & `ff_voice_browser_test.mjs`:** Unbehandeltes `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`-Promise mit Fallback versehen, überlappende Quantoren in `labelAround()` entschärft, doppelte `var`-Deklarationen bereinigt und `activePage`/`activeBrowser`/`activeServer` für saubere Fehlerdiagnose & Bereinigung im `catch`-Block gehoistet.

2. **Kanonische URL-Host-Prüfung statt Teilstring-/lstrip-Heuristik**
   - **`pinterest_plan_guard`:** `.lstrip("www.")` (`B005`) und Teilstring-Hostprüfung durch `url_host` (`host_von`, `ist_host_oder_subdomain`) + `urlsplit` ersetzt, CLI-Lauf in `main()` gekapselt und Selbsttest um Host-Spoofing-Gegenproben erweitert.

3. **Transportschutz gegen `file://`-LFI, SSRF, Cross-Zone-Redirects & OOM**
   - **Neues Stdlib-Modul `scripts/net_safety.py`** (`--selftest` mit 21 Fällen): Erzwingt `http`/`https`, blockiert Cloud-Metadaten (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`, `metadata.google.internal`), RFC1918, CGNAT, ULA, Multicast, `0.0.0.0`/`::` und IPv4-gemapptes IPv6 (`::ffff:...`), prüft jedes 3xx-Redirect-Ziel erneut (inkl. harter Cross-Zone-Sperre extern → Loopback) und begrenzt Antwortgrößen.
   - Verdrahtet in `werkbank_adapters`, `schaltwerk_triggers`, `faktenfrische`, `agent_reach_research` und `belegketten_wache`.
   - **Playwright-Brücke `tools/werkbank/render.mjs`** (`--selftest` mit 14 Proben): Vorab-Prüfung + `context.route('**/*', ...)`-Sperre inkl. DNS-Auflösung und WHATWG-Hex-Normalisierung (`[::ffff:7f00:1]`).

4. **Deterministische XML-Härtung gegen Billion Laughs & XXE**
   - **Neues Stdlib-Modul `scripts/safe_xml.py`** (`--selftest` mit 6 Fällen): Vorgeschaltete `pyexpat`-Prüfung weist Entity-Deklarationen (`<!ENTITY ...>`), interne DTD-Subsets sowie externe `SYSTEM`/`PUBLIC`-Referenzen deterministisch vor dem Baumaufbau ab (Größenlimit 50 MiB).
   - Verdrahtet in `publication_check`, `indexierbare_seiten`, `gsc_abdeckung` (3 Stellen), `seo_cockpit`, `spam_guard` und `tools/seo-spider/crawler.py`.

5. **CI-/Berechtigungs- & Container-Härtung**
   - **0 `${{ ... }}` in `run:`-Blöcken über alle 97 Dateien** (`template-injection` → **0**).
   - **Job-Level Least Privilege** in `codeql.yml`, `redaktionelle-ymyl-pruefung.yml` und `alert-on-failure.yml` (`excessive-permissions` → **0**).
   - **`tools/n8n/Dockerfile.whisper`:** Entfernt `git` und `build-essential` in derselben `RUN`-Schicht nach `pip install`.

6. **Python-Sicherheits- & Qualitäts-Hygiene**
   - `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` in `fristen_check` (`B108`), `usedforsecurity=False` bei `md5`/`sha1` (`B324`), Bereinigung doppelter Dict-Keys (`F601`), maskierte Zero-Width-Literale (`PLE2515`), `maxsplit=1` (`B034`), Schleifen-/Exception-Korrekturen (`B020`, `B025`, `F811`), `frozenset`-Klassenattribute (`RUF012`) sowie Bindung aller 12 `B023`-Closures im unversiegelten Produktionsbestand.

## Prüf- & Verifikationsnachweise

- Vollständiger Auditbericht: `UNABHAENGIGER-SICHERHEITS-UND-FEHLER-TIEFENCHECK-HIGHEND-2026-10-30.md`
- `python3 -m unittest scripts/tests/test_unabhaengiger_tiefencheck.py` (11/11 grün)
- `python3 scripts/safe_xml.py --selftest` (6/6) · `python3 scripts/net_safety.py --selftest` (21/21) · `node tools/werkbank/render.mjs --selftest` (14/14)
- `integrity_guard.py --gate` (50/50), `skript_syntax_wache.py` (599 Dateien), `wachen_vertrag.py` (0 Funde), `artefakt_waechter.py` (527 Artefakte), `actions_version_guard.py`, `url_substring_guard.py`, `clear_text_logging_guard.py`, `npm run test:sicherheit`, `npm run test:redos`, `selftest_ki.py --trap-workflows`, `ff_voice_functional_test.mjs` (265/265), `newsletter-worker` (93/93), `ki-assistent` (17/17) und `klick-zaehler` (34/34) – alle grün.

author: frostblooded
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"frostblooded"} -->
_Requested by **frostblooded** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0144Z7iQLTuZW5JvMzhivLQ1?thread=cmsg_0144Z7iQLTuZW5JvMzhivLQ1AVZvTu28EqaqWHoUpanhKZ)_

## What

His needs now drive both his next goal and the action he does there, Sims-style:

- **Urge curve:** each meter is a need below 40 and its urge is the square of how far below it is (0 at 40, 0.25 at 20, 1 at 0). Money is a need below €20 the same way, and at least 0.25 while saving up.
- **Need score:** an action scores the urge of each meter it raises times how much of the need it meets (a raise of 30+ meets it in full). Needs add up. Paid work scores the money urge.
- **Pull:** a place weighs 1 + 49 x its best action's score (x50 when empty, was x5), times how well it suits him. Actions use the same multiplier on their base weight.
- **Urgent (meter < 15):** he only heads for places that fix an urgent need, and the nearest wins (rank, 500 m bump and heading drop out). At the place he only picks fixing actions. 10% of the time he does as he likes anyway, unless the meter is under 5 (rock bottom): then always.
- **Drain:** an action that lowers a needed meter weighs (1 - urge) as much, at least 2%.
- **Strengths:** actions that train or need his best attribute weigh up to x2 (attribute / average).
- **Feed:** a strong (meter ≤ 20) or urgent need that picks his goal says so: "Thirsty, heading for Cafe Near".
- Same rules in the while-you-were-away catch-up.
- Help: new page **His needs**, rewritten Need paragraph in Picking the next goal, How he chooses, meter and saving pages. All numbers come from `help.ts` placeholders.

## Tests

Unit (life, walker, catch-up), integration (feed line in game), e2e all pass: `npm run lint`, `typecheck`, `test` (526), `e2e` (32 passed, 1 skipped). Two catch-up trip tests were fixed to roll one trip, since they depended on whether he ended on an odd or even trip.

## Perf

`npm run perf` (4G + 4x CPU), master → this branch, steady runs:

| Metric | master | branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| transfer_kb | 92 | 61 |
| app_js_kb | 56 | 57 |
| first_paint_ms | 472 | 416-440 |
| ready_ms | 589 | 515-517 |
| main_thread_busy_pct | 3 | 3 |
| long_tasks_after_ready | 0 | 0 |

All JS gzip: 356.3 KB → 357.0 KB (+0.7 KB). Transfer and paint differences are run noise.

Catch-up, 24 h on a 5000-place city (desktop, median of 7): 230 ms / 145 stops on master → ~420 ms / 242 stops. Per stop it stays ~1.7 ms; he makes more stops because urgent picks are short walks to the nearest fix. Catch-up yields between stops, so this adds no long task.

author: adrian-lee-dev
body:
## Problem

Team cancellation confirmation needs the appointment and notification consequences, including the hosts’ local times. Administrators also need reliable manual rebooking guidance when an original host has left the team.

## Change

- Summarize the appointment, saved hosts, invitee/guest recipients and cancellation delivery rules before submission.
- Prevent repeated submissions, preserve failed drafts, refresh successful cancellations and retain visible keyboard focus.
- Keep actions bound to their opening team and preserve recovery for changed access, cancelled bookings and started meetings.

## Round 2

- Add only nullable, read-only `hosts[].timeZone`, `hosts[].isCurrentMember` and `eventType.publicBookingPath` to `GET /api/v1/team/bookings`, documented as additive in OpenAPI. Host zones come from public profiles; no private schedule/calendar fallback or additional email fields are returned. The public profile time-zone exposure was checked against the team policy boundary and existing public booking endpoints.
- Keep member-departure/removal projections unchanged through a dedicated list schema. Resolve public paths with the existing public booking rules and deduplicate event lookups per page; disabled, deleted and unavailable events have a null path.
- Show the viewer’s time and each differing saved host’s local range in the confirmation. Show affirmative rebooking steps only when a saved host is no longer a team member. Use the returned public link immediately, or explicitly state that the event is no longer bookable and explain repair/reactivation.
- Update English/Simplified Chinese copy, the API field documentation and generated web types.

## Validation

- Full local suite with isolated PostgreSQL test databases: 401 files / 10,176 tests passed, exit 0, `--maxWorkers=2`; run once after implementation.
- Focused server/scheduling tests: 4 files / 158 tests; focused web tests: 5 files / 83 tests, all exit 0.
- PostgreSQL HTTP cases cover saved departed hosts, repaired event host configuration, disabled/soft-deleted/hard-deleted events, personal/team public paths, missing profiles without private schedule fallback and organization isolation.
- Local Chrome with synthetic API fixtures: English and Simplified Chinese at 320px; correct viewer/host times, departed/current/unknown membership, available/unavailable link states, no horizontal overflow, one cancellation request and visible keyboard focus after success.
- Existing shared test/auth pools are reused and closed; no new pools, migrations or third-party provider calls.

## Mutation checks

All source-copy baselines and restored copies pass. Production source files were not mutated.

- Web: hiding differing host zones fails both English/Chinese range assertions; showing rebooking for current or unknown membership fails both visibility assertions. Mutated probes exit 1; baseline and restored probes exit 0.
- Real PostgreSQL HTTP: suppressing the profile zone, ignoring the membership’s team, supplying a path for an unavailable event and removing booking-team scopes each trigger a real `AssertionError`. The cross-organization assertion checks that the foreign booking’s path and zone are absent before checking booking IDs.

## Gates

| Gate | Exit |
| --- | --- |
| `npx biome check .` | 0 (4 existing warnings) |
| `npm run typecheck` | 0 |
| `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` with test database bootstrap URL | 0; 401 files / 10,176 tests |
| `npm run build` | 0 |
| `docker build .` | 0 |
| `npm run api:types` | 0; generated types committed |

## Follow-ups

The notification guide still states that a booking without a verified host sends no messages. Current cancellation delivery can notify the invitee/guests in that case. Correct that documentation separately.

author: brunodmsi
body:
## Why

The E2E workflow has been red on `main` since d29a8b9 (#175). Six push runs failed in a row: the last green run was 40987027432 on ff5a402, the first red one was 40993747573, and the most recent is 41058875995. The nightly full suite (41044533313) fails for the same reason.

## Root cause

#175 (0b9bf7e, "name the apply button by its destination host") deliberately changed the detail page's primary action from `Apply on <Org>’s site` to `Apply on <host>`. The host comes from the listing's `applicationUrl`, parsed by `linkHost`. Two specs still located the link with `/Apply on .+’s site/`, so the locator never matched:

- `13-responsive.spec.ts:490`, mobile (375×667): `waitForLoaded` races the apply link against the empty and error states. The page loaded fine, but none of the three became visible, so the case timed out after 20s. This is the only failure in the push-triggered `responsive` suite.
- `10-public-browse.spec.ts:353` (anonymous read counts as a view, apply counts as a click): `toBeVisible` timed out on the same locator. This runs only in the nightly full suite.

The product change is intended, so the stale part is the test, not the code.

## Change

Both fixtures publish with `applicationUrl = stack.urls.programme`. Both specs now locate the link by `Apply on ${new URL(stack.urls.programme).host}`, using the same substring match as before so the trailing ↗ is still tolerated. This makes the locators more specific than the old pattern. No timeouts were changed and no test was skipped.

## Verification

- `biome check` on both files and `tsc --noEmit` for `@the-rfp-hub/e2e` pass locally.
- E2E `workflow_dispatch` runs on this branch:
  - full suite: https://github.com/The-RFP-Hub/the-rfp-hub/actions/runs/41059991490 (success: 118 passed, 1 skipped by design, 0 blocked; both previously failing cases pass)
  - responsive: https://github.com/The-RFP-Hub/the-rfp-hub/actions/runs/41059996008 (success: responsive.spec.ts total=15, skipped=0)

Recognition audit stack 5/5 — findings 18 and 19. Targets main after merging #1038–#1041.

Complete face vetoes and simultaneous face claims share the scene body comparison budget, with bounded score reuse for identical features, cooperative cancellation and progress. Distinct face comparisons cannot exceed max_witness_comparisons.

author: valentin5629
body:
## Ce que fait cette PR

Ajoute une ligne « Logo du client » dans l'onglet Documents de la fiche collecte Admin et dans l'onglet « Bilan & documents » de la fiche client. On y dépose, remplace ou retire le logo du client avant de télécharger le rapport.

Décisions de Val (2026-10-30) :
- le logo figure sur les **deux « Rapport de don »** : attestation de don (gabarit `attestation-don@4`, logo à côté de « Savr ») et rapport « sans excédent » ;
- il est **rangé sur l'événement** (`evenements.logo_client_organisateur_url`) et vaut pour tous ceux qui téléchargent ;
- **tout utilisateur qui peut télécharger le rapport** peut le déposer : Admin, traiteur (manager et commercial), agence, gestionnaire de lieux ;
- emplacement simple dans l'en-tête, à reprendre par le redesign annoncé du rapport.

Choix à valider (fiche `_Divergences/M1.6_20261030_logo-client-rapport-de-don.md`, type ambigu) :
- le logo déposé **passe en tête** de la cascade (devant l'agence et le compte du client organisateur), y compris pour le rapport de recyclage ZD ;
- un dépôt ou un retrait **refait automatiquement** les rapports de don déjà produits de l'événement (mention « Version mise à jour ») ; la régénération relit le logo, le reste du document reste figé ;
- un gestionnaire de lieux peut changer le logo de l'événement d'un traiteur ou d'une agence tenu sur ses lieux (C3 au pied de la lettre) ;
- dépôt plafonné à **1 Mo** (au-delà, le PDF n'inlinait pas le logo) ;
- pas de dépôt pour le client organisateur (il n'a pas de fiche collecte).

## Fiche événement (ajout du 2026-10-30)

- Même ligne « Logo du client » en tête du bloc Documents de l'onglet « Bilan & documents » de la fiche événement, commune à tous les rôles, **client organisateur compris** (décision Val), affichée même sans rapport disponible.
- Route `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/evenements/[id]/logo-client` : événement visible sous la RLS de l'utilisateur, même règle du donneur d'ordre pour les traiteurs.
- Les deux rapports cumulés de l'événement impriment déjà le logo du client par l'en-tête commun : avec la nouvelle priorité, le logo déposé y apparaît (aucun gabarit modifié).

## Sécurité

- Routes `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/{admin,traiteur,agence,gestionnaire}/collectes/[id]/logo-client`, garde propre dans chaque handler.
- Même accès que le téléchargement : collecte visible sous RLS, non annulée, rapport non réservé au donneur d'ordre ; règle du donneur d'ordre **jugée sur l'événement** (un traiteur qui opère pour une agence ne peut pas passer par une collecte ZD voisine — trouvé par la revue sécurité).
- Contrôle d'accès avant tout envoi au stockage ; écriture en service-role après ce contrôle ; clé bornée (`parseCleLogo` + `trg_garde_format_logo`) ; trace `audit_log` avec impersonation.
- Aucune migration.

## Vérifications

- Suite complète verte sur le commit final : 472 fichiers, 5 981 tests. `check:coverage M1.6` complet, `check:ratchet` OK, anti-couplage OK.
- Relectures : sécurité GO (après correctif), conformité GO, principale GO (correctifs appliqués : logo d'une attestation corrigée par le trigger de volume, panne du stockage, cache de l'aperçu), sobriété (cascade du rapport sans excédent remise dans le module commun).

author: seashell86
body:
Calling a `mut self` method that changes a list field copied the whole list on every call, so a loop of n such calls was quadratic. The self-hosted lexer and parser ran into it: lexing a file took four times as long when the file doubled.

## Why

`call_user` cloned each argument into the callee's frame, and the bound arguments stayed alive until the call ended. A `mut self` receiver was therefore always shared while the method ran. The first write to it copied the instance, which left each of its lists shared too, so the first `append` copied the list.

## The fix

Arguments now move into the frame. After the call, the `mut` ones are taken out of the frame, not cloned, and put back in their places. Nothing else changes.

## Numbers

Release build, this program with n calls:

```fennec
struct Acc:
    items: list[str] = []
    pos = 0

    def push(mut self):
        self.items.append("x")
        self.pos += 1

def main(stdout: Stdout):
    mut acc = Acc()
    while acc.pos < n:
        acc.push()
    stdout.print(len(acc.items))
```

| n | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20,000 | 0.64 s | 0.36 s |
| 40,000 | 2.35 s | 0.43 s |
| 80,000 | about 10 s | 0.45 s |

The machine was busy with other builds, so the small numbers are noisy, but the curve is now flat.

`--jit` still copies: it takes about 2.8 s at n = 40,000 either way. That's in the JIT's own handling of `mut self` and is left to the JIT work.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.

author: hsbt
body:
Since d411489ce5, clang-cl warns `'_addcarry_u64' is not a recognized builtin [-Wignored-pragma-intrinsic]` in every translation unit that includes `ruby.h`. mkmf compiles its checks with `-WX`, so on a clang-cl build the warning becomes an error and `TestMkmfConvertible#test_typeof_builtin` and `#test_typeof_typedef` fail.

clang provides `_addcarry_u64` as an inline function rather than a builtin, and clang-cl takes the `__builtin_add_overflow` branch of `rbimpl_size_add_overflow` anyway. This skips the pragma only for clang, so cl keeps the same intrinsic path.

I ran `make check` on a GNU make + clang-cl + YJIT build, and `test/mkmf/test_convertible.rb` on a full cl build.

body: ## What Wraps the existing PWA (`https://justrefundme.netlify.app`) as a Trusted Web Activity. The site stays the source of truth: web updates show up without a store release. A store release is only needed when the Android shell changes. - Android project in `android/`, app name **Refunds Bag**, package id `app.refundsbag` (`APP_ID` in `android/gradle.properties`; also `twa-manifest.json` and `assetlinks.json`). - `minSdk` 24, `targetSdk` / `compileSdk` 36 (Play's August 31, 2026 target). - Maskable icons added to the web manifest. Existing `any` icons, URLs, and auth behavior are unchanged. - `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` is served as `application/json` (Next headers + Netlify headers). The auth proxy skips `/.well-known/` so the file does not depend on Supabase. - Play steps, signing, and the before/after URL-bar explanation are in `android/PLAY_STORE.md` (Hebrew). ## Signing No keystore or password is committed. `android/.signing/` is gitignored. The fingerprint in `assetlinks.json` is a throwaway test key created for this build: `B0:6C:CF:F1:E3:0E:23:31:C8:E2:2A:1E:12:BD:EA:CD:0E:40:B3:88:E7:AF:2E:95:51:F6:73:76:F1:69:3B:C0` The debug APK and the release AAB are signed with that key. The private key is not in git. After the first Play upload, add the **Play App Signing** SHA-256 (not the upload key) to `sha256_cert_fingerprints`, then deploy the site. Play re-signs the store build, so without that fingerprint the URL bar comes back. ## URL bar, before and after this merges Checked live just now: - `https://justrefundme.netlify.app/.well-known/assetlinks.json` returns **404**. - `https://justrefundme.netlify.app/dashboard` returns **307 → /login**. So a build installed today opens the site **with** the Chrome URL bar. That is expected. After this is deployed, a build signed by the test certificate above opens full-screen (no URL bar), once Chrome finishes Digital Asset Links verification. Store installs need the Play App Signing fingerprint as well. ## Verification - `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build` passed. - `next start` serves `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` as **200** `Content-Type: application/json` (no redirect). `/login` is still 200. - `./gradlew assembleDebug bundleRelease` succeeded. - `aapt dump badging`: package `app.refundsbag`, version `1.0.0`, `minSdk` 24, `targetSdk` 36, label Refunds Bag. Launch URL in the APK is `https://justrefundme.netlify.app/dashboard`. - `apksigner` / `keytool -printcert` on the APK and the AAB both match the fingerprint above. `jarsigner -verify` reports `jar verified` (self-signed test cert, as expected). - **Emulator did not boot.** KVM is present and `emulator -accel-check` says it is usable, but starting a headless Android 35 Play image hit a kernel `kvm_spurious_fault`. The guest stayed offline in adb (no login screen, no URL-bar check). Fallback was `aapt` / `apksigner` / `jarsigner`, plus the local HTTP check above. Built artifacts (not committed): `refunds-bag-debug.apk`, `refunds-bag-release.aab`.

author: schiste
body:
## Summary

Add read-only deterministic discovery so a repository and its linked worktrees select one service address under an explicitly chosen private root.

Depends on #1279; merge after it. This PR does not start processes or change existing request routing. Opt-in startup follows in a dependent PR.

## Contract

- [x] **introduce** — `broker advanced service directory <private-service-root> --jobs-for <repository> [--json]`.

Both output modes emit one JSON object: `schema_version: 1`, `directory`, and the complete repository identity (`key`, `repository_uuid`, `root`, `common_dir`). The root must exist, be canonical, private and owned by the caller; the repository must already have a verified broker identity. Discovery creates no root, leaf, socket, job store or broker state and performs no startup maintenance.

The leaf uses 32 hexadecimal characters of the full identity key to fit Unix socket path limits; the complete key and identity remain mandatory for the service handshake and requests. Existing unsafe leaves and overlong socket paths are refused without repair. Unix only. The architecture and consumer registry document the new contract.

## Validation

- Rust 2024 formatting, diff checks and exact-prerequisite contract checks passed.
- Native macOS combined-stack integration at `c2d4959aca589eb19d59a9f71f9b14411c4f6d30`: all 45 expected protocol, transport, durable-job and worker cases passed, zero skipped; selected names and counts were verified. This includes all three discovery cases and all four ensure cases. This qualifies the combined startup tree, not an independent native full-workspace run of every earlier PR.
- All applicable current-head CI checks passed at `a72166d985d02394f0fa962f462c6bf8e3d42896`: 6,601 workspace tests passed (37 skipped), lint, examples/doctests, product-path smoke and tested-tree recording, plus Windows build/smoke where configured. Superseded cancelled runs are excluded.

The transport prerequisite now uses nonblocking socket I/O with absolute per-frame deadlines. A native macOS trace reproduced `setsockopt(... SO_RCVTIMEO ...) = EINVAL` after peer closure; the replacement drains buffered replies without changing timeout options on a closed peer. All five tests of the actual production I/O module passed natively, including closed peers, silent readers, stalled writers and trickling frames. This module-only run is separate from broker integration qualification.

Dependency preparation refuses the existing shared-cache recovery-journal identity mismatch. The cache and policy are preserved; this is not a passing preparation result. Native Rust checks do not require the missing eval environment.

The broker preflight refused normalized replay because the inherited, published stack contains an owned merge commit. No gates ran. The tested PR chain is preserved; default-branch preflight must be retried after prerequisites land. Earlier parent full native preflights timed out: entry 784 ran 4,173 cases (4,144 passed, 29 failed; 43 skipped), and entry 785 ran 4,946 (4,898 passed, 48 failed; 43 skipped). Three representative failures reproduce on unchanged base `989d7c97b2e52e056cdf78620fb1b5e422e37e32`; canonical TMPDIR fixes two path cases, while a non-UTF-8 fixture cannot be created on this filesystem. Remaining failures are unclassified; neither preflight is a pass.

author: maxbrunet
body:
Client response reads and close errors now return CodeUnavailable for EPIPE and ECONNRESET. Server writes are unchanged from #1053, and client Do behavior is unchanged.

Response reads map EPIPE and ECONNRESET to CodeUnavailable after checking context cancellation and deadline. The first close before EOF does the same. CloseRead is idempotent, and a close error after the body reached EOF is ignored so a completed RPC stays successful. After a complete end-stream, a failed drain keeps the server's end-stream error.

TestConnectionReset covers Connect, gRPC, and gRPC-Web for read, close, early close, unary close, cancellation, deadline, and drain. TestWrapIfClientTransportError pins the mapping boundary.

CodeUnavailable is retryable. A reset during a response can arrive after the server handled the request, so retry only idempotent RPCs. The client cannot tell whether the server acted.

No exported API or wire-format changes.

author: matipan
body:
## Why

An agent often works on many features of one domain over time. To start a new feature or to review a pull request, agents made their own Git worktrees and clones outside Galpon:

- The Git mirrors list 26 worktrees outside `~/.local/state/galpon/worktrees`. Ten are in `~/.cache/godmode-billing`. Sixteen are in the Claude Code scratchpad under `/tmp`, and 15 of these folders do not exist now.
- The Pi sessions contain more than 100 `git worktree add` commands. Most of them put the worktree in `/tmp`.
- Agents ran 13 `git clone` commands for repositories that Galpon already has.

Galpon does not know about these checkouts. The command center does not show them, checkpoints do not include them, and cleanup does not remove them. The cause: an agent cannot add a worktree to its placement, and its instructions do not tell it where new checkouts go.

Galpon also stores the branch of a worktree only when it creates the worktree. When an agent starts the next feature on a new branch in the same worktree, the stored branch becomes incorrect. A placement copy then started from the old stored branch, and the command center and the agent instructions showed the old branch. Before this change, 30 agent worktrees were on a branch that was different from the stored branch.

## What

- Each agent has a Galpon folder, `worktrees/<workspace>/<agent>`. The folder holds the agent's worktrees and a `scratch` folder for work files that are not in a repository.
- New agent tools `galpon_add_worktree` and `galpon_remove_worktree` for Pi, Claude Code, and Codex. New CLI commands `galpon agent worktree add` and `galpon agent worktree remove`.
- The instructions of all three harnesses include the folder and this rule:
  - Continue a feature in its worktree.
  - When the work on the current branch is done, start the next feature on a new branch in that worktree.
  - When the work is not done, or another checkout is necessary for a review or a comparison, use `galpon_add_worktree`.
  - Do not create worktrees, clones, or work folders outside the folder, unless the user asks for another place.
- Galpon uses the branch that a worktree has checked out now. Placement copies start from the current commit. The command center and the agent instructions show the current branch. Checkpoints restore the current branch.
- Agents with a managed directory, such as Reviewer, can also add worktrees. A copy of such an agent takes its extra worktrees, as a copy of a worktree agent takes all of its worktrees.
- Cleanup removes the scratch folder, and then the agent folder when it is empty.

## How

- `gitx.AddWorktree` creates a worktree from the shared mirror. It checks out an existing local branch, continues a remote branch with the same name, or starts a new branch or a detached checkout from a base. It fetches a base that only the remote has, such as `pull/123/head`, into a temporary reference. It deletes that reference after it creates the worktree.
- `gitx.RemoveAgentWorktree` stops when the worktree has uncommitted changes, unless `force` is set. It deletes the stored branch and the checked-out branch only when the remote-tracking references contain all of their commits. It keeps all other branches, so a removal does not lose a commit.
- `App.AddAgentWorktree` adds the worktree as a private assignment after the existing assignments. Position zero stays reserved for the primary worktree, so the extra worktrees of a directory placement start at position 1. `App.RemoveAgentWorktree` refuses the primary worktree and a worktree that another agent uses.
- The runtime tool route runs the two tools under the repository gate and records idempotency receipts, as it does for `create_agent`.
- `AgentFolder` uses the folder of an existing private worktree of the agent. If there is none, it uses the name from the workspace and agent titles, which is the name that placement creation uses.
- Pi gets the folder rule in `GALPON_FOLDER_INSTRUCTIONS`. Claude Code gets it in `--append-system-prompt`, and Codex gets it in its developer instructions. Claude Code starts with `--add-dir <folder>`. Codex gets `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` as a thread config override with the configured roots plus the folder. The sandbox mode does not change.
- The daemon reads the checkout of all worktrees of one mirror with one `git worktree list --porcelain -z` command. It keeps the result for 2 seconds and adds `currentBranch`, `head`, and `detached` to the dashboard and agent views. `Worktree.CheckoutLabel` gives the label for the command center and the instructions.
- A placement copy forks each worktree from the `HEAD` commit of the source worktree. A checkpoint snapshot records the checked-out branch or a detached `HEAD`, and a restore uses it. A snapshot from an older version uses the stored branch.

## Testing

- `go test ./...` and `go test ./e2e -count=1` pass.
- `dagger --x-release v1.0.0-beta.21 check` passes.
- New Git tests: a fetch of a reference that only the remote has, the continuation of a remote branch, branch deletion only for published branches, and a checkpoint restore of the checked-out branch and of a detached `HEAD`.
- New app tests: worktrees go in the agent folder. A removal keeps the primary worktree, a shared worktree, uncommitted changes, and unpublished commits. Copies start from the current commit of every worktree. Directory agents add worktrees, copies take them, and cleanup removes the worktrees, the scratch folder, and the agent folder.
- New end-to-end test: a real Pi agent calls `galpon_add_worktree` and `galpon_remove_worktree` through the daemon. When the Galpon system prompt reaches the model, the test also requires the folder instructions in it. This passes with Pi 1.4.0 and Pi 1.0.4. With Pi 1.4.0, the test fails when the folder instructions are empty.
- I put back the old behavior for three rules: a copy from the stored branch, a restore on the stored branch, and deletion of unpublished branches. Each time, the new tests failed.
- A probe with the Codex 0.166 app-server showed that a thread `config` override for `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` replaces the configured roots. For this reason, Galpon merges the configured roots with the folder.

## Notes

- The folder rule is guidance in the agent instructions. Galpon does not block Git commands. We can add a guard later if agents do not obey the rule.
- Galpon does not change or move existing worktrees outside the agent folders.
- This PR also removes a stale "Plan" reference from `docs/harnesses.md`.
- Finding outside this change: with Pi 1.0.4, which the Dagger test container uses, the model request of a Galpon Pi agent does not contain the Galpon system prompt at all. Pi 1.4.0 sends it. For this reason, the prompt check in the new end-to-end test has no effect in the Dagger check. A later change can update the pinned Pi version.
- The daemon must restart to load the new tools. Running Pi agents get the new tool definitions when they reload the extension. Agents get the folder rule when they start again.

`docs/api.md` freezes the factorization options for 1.x. Until now that included research knobs, sentinel values and a free-form partitioner string, and each frontend exposed a different subset. This PR defines the stable set and moves everything else out of the promise.

author: undivisible
body:
First agent-API piece, stacked on #8. Moves renewal scheduling, pre-send/pre-reconnect checks and prekey republication from the TUI into `@nexnet/client`. A certificate-only signer callback prepares the boundary for a persistent principal-controlled daemon; no daemon or agent execution API is exposed yet.

## AD-6 policy amendment — 2026-10-30
Explicitly permits principal-delegated non-interactive jobs to obtain certificates from an authorised persistent signer without a passkey on every job start. Interactive cold starts still require passkeys. Keep 11-hour certificates and renewal: missing revocation (#4) makes extending credential lifetime unsafe. Root keys must never enter jobs, container images or model context.

Certificates prove identity only. The closed pilot still requires receiver-verifiable grants covering peers, capabilities, budget and validity; no redelegation or human-approval-bound operations. Capability advertisements remain claims, with no incomplete-reputation exclusion.

## Failure handling
- Validate root signatures, unchanged identity/device/keys/capabilities and bounded validity before installing renewals; keep existing encryption keys.
- Coalesce concurrent renewals, validate certificate times at response arrival, bound signer waits to 15 seconds, and discard abandoned responses without disturbing replacement connections.
- Retry failed prekey publication even after the new certificate is installed. Emit failures and reject sends; stop authentication retries when credentials cannot be renewed.
- Stop lifecycle timers on disconnect. Keep queued/delivered transport states separate from later accepted/completed/failed execution states.

## Verification
The new real-relay headless expiry test failed on the parent commit with `device certificate expired; renew it before reconnecting`, and passes after extraction. Additional tests cover idle timer renewal, expiry disconnect, signer timeout, publication retry, late signer responses, and genuine root-signed certificates with invalid scope/validity.

Local: 482 root tests and 7 TUI integration tests pass; workspace typechecks, formatting and lint pass (existing lint warnings remain). No Rust build was needed locally.

## Remaining boundary
This is lifecycle extraction, not a complete delegated agent service. Durable recovery and locking come next, then the authenticated daemon/SDK and receiver-enforced grants. Legacy delivery receipts still verify root signatures; certificate-aware receipts must be migrated before exposing a root-free receiving client. The headless test proves renewal and transport reception, not completion of that receipt migration. No A2A-over-Nexnet binding is planned. Nothing is deployed.

Add an **isolated real FreeBSD15.1 + upstream dvtws2 v1.0.6 TCP sender/receiver byte witness** for genuine pinned upstream `http_hostcase` Lua, complementing the existing test-only DROP Exclude harness.
