author: tehas-app-bot[bot]
body:
## TL;DR

Make `tehas-merge`'s answer truthful on a host: `"model": true` whenever the pi session was asked, the `calls` key its usage text promises actually printed, and `--head`/`--base` accepted in upper case and matched against git's lower-case sha…

Automated by pi-rukas /work driver (mechanized commit-pr).

Fixes #1149


## Assumptions made while resolving this issue

The issue did not fully specify the following. Each was resolved with a defensible default rather than blocking — check them:

- **The upper-case-head case is tested at the `Plan` boundary, not through `main`: `refuse()` calls `std::process::exit`, so argument parsing is unreachable from `console/merge/src/tests.rs`, and there is no `console/merge/tests/` harness** — the case sets `head` upper case and scripts `git rev-parse HEAD` to answer lower case.
- **Deliverable 1 is a deletion plus comment upkeep: `out.model = true` at `lib.rs:381` is then the only writer of the field.**
- **`calls` in `main.rs`'s printed answer becomes the empty list the usage text promises for a runner that holds none.**
- **The three existing `assert!(out.model)` cases (tests.rs:280, 320, 424) keep passing: they all go through `merge_and_settle`.**

## Adversarial review — non-blocking findings

The adversarial gate passed this diff but left these unresolved. They did not
block the commit (only `CRITICAL_ISSUES_FOUND` does); they are recorded here so
they are decided deliberately rather than forgotten.

### default

I'll start by reading the issue body and the changed files.




Status: done — analysis complete, tests/lint/verify --changed all pass; writing verdict now.



I'm looping on redundant verification calls. Stopping and producing the verdict from what I already have.

VERDICT: MINOR_OBSERVATIONS

**Scope reviewed:** `console/merge/src/lib.rs`, `console/merge/src/main.rs`, `console/merge/src/tests.rs` (commit `e23b3ef3`).

**Checks run (targeted only):**
- `cargo test --locked --manifest-path console/Cargo.toml -p tehas-merge` → 18 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p tehas-merge --all-targets` → clean.
- `cargo fmt -p tehas-merge --check` → clean.
- `scripts/verify.sh --changed` → all steps `ok` (the driver's own gate, run once).

**Comment-removal audit (all LEGITIMATE):**
- The four `report` lines about "read from what the runner was asked" were replaced by an equivalent, corrected block — the old text was factually wrong (on a host `Real` records no calls, so the calls-derived answer was always false). Replacement is accurate.
- `modelled`'s doc comment was removed with the function it documented — the code it described is gone.
- The `// not the pull request this decision was made about.` line survives verbatim; only a sentence was added. No loss.

**Attack vectors considered and why they held:**
- *`asked_model` desync with `out.model`.* Both are set on the same two adjacent lines (`out.model = true; *asked_model = true;`) immediately before `ask_model`. Every later `Ok(out)` return path carries the same `out` (which already holds `model = true`), and the `Err` path reads `asked_model` back in `report`. No path sets one without the other.
- *Stale `asked_model` on a re-run.* `report` declares `let mut asked_model = false;` per call; `merge_and_settle` takes `&mut bool` and never sees a previous value. No bleed between merges.
- *Caseless comparison widening the head check.* `eq_ignore_ascii_case` is applied after `trim()` on both sides, and `main.rs` still enforces `len() == 40 && all(is_ascii_hexdigit)` before the value reaches the plan (main.rs:242), so the comparison can only ever be over 40 hex digits. ASCII-only case folding cannot fold a non-hex byte into a hex byte. A head of `ABCDEF1111…` now matches git's `abcdef1111…`; a genuinely different commit still refuses (covered by `a_tree_at_another_commit_is_not_the_pull_request`).
- *Lower-casing before validation changes the refusal contract?* No — the hex-digit test is case-insensitive by nature, so the set of accepted `--head`/`--base` values is unchanged, and 64 is still the exit for a non-commit.
- *The new `Silent` runner hiding a regression.* `a_runner_that_records_no_calls_still_says_the_model_ran` asserts both `r.calls.is_empty()` and `f.of("pi").len() == 1`, so it cannot pass on a merge that never asked the model. The `!out.model` case (`a_merge_with_no_conflict_says_no_model_ran`) closes the opposite direction.
- *`"calls": Vec::<String>::new()` in main.rs.* Matches the usage text's promised key and the empty list `Real` actually holds; `Report::json()` still emits real calls for library callers, and the only caller (`libexec/easy-merge`, not in this repo) is outside the diff.
- *Test-fixture correctness.* `HEAD_UPPER`/`HEAD_LOWER` are the same 40 characters in the two cases (`ABCDEF` + 34 `1`s vs `abcdef` + 34 `1`s); the upper-case case scripts git's lower-case answer explicitly, so it does not depend on the default stub.

MINOR_OBSERVATIONS:
1. The upper-case head test exercises the caseless comparison in `merge_and_settle` only, not the lower-casing in `main.rs` — `p.head = HEAD_UPPER` is set directly on the `Plan`, bypassing the `need("head").to_ascii_lowercase()` line. The CLI half of deliverable 2 has no test. That path is trivial (one `to_ascii_lowercase()` before an existing case-insensitive check), and `console/merge` has no CLI test harness today, so this is an author's-discretion note, not a gap that can produce wrong behavior. - `console/merge/src/tests.rs:536`
   Quote: `p.head = HEAD_UPPER;`
2. `asked_model` is threaded as an out-parameter on `merge_and_settle`, duplicating state `out.model` already carries for every path except the `Err(Why)` path that drops the outcome. A `Why`-carrying-flag or returning `(Outcome, bool)` would make the coupling explicit and keep the two from drifting if a future `Err` is raised after the model is asked. Non-blocking; today the two are set on adjacent lines and cannot diverge. - `console/merge/src/lib.rs:382`
   Quote: `*asked_model = true;`

REASONING SUMMARY:
I attacked the three real risks in this diff: the out-parameter `asked_model` drifting out of sync with `out.model`, the caseless head comparison widening the "tree is not the pull request's head" guard, and the new `Silent` runner letting the model flag pass a test without a session actually running. On the first, both writes are adjacent and every return path preserves the flag; on the second, the 40-hex-digit validation in `main.rs` still runs before the comparison and ASCII case folding cannot map a non-hex byte into a hex byte, so a wrong commit still refuses (and the pre-existing negative case still passes); on the third, the test asserts a real `pi` call through the inner `Fake` while the outer runner reports no calls, which is exactly the host behaviour the issue says was broken. The `calls` key added in `main.rs` matches the usage text and the `Real` runner's actual (empty) call list. Comment removals are all replacements of text that had become false or that documented deleted code — no rationale was lost. Verification was targeted only: package tests (18 pass), clippy, fmt, and one `verify.sh --changed`. Confidence: HIGH.

VERDICT: MINOR_OBSERVATIONS

## Planner refused some workstream calls

The plan went ahead on the workstream calls it accepted. These `report_workstream` calls were refused and contributed nothing to it:

- `plan` · id `default`: workstream id 'default' was already reported in this plan — each workstream needs a distinct id. This call was refused and added nothing; call again with a dist…

author: sharpvik
body:
## What

`gg build` with no tag, and `gg ship` (which never takes one), now tag the image with the short hash of `HEAD`, but only when the work tree is clean. Otherwise the tag is the clock, as before.

| situation | tag |
|---|---|
| clean tree | `git rev-parse --short HEAD` |
| modified or **untracked** files anywhere in the repo | clock, with a line on stderr saying why |
| ignored files only | hash (ignored files don't count) |
| not a repo, no commits yet, or no `git` on PATH | clock, silently |
| `gg build P/IMAGE:TAG` | `TAG`, unchanged, and git is never run |

`gg ship` gets **no** tag flag. Wanting a specific name is when build/push/deploy are worth running separately.

## Why

A clock tag says nothing about which code is in the image. The hash makes `gg history` and `gg rollback` say which commit they put back. A dirty tree falls back to the clock because the hash would name code the image doesn't contain.

## Notes

- The whole repository is checked, not just `--context`, since `--file` can point at a Dockerfile outside the context. In a monorepo, a dirty file elsewhere means a clock tag. That's the conservative choice.
- Rebuilding the same clean commit reuses the tag. `gg ship` deploys by the digest the push reports, so the new build is the one that runs.
- `gg push` still requires a tag. `gg deploy` and `gg run` are untouched.

## Tests

- `TestCommitTag` (9 cases): clean tree, context in a subdirectory, modified file, untracked file, dirty outside the context, ignored file, no commits, not a repo, no git. Git config is isolated from the machine running the tests.
- `TestBuildAndShipTagWithTheCommit` (7 cases) runs `cmdBuild` and `cmdShip` against a fake docker, a git wrapper that records each call, and a fake API. It checks:
  - the `docker build -t` tag: the hash, a clock tag, or the explicit tag;
  - that `--push` and `ship` push the image they built;
  - that `ship`'s deploy request names that image with the digest from the push;
  - that git is never run when a tag is given;
  - that stderr explains a clock tag only for a dirty tree.
- `TestBuildOutsideARepositoryIsQuietlyTheClock`: a build outside any repo gets a clock tag and prints nothing on stderr.
- Mutation checks: I broke the code four ways and the tests failed each time (7 failures, then 3 for each of the others):
  - `commitTag` never returns the hash
  - `ship` ignores the hash
  - `build` runs git despite an explicit tag
  - the stderr note is removed

author: transfix
body:
Without `CVCPKG_DATABASE_URL` (the YAML backend), the server drops a build's description, homepage, license, maintainer and tags.

## The bug

- **On publish:** `/v1/publish` and `/v1/upload/{id}/complete` never write those fields into the index's bundle. The chunked path drops `org` too.
- **On read:** `/v1/packages`, `/v1/packages/{name}` and `/v1/packages/{name}/latest` build their rows without those fields (`_index_package_info`). A mirror's index has them, and these endpoints still drop them.
- **What still works:** only `/v1/search` and the RSS feed read the fields. So against a YAML-backed server, cypkg's package page showed blank description, license, homepage and tags. The DB backend, SQLite or PostgreSQL, sends them all.

Found while adding cy-pca/cypkg#4, which runs cypkg against a local `cvcpkg-server`. That PR uses SQLite to work around this bug.

## The fix

- **Publish:** both publish paths store the five fields, and the chunked path stores `org`.
- **Read:** `_index_package_info` now builds every field a bundle carries, as the search path already did. That adds `published_by_email`, `release_tag`, `recipe_version`, `signature`, `key_fingerprint`, `required_deps` and `provides`.
- **One builder:** `/v1/packages` and `/v1/search` now build their rows with `_index_package_info`, so the four YAML read endpoints answer alike. `/v1/cache` is unchanged.

## Tests

- **New:** `TestPublishMetadata` in `tests/unit/test_server.py` publishes through `/v1/publish` and through a chunked upload. It reads the metadata back from `/v1/packages/{name}`, `/v1/packages`, `/v1/search` and `/latest`. Both tests fail on master with `('/v1/packages/{name}', 'description', ...)`.
- **Existing:** I ran every unit test file that touches these endpoints, 34 files: 1294 passed, 37 skipped. `tests/unit/test_server.py` alone: 187 passed. `black --check src/ tests/` is clean.
- **End to end:** a YAML-mode `cvcpkg-server run`, then `cvcpkg publish` of a real bundle. `/v1/packages/<name>` now returns the manifest's description, license, homepage, tags and maintainer.

Bundles a YAML server stored before this fix have no metadata in its index, so they still come back blank until they are published again.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## What changed

Implements the cooking session at the largest text sizes, AX3 to AX5, as signed off in #149 (`docs/design/karta-v1.md` → *The cooking session* → *Text size* → *From AX3 to AX5*). All changes are in `Karta/` and keyed on a new `largeAccessibilitySize` check (`dynamicTypeSize` ∈ `.accessibility3`–`.accessibility5`).

- **Temporizador** (`Karta/Sources/CookingSessionView.swift`): in every timed state the label sits under the time, left-aligned, 2 pt below (`timerTimeLabelGap` in `KartaDesign`), via a new `timerDigitsAndLabel` that stacks a `VStack` from AX3 and keeps the existing row below it. The 44 pt circles stay on the right, centred on the two-line block; ready, running and paused share the layout so the time never moves between states. Digits and labels use `lineLimit(1)` + `fixedSize` so no word and no time breaks in the middle.
- ***Time's up***: keeps its one row; wraps only between its two words, `Stop` stays on the right inside its pill, which grows with its label.
- **Media window chip**: from AX3 the chip's text leaves the window and sits 8 pt under it (`mediaChipUnderGap`) on the 20 pt inner edge, with no fill — Figtree 800 `.caption1`, suit `chipInk`, wrapping as needed, never truncated. Applies to *When it looks like this, move on*, the clip's name + length, and *Clip unavailable* with its glyph. The clip's `· 6 s` tail is bound with non-breaking spaces so it wraps as one unit. The play circle, expand button, progress line and the 220 → 160 pt give-way are unchanged — the under-window chip block is measured (`onGeometryChange` → `chipUnderHeight`, 0 below AX3) and added to `rest` in `mediaHeight(extra:)`, so the give-way order (free space → 20 pt, window 220 → 160, then scroll) is preserved.
- **Signal chip**: from AX3 reads `N more` (`1 more`) and `More`. Arrow, fade, place and tap unchanged.
- **Debug seed** (`Karta/Sources/DebugSeeds.swift`): `cooking-short-photo` cooks `baked-salmon-with-lemon` on Paso 1 (*Preheat the oven*) for the give-way evidence capture.

## Seams under test

Rendering-only change inside `Karta/`; `KartaCore`/`KartaPresentation` untouched. Verified against `xcodebuild test` (Karta scheme, 47 tests) and `cd KartaCore && swift test` (325 tests), all green.

## How I verified

Built with Xcode 27.0 RC and captured on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.0, E0224A22-…) with the size applied via `xcrun simctl ui <device> content_size <name>` and read back before each shot (AX1 = `accessibility-medium`, AX3 = `accessibility-extra-large`, AX5 = `accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large`). Seeds `cooking-timer`, `cooking-t1-running`, `cooking-t1-paused`, `cooking-t1-done`, `cooking-clip`, `cooking-clip-unavailable`, `cooking-short-photo`; evidence and notes in `Karta/Documentation/Issue150/`.

Tested commit: `4140a61ddd324a4122685602d356118716f21fda`.

## Open decisions

None — every drawn state was implemented as specified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] At AX3 and AX5, paused shows *PAUSED* under the time, no word or digit broken, both circles at 44 pt on the right — `iphone17-ios27-ax3-t1-paused.png`, `iphone17-ios27-ax5-t1-paused.png`.
- [x] At AX3 and AX5, running and ready use the same layout (*LEFT* / *TIMER* under the time); the time never moves between states — `…-ax3-t1-running.png`, `…-ax3-t1-ready.png`, `…-ax5-t1-running.png`, `…-ax5-t1-ready.png`.
- [x] At AX3 and AX5, *Time's up* wraps only between its words and *Stop* stays inside its pill — `…-ax3-t1-done.png`, `…-ax5-t1-done.png`.
- [x] At AX3 and AX5, the window's chip text is under the window and never truncated (clip name+length, photo cue, *Clip unavailable*); play circle uncovered — `…-ax5-clip.png`, `…-ax5-clip-unavailable.png`, `…-ax3-photo-chip.png`.
- [x] At AX3 and AX5, the signal chip reads *N more* / *More*, never truncated — `…-ax3-photo-chip.png` (`3 more`), `…-ax5-clip-top.png` and `…-ax5-clip-unavailable.png` (`4 more`), `…-ax5-clip.png` (`2 more`).
- [x] Default size, AX1 and AX2 unchanged — `…-default-t1-paused.png`, `…-ax1-t1-paused.png` (plus `…-xxxl-t1-paused.png` reference).
- [x] Give-way order preserved: the under-window chip's height counts in `rest` — `…-ax3-short-photo.png` shows the short Paso at AX3 with the window at 220 pt and no scroll.
- [x] Only `Karta/` changes; `gate` green pending CI; ralph reviewer to run.

## Scope
- Add **read-only** Type 1/2 OSPFv2 LSA header comparison following RFC 2328 §13.1 (signed sequence, checksum, MaxAge, MaxAgeDiff).
- Build bounded, deterministic Link State Request **intents** for missing or remote-newer identities from synthetic, externally admitted DD summary snapshots.
- Reject malformed, unsupported and duplicate LSA identities, forged request ledgers, stale Exchange/Engine snapshots, and over-budget pages with no partial modifications.
- Preserve existing Hello/Dead, ExStart and Exchange code, including existing rejection of nonempty DD LSA headers. No LSDB installs, real packets, SPF/routes, or FULL adjacency are claimed.
- Add explicit 1000-replay adversarial tests, unconditional required PR CI and independent Linux release tests, and source-grounded architecture documentation.

**Verification pending**: do not merge until all applicable exact-head GitHub checks succeed. After protected merge, require a separate exact-`main` Linux release and inspect its artifacts before declaring complete.

author: simoleolife
body:
## Summary
`AnswerPollEvent` stored an answer for any question id, and gave the badge when the id equalled the poll's last question, so sending only that id was enough.

`Poll.hasQuestion` (questions and their sub-questions) gates the answer and the badge.

Deep audit item NE15.

- `AnswerPollQuestionContractTest` (new), poll tests, spotless

author: lazbutton
body:
Suite de #30, maintenant fusionnée. La branche partait de sa pointe (514fc79), et `main` y est fusionné, avec #30 : la PR ne porte plus que ses deux commits.

Elle reprend les deux points du « Laissé pour plus tard » de #30. Quand le serveur du flux acceptait la connexion sans jamais envoyer d'en-têtes, `play()` attendait son `fetch` sans limite. C'est le cas d'une machine injoignable derrière un proxy qui attend son amont. Le casque restait muet, `streamDown` restait faux, et le bouton affichait « Retard du casque : N ms ». Et les replis MSE et `<audio>` n'avaient pas la règle des 3 s.

## Les deux commits

| Commit | Avant | Maintenant |
|---|---|---|
| Le casque n'attend plus sans fin un serveur qui ne répond pas | Chaque chemin, PCM, WAV ou MSE, faisait son `fetch` sans limite. `audio.play()` aussi : sa garde de calage (`waiting`, puis 8 s) relançait par `bump`, et la génération suivante remplaçait l'essai sans que le bouton le dise | Les trois `fetch` passent par `requestStream`. Sans en-têtes en 8 s (`STALL_MS`), `answerWithin` (`api/monitorStream.ts`, testé) abandonne la demande. Le bouton dit alors « Le flux ne répond pas : le casque réessaie seul », et l'essai passe au chemin suivant, puis au backoff. `audio.play()` n'attend pas plus : l'essai échoue par le `catch` de `play()`, qui le dit |
| Les replis MSE et audio du casque suivent la règle des 3 s | La reprise par l'élément comptait dès qu'il jouait : le backoff repartait à 200 ms, et l'alerte s'effaçait. Un serveur qui rend 0,1 s puis ferme était redemandé 17 fois en 5 s, sans un mot. Une erreur de lecture en MSE relançait à 200 ms fixes | Comme en PCM, la reprise ne compte qu'une fois que l'élément a joué 3 s (`STEADY_MS`, d'après `audio.played`, sur `timeupdate`), et jamais pendant l'attente d'une relance. `bump` et le `catch` du MSE lèvent l'alerte pour un élément qui n'a pas tenu ce temps, et suivent le backoff : 6 demandes en 5 s, et le bouton le dit |

## Ce qui change pour la relecture

- Le bouton le dit dès la première demande restée sans réponse, au bout de 8 s, sans attendre la fin de l'essai. Un essai demande le flux trois fois (PCM, MSE, élément) : attendre sa fin ferait 24 s de silence sans un mot, et 32 s pour un flux WAV avec son repli MP3. C'est la règle de la garde de #30, qui le dit après 8 s sans un octet. Si un chemin suivant joue, l'alerte s'efface comme à toute reprise : après 3 s de son.
- Après une demande sans réponse, l'essai passe quand même au chemin suivant, comme le demandait la tâche. Pour un flux MP3, les trois chemins visent la même adresse : un cycle dure donc 24 s, contre 8 s si l'on allait droit au backoff.
- Un serveur qui met plus de 8 s à répondre n'est plus jamais entendu. Avant, il finissait par jouer.
- Les trois `fetch` identiques de `startWav`, `startPcm` et `startMse` n'en font plus qu'un, `requestStream`.
- La borne de `audio.play()` et la garde de calage durent 8 s toutes les deux. La borne est armée avant `waiting`, donc c'est elle qui finit l'essai d'un élément qui n'a pas démarré. La garde reste pour un élément qui jouait, puis cale.
- L'attente de `AudioContext.resume()`, qui dure jusqu'au premier geste, reste hors de toute borne : chaque borne commence avec sa demande. Un commentaire le dit.
- Fusions de `main` : chaque fois, un seul conflit, dans `CHANGELOG.md`. Les lignes de `main` y gardent leur ordre, et la ligne de cette PR vient en dernier.

## Vérifié

- Cinq nouveaux parcours dans `barre.spec.ts`. Leur `page.route` sert le flux par un seul chemin, ou le laisse sans réponse ; `page.clock` saute les 8 s.
  - « un flux qui ne répond jamais » : le bouton ne dit rien tant que la demande attend, puis « ne répond pas » au bout de 8 s. Les demandes suivent l'ordre PCM, MSE, élément, puis de nouveau PCM après le backoff.
  - « l'élément audio sans réponse » : PCM et MSE échouent tout de suite, et l'événement `waiting` ne parvient pas à l'élément. Seule la borne de `play()` peut finir l'essai.
  - « par l'élément audio » et « en MSE, un flux qui s'arrête » : 0,1 s par connexion, jouée jusqu'au bout. Le bouton le dit, et le casque ne martèle plus.
  - « par l'élément audio, la reprise ne compte qu'après 3 s de son » : le flux revient, l'alerte tient encore 1 s après sa demande, puis le bouton redonne le retard du casque.
- Chaque mécanisme cassé exprès fait échouer ses parcours :
  - sans ces commits, les deux premiers restent sur « Retard du casque : 77 ms » et « Couper le casque » ;
  - sans la borne de `play()`, « l'élément audio sans réponse » échoue ;
  - en remettant le backoff à zéro au premier son, ou sans l'alerte de `bump`, les trois parcours « un flux qui s'arrête » et « 3 s de son » échouent, en MSE comme par l'élément ;
  - sans `onProgress`, l'alerte ne s'efface plus.
- `audio.played` dans Chromium vaut 1 après une lecture. Il revient à 0 après le démontage de `teardownStream`, et avec une nouvelle source.
- L'attente du premier geste : sous Playwright, Chromium démarre l'`AudioContext` sans geste, et aucun parcours versionné ne peut la montrer. Un parcours jetable, non commité, simule donc un contexte suspendu dont `resume()` attend un clic. Page rechargée sans geste, puis 20 s passées : aucune demande du flux, rien de signalé. Après le clic, la demande part, et le bouton ne dit rien avant ses 8 s.
- Tests de `monitorStream` : cinq nouveaux tests, quatre pour `answerWithin` (abandon à 8 s, réponse à temps, refus transmis tel quel, demande coupée qui échoue après coup) et un pour `playedSeconds`. Une version d'`answerWithin` qui ne gère pas l'échec tardif fait échouer le fichier (rejet non géré).
- Avant la fusion de `main` : 41 parcours verts, aussi avec une seconde suite lancée en parallèle. Les parcours du casque : 5 passages sur 5 chacun, la machine chargée par cette seconde suite.
- Après la dernière fusion de `main`, avec #30 : `./scripts/e2e.sh`, 47 parcours verts. `./scripts/verifier.sh` est bon sur moteur, liquidsoap, console, nginx et deploy. Services est sauté : l'environnement du catalogue n'est pas installé dans ce worktree, et la PR n'y touche pas.
- Relu deux fois par un agent sans le contexte de l'auteur, à partir du diff et de la tâche. Aucun défaut bloquant. Repris des relectures :
  - la borne de `play()` faisait double emploi avec la garde de calage, et aucun parcours ne la tenait seule. Un parcours la tient maintenant, en retenant `waiting` ;
  - la règle des 3 s : le MSE a son parcours, et `onProgress` ne compte plus le tampon d'une connexion perdue pendant l'attente d'une relance ;
  - le parcours « 3 s de son » se cale sur l'heure de la demande, et attend un nom précis à la fin ;
  - les parcours « un flux qui s'arrête » vérifient que l'élément a bien joué jusqu'au bout.

## Laissé pour plus tard

- Par l'élément seul, la reprise se juge sur le son joué, pas sur le débit comme en PCM. À la connexion, Icecast envoie d'un coup environ 4 s d'avance, à 128 kbit/s. Une connexion qui ne rend que cette avance, puis se tait, compte donc comme une reprise tenue : le bouton se tait, là où le PCM le dit. Il n'y a pas de martèlement, car un cycle dure au moins ces 4 s. Le MSE y échappe : il rattrape le direct et ne joue qu'1,2 s de cette avance. Ce chemin ne sert que si le décodeur PCM ne se charge pas et que le MSE manque.
- Une fausse alerte possible. Si Icecast est servi en HTTP/1.1, Chrome ouvre au plus 6 connexions par hôte, tous onglets confondus, et chaque console ouverte en tient une pour son casque. Au septième onglet, la demande reste en file chez le navigateur : le bouton dit alors que le flux ne répond pas, alors que c'est le navigateur qui la retient. Avant, l'attente était muette.

author: anth-volk
body:
Fixes #66

Part of #53.

## What this does

The fourth of the pull requests stacked on #55 that fix the Ruff findings #55 leaves ignored. It covers the findings in `BLE`, `S`, `T20` and `SLF`: 131 on #55, and 130 here, since #65 moved the root `conftest.py` under the tests' exemptions. Afterwards `pyproject.toml` no longer ignores those four families. Stacked on #65.

The emitter catches broad exceptions and prints to standard error on purpose: no call may raise into the build, a module's failure must not stop the host, and a failed cycle must leave the work queued. So most findings are kept with a `# noqa`, each with its reason in a comment above it, taken from the code. The fixes that change code don't change what a caller sees under the normal interpreter.

- **Two per-file ignores, each registered:**
  - **`emitter.quality.program-ruff-exemptions` (new):** `microcosm_emitter.cli` and `microcosm_emitter.host.__main__` run as programs (each has `if __name__ == "__main__":`), so they may print (`T201`), as the Public API's modules that run as programs do. This covers 6 findings. `orrery/cli.py` has no such guard, so its two prints keep a `# noqa`.
  - **`emitter.quality.installed-smoke-ruff-exemptions` (new):** `SLF001` for `tools/installed-smoke.py` and `tools/installed-interface-smoke.py`, which read the clients' private members to check the processes they started, as tests do. This covers 4 findings. `check-installed.py` has none, so it is not covered (round 1).
- **`BLE001` (61):** 60 handlers keep `except Exception` with `# noqa: BLE001`, because narrowing them would let exceptions reach the build, the host or the queue. The reasons fall into a few kinds: no call raises into the build, and the failure is reported instead; a failure rejects only this request; a failed cycle leaves the job queued for the next one. One `try`/`except`/`pass` becomes `contextlib.suppress(Exception)`, which behaves the same and also clears its `S110`.
- **`S101` (21):**
  - **19 become explicit checks.** Each invariant `assert x is not None, "message"` in package code becomes `if x is None: raise AssertionError(...)`, with the same message. Under the normal interpreter this behaves the same. Under `python -O` the check now runs, where the assert was skipped.
  - **The other two too (round 1):** the runtime's worker shutdown gets its dispatcher from a new `_started_requests` helper, which raises the same `AssertionError` outside the `try` block, as the stack handles `TRY301` elsewhere. The sanitizer's invariant is an explicit check that raises `AssertionError`, with `# noqa: TRY004` and its reason, as #58 handles type checks that keep their exception.
- **`T201` (16 more):** messages written on purpose keep `print`, with `# noqa: T201`. One note per module, after its imports, says why: each print marked so writes one of its messages to standard error on purpose, and none is leftover debugging output. `orrery/cli.py`'s two prints write the command's receipt on standard output. (Round 1 removed 14 copies of a comment claiming `print` cannot raise on a missing `sys.stderr`, which was not the reason and not exact.)
- **`S105` (13):** environment variable names, a URL path, status codes and messages whose constant names contain "TOKEN". None is a secret, and the constants keep their names.
- **`S603` (2):** both launchers run the emitter's own command.
- **`S310` (1):** an origin the code checked first.
- **`S506` (3, tests):** `yaml.BaseLoader` stays. It keeps YAML's `on` key a string, as GitHub reads it.
- **`S324` (1, a test fake):** SHA-1 is called with `usedforsecurity=False`, which changes no digest.
- **`SLF001` (1 more):** the host client's `ModuleClient` calls `SocketClient._request` in the same module.
- **Ruff no longer ignores `BLE`, `S`, `SLF` and `T20`.**

A helper agent wrote the suppressions and reasons from a brief I gave it, with the decisions above. I checked the result: of the 36 changed Python files, 28 changed only in comments or layout (their syntax trees are identical). The other 8 hold the explicit checks, `contextlib.suppress` and `usedforsecurity`.

## Test-first record

There is no red step, since nothing changes behaviour under the normal interpreter.

| Commit | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `9478355` The fixes and the two per-file ignores | `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass. All five guards pass with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main`. The 8 test functions whose source lines changed (only comments, in their `except` lines) pass by node ID (9 cases). |
| `59fc416` Merge of #65's round 1 | `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass. |
| `faa6a99` The changelog fragment | `tools/bump-version.py --check` passes. |

Review round 1:

| Commit | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `5b2be26` The last two asserts, the narrower `SLF001` exemption, one print note per module, the configuration comment and the fragment | `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and the five guards pass. No test function changed. |

No other test was run; CI runs them.

## CI

No workflow, trigger or script changes, and no environment variable or secret is read differently.

## Release

The fragment is `changelog.d/ruff-safety.changed.md`. With #65's `added` fragment below it in the stack, merging releases a minor version (0.12.0 now); on its own this fragment would give a patch bump.

_Requested by **Luca** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GwSC4gJZ8haoLRuWg8HXdW?thread=cmsg_01GwSC4gJZ8haoLRuWg8HXdWBaRfjBJWgmV2fpW2GAE3UZ)_

Task: t-044 · card q-lan-match (Luca OK'd 30 Oct) · brief `docs/lan-step2.md` (PR #64), part 2.

**This PR contains PR #67 (t-043, two humans) and must merge after it.** It's branched from `worker-l/t-043-two-humans`; once #67 is in, this diff shrinks to the network part.

## What changed and why
The co-designer, 30 Oct: "Players should only have to press Host or Join." Step 1 showed claude.ai pages have no WebRTC, but a copy served on one laptop connects PC to PC (avg 34.5 ms, 121 ms spikes). So:
- **`tools/lan/serve.py`** (Python 3, standard library only): serves `game/` on port 8770 to the Wi-Fi and is the **matchmaker**: HOST posts its offer, JOIN reads the rooms (one = straight in, several = pick), the answer goes back by long poll. No codes on screen. Rooms close when answered or after 2 min. It never carries match traffic.
- **`Start LAN.command`** (Mac) / **`Start LAN.bat`** (Windows): double-click to start; the window shows the address for PC 2 (the laptop's name, e.g. `xxx.local:8770`, plus the IP as backup) and opens the game.
- **`game/src/lan.js`**: **PLAY ON LAN** on the start screen (only when the page comes from serve.py: hidden on claude.ai). HOST / JOIN, then a FIFA-style friendly lobby: each picks his own team as YOU (host = home), both READY. The host then goes through settings, team sheet, walk-out as normal; PC 2 sees those menus.
- **The host runs the only match.** PC 2 sends its buttons every frame (io.js `netPad`: state + a press counter per button, so a quick tap or a lost packet never loses a press) and they drive part 1's away human. The host sends 30 snapshots/s on an unordered, no-resend channel; **PC 2 draws them ~100 ms behind, sliding between two**, so a 120 ms spike is a short hold, not a desync. It never simulates.
- **Edges:** either PC pauses both; only the one who paused can resume (PC 2: ENTER resume, Q quit). QUIT sends both to the menu. A silent line for 3 s = CONNECTION LOST on both, back to the menu after 10 s; no AI takes over.
- **Part 1's review note fixed:** the hints show each player's own keys (`keyset(team)`): #2p home = ARROWS, away = WASD; a LAN guest's hints use the key set he picked. #2p help line shows both players' keys.

### How real football / other games do it (used here)
FIFA / EA FC and eFootball online: one authoritative side, inputs in, state out, the client smooths with a small delay. Sensible Soccer / Kick Off's 2-machine link: one host, the other sends input. Rollback (Rocket League, fighting games) skipped, as the brief says. Football-wise: both screens show the same score, clock, kick-off, goals, replays and Rami; a pause or a disconnect stops it for both.

### Choices I made (worth a look)
- **PC 2 mirrors the picture, not the rules.** Each snapshot carries every sprite as the host drew it (frame, position, depth, origin, flip) plus camera, score bug, messages, SP meters, the menus' text, sounds and Rami's lines. So walk-outs, replays, dives, rigs and celebrations all show without PC 2 knowing how they work. ~2 KB per snapshot, fine on Wi-Fi.
- **Input delay:** the host applies the newest guest packet as it arrives (it's ~1-3 frames on Wi-Fi anyway); the press counters do the job the brief's 2-3 frame buffer was for (no lost presses).
- **Not mirrored yet:** the special-save cut-in art, the power / aim graphics under PC 2's own man (he sees his cursor, the radar, energy and messages), and the pass ring. Easy follow-ups if they matter in the 2-PC test.
- **No hand-copy fallback.** If PC 2 can't reach the laptop it can't load the game either, so the codes wouldn't help; "TROUBLE CONNECTING?" gives the firewall steps instead.
- index.html loads Phaser from the CDN as always, so the Wi-Fi needs internet (a home Wi-Fi does).
- Tiny edits in `matchflow.js` and `specials.js` (outside the brief's file list) to pass the team into the key hints. Same strings in single-player.
- Security: serve.py answers private / loopback addresses only (others get 403), serves `game/` only (no folder listings, no uploads), keeps offers/answers in memory 2 min max.

## After the first 2-PC test (30 Oct, Luca: "terrible connection, it was lost immediately")
Cause not known yet (no log from the PCs), so three changes on this branch:
- **serve.py fixes the hidden addresses:** Chrome / Edge hide each PC's address behind a random `.local` name, which some routers and Windows setups can't look up. The server sees each PC's real address, so it adds a copy of every `.local` candidate with that address.
- **The black window now logs the link** from both PCs: candidates, the route chosen, ping every 15 s, and *why* it was lost (closed channel, failed link, or nothing heard; page hidden or not).
- CONNECTION LOST after 5 s of silence (was 3 s: too touchy while a laptop loads the kits). If the PCs never connect, the screen says so instead of "CONNECTING..." forever.
`node tools/lanmatch.js`: OK again (with `SRVLOG=1` it prints the server window's lines).

## How to try it
**The published preview on claude.ai can't run LAN (its sandbox has no WebRTC), so trying it means serve.py.**

**The 2-PC test (Luca + the co-designer), about 10 minutes:**
1. On the laptop that serves, get this branch: GitHub Desktop or `git fetch && git checkout worker-l/t-044-lan-network` in the repo folder.
2. **Mac:** Finder → the repo → `tools/lan` → double-click **Start LAN.command**. Blocked? Right-click it → **Open** → **Open**. Asked to install developer tools? **Install**, then double-click again.
   **Windows:** File Explorer → the repo → `tools\lan` → double-click **Start LAN.bat**. No Python? Install from python.org with "Add python.exe to PATH" ticked. **Windows Security** pops up → tick **Private networks** → **Allow access**.
3. A window shows two addresses. On the **other PC**, type the first one into Chrome or Edge (if it doesn't open, the second, the number). Bookmark it.
4. One PC: **PLAY ON LAN → HOST**. Other PC: pick your team under YOU, then **PLAY ON LAN → JOIN**. Both **READY**.
5. Play a half. Note: the ping feel, any stutter, whether the goals / replays / Rami show on both. Try a pause from each side.
6. Doesn't open on PC 2: the laptop firewall (Mac: System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options → allow Python). Steps also under "TROUBLE CONNECTING?" in the game.

**Test Lab:** nothing new. **FREE PLAY button:** not needed, there's no new move.

## Files
New: `game/src/lan.js`, `tools/lan/serve.py`, `tools/lan/Start LAN.command`, `tools/lan/Start LAN.bat`, `tools/lanmatch.js`.
Changed: `game/src/io.js` (netPad, keyset per team), `match.js` (guest branch, pause hold, teams hook), `ui.js` (pause / quit hooks, guest cursor colour, hints), `matchflow.js` + `specials.js` (hint team arg), `game/index.html` / `lab.html` / `test.html` (lan.js in load order), `game/src/README.md`, `tools/lan/README.md` ("Play a LAN match").

## Test results
- `node tools/lanmatch.js` (serve.py + two headless pages that only press PLAY ON LAN, HOST / JOIN, READY; host ENTERs through the settings; 60 s of play):
  ```
  ok   HOST + JOIN connected through serve.py
  away human (the guest's stick, on the host): moved 846 frames, 763 along the stick, 83 not
  guest drew 1164 frames (33 during the spikes)
  ok   the guest's scripted inputs move the away player
  ok   the guest kept drawing through the 120 ms spikes
  host  IS 0-0 IRO · 1ST 09:30
  guest IS 0-0 IRO · 1ST 09:30
  ok   score and clock agree on both pages
  ok   the host paused: both stop, the guest is told
  ok   the guest paused both, the host couldn't resume, the guest did
  ok   the guest left: CONNECTION LOST on the host after 3.1 s, the match stopped
  ok   back to the menu 10 s later
  ok   no page errors
  lan match: OK
  ```
- Single-player u

author: gomaja
body: Regenerate TCAP and MAP with the compiler from gomaja/protocol-compilers#158. - **IMPLICIT and EXPLICIT positions:** with `TrackTCAPForm`, `ValidateBERElement` checks the X.690 form and contents rules at every schema-known position of TCAP's own syntax where the grammar admits the tag: - the IMPLICIT base types, including the absent linked ID's NULL (X.690 (02/2021) §8.14.4); - EXPLICIT tags, which must be constructed (§8.14.3). A well-formed element at a position the grammar does not admit still passes the scan, and decoders report it with `ErrUnexpectedElement` as before. - **Open values:** `ROSSingleAS`, `ROSConsumerAS`, `ROSSupplierAS`, `Bind` and `Unbind` apply Q.773 (06/97) §4.1.1 to their envelope and stop at the TC-user's open values, as `ROS` does since #184. X.690's own rules still apply inside those values. - **REAL:** both runtimes check REAL contents under X.690 §8.5 in BER, with a byte scan that does not allocate. A malformed REAL keeps its X.690 sentinel. DER keeps the §11.3 normalization. - **Speed:** TCAP's scan carries compact schema kinds and reads its parent frame in place, so the new checks keep the validator's throughput. Results: - The SS7 and validation suites pass. Two generations of each package are byte-identical. - The 160 TCAP and 99 MAP fixed-input comparison rows are unchanged against main `1eddc4da`. The only new acceptances are the open values of #248. - Decode and scan allocation counts are unchanged. - Speed against main: TCAP's 15 scorecard rows are within 5% (geomean +1.1%), and MAP's 268 rows give +0.89% with no row confirmed above 5%. Bytes and allocations per operation are unchanged. #247 stays open for the shared `runtime/ber` package, which only the eSIM packages use. #250 (primitive Bind and Unbind tags) and #251 (a primitive EXTERNAL `single-ASN1-type` inside TC-user values) predate this change and are tracked separately. Closes #246 Closes #248 Closes #249 Refs #247 --- ## Summary by cubic Regenerates TCAP and MAP with the updated compiler so TCAP validation checks X.690 form and contents rules at schema-known IMPLICIT and EXPLICIT positions, and both BER runtimes validate REAL contents in BER. Closes #246, #248, and #249. - IMPLICIT base types (including the absent linked ID's NULL) and EXPLICIT tags, which must be constructed, are now checked where TCAP's grammar admits them. - `ROSSingleAS`, `ROSConsumerAS`, `ROSSupplierAS`, `Bind`, and `Unbind` now stop at the TC-user's open values, as `ROS` already does; X.690 rules still apply inside those values. - REAL contents are validated with a non-allocating byte scan; DER keeps its existing normalization, and malformed REALs retain their X.690 sentinel. - The SS7 and validation suites pass, and decode and scan allocation counts are unchanged. Written for commit f34a3dc3b560a367177c3b439baf93796ce5d843. Summary will update on new commits.

## Wat

Story #51: de eisen die Omnibus stelt voordat het aan de Rijksmap koppelt ([Omnibus #151](https://github.com/Robert-Worm/omnibus/issues/151), Omnibus-besluit B-020). Elke eis hoort nu bij een story.

| # | Eis van Omnibus | Story |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Vaste ID's per rapport, nooit hergebruikt of hernoemd | #23 (ID's), #27 (oude adressen koppelen). **Let op voor #23:** Omnibus gebruikt nu al de slug uit `rijksmap.nl/rapport/<slug>/` voor claims en dubbelingen. Die slug moet een blijvende verwijzing houden. |
| 2 | Database met versies: downloadbare release met datum en inhoudsopgave | **Nieuw: R11-2** |
| 3 | SHA-256 per document en per release | **Nieuw: R11-2** (release) en **R11-3** (document) |
| 4 | Open, gedocumenteerde toegang, alleen lezen, zonder account, met licentie | #31 (API), #32 (open data), #52 (MCP); licentie CC0 bestaat al |
| 5 | Dezelfde kwaliteitsregels: herkomst, HOLD bij twijfel, tests | #24 (herkomst), #10 (tests), **nieuw: R11-4** (HOLD) |
| 6 | Relaties tussen rapporten (dubbelingen, managementreacties) met eigen ID | **Nieuw: R11-1** |
| | Toets door de beheerder (B-020) | **Nieuw: R11-5** |

## Bestanden

- `.github/backlog/koppeling-omnibus-2026-10.mjs`: epic **EP-R11 · Klaar voor de koppeling met Omnibus**, met vijf stories.
- `.github/backlog/volgorde.mjs`: plek per story.
  - HOLD (R11-4) in het datamodel, direct na de herkomst.
  - Relaties (R11-1) na de extractie.
  - Release (R11-2) na de gelijkheidstest.
  - Controlegetal per document (R11-3) later: veel ophaalwerk.
  - Toets (R11-5) aan het eind.
- `docs/routekaart.md`: EP-R11 in de tabel.

## Volgorde van samenvoegen

Bouwt voort op #74 (en daarmee op #69, #70, #72 en #73).

## Getest

- `node --test .github/scripts/backlog.test.mjs hosting/site/server.test.mjs`: 16 van 16 geslaagd. De test controleert ook dat elke nieuwe story een plek in de volgorde heeft, na zijn voorgangers.
- Droge run van de werkvolgorde: 68 stories, de nieuwe op de verwachte plekken.

## Raakt dit de live site?

Nee.

Closes #51

author: kaike-vitorino
body:
O editor de Workflows passa a executar fluxos no motor nativo do MLX Pilot, com persistência e histórico no daemon, importação de arquivos n8n, webhooks e ferramentas MCP por stdio. Esta integração recupera os cinco commits ainda não mesclados de `feat/native-flow-engine`, preservando a autoria original.

- Adiciona o crate `mlx-flow`, catálogo de 11 nós, expressões, ramificações, tentativas e execução paralela limitada; remove a dependência do runtime n8n.
- Integra seletores de provedor/modelo, conexões no canvas, duplicação de nós, contagem de itens e cadastro/sondagem de servidores MCP.
- Corrige prazo global da execução, registros de irmãos já executados, respostas HTTP truncadas e duas quebras de sintaxe no CSS do editor.
- Inclui previews reproduzíveis e protege caminhos fora da pasta servida, URLs malformadas e NUL; preserva a demonstração gravada e seu script.
- Acrescenta smoke com daemon real e dados temporários ao CI, além das regressões dos previews e de toda a interface desktop.

Validação local em Windows: 472 testes Rust e 1 doctest; Clippy com `-D warnings`; rustfmt; 41 testes da interface; 16 testes de preview. O smoke com o binário final passou para salvar/carregar/excluir fluxos, ambos os ramos de condição, expressões, histórico, ciclos inválidos, importação, webhook, MCP real por stdio e ferramenta no workspace isolado. A verificação no navegador confirmou criação, execução e histórico de um fluxo, além do carregamento do Presentation Studio, sem erros de console. Inferência com um modelo de IA real não foi repetida nesta integração.

As correções estão em microcommits separados, com `Authorized-by: Kaike-Vitorino`; o merge deve preservar os commits.

author: ginwa123
body:
## What

A workspace has **members** with roles, and an invite is a **request the invitee accepts** —
nobody gets a workspace handed to them by a stranger.

- **Settings → Workspace → Members**: roster, invite form (creates an *invitation*), a revocable
  "Pending invitations" block, per-row role change, removal.
- **The inbox**: the invitee sees `INVITATIONS · <workspace> · Accept / Decline` at the top of the
  sidebar workspace switcher. Accept is what creates the membership.

`workspace_members` (Migration 100) already decided *who may see a workspace*; this PR adds the
feature on top of it, plus **Migration 123** for the pending asks.

## The rule this PR exists for

| step | membership row | what the invitee can do |
|---|---|---|
| owner invites by email | **none** | nothing — the workspace is not in their list |
| invitee accepts | created, with the invited role, in one transaction | reads the roster, opens the workspace |
| invitee declines / owner revokes | none, and the ask is deleted | nothing |

There is **no direct add**: `POST /api/workspaces/:id/members` is gone. The only way a membership
row appears is `accept`.

## API

| method | path | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/members` | `{members, count}` — owners first; each row carries `workspace_id` now |
| `PATCH` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/members/:user_id` | `{role}`; last owner → 409 |
| `DELETE` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/members/:user_id` | last owner → 409 |
| `GET` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/invitations` | pending asks (owner/admin: rows carry emails) |
| `POST` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/invitations` | `{email, role}` → 201 *pending*; 404 names the address; 409 member/duplicate |
| `DELETE` | `/api/workspaces/:workspace_id/invitations/:invitation_id` | revoke |
| `GET` | `/api/invitations` | the caller's own inbox — keyed on the resolved caller, never a parameter |
| `POST` | `/api/invitations/:invitation_id/accept` | **the only writer of a membership row** |
| `POST` | `/api/invitations/:invitation_id/decline` | the ask is deleted, nothing else changes |

Gate (`workspace_members_gate.zig`): read = your own member row; write = owner/admin; an invisible
workspace is **404**, a visible one you may not administer is **403**; somebody else's invitation is
**404**, never 403.

## UI proof — driven through the real browser on an isolated instance

Server: the built binary, `HOME=/tmp/...` (throwaway), `--auth`, port **8099** (8081 untouched),
serving the real Vite bundle. Two accounts via `create-admin`: `owner@example.com` and
`teammate@example.com`. Driven with `agent-browser`; the steps below are the actual DOM read back.

**1. Owner invites `teammate@example.com` as Editor** — the roster still has ONE member:

```
Members panel:
  "People who can open ws_…fb501. An invite is a request: the account you name is asked first
   and gains nothing until it accepts. Owners and Admins can manage this list."
  Email [teammate@example.com]   Role [Editor]   [Invite]
  Pending invitations
  "Waiting for an answer. These accounts cannot see this workspace yet."
    teammate@example.com   EDITOR   [Revoke]
  list: owner@example.com  (Owner)  ⌫(disabled — last owner)
```

**2. The invited account, before answering** — the workspace is not theirs:

```
workspace switcher:
  INVITATIONS
    Acme (owner)   [Accept] [Decline]
  Default 1 ✓            ← their own workspace, the only one
```
A deep link to the owner's workspace renders an **empty main pane** (the API 404s; nothing leaks).

**3. After clicking Accept — no reload**:

```
workspace switcher:
  Default 1
  Acme (owner) 1 ✓       ← appears and becomes active
  (INVITATIONS block gone)
URL: /app/ws_…fb501      ← navigated by the accept handler
```

**4. The invitee is an editor** — the roster is readable, the controls are not there:

```
"Only owners and admins can invite or remove people in this workspace."
owner@example.com
teammate@example.com
(no invite form, no role select, no remove button, and NO red error banner)
```

**5. Back on the owner's side** — the invitee is a member, the ask is gone:

```
list: owner@example.com (Owner) ⌫   |   teammate@example.com (Editor) ⌫
(no Pending invitations block)
```

### Two bugs this walkthrough found (both fixed here)

1. **Accept did nothing visible.** The accept response carried no `workspace_id`, so the client
   no-oped after a successful accept and the new workspace only appeared after a manual reload.
   `MemberRow` / `WorkspaceMember` now carry `workspace_id`; verified live (step 3 above).
2. **An editor got a red error banner** for a permission they simply lack (`invitations pending
   failed: Only a workspace owner or admin can do that`). A 403 is now an *answer*: the panel goes
   read-only with a note instead of reporting a broken request.

## Wire proof (isolated `--auth` server, random port)

`tests/functional/workspace_members_test.zig` — 6 tests, all green, no leaks:

```
1/6 an invite is a pending request: the invitee gains NO access until it is accepted...OK
2/6 accepting the invitation is what creates the membership...OK
3/6 declining and revoking both remove the request and grant nothing...OK
4/6 inviting needs owner or admin; an invited editor may read but not invite...OK
5/6 invite answers 404 for an unknown address and 409 for a duplicate ask...OK
6/6 a workspace cannot be left without an owner...OK
All 6 tests passed.
```

They assert, among other things: the inviter's member list still has one row after the invite; the
invitee's `/members` is 404; the inbox shows the ask; a third party's `accept` is 404 and the ask
stays pending; after accept the roster has two rows and the workspace appears in the invitee's
`/api/workspaces`.

## Red-before-green

Removing the membership `INSERT` from `store.accept` (mutation) turns the store test red:

```
error: 'agentic_loop.workspace_invitations_store.test.accept turns the invitation into a
        membership with the invited role, and deletes the ask' failed
Build Summary: 30/32 steps succeeded (1 failed); 5489/5494 tests passed (4 skipped, 1 failed)
```
Restored → green. (An earlier mutation of the gate's `.manage` prong also turned 2 unit tests and 1
wire test red.)

## Gates

- `zig build test --summary all` → **32/32 steps, 5490/5494 passed** (4 pre-existing platform skips).
- `scripts/check-zig-test-output-clean.sh --run` → **"ok green run: no logger line and no
  'failed command:' block"**.
- `npx vitest --run` → **27 failed files | 612 passed (639)**, against **28 failed | 610** on the
  base commit (`git stash` baseline): **no new failures**, one base flake passed.
- `pnpm run lint:check` → **0 errors**; 87 pre-existing `max-file-lines` warnings, none in the new
  files.
- `zginlint` / comment rule: every comment block ≤3 lines, verified by CI's
  `zginlint (comment-block ceiling, zero findings)`.

## Not done / knowingly left

- **No email delivery**, so the inbox is in-app only (switcher + Members section). The invitation
  row is the right anchor for a token the day mail exists.
- Migration 123 refuses no legacy data because the table is new; a DB that already had direct adds
  keeps those members (they consented to nothing, but they were also added by this PR's own
  unmerged commit — no production DB has them).
- Pre-existing CI flake, unchanged by this PR: `functional_ui/agent_system_prompt_ui_test.py::test_edit_system_prompt_via_dialog`
  fails on `main` (run 41121491568) too.

author: kadi-r
body:
Every Tulevane Mina text now has English, written step by step from the Estonian (plan PRs 4–9 in one pull request). Terms follow the Tulevane Mina term table, tuleva.ee and the Social Insurance Board: retirement age, II/III pillar, monthly payouts, payout agreement, Keep saving, yearly rate, additional contribution, tax benefit; dates as "1 November 2026"; UK English.

## Commits

1. **Tests: useIntl reads the IntlProvider of the test, with English as the fallback.** `setupTests.js` mocked `useIntl` to always return English, so components using `useIntl` showed English even under an Estonian `IntlProvider`. Tulevane Mina tests only passed because its English was still Estonian. Separate commit so it can be reviewed on its own.
2. **Sina:** the step, the trail and navigation, the running summary bar, required marks, the error summary, the FAQ and the 24 help topics of the step. The trail is announced as „Tulevase Mina sammud“ instead of „Loo etapid“. Block headings and FAQ questions use `text-balance`; „list 1 or 2“ keeps together.
3. **Kulud:** cost levels, breakdown, household, care home and source line, household and care home help.
4. **55 ja 60:** the III pillar step at 55, the II and III pillar step five years before retirement age (including the new outcome texts from PR89), payout choices and the monthly payouts FAQ.
5. **65 ja eripension:** retirement age step (early retirement, working on, deferring or taking half, pillar choices, comparison tables and FAQ), special pension step and the special or old-age pension choice.
6. **66+:** monthly payout start, agreement, end age and locked states; the FAQ says "agreement" instead of "contract".
7. **Tulemus:** answer, tiles, income list, chart (legend, events, notes, table, screen reader texts), warning and surplus, decisions, assumptions, legacy, rules, saving the result, and the result help.
8. **Final check:** every `futureMe` key belongs to a step and has English that is not the Estonian text.

Estonian changes are small: sentences in the "we" form now say „arvutus“ or „Tulevane Mina“.

## Tests

`stepTexts.test.ts` checks each step's texts: translated, no Estonian letters in English, the agreed terms, English dates, and the same tags and ICU placeholders as the Estonian. Each step was added to the check first (red), then translated (green). Full suite green: 6054 tests, `tsc` and `lint` clean.

author: ascoding11
body:
Each clock starts the next one while it is itself still finishing. The successor's stand-aside check therefore always found a "running" clock and quit, and the chain died. On 2026-10-30 nothing ran after 17:04 UTC, so the flip, auction, foreign and end-of-day jobs were all missed.

The successor is now started with `successor=true` and skips the check. Only watchdog and manual runs stand aside.

author: cjgimena
body:
## Problem

In the fullscreen video: click a point in the list, move to another point with the arrow keys, then press Space to pause. The film jumps back to the point that was clicked. Enter did the same.

## Cause

A point row or shot keeps focus after its click, and the room's arrow keys walk the film without moving that focus. Space then reached the row's own key handler first, which seeked to that row, and the room's window handler toggled play on top of it.

## Fix

- **Pressing a row or shot in the room's drawer no longer gives it focus, and clears focus from whatever held it** (`film-room-drawer.tsx`), so Enter cannot re-trigger an older control such as Next point. This covers the row's bookmark button too, since its press bubbles up to the drawer.
- **The room owns Space** (`spaceIsPlayPause` on `PointList`, set only by `FilmRoomDrawer`). A row reached with Tab answers Enter, and Space stays play and pause.
- **A row answers only its own keys** (`point-list.tsx`). Enter on the bookmark used to seek and cancel the toggle. This one applies on the Video tab as well as in the room.

## Behaviour notes

- A row clicked with a mouse no longer holds the room's chrome awake, because the idle hold was reading that focus. The chrome now fades after 3s of playing as it does elsewhere; any mouse movement or key brings it back.
- Space on a focused bookmark in the room plays or pauses rather than toggling it, because the room claims Space. Enter and the S shortcut toggle it.

## Not changed

The non-fullscreen Video tab's rows keep Space and the arrows on purpose, as the comment in `film-tab.tsx` explains. So clicking a row there and pressing Space still restarts that point.

## Testing

- Five new tests in `tests/film-playback-refresh.spec.ts`: a clicked row (including pausing a playing film and Enter), a clicked row clearing focus from an older control, a tabbed-to row, a clicked shot, and Enter on a bookmark. Each part of the fix was removed in turn and a test failed without it.
- The no-seek checks count writes to the video's `currentTime`, so they need no timed wait.
- The full suite passes on this tip (8587 passed, 442 skipped), with lint and typecheck clean.
- The key and focus behaviour is tested in the offline harness only, not by hand on a real match. The eyes-on pass reached a film room on a match with video and saw no regression on screen, but its harness cannot press keys or a room row.

author: pinetheapple
body:
## What changed

With the system's remove-animations setting on, the metronome's continuous motion now holds still. The on-beat colour swap still carries the beat (SPEC §12.3).

- **Bar sweep** (`BarSweep.tsx`): under reduce motion, `sweepFill` returns an empty fill and the track is hidden (opacity 0, height kept, so the tempo arrows' hit areas don't move). Before, an empty track while playing looked frozen.
- **Ramp progress bar** (`StatusStack.tsx`): the engine reports step progress continuously (`tempo_ramp.cpp:106-113`), and a step can be 1 bar long, so this was a second sweep. Under reduce motion, `rampProgressFill` now builds the fill from the countdown's own ticks (`rampRemainingTicks` in `statusRows.ts`, the single source shared with `rampRemainingText`). The bar steps exactly when the countdown text changes, including fractional time intervals such as 2.5 s or 0.05 min. When a step is a single tick (for example a 1-bar ramp), the track is hidden instead of sitting permanently empty.
- One small hook, `useStillMotion`, mirrors Reanimated's `useReducedMotion()` into a SharedValue that both worklets read. Only the setting goes through React; per-frame values stay on the UI thread (§13.3).
- The sweep clamp now reuses `clampUnit` from core-design.

**Checked, already compliant:** beat LEDs, beat dots, poly dots, count-in squares and mute status swap colour or opacity in one step. Pulse marks and status rows jump without easing. Swipe-tempo feedback only changes the number (and a haptic tick). The swipe hint and sheets were already gated. The LED pulse in the HTML design was never built natively.

**Known limit:** Reanimated's `useReducedMotion()` reads the setting once at startup. A change takes effect after an app restart, and the same is true of the tuner and the sheets today. A live toggle would need a shared `AccessibilityInfo` listener in core-design; that is not part of this PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With reduce motion on, the beat cue is a static on-beat colour change: no sweep or pulse movement (code and tests say so; needs the device)
- [ ] With it off, nothing changes from today (needs the device)
- [x] No realtime value moves into React state (§13.3)
- [ ] Verified on a device with the setting toggled

## Verification

- tool-metronome vitest: `Tests 185 passed (185)`
- `bash scripts/preflight.sh --skip-android --no-fix`: `preflight: all gates passed`
- `pnpm -w test --force --concurrency=2`: `Tasks: 10 successful, 10 total`
- Sabotage:
  - `sweepFill` ignoring reduce motion: "holds still at every phase" fails.
  - Ramp fill ignoring reduce motion: 8 of 12 fail.
  - Ramp fill computed from progress instead of the countdown: the 2.5 s case and the fractional-interval property tests fail.
  - Each file was restored with an empty `git diff`.

## Still needs the device

- Turn remove animations on, **restart the app**, and play with a ramp (1-bar and 4-bar steps, plus a seconds-based ramp). The sweep track should be hidden and the ramp bar should only step when its countdown text changes (hidden for 1-bar steps). The dots and LEDs should still change colour on each beat.
- Turn it off, restart, and check the sweep and ramp bar move smoothly as before.

Closes #188

author: jaygeraghty
body:
When Traeger refuses the login, the error now says **why**.

- It includes Amazon Cognito's own reason, for example "User does not exist.", "Incorrect username or password." or "Password attempts exceeded". The password is scrubbed out of the message, and a test checks that.

- `config.example.toml` notes that the password is plain text, and that it needs single quotes if it contains `\` or `"`.

The login itself is unchanged. It sends the email and password as plain text over HTTPS (`USER_PASSWORD_AUTH`), the same as the Home Assistant Traeger integrations, and a test now pins that down.

author: tapionx
body:
## Summary

Sandbox design for phase 0, revised after three spikes run on 2026-10-30.

- **ADR-0021 (Accepted): enforce sandbox egress on the host with a dedicated nftables table.** A network guard container maintains `table inet mazzamurello`, which matches only traffic from the sandbox bridge: it drops the ranges of SBX-005, all IPv6, and everything addressed to the host. It does not touch Docker's rules or firewall managers.
- **ADR-0022 (Accepted): a minimal sandbox driver**, sole holder of Docker API access, with a fixed policy (runsc only, no privileges, no host mounts, no credentials), file transfer to and from the workspace, and fail-closed startup checks (gVisor release, egress table, canary sandbox).
- **ADR-0023 (Accepted): gVisor as the single isolation runtime.** Mazzamurello must run on cloud VMs without `/dev/kvm`, and ships one sandbox implementation. microVMs (microsandbox, Firecracker, Kata, libkrun) are rejected because they require KVM.

## Evidence

| Spike | Host | Design | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | Debian 12, Intel N95, gVisor `release-20261026.0` | nftables in a sidecar sharing the sandbox's network namespace | Failed: the gVisor sandbox reached the host's LAN address (gVisor sends frames through an `AF_PACKET` socket, bypassing the namespace's netfilter) |
| v2 | Ubuntu 26.04 | Router container as the gateway of a Docker `--internal` network | Failed: Docker drops off-subnet destinations on internal networks |
| v3 | Ubuntu 26.04, AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, **no `/dev/kvm`**, gVisor `release-20261026.0` | Dedicated host nftables table on the sandbox bridge | Passed: internet and DNS work; host LAN address, `docker0`, bridge gateway, other sandboxes and IPv6 blocked, each checked against a control container; also blocked for a container with `NET_ADMIN` and raw sockets rewriting its own routes |

Also measured: target workloads (apt, pip, ffmpeg, ImageMagick, poppler, LibreOffice, matplotlib) run under gVisor with acceptable overhead; memory and CPU limits work; `--pids-limit` does not count gVisor processes while `--ulimit nproc` does (even for root); `--storage-opt size` is unsupported on ext4.

Not yet verified: blocking of the cloud metadata endpoint on a real cloud VM (covered by the blocked ranges; required in the SBX-005 security tests).

## Requirements

Refs: SBX-002, SBX-003, SBX-005, SBX-007, SBX-011, SBX-013, SBX-014, SBX-015, SBX-016, SBX-017, OPS-002, OPS-009

- Revised: SBX-002, SBX-003, SBX-005, SBX-007, SBX-011, SBX-015, OPS-002.
- New: SBX-013 (no unfiltered IPv6), SBX-014 (file exchange), SBX-016 (disk limit), SBX-017 (minimum gVisor release), OPS-009 (hosts without KVM).
- Threat model: new T-18 (egress rules disappear while sandboxes run). Glossary: sandbox bridge, network guard, egress table, canary sandbox.

## Checklist

- [x] Every commit is signed off.
- [x] Artifacts are in English and use glossary terms.

author: yoyobatty
body:
A player reported that the E-V Plasma Cannon 9000 gets no more ammo from the ammo slider, and asked for the rate of fire slider to go up to 3.

### Magazine Size Scale on guns with no magazine
The scale only touched magazines, so the guns that fire straight from their cells ignored it: HVPC Mk5, HVPC Mk66 (the E-V Plasma Cannon 9000), HMC, HVC Mk9 and Supercharger.

`Ammo_HVPCCells` and `Ammo_HVCCells` now have `bScalesAsMagazine`. Their cap and what a new gun comes with follow the scale, on the server and on clients, as `MaxAmmo` isn't replicated. It sits on the ammo so that the cap is right from the moment the ammo exists, and so that everything on those cells follows, including the LS14 Laser Gatling layout and the Wendigo's secondary fire.

| Scale | Mk5, Mk66, HMC: most / new gun | HVC Mk9, Supercharger: most / new gun |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 125 / 100 | 75 / 75 |
| 1 | 250 / 100 | 150 / 150 |
| 1.5 | 375 / 150 | 225 / 225 |
| 3 | 750 / 300 | 450 / 450 |

- Under 1 the cap shrinks, but what a gun comes with only stops at the cap: one Mk66 shot can take 100 cells, and at 0.5 a new one could not fire otherwise.
- A thrown gun, a spare gun picked up and `GetKillResupplyAmmo` use the scaled figure. Cell pick-ups, ammo packs and extra loadout copies give what they always gave, and the Conflict loadout list still shows the class's figure.
- The Proton Streamer stays out: its ammo is charge that builds up, and it stops firing at the class's cap.
- The hint says so. The line in `BallisticProV55.int` needs the same change, or it overrides the new text.

### Weapons report the ammo's own cap
The engine's `Weapon.MaxAmmo` reads the class default, so `AmmoMaxed` and `DesireAmmo` ignored a scaled cap and the magazine added with reloading off. At scale 3 a bot would call a gun full at 250 of 750 cells, and at 0.5 go after cells it can't carry. `BallisticWeapon.MaxAmmo` now reads the ammo.

### A dropped gun keeps what it holds
Found by the test below, and older than this change. With reloading off, and on the LS14 Laser Gatling layout, the cap only grew after the gun's rounds had gone in, so a player with none of that ammo got at most the class's cap from a dropped gun. `RaiseNoMagCap` now comes first, in `GiveAmmo` and in the four weapons with their own copy of it (RCS-715, MK781, Pug, Bulldog).

| Dropped holding, scale 1 | Picked up, before | After |
|---|---|---|
| M50, reloading off, 270 | 240 | 270 |
| LS14 Laser Gatling, 750 | 250 | 750 |

### Fire Rate Scale
The box goes up to 3 instead of 2. Nothing else limits it, but a server still fires a gun at most once a tick: see the XMV-850 below.

### Testing
A dedicated server and one client, in Classic. A new rig step takes each gun through a new gun, a spare gun from the map, filling up, throwing it, picking it up again, filling up and dying, and the next life picking up what was dropped, and logs the ammo on the server and the client at each point.

- **Scales 0.5, 1 and 3:** the five guns above follow the table at every point, on the server and the client, and the LS14 Laser Gatling scales with them. The Proton Streamer doesn't change. The M50's reserve doesn't change and its magazine reads 15, 30 and 90.
- **Reloading off, scales 1 and 3:** LS14 Laser Gatling, M50, MK781, RCS-715, Pug and Bulldog keep what they hold when dropped.
- **HUD:** the ammo figures are the same on client and server in all 180 readings of those runs.
- **Tactical at 0.5:** a new Mk66 has 100 of 125 cells and fires its one 100 cell shot.
- **Menu:** Fire Rate Scale and Magazine Size Scale set to 3 save and read back, typing 5 stops at 3, and the longer hint wraps and shows in full at 800x600.
- **Script warnings:** none in any of these logs.
- **Fire rate,** shots a minute counted by the server:

| Gun | Scale 1 | Scale 2 | Scale 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| M50, held | 602 | 1205 | 1807 |
| XMV-850, held | 1095 | 2177 | 3012 |
| MD24, tapped | 207 | 400 | 599 |
| M763, tapped | 49 | 95 | 133 |
| R78, tapped | 24 | 47 | 68 |

The M763 and R78 fire only a few shots in the 4 seconds, so their figures are rough. The XMV-850 stops at about 50 shots a second, close to the test server's real tick rate of about 52, which looks like the once-a-tick limit.

**Not tested:** bots with the new cap, and the Wendigo's secondary fire.

Merges cleanly with #510, #511 and #512.

## What (PR 9B, on top of 9A #52)
**Per-item visibility.** `Post.visibility`, `Feedback.visibility` (reviews), `Goal.visibility` (default public), and `Shelf.visibility` now accepts `friends`. The central registry already marked these as items, so every where-helper (`postVisibleWhere`, `reviewVisibleWhere`, `goalVisibleWhere`, `shelfVisibleWhere`) and the raw-SQL feed include the item column. Review and goal detail pages that checked only the author's section setting now go through the helper too. New members' defaults for new posts and new shelves live in Settings > Privacy (`defaultPostVisibility`, `defaultShelfVisibility`).

**Notifications and mentions follow the item level:** a friends-only post notifies friends only, an only-me post nobody; a mention of someone who cannot see the content stays plain text and sends nothing. View tracking skips what the viewer cannot open.

**Locked and unavailable items.** A friends-level item gives a locked page (200, noindex: who owns it and a friend button; masked OG card "Friends-only post by X"); an only-me item (or a blocked viewer) is simply not found, so nothing shows it exists. The cached post page is the locked stub for an anonymous visitor and a signed-in friend fetches the real post per viewer; review and shelf pages are dynamic. Pure decision `decidePeek` with tests.

**Feed.** Home has two big tabs, For You and From Friends (`?feed=` via nuqs; `post.list` `friendsOnly`). Book pages show "friends who read this" (`friend.whoRead`) per viewer from a client component.

**Also:** friend button on the post page; `visibility` on the review, goal and sitting-review outputs; migration `20261114120000_item_visibility`.

## Before deploy
Apply migration `20261114120000_item_visibility` (adds `visibility` to post, feedback and goal, and two default columns on user; all default public, so nothing changes for existing content).

Typecheck, 335 API tests (peek decision, feed SQL, where-builders vs `canView`), 554 shared tests, friends-who-read wording tests. author: matthewbonanni
body:
Part of #594 (region probes join the reference case once #500 lands; that follow-up closes it)

## What and why

Every probe test compared runs within one build and backend, so nothing checked that a GPU run writes the CPU's probe output. `ProbesTest.EveryBackendReproducesTheCpuReference` (`test/probe_reference_test.cpp`) runs a small smooth Navier-Stokes case (TENO 3, triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D, an isothermal and an adiabatic wall, open ends, fixed `dt`, 6 steps). Its probes are points, a line, a circle, a cut plane, a resampled sphere (3D), `boundary_type = "wall"` and a `boundary = ["left", "right"]` zone, all with `sampling = "point"` and all six reductions. The test compares their CSV files with committed CPU references in `test/data/probes/{2d,3d}`. GPU CI already runs the full `mallard-test2d`/`mallard-test3d` suites on the A100s, so it picks the test up with no devtools change. `MALLARD_UPDATE_PROBE_REFERENCE=1` rewrites the references from a CPU build.

The contract, also stated in `docs/guide/output.md`:
- **Exact:** the header, row count and order, sample index, `step` and `t`. The geometry is set up on the host, so on one host it is the same bit for bit on every backend.
- **Geometry** (`x`, `y`, `z`, `s`, normals, `area`, reduction measures): within 1e-14 of the column's largest magnitude. This only absorbs other CPUs and compilers (the reference comes from arm64 clang, which contracts FMAs, and CI is x86 GCC).
- **Values and reductions:** within 1e-10 of the column's largest magnitude. The device rounds the solution and point values differently (nvcc FMA contraction, CUDA libm). Reductions are summed on rank 0 on the host in sample order, so they differ only through their samples.

Why 1e-10, measured on the 2D case: a 4e-16 relative perturbation of the initial state (about two ulps, a stand-in for device rounding) moves the outputs by at most 7.8e-14 of a column's scale. A 1e-10 perturbation moves them by 1.4e-9, which fails the test. The response is linear from 1e-14 to 1e-10, with no TENO stencil flips. That leaves three orders of magnitude of margin over rounding, while a wrong cell, polynomial, halo or missed copy (errors of 1e-5 or more) still fails. Moving the probe geometry by 1e-12 also changes the values only linearly (at most 1e-10 relative) in 2D and 3D, so no sample or cut-plane vertex sits on a mesh edge where rounding could pick another cell.

Single-precision builds skip the test (the reference is double). Region probes (#500) are not on `main` yet. Once they land they should join this case.

## Validation

macOS arm64, Apple clang 21, Kokkos Threads, 2 threads:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_SYSTEM_KOKKOS=OFF -DKokkos_ENABLE_THREADS=ON -DMallard_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON
cmake -S . -B build-3d -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_SYSTEM_KOKKOS=OFF -DKokkos_ENABLE_THREADS=ON -DMallard_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON -DMallard_DIM=3
cmake --build build -j3 && cmake --build build-3d -j3
./build/test/mallard-test2d --kokkos-num-threads=2 --gtest_filter='ProbesTest.*'      # 15 passed
./build-3d/test/mallard-test3d --kokkos-num-threads=2 --gtest_filter='ProbesTest.*'   # 14 passed
```

CPU CI (x86 GCC/Clang, serial, OpenMP, MPI on 1-4 ranks) checks that the arm64 reference holds across CPUs. The GPU comparison needs one GPU CI run (`~/local/mallard-devtools/gpu_ci.py`). The PR changes no device code (`tools/dev/device_changes.sh` prints `false`), but that run is what closes the issue.

## Device code

- [ ] This PR changes code that runs on the GPU. It does not, but it adds a test for the GPU CI run.
