author: afbora
body:
## Summary

Bug fixes for the current line, released as 1.0.3. The most important one: with the default empty `icons` option, the `pwa` snippet threw a `TypeError` on Kirby 5 and took the whole page down.

## Changes

- `helpers.php`, `snippets/pwa.php`: the snippet renders without icons. The icon, Apple touch icon and tile image tags are skipped when no icons are set. On Kirby 3 and 4 the snippet didn't crash, but printed these tags with empty values. This also removes the PHP 8 deprecation of `getArrayLastItem()` (optional parameter before a required one).
- `helpers.php`: `snippetKirbyPwa()` returns `null` when it echoes the snippet, instead of throwing a `TypeError` after the output.
- `index.php`, `helpers.php`: a string value for the `manifest.json` and `serviceworker.js` options was ignored and ended in a 404. It is now the path to a file, absolute or relative to the site root. A missing file still gives a 404.
- `helpers.php`: icon types come from Kirby's MIME table, so `.svg` is `image/svg+xml` and `.jpg` is `image/jpeg` (before: `image/svg`, `image/jpg`).
- `helpers.php`: shortcuts without `description`, or with an icon without `purpose`, no longer throw a warning (an error page in debug mode). A shortcut without icons gets an empty `icons` list instead of a list with an empty object.
- `snippets/pwa.php`: the service worker scope was resolved against the page URL, so the default `.` registered a separate worker for every section (`/notes/`, `/photography/` ...). The scope is now resolved against the manifest URL, the same way browsers resolve the manifest `scope`, so every page registers the same scope. Absolute scopes like `/app/` don't change. The registrations that 1.0.2 created for other scopes with the same script are removed.
- `snippets/pwa.php`: the `media` of a splash screen is printed. Before, it was ignored and every splash screen got the same fixed media query. Splash screens without `media` keep that default.
- `composer.json`: `extra.kirby.compatible: ^3.6 || ^4.0 || ^5.0`, version 1.0.3, Kirby 3 keywords and `minimum-stability`/`prefer-stable` removed. Kirby 3.6 is the lower bound because the routes use `Kirby\Filesystem\F`, which exists since 3.6.0.
- `README.md`: no more "Kirby 3", and the string options and splash `media` are documented.

## Testing

A CLI test with 15 checks (snippet with and without icons, `snippetKirbyPwa()`, both routes with absolute, relative, missing and closure values, disabled plugin, shortcuts, splash media):

| Kirby | PHP | 1.0.2 | 1.0.3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.6.0 | 7.4, 8.0 | 9 failed | all pass |
| 3.10.1.2 | 8.1, 8.3 | 9 failed | all pass |
| 4.9.4 | 8.1, 8.4 | 9 failed | all pass |
| 5.6.2 | 8.2, 8.5 | 9 failed (page crash without icons) | all pass |

In a browser on Kirby 5.6.2 (localhost): the manifest has the right icon types and shortcuts, and a deep page like `/notes/across-the-ocean` registers the service worker with the site root as scope. After registering `/notes/` and `/photography/` the way 1.0.2 did, one page view of 1.0.3 left only the root registration.

## Notes

- The service worker itself is unchanged: it still caches nothing. It gets rewritten in the next major.

author: wking53214
body:
## What this does

Builds the milestone the 2026-10-30 assessment named as the biggest lever for the universal AI interface score: two independent systems, in two languages, exchange a request, negotiate boundaries, disclose only what was agreed, and each independently verifies the other's signed decision, without either giving up its own identity, rules or authority.

A new sibling package, `cns_interop` (UAI-1), sits beside `cns` and `cns_composition`. `cns` does not import it; it imports only `cns`, `cns_composition` and the standard library.

| layer | what it adds |
|---|---|
| Signatures | Ed25519 (RFC 8032), so a decision can be checked by a process that holds no secret |
| Envelope | one versioned, signed message shape over the existing CNS canonical digest; strict JSON wire |
| Identity and trust | self-certifying identities; each receiver's own trust policy (pinning, domain-scoped expiring endorsements, revocation) |
| Discovery and negotiation | signed capability manifests; the decider sets terms, the requester checks them before disclosing anything |
| Selective disclosure | salted per-field commitments; only agreed fields are opened; over-disclosure is refused |
| Portable decisions | signed verdicts in CNS vocabulary; `from_super_gate` exports a real SuperGate decision with its root |
| Distributed authorization | receiver ledgers (one shared by processes on a host) and `RemoteDecisionGuard`, which acts once on the one judged document |

A second implementation in Node (`interop/node/`) shares no code, uses OpenSSL's Ed25519, and is held to the same answer key (`contracts/uai-vectors.json`). It reproduces the Python reference's signatures byte for byte. `python interop/demo.py` runs the two against each other in both directions, plus a third process (`interop/act.py`) that acts once on the result.

## Independent review

A separate reviewer attacked the work before this PR and proved ten findings. All are fixed in Step 10 and kept as tests; `docs/interop/SCORECARD.md` lists them.

## Scorecard

`docs/interop/SCORECARD.md` maps each of the assessment's ten dimensions. Projected average: **2.4 to 4.0**. This is a self-assessment; the assessor's rubric is not published. External adoption stays at 1, and the STACK spine score is untouched.

## Verification

- Full suite: 1412 passed (1295 before, plus 117 new)
- `ruff check .`, `mypy --strict cns/`, `mypy cns_composition`, `mypy cns_interop`: clean
- Wheel carries `cns`, `cns_composition`, `cns_interop`; tests excluded
- CI gains `mypy cns_interop` and a `node --version` check; the Node tests need Node 20+ and fail loudly without it

## For the owner

- `v2.3.0` was tagged at `41592fb` but `contracts/cns-releases.json` has no row for it yet. In a checkout that has the tag, `tests/test_release.py` fails on any commit after it until `python -m cns_composition.release --record v2.3.0` runs on main. CI does not fetch tags, so it is unaffected. Not changed here: recording a release is the owner's step.
- This work sits under `## [Unreleased]` in the changelog; which version ships it is the owner's decision.

## Still open (docs/interop/UAI-1.md, section 8)

Encryption and sessions, endorsement chains and key rotation, a ledger shared across hosts, adapters for real model APIs, richer policy terms, a registry, and constant-time signing in the Python path.

**What each constraint does now with `--engine nextpnr`**

| Several PERIODs | checked by the timing step | also nextpnr's per-clock targets: one `create_clock` per PERIOD in an SDC (`--sdc`), on the net after the global buffer; the tightest stays as `--freq` |
| OFFSET | checked by the timing step only | the same shared step |
| TIG, CLOCK_DEDICATED_ROUTE | parsed; neither the placer nor the router reads them | no effect, no warning |

An input nothing reads now gets no pad, as with Silinx's packer. No fork release is needed: `--sdc` is already in nextpnr. Nothing needed a "cannot honour" warning, because nextpnr honours everything Silinx's flow acts on here, so the tests assert no warnings.

**Evidence**
- `research/nextpnr-s3e/ucf_all.v` (two clocks, an unused input, a tristate output with a pull-down, each attribute): all 10 IOBs' settings equal Silinx's engine's for the same UCF; a test compares them with Silinx's packer. Both engines give the same PERIOD and OFFSET verdicts (a test).
- nextpnr's log shows the two targets: 50 and 100 MHz.
- Routing check OK, every feature in the bit database, simCheck equal with random inputs.
- ISE on `ucf_all` and all seven examples (Basys2-250, v0.5.0): `drc` 0 errors and 0 warnings, its bitgen's `.bit` byte-identical (CRC on; `ucf_all` also CRC off, on v0.4.0).
- `node scripts/related-tests.mjs origin/main HEAD`: 0 failures.

**Known difference:** traffic's `btn`, vga's `sw` and stopwatch's `sw` are placed differently by the two engines. That is #2199: Silinx's packer drops `name<0>` on a one-bit bus, and nextpnr's placement is the one the UCF asks for.

**Not covered**
- Only the Basys2-250 went through ISE, and nothing was run on a board.
- LVCMOS12 and LVCMOS18 stop at bitgen on the pads tried (P6, M11), in both engines: the bit database has no features for them there.
- A UCF `IOB` on an inferred register's HDL attribute does not survive synthesis, in either engine.
- A `PERIOD` through a DCM gives no nextpnr target yet (#2194); the timing step still checks it.

author: yusuf-gundogdu
body:
## Why

A release waited for two approvals. `docs/release.md:152` said why: the `refs/tags/v*` ruleset blocked **updating** and **deleting** a tag but not **creating** one, so a workflow on another branch with `contents: write` could cut a `v*` tag, pass the environment's branch and tag limit, and reach the upload key. The required reviewer was the only thing in its way.

Guarding the key by *who may tag* is the stronger control, and it costs no clicks.

## What changed outside the repository

Measured, in this order, so the key was never unguarded:

1. The `refs/tags/v*` ruleset gained a `creation` rule. Bypass list unchanged: the organization's admins.
2. The required reviewers of `release-signing` and `play-internal` were removed. Both keep their branch and tag policy (`main`, `v*.*.*`).
3. The repository variable `PLAY_RELEASE_STATUS` was deleted, so an upload reaches the testers instead of parking as a draft.

## The thing that could have broken, and the measurement

`docs/release.md` used to say a creation rule "would block every release", because release-please tagged with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and GitHub accepts no GitHub Actions app as a bypass actor. That stopped being true with #468: release-please now tags with the owner's fine-grained token, which bypasses as an organization admin.

Verified against the live ruleset before this commit — a `v*` tag created with that token succeeded, and the test tag was deleted again.

`test/architecture/release_tag_creation_test.dart` is new and fails if that input is ever lost or renamed, which is the one way this setup silently stops releasing.

## In the repository

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — three comments that described the approvals, and a note on the now-unset variable.
- `docs/release.md` — the flow, the environment list, the variable row, and setup steps 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 14.
- `docs/testing-architecture.md`, `docs/usability-findings.md` — the new guard, and the guard count 44 → 45.

## Checks

Analyze clean, format clean, full suite run locally: 52 failures, all of them this machine's known golden pixel diffs — the same 52 as the baseline, no new red.

author: chtsai0105
body:
## Summary

Two independent changes:

1. **contamdb no longer uses UniVec.** `AAFTF database contamdb` now builds `contamdb.fa` from NCBI's adaptor set for screening eukaryote assemblies (`adaptors_for_screening_euks.fa`), plus PhiX and the BBTools `lambda.fa.gz` / `adapters.fa`. UniVec_Core's cloning vectors carry yeast and other fungal DNA (ADH1, LEU2, 2-micron, CEN/ARS, …). The old name-based exclusion list didn't catch all of it, so `vecscreen` could still split genuine fungal contigs and `filter` could still remove genuine fungal reads.
2. **CI and releases use the org's shared workflows** from [stajichlab/gh_workflows](https://github.com/stajichlab/gh_workflows) (`@v1`). Releases now go through a release PR instead of pushing straight to `main`, which branch protection blocked.

## contamdb changes

- `resources.py`: the `univec` database entry and `VECSCREEN_EXCLUDE_TERMS` are removed. The new `euk_adaptors` entry points to `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/kitts/adaptors_for_screening_euks.fa`, and `contamdb` is now built from `euk_adaptors` + `phix`.
- `database.build_contamdb()` concatenates the NCBI adaptors, PhiX and the BBTools files, then deduplicates them with `dedupe.sh` as before. It no longer filters UniVec entries.
- Help text, module docstrings and the `database` / `filter` / `vecscreen` docs are updated. `AAFTF database univec` no longer exists; use `AAFTF database contamdb`.
- Tests in `test_database.py`, `test_filter.py` and `test_utility.py` are updated.

**Upgrade note:** an existing `contamdb.fa` is kept on purpose, since users may have added their own sequences. Run `AAFTF database contamdb --force` to rebuild it without UniVec.

## CI / release changes

- **Release flow:**
  - `publish_release.yml` is replaced by `release.yml`. Run manually, it bumps the version from the latest `v*` tag, moves the `[Unreleased]` notes in `CHANGELOG.md` to that version, updates `CITATION.cff` and opens a `Release v<version>` PR into `main`.
  - Merging that PR runs `publish.yml`, which tags the release and creates the GitHub release, waiting for approval in the `Release` environment.
  - `publish.yml` then calls `python-publish.yml` (PyPI, plus attaching the dists to the release), `conda-build.yml` and `docker-build.yml` with the tag, and finally merges `main` back into `dev`.
  - The publish workflows are now `workflow_call` workflows (also runnable by hand with a tag) instead of `release: published` triggers, which don't fire for releases created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- **Shared workflows:**
  - `ci.yml` and `ci-conda.yml` use the shared `python_test` workflow.
  - `docker-build.yml` uses the shared `container_build` workflow.
  - `dependabot-pixi-lock.yml` uses the shared `pixi_lock_refresh` workflow.
- **New checks:**
  - `changelog.yml` requires every PR to add an entry under `[Unreleased]`. Label a PR `skip-changelog` to skip it.
  - `citation.yml` validates `CITATION.cff`.
- **Changelog:** `CHANGES.md` is renamed to `CHANGELOG.md` and switched to [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com) format. References in `README.md`, `pyproject.toml` (the sdist include) and `DEVELOPERS.md` are updated.
- `codecov.yml` comments are updated for the new upload flag names (`pip-<version>`, `pixi-dev`).

## Repo settings needed before the first release

- [ ] A `Release` environment with required reviewers (Settings → Environments)
- [ ] "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" enabled (Settings → Actions → General)
- [ ] Optional: a `RELEASE_TOKEN` secret (PAT or GitHub App token with contents and pull requests: write) so CI runs on the release PR

## Testing

- [ ] `pixi run -e dev pytest tests/ -v`
- [ ] `pixi run -e dev pre-commit run --all-files`
- [ ] `AAFTF database contamdb --force` builds `contamdb.fa` from the NCBI adaptors
- [ ] CI passes on this PR using the shared workflows

author: runkids
body:
Refs #95

Image search needs stored source renders and, when a vision profile is configured, their vectors. Rendering and image inference must never delay a save or a text publication. This adds the job that prepares those layers. It runs on its own lane, the same way an embed job prepares the semantic layer.

## What it adds

- **API:** `jobs::visual(storage: &Storage, select: &Select, source: Option<&str>, scope: Option<&str>, request_id: Option<&str>) -> Result<Outcome>`. It has the same shape as `jobs::embed`. The scope is required and is never widened to the whole file. The scope root also becomes a unit when it is below a page.
- **CLI / MCP / OpenCode:** `figlens index visual <select> --scope NODE [--source ID] [--request-id ID]` and the MCP `index` action `visual`. It shows as kind `visual` in `jobs status`. An interrupted visual job is retried as `visual`. A scope that was never published returns a `refresh` recovery.
- **Worker model:**
  - Hash-only jobs run figlens's own `__visual-worker`.
  - With a vision profile, the profile's `figlens-embed` runs `__visual-worker` as one process. It renders and embeds through an injected loader (`workspace::visual_job::run_visual_worker`), so cancel kills one process tree.
  - The worker stages the registered bytes, which must match the published snapshot, and rebuilds the full index from them. It checks each unit's rid against the stored records. Units come from `search::visual::scope_units`, at most 2,000.
  - The tree and bytes are dropped before the model loads. Units commit 8 per batch and images at most 4 per batch, each commit under the fence.
- **Rows (what the #95 query reads):**
  - `visual_units` / `visual_rasters`
  - `model_layers(gen, 'visual-hash-1', visual POLICY)`: chunks = units, embedded = rendered, refused = render errors
  - Vision: `model_vectors(profileId, raster_key)`, `model_refs(gen, profileId, POLICY, raster_key)` for rendered units only, plus a vision layer row
  - A render error is recorded on that unit and makes the layer `partial`; the job still succeeds. Vectors are reused by raster key per profile, so an unchanged rebuild loads no model.
- **Auto-queue rule:** the job is queued automatically only for a scope whose replaced generation had a visual layer. The MCP model lane and the watch runner then render it again after a text build publishes. The one-shot CLI lists the step in `nextSteps` instead. No other scope is rendered implicitly.
- **Schema 10 slots:** `jobs_active` excludes `embed`/`visual`. A new `jobs_visual` unique index covers (source, scope, expected_gen, profile_id). A visual job never joins or blocks a text build, and a newer submit cancels an obsolete one.
- **Failed-state rule:** when an embed or visual job ends failed or cancelled, the same write marks its layers still `building` as `failed`, keeping the counts. Workspace semantic search then reports `failed` with an embed step. A later success overwrites the row.

## Evidence (Docker, offline)

| Check | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy --locked --features embed --bin figlens-embed -- -D warnings` | 0 |
| `cargo test --locked` (lib 691 passed / 1 ignored, 102, index_jobs 124, 3, 12, 33, 0; semantic_child 49 ok) | 0 |
| `python3 scripts/ai-context.py check` | 0 |
| `npm test` (116 passed) | 0 |
| `(cd npm && node --test)` (11 passed) | 0 |

The new process tests cover:
- a hash-only ready layer
- vision refs and vectors, reused after a rebuild with no model load
- cancel kills the worker and marks the layer `failed` (embed and visual)
- a newer publication fences out the job
- a render error is per-unit coverage and leaves the layer `partial`
- an unpublished scope returns a refresh step
- an interrupted job is retried as `visual`

## Open items

- `index status` does not report visual (or embed) layer progress; `jobs status` does.
- This branch does not run a visual job with the real SigLIP weights; the vision path is tested with a fake embedder.
- An image the runtime refuses fails the whole job. There is no per-image retry; inputs are pre-validated normalized RGB.
- A job whose owner died (interrupted) leaves its layers `building` until it is retried.
- Depends on #152. I will retarget or merge after #152 lands.

## Cause
Mesurée en Chromium : avec la barre à VU-mètres (réglage `barreVuMetres`), dès que la barre atteint `SEUIL_VU_PX` (1280 px, la largeur CSS de la Tab S4 en paysage), la colonne de droite (~296 px) doit porter le cadran (84 px) plus la pile d'icônes en `min-width: max-content` (#1712). Transfert, curseur de volume et zone sortent de 20 à 60 px à droite, jusqu'à ~1750 px de barre.

Requête de conteneur `1200-1800 px` sous `.vu` : libellé de zone masqué (pastille carrée, infobulle conservée), boutons de pas de volume masqués, écarts et curseur resserrés. Commandes de lecture et cadrans intacts ; téléphone et bureau > 1800 px inchangés.

- Chromium (Shrek), zones UPnP et navigateur, VU allumés : aucun dépassement à 1280, 1300, 1366, 1440, 1600, 1700, 1800 px. Avant : dépassement à toutes ces largeurs sauf 1800.

body:
Termine le regroupement Fournisseurs, Modèles et Voix en retirant les anciens écrans en double. Les logins CLI, chemins personnalisés, options de fournisseurs et voix du Mac jumelé restent disponibles. La lecture suit le choix vocal personnel en solo et en organisation; la migration conserve une préférence personnelle existante.

Le switch every-Claude est retiré en conservant les comptes qui paient déjà : sélections, modèles rapides, defaults et secours migrent vers les instances API dédiées, y compris les CLI personnalisés, avant l'enregistrement du marqueur. Les permissions sont conservées. Ajouter une nouvelle clé laisse les bots par abonnement sur leur compte.

Les actions du bot gèrent les clés et endpoints personnels. Un ancien host Perspicax affiche l'état explicite de mise à jour; les clés distantes déjà prises en charge et imports locaux en attente restent résolus avec les vérifications d'identité existantes. Le parcours complet en organisation exige le backend [Perspicax #674](https://github.com/pulsatrixtechnologies/perspicax/pull/674) et les assets de [#668](https://github.com/pulsatrixtechnologies/perspicax/pull/668) déployés; la version 1.9.12 n'expose pas les nouvelles routes de gestion des 17 fournisseurs.

Le choix vocal courant, Auto compris, est résolu avant de proposer sa voix et transmis explicitement aux requêtes audio, même avant la synchronisation des préférences. La voix reste associée à son fournisseur; la lecture du status ne modifie aucune préférence.

Validation : tests ciblés de migration, config, runtime, voix et UI verts, ainsi que typecheck, lint et catalogues. Les transitions OpenAI vers Auto sont couvertes dans le renderer pour la personne et le bot, et sur les deux transports de reconnaissance avec ou sans bot. La migration est vérifiée jusqu'à la réponse finale réussie et au tour terminé. Un parcours renderer/serveur isolé enregistre une clé, découvre les modèles d'un endpoint Azure-compatible contrôlé localement, en choisit un et reçoit une réponse. Captures de ce parcours et des réglages solo/organisation dans le handoff local. Gate normale et revue indépendante suivies au SHA publié.

Travail repris et complété avec Codex. L'intégration reste au coordonnateur de livraison.

Publication immédiate sur instruction explicite de JC de skipper les tests restants. Les preuves ciblées déjà obtenues restent consignées; aucune gate complète du nouveau head n’est revendiquée. Push avec le flag officiel `SAGAX_SKIP_HOOKS=1`; scan public SUCCESS sur le SHA exact requis avant intégration.

author: tee8z
body:
Existing agents currently require individual provider changes to move to Remote workspace. This adds a native batch flow for any saved team or selection of existing agents.

| Entry point | Selection |
| --- | --- |
| Agents → Your agents → Move to remote | Individual agents or all agents |
| Teams → Move to remote | That team's members |

The flow supports a new destination configuration or an existing remote agent's configuration. It preserves each identity, memberships, instructions, and Claude/Codex model options. Already-remote agents remain unchanged. Local workspaces and sessions stay local; credentials use the enrolled remote profile.

Changes reuse the existing single-agent operation. A private, bounded, atomic journal precedes host mutations. Resume reconciles completed writes and unfinished type/config changes. Account, community, roster, reference, and source checks prevent applying a stale review. Corrupt journals can be archived through the dialog.

The macOS verification job now uses `macos-15`. GitHub is retiring the prior runner and cancelled the macOS check during its [scheduled macOS 14 brownout](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13518).

Validation:

- Native app tests with `voltage-sandbox`, run serially: 1,082 passed, two ignored; includes eight batch/recovery regressions.
- Native build, Clippy with all targets and `-D warnings`, default-feature check, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Exercised the native app under Xvfb with synthetic identities and an isolated HTTP community fixture: subset migration, the Teams shortcut, destination editing, already-remote skips, retained keys/configuration/roster, lost-acknowledgement reconciliation, and corrupt-record recovery.
- The new migration controls use native semantic buttons and checkboxes. Space, Tab, and Enter checks caught and corrected keyboard selection and focus issues.
- Parallel suite reruns exposed intermittent failures in unchanged Codex runtime tests (`does_not_clean_after_the_last_agent_closes_the_server` and `coalesces_concurrent_core_reads`). The serial suite passes; the first failure also passed in isolation.
- Real Sandbox launch and human app verification remain required. Local test coverage does not attest those steps.

For the feature build, run `nix develop --command cargo run -p buzz-gpui --features voltage-sandbox` from `apps/buzz-gpui`. Close other app instances using the same profile so this instance can hold its agents.

Manual check: open **Agents → Your agents → Move to remote**, select a mixed Claude/Codex team containing an already-remote agent, review, and apply. Verify identities, memberships, instructions, and individual model options. Interrupt and resume another batch, and verify that changing settings after review stops the batch. Verify a real remote session separately.

Human app validation and a real Sandbox launch remain outstanding for review. No human test completion is attested.

author: sandeepkomal
body:
## Why

To make this repository a free, complete course in Python for DevOps automation. It is built around the nine scripts already here and served as static files on GitHub Pages, with no servers, accounts, trackers or costs.

## What it adds (`site/`)

- **Homepage:** a live log-analysis chart (the `log_analyzer.py` output) on the immersive design.
- **Playground:** 48 real-world script incidents in 11 groups, from basics to production:
  - hangs without a timeout
  - shell injection
  - 10 GB logs
  - retries without backoff
  - secrets in logs
  - cron using the wrong Python
  - PEP 668 pip errors
  - unsafe YAML or pickle
  - graceful shutdown
  - atomic writes

  The learner edits the script and runs it. This is a guided simulation, labelled as one on the page, that checks the fix and plays out the scenario with tracebacks captured from real Python 3.13. Each scenario also has the commands to run it for real.
- **Path:** 14 levels.
- **Scripts:** the nine scripts with usage and real sample output.
- **Quiz:** 70 questions.
- **Script X-ray:** explains every line and flags risky patterns.
- **Troubleshoot:** 37 errors, searchable by pasted traceback, each with a stable `#fix/<id>` link.
- **Cheat sheet:** 66 rows, each marked Try or Lab.
- **Python arch:** an interactive page covering the interpreter, the GIL, venvs and a standard-library map for ops.
- **`problems.html`:** a generated page that works without JavaScript, plus a sitemap and robots file so the reference can be indexed.
- **Privacy and security:**
  - Progress stays in the browser (`dq-python:`), with a Clear it button.
  - Same strict CSP as the other tracks; no CDN and no Pyodide.
  - An original logo and the PSF trademark notice.

## Checks

- **Site tests (`site-tests/`):** every scenario starts broken, its fix wins and its wrong edits fail. They also check:
  - the data and the links
  - that the X-ray explains all 649 lines of the nine scripts with no false warnings
  - that `problems.html` is in sync
- **Fuzzer:** 6,000 mangled scripts through the evaluator and the X-ray, with no exceptions.
- **Existing Python unit tests:** pass. CI keeps the test job and adds a site job.
- **Browser:** no console errors and no horizontal scroll at 1440 light, 1440 dark and 390.
- **Secret scan:** clean. `.secretsallow` gains one entry for a made-up practice key.
- **Workflows:** actions are pinned to full commit SHAs and permissions are minimal.

author: thesevenpens
body:
## What

Three things found by clicking presets on Home:

1. **Loading a preset could pause editing for the whole app.** A preset holds profiles only for the tablets known when it was saved. Applied to a driver with another tablet plugged in, the daemon generates that tablet's profile during `SetSettings` (`ProfileCollection.GetProfile` adds it), the read-back no longer matches what was sent, and the apply is reported as rejected. A tablet the preset has no profile for now keeps the profile it has (`PresetCompletion`). This covers every such tablet, not only plugged-in ones, so a remembered tablet's setup is not dropped by an older preset.
2. **The pause panel blamed "something" for the artist's own change.** An apply that fails read-back now says so (`SettingsPauseCauseText`). The other pauses keep their wording.
3. **Clicking the preset that is already live asked about unsaved settings.** Those unsaved changes were the preset itself. `SwitchToAsync` now asks the coordinator whether the completed preset would change what is live (`SettingsWorkspace.WouldChange`, weighed after the same preparation an apply uses). If not, it reports the preset as loaded: no prompt, no apply. Loading a different preset still asks. The tray and hotkeys use the same path.

## Verification

- Logic tests: pass except the 3 known `PluginTypeNameGuardTests` failures, which only occur in OutDir builds. UI tests: 331 pass, 0 fail.
- Each new test fails when its fix is removed (mutation-checked).
- Against a real daemon: the "CSP Preset" that failed before loads without pausing; revert, click, click shows no dialog on the second click; "Revert to saved" restores everything.

## Not changed

- Switching from one preset to a different one still asks, because the first is unsaved. Kept on purpose.
- A stale preset for a connected tablet could still read back differently if its button counts are out of date. "Revert to saved" already adjusts for that; preset loading does not. Not observed.

author: lucainnocenti
body:
Moves the shot-noise visualization's worker onto QELM Lab 0.3.0 from [lucainnocenti/qelm-js#1](https://github.com/lucainnocenti/qelm-js/pull/1), which is now merged as `f9dfeb9`.

The page imports `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lucainnocenti/qelm-js@f9dfeb9e027b523d38cd8705fc0f8adae1e72bc7/dist/qelm.js`. That pins it to the 0.3.0 merge commit, so the page needs no release tag and the library can't change underneath it.

## Changes
- **Worker imports the library.** The worker imports the single-file 0.3.0 bundle. About 200 lines of local copies are gone: seed mixing, the draw-order shim, frame renormalization, the binomial and Gaussian samplers, Hilbert–Schmidt coordinates, and the Jacobi SVD.
- **`solvePseudo` uses the library `svd()`.** The model code (the analytic Haar averages, `predictStats`, `run`) is unchanged.
- **Cache key includes the library URL.** The preset-cache fingerprint now hashes the pinned library URL together with the worker source, so a future library upgrade invalidates stale presets. The legacy-compatibility exception is removed.
- **Presets regenerated.** The new library's random streams differ, so the three presets were regenerated with the page's own aggregation code.

## Verification
- **Old and new solvers agree.** On identical inputs across 720 configurations, the old and new `solvePseudo` give:
  - weights equal to 2e-15 relative;
  - the same ranks;
  - Haar bias equal to within 4e-10 absolute;
  - shot variance equal to 2e-14 relative.
- **Regenerated presets match the old ones within sampling noise.** Per-point median losses are within ×0.87–1.31 of the old presets. Only the mean losses at the interpolation peak (n_out ≈ n_tr) differ substantially; that's expected for heavy-tailed losses averaged over R = 100.
- **Headless Chromium, with the commit-pinned URL served from the merged `dist/qelm.js`:** a live run (8,640 fits in 0.8 s) completes with no console errors, and all three presets load from cache.

author: svanvliet
body:
## Problem

Automatic provider-version and T3 release checks contact `registry.npmjs.org` directly instead of honoring the server's configured npm registry. In a managed environment this triggers network protection and prevents update discovery, even though npm itself is configured to use the corporate proxy.

Related: #24369. Overlaps the provider-lookup fix in #24372; this draft also addresses browser-side T3 release checks.

## Change

- Resolve npm-based provider versions through configured `npm view --global`, including native/manual installations and fallback after a failed installer-specific lookup. Preserve installer-authoritative results and existing provider behavior when npm is absent. A configured-npm lookup failure does not retry public npm.
- Move T3 release metadata behind an authenticated, read-scoped server RPC. Preserve database-migration metadata, validate release specs, bound subprocess output/time, and share a one-minute cache across WebSocket connections.
- Check publication against each target environment's registry. Advertise the RPC as a capability: older servers remain eligible for their existing updater instead of being permanently excluded by an unsupported precheck.
- Surface safe lookup errors in track-switch and update planning, and document registry behavior.

## Scope and approval

This addresses one underlying problem: release discovery bypassing configured npm registries. No maintainer approval of the broader scope or the compatibility tradeoff below is claimed. Submitting as a draft for feedback; draft status does not waive contribution requirements.

**Unresolved behavior needing direction:** T3 release-track switching currently requires npm on the primary server's PATH, including standalone/desktop installations. Missing npm now produces an actionable error, but this is still a functional regression from the old browser lookup. This is separate from provider-version resolution, which retains its existing npm-absent behavior.

Possible directions are a narrowly scoped public lookup when npm is genuinely absent, or publishing database-compatibility metadata with first-party release artifacts. This draft does not choose either approach or silently fall back after a configured-registry failure.

## Verification

Using the already-installed partial toolchain:

- Added regression cases first: the older-server update case and two missing-npm cases failed before their fixes.
- Final focused suites: **20 web tests** (release state, update planning, track-switch planning) and **34 server tests** (release service and RPC authorization) passed.
- Contracts, provider-core, and client-runtime typechecks passed; targeted formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Corrected a missing exhaustive RPC instrumentation entry identified during review. A full server compiler rerun removed exactly its two diagnostics and added none; remaining server diagnostics persist. The web compiler's normalized diagnostics are unchanged from the prior dependency-blocked run.
- Earlier focused checks passed for provider resolution (62 tests), shared client state/runtime (54 tests), and RPC contracts (2 tests).
- Earlier controlled network probes passed 34 service cases plus a guard positive control, with real npm subprocesses against isolated registries. These did not observe public-registry attempts in the exercised service paths. The client probe used IPC and virtual time, not the full app; it predates the final capability/error/cache-wiring fixes.

**Before merge, confirm all required checks run and pass in CI.** Local full-app verification is blocked by dependency availability and quarantine in the corporate registry—the same environment that exposed this bug, not the same code defect. The locked `electron@44.10.0` was confirmed quarantined until November 3, 2026, 10:06:18 AM Pacific.

`vp run check:changed`, complete builds/typechecks, and full-app verification have not passed. Actual WebSocket/multi-connection behavior, mounted UI/network behavior, genuine pnpm behavior, and Windows integration remain unverified. No integrated UI captures are available. Green CI would cover automated checks; integrated app/network verification and the npm-less compatibility decision remain outstanding.

Implemented with GPT-6 Astra in T3 Code through the acpRegistry harness. Static review by Claude Opus 5.5.

Esconde os 2.

Contexto: "os 2" são as páginas "Em alta" e "Temas" do site. author: gamesbyian
body:
## Motivation / measured bottleneck

Passing [HP main Windows run #41122361691](https://github.com/gamesbyian/UR-Recomp/actions/runs/41122361691) at `214085eacc2a471b7c564035426952fd0cde5f90` took **220 seconds inside compilation** at **21.2% mean host CPU over ten-second windows** with six MSBuild project workers. `SDL3-static.vcxproj` alone occupied **~88 seconds** before the game's own build. This third-party library is repeatedly rebuilt despite unchanged SDL3 source and toolchain. Four-vs-six MSBuild parallelism was flat; separate disposable Ninja experiment #2881 addresses different within-project scheduling.

**Goal:** reuse a provably source-built static SDL3 install on the trusted HP runner without weakening any source, compiler, executable, packaging, QA or physical playtest boundary.

## Implementation

- New `tools/devnode_benchmark/prepare_sdl3_cache.py` builds pinned SDL3 3.4.10 using VS 2022 ClangCL, Release, static CRT and exact SDL static configuration. It hashes the repository-owned source archive, entire staged source tree, ClangCL/MSBuild/CMake binaries, installed Windows SDK version set, and build options into a cache identity.
- Publish an **installed static development package** atomically only after the build succeeds. Hash every installed byte. Reject mismatched identity, tampering, missing `SDL3Config.cmake`/`SDL3-static.lib`, or an SDL DLL. author: weselben
body:
## Rebase notice

This branch is based on the current head of PR #1343. Rebase it onto updated `main` after PR #1343 merges, before marking this draft ready for review.

## Scope

Follow-up for #1344, which is a sub-issue of #723. Verify whether interleaved Anthropic thinking blocks and tool calls preserve ordering across the full Messages → chat → Responses → chat → Messages path, and fix the protocol defects the verification exposes.

## What the verification found

Two defects in the Anthropic Messages stream converter, both on the path where a Responses-only upstream interleaves reasoning with the argument deltas of a tool call.

**A tool_use block closed before its arguments were done.** Anthropic streams one content block at a time. When reasoning arrived between the argument deltas of a call, the reasoning opened a thinking block, which closed the tool_use block; the remaining argument deltas then landed on a stopped block index. No Anthropic client accepts that.

The content that arrives while a tool_use block streams its arguments is now held back and rendered once the tool call is complete: when the next tool call starts, or when the turn ends. The reasoning is not lost and the tool_use block never closes before its arguments are done.

**The thinking block the held reasoning opened was never closed.** The flush opens a block of its own. That block was left open: the next tool block opened on top of it and the message ended with it still open, which leaves the client with a dangling index. It is now closed before the next block opens and before the message ends.

## Ordering: what is preserved and what is not

The streaming path preserves the upstream order, because it emits the blocks as they arrive: `thinking A → tool call A → thinking B → tool call B` reaches the client in that order.

The buffered path cannot. The canonical chat shape carries the reasoning in one member beside the answer text and the tool calls, so the buffered response renders `thinking` first, then `text`, then `tool_use`. That is what the Anthropic contract asks for, and the upstream interleaving is not representable in that shape. This is documented in ADR-0011 rather than papered over.

The two directions are separate contracts, and ADR-0011 now states both: a signed `thinking` block in the request history is the client's artifact and is not replayed to a Responses-only upstream, while the upstream's reasoning summary is rendered as a `thinking` block in the response with an empty signature.

## Tests

`internal/server/messages_interleaved_test.go` drives the real Messages handler over the real ChatGPT provider against a fake Responses upstream, reusing `echotest` and `providertest`:

- the streaming block order and the block indexes, with the assertion that no delta targets a closed block
- the buffered response: thinking first, then both tool calls with their IDs and arguments intact
- the request replay: user, assistant, tool call and tool result reach the upstream, and the reasoning does not
- the assembled stream compared with the buffered result
- a tool result stays bound to the call ID it answers
- every content block that is opened is also closed

`internal/anthropicapi/stream_test.go` pins the two defects at the converter level, and `internal/providers/chatgpt/interleaved_reasoning_test.go` covers the composed path.

Each regression test fails on the unfixed code.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), the full `./internal/...` suite, `-race` on the touched packages, and the repository's test conventions all pass.

author: springfall2008
body:
## Summary

`battery_value_rate()` prices a kWh left in the battery at the end of the plan. Two of its inputs were scanned **after** the saving, free and Axle sessions are written into the rate tables, so a one-off event decided what every stored kWh was worth.

- **Replacement cost (`rate_min_forward`)** was built in `rate_scan(print=True)`, after `load_free_slot()`. A 0p free-electricity session tomorrow afternoon made refilling the battery look free, so the value fell through to the export floor. On the 30 Oct debug dump from #5566 (a free session on Sunday 13:00–15:00), the value at `end_record` was **15.61p instead of 9.18p**.
- **Export floor (`rate_export_min`)** was also scanned after the export sessions.

Found while reviewing #5566; it doesn't change that issue's outcome.

## Changes

- **`fetch.py`:** `rate_min_forward` is built in `fetch_sensor_data()` at the `rate_import_pre_saving` snapshot. That is after `rate_replicate()` and the IOG dispatch overlay, before any session. `rate_scan()` no longer builds it.
  - The forward minimum no longer includes `rates_import_override` or manual rates, which are applied after the snapshot.
- **`fetch.py`:** a new `rate_export_min_base` comes from `rate_export_base`, next to `rate_export_max_forward`, which was already built before the sessions.
- **`plan.py`:** `battery_value_rate()` uses `rate_export_min_base` for the export floor.
  - It falls back to `rate_export_min` when the new value is `None`, as with older debug dumps. A 0p minimum is a real value.
  - `rate_export_min` itself is unchanged, because it also drives the export colour scale, the published `min` attribute and the threshold fallback.
- **`compare.py`:** a tariff with its own rates gets its own `rate_min_forward`, `rate_export_max_forward` and `rate_export_min_base`. A tariff reusing the live rates gets the live cycle's values back, taken from the existing `live_saving_state` snapshot.
  - Before this, compare never rebuilt `rate_export_max_forward`, and it doesn't restore these between tariffs, so a tariff on the live rates inherited whatever the previous tariff left.

- **Debug replay (`tests/test_single_debug.py`):** `--redo` now rebuilds these values the way `fetch_sensor_data()` does. Before, a replay reused the dump's stored `rate_min_forward`, which was built from rates with the sessions in, even with `--redo`.
  - A dump keeps the pre-saving import rates only for the session minutes, so the replay puts those minutes back into the dumped import rates. The export terms come from `rate_export_base`.
  - The golden `debug_cases` replay without `--redo`, so they are unaffected.
  - Replaying the #5566 dump with `--redo` now values a stored kWh at 9.18p, and the plan is unchanged row for row.

## Tests

Each new check failed against `main` and passes with the fix.

- `test_rate_min_forward_calc` test 7: `rate_scan()` leaves `rate_min_forward` alone when given rates with a free session in them.
- `test_fetch_snapshots_are_taken_in_the_right_order` pins both new build points between the pre-saving snapshot and the session loaders.
- `test_compare_rate_min_forward_ignores_live_sessions`: a tariff with its own rates, then one on the live rates, which carry a 0p session. It checks both the import and export terms.
- `test_rate_min_forward_calc` test 8: the replay rebuild ignores a free session, including a minute the session created from nothing, and takes the export terms from `rate_export_base`.
- `battery_value_export_min_base_test`: a session lifting the scanned minimum from 5p to 20p doesn't move the floor. It also covers the fallback when `rate_export_min_base` is `None`, and a genuine 0p minimum.
- Housekeeping: the two new values are in the threshold tests' snapshot lists so they don't leak between tests; `compute_metric_test` and the replay harness set `rate_export_min_base` to `None`; the `compare` test's fake PredBat stubs the new calls.

`./run_all --quick` passes, with the 4 slow tests skipped, and so does pre-commit. The full suite hasn't been run.

The wave port boundary condition and excitation used only the real part of the propagation constant, and the S-parameters the conjugated projection onto the mode normalized to |P| = 1. For a lossy port mode, as with finite-conductivity or impedance boundaries on the port, or lossy dielectrics, the port was then not matched to its own mode, and the projection gave S_ii = P - 1 at a matched port, with P the complex power of the mode, which has a phase. A uniform lossy line had |S11| up to 0.45 and a non-passive S-matrix (issue #1109). The synthesized circuits from AdaptiveCircuitSynthesis suffered from the same issue.

The changes in this PR switch to using the full complex propagation constant in the boundary condition, in the mode n x H of the excitation and of the modal correction, and project the S-parameters on the unconjugated reaction, under which the modes of a reciprocal cross-section are orthogonal also when they are lossy, relative to that of the mode itself. The modes keep their unit power normalization, with a phase such that their reaction is real, so that the S-matrix of a reciprocal structure stays symmetric. The characteristic impedance Z_PV now uses the complex power of the mode. Circuit synthesis was also changes to handle complex propagation constants and lossy modes, and some changes were made to accelerate the reduced wave port solves which could become slow for lossy modes. Results are unchanged for lossless port modes.

Closes #1109. Closes #1115.

body:
## What was wrong

`pgcolumnar.iceberg_data_files` refused every Iceberg table whose current snapshot removed a data file (after a copy-on-write delete or a filtered overwrite), reporting "has delete files" although the table had none.

Closes #1791

## The change

Such a commit records the file it replaced as a manifest entry with status 2 (DELETED). In `src/columnar_iceberg.c`, the lister branch refused `e->content != 0 || e->status == 2`. It now refuses only `e->content != 0` and skips `e->status == 2`, as the `iceberg_scan` branch already did. Delete manifests and delete files are still refused with 0A000. An entry that is both a delete file and removed (content != 0, status 2) is still refused, because the content check runs first.

`docs/sql-reference.md` now says a removed file is skipped, and says "delete file" where it said "delete entry". CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased / Fixed.

What this PR does not change is listed under **Out of scope** below.

## This round: review fixes in 01a77d2d

Commit `01a77d2d` answers four review findings.

1. **Source comment.** The comment above `pgcolumnar_iceberg_data_files` said a DELETED entry raises 0A000. It now says a removed entry (status 2) is skipped, neither listed nor refused, and that delete manifests and delete files are still refused. Comment only.
2. **The premise reads the Avro fixture itself.** Before, it read only `expected_files.json`, the oracle. Now it decodes the current snapshot's manifest list and manifests with `json` and `zlib` only (what the suite already requires), counts the DELETED (status 2) data (content 0) entries there and in the oracle, and shows both counts. The check name is unchanged; its expected value is now `cow: avro=1 oracle=1; cow_all: avro=1 oracle=1`. Shell suite and twin carry the same reader.

The old arm would have passed on that tree.
3. **Out of scope** is now listed below, with the delete-manifest sibling (#1829).
4. **Ledger dating.** The three checks seen red before the fix are dated `2026-10-30`, merged with `--mutation 'columnar_iceberg.c: the lister refuses a DELETED (status 2) data entry again, the #1791 defect (#1791)'`, three `--target`s and `--reds-are-real`, from one PG 18 log of the suite with the fix reverted (`19 passed + 3 failed`). The log sat in a directory inside this worktree. Census: `rows=8319 never=4604 dated=3715` (was never=4607, dated=3712). The merge also sorted the mutation lists of five `rewrite_storage_oid` rows; the set of mutations in each is unchanged.

author: lacraig2
body:
## Why

Measured from the last ~130 workflow runs:
- A PR whose engine misses the Cachix cache spends **~26 min** in `CI / build`. With a hit it takes **~4.4 min**. PRs never push, so every stacked PR, every re-run and main after the merge rebuilds an engine that was just built.
- `Engine / engine` rebuilds a one-target engine with no cache at all, adding **~7 min** to every engine PR. Everything it checks is either a flake check or can be one.
- "Free disk space" costs **~2.6 min** per run. The runner has 86 GB free before it and the build peaks at ~15 GB.
- The engine also compiles QEMU's unit and qtest programs, which nothing installs or runs.

## What

| | Change |
|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | Same-repo PRs push to Cachix (`skip-push` is true only for forks, which have no secret). Main's runs are no longer cancelled by the next push; they fill the cache. "Free disk space" removed. |
| `flake.nix` | The engine builds `all` minus `tests/` (from `ninja -t query all`) and installs with `meson install --no-rebuild`. New `engine-delta` flake check runs `check-delta-present.sh` on the full 13-target engine. |
| `engine.yml` | `engine` job removed (covered by `engine-src`, `engine-delta`, `qemu-system` in ci.yml's flake check). The `series` gate now also runs on `ready_for_review` and on pushes to main. #30 merged a series that fails the round trip and nothing flagged it on main (fixed in #36). Concurrency per PR. |
| `guest.yml` | Adding a label other than `guest-suite` no longer starts the five-image suite. "Build the image" times out at 45 min (longest seen: 16; stalled downloads held runners for hours). |
| `release.yaml` | `concurrency: release`, not cancelled: two overlapping runs would compute the same next version. |

## Validation

- `nix build .#engine-x86_64` with the new build/install phases: builds in 3.5 min on 8 cores. Installs the same bin/ and lib/ (qemu-system-x86_64, tools, libpanda/libqemu-system/plugin-interface .so). `check-delta-present.sh` passes on it.
- `nix flake check --no-build` evaluates, including `engine-delta`.
- The full 13-target engine and the flake checks are built by this PR's own CI run.

## Not done here

- **Plugins rebuild on every engine change** (4–9 min). They link each target's engine (DT_NEEDED + RUNPATH), so depending on headers only would need link stubs or a different linkage model. That's a design change, not a CI tweak.
- **release.yaml reuses nothing from CI** (~110 runner-min per push). It writes `VERSION` before building, so every derivation differs from CI's. Fixing that means deriving the version at install time.

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## What and why

A dial window at a depth is the position's tones the depth draws as distinct colours, widened along the ladder where the depth draws two alike. It widened only until it held two tones. Golden angle keeps neighbours apart only over three (`DISTRIBUTIONS`: over two no rule can), so a three-tone position whose depth rounds two tones alike left an authored `distribution: "golden-angle"` container with neighbours drawn as one colour at 256 and ansi.

The coordinator's ruling on candybar-joiners-e5r4.cfm, as refined after the first commit's press counts:
- A window widens toward its position's count.
- It never takes the last colour the depth draws of a ladder that draws more than two, because the button pressed in that hue stands beside every tone of its band's window and needs a colour none of them wears. A press drawn like its neighbour breaks Brandon's rule; a third closed tone is only the look.
- Two tones is the floor.

As a size: **max(2, min(count, colours the depth draws of the ladder − 1))**. "Colours" means distinct by identity after rounding over the whole ladder, with the muted form excluded.

`windowAt` keeps the position's tones the depth draws apart, in the position's order, up to that size. It then calls the one `widen` once per tone short of the size, each time with every colour the window already holds as taken. The search runs along the ladder, by identity after rounding, nearest rung to the position's tones first, and on a tie the rung away from the background. A window of three is then listed as the dial lists every position of three: lowest rung, highest, then the one between (`inWalkOrder`). The window is still built once per (palette, hue, position, depth) and memoised. `windowSize` is a pure function of the two counts.

Unchanged: the pressed shade's rule, the hue-turn rule's own logic, the lineages and the distributions' reading rules.

Five commits:
- `adb77e06` widened every window to its position's count.
- `5c0fc809` applies the refinement.
- `92abec87` (review) lists a window of three lowest, highest, between. Appended, a widened rung took the slot van der Corput deals at every other cell. See "Where the added rung lands".
- `c6df7a2d` (review) corrects the docs and memory on the walk order and on how a dial step moves cells at depth.
- `df74cdc6` (review) keeps every tone when ordering a window longer than three.

Rebased onto main after #511, so the five are now `3f50fee9`, `cd0c71f5`, `513488fd`, `7b61d379` and `477bdb63`, in that order. The review comment uses the pre-rebase ids.

The counts below are for the branch as it stands, against main. The reviewer re-measured them after `92abec87`.

## Where the window changes

Over every bundled theme × hue × dial position × depth (2,070 windows), 251 windows change against main:
- **256:** 149 windows widen from two tones to three, one rung each, in 19 themes. Every ladder at 256 draws at least four colours except textual-ansi's, which draw one. So the restored count stands everywhere at 256, and nothing at 256 stays at two.
- **ansi, widened:** 54 windows widen from two to three where the ladder draws four or more colours.
- **ansi, held at two:** 48 windows that are three on main drop to two. On a three-slot ladder at ansi, the position's own three tones took every slot. They keep the first two of the position's order (low and high), so the press keeps the third.
  - By position: `widest` 28, `wide` 7, `brighter` 6, `deeper` 3, `brightest` 3, `middle` 1.
- **Truecolor:** none.

Every widened window holds main's tones and one rung more, listed lowest, highest, between. Every held window is a prefix of main's: the position's low and high. All 1,001 windows of three at every depth are in that order; on main all 846 were.

| theme | 256 widened 2→3 | ansi widened 2→3 | ansi held 3→2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| atom-one-dark | 3 | 6 | 2 |
| atom-one-light | 11 | 0 | 2 |
| catppuccin-frappe | 6 | 0 | 3 |
| catppuccin-latte | 5 | 5 | 1 |
| catppuccin-macchiato | 12 | 0 | 4 |
| catppuccin-mocha | 6 | 0 | 2 |
| cyberpunk | 9 | 0 | 2 |
| default | 12 | 10 | 1 |
| dracula | 9 | 9 | 2 |
| flexoki | 7 | 4 | 1 |
| gruvbox | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| monokai | 12 | 8 | 1 |
| nord | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| rose-pine | 9 | 6 | 3 |
| rose-pine-dawn | 5 | 0 | 1 |
| rose-pine-moon | 9 | 0 | 4 |
| solarized-dark | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| solarized-light | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| svg-export | 5 | 6 | 4 |
| textual-ansi | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| textual-dark | 9 | 0 | 2 |
| textual-light | 9 | 0 | 2 |
| tokyo-night | 9 | 0 | 3 |
| **total** | **149** | **54** | **48** |

At ansi, the windows of the seven three-tone positions are:
- two tones where the ladder draws two or three slots (385 windows)
- three where it draws four or more (77)
- one on textual-ansi's flat ladders (21)

**Golden angle's neighbours.** I counted one-hue adjacent pairs drawn alike under golden angle at the three-tone positions. The count covers all 16 variations, every theme, row 0 and 1, and rows of 2 to 16:

| depth | main | `5c0fc809` | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| truecolor | 23,639 | 23,639 | 23,639 |
| 256 | 56,464 | 23,639 | 23,639 |
| ansi | 105,749 | 98,885 | 98,894 |

- At 256 the remainder is exactly the truecolor set, all textual-ansi's flat ladders.
- The ticket's example (atom-one-dark, `accent` variation, `deepest`, 256, where cells 4 and 5 of six were both secondary-darken-3) is fixed. The secondary window there is darken-3, base, darken-1.
- At ansi, the 54 widened windows fix pairs, and the trade the refinement chose adds 7,631 newly alike pairs. 7,628 of them are under a position whose window the cap holds at two where main had three.
- The walk order nets 9 more at ansi (18 new, 9 gone), all under `alt` at places 12 and 13. All are golden angle over a window of two. The secondary window's new order changes which hue turns need a moved cell, and a cell that no longer moves keeps the tone golden angle dealt it, beside its own hue.

## Where the added rung lands

Widening takes the nearest rung drawn apart from what the window holds, nearest the position's own tones first, and on a tie the rung away from the background. Where the rungs on a position's own side round alike, the third tone is the role itself or a rung past it:
- **256** (149 windows): `deepest` takes `base` in 29 and `lighten-1` in 7. `brightest` takes `base` in 33 and `darken-1` in 8. In 42 of the 149, the added rung is on the far side of the role from the position's own tones: `deepest` and `deeper` take a lightening, `brighter` and `brightest` a darkening.
- **ansi** (54 windows): 20 cross the role the same way. default's and flexoki's `deepest` primary take `lighten-2` (grey `#808080`) beside navy and teal.

So at 256 and ansi a `deepest` or `brightest` row that widened deals one tone from the other side of the role. The ruling accepts this, since the window widens to its count wherever the ladder has the colours. It shows only with the dial off `middle`, the bundled default.

The window's order decides how often a row deals that tone. Van der Corput deals a window of three as entries 0, 2, 1, 2. Appended, the added rung took entry 2 and wore half the row. Listed lowest, highest, between, it stands at an end and wears a quarter. Of the 219 rungs the dial does not name in windows of three, 215 now stand at an end. The other 4 are in windows that widened twice: flexoki's and rose-pine-dawn's secondary `deepest` at 256, and default's primary and accent `middle` at ansi. There one widened rung lies between the other two, and the walk is still a rung at a time as drawn. Example: default's primary at `deepest`, 256, `duo` row 0, 8 cells:
- main: darken-3, darken-1, darken-3, darken-1, …
- before `92abec87`: darken-3, lighten-1, darken-1, lighten-1, darken-3, lighten-1, darken-1, lighten-1
- now: darken-3, darken-1, lighten-1, darken-1, darken-3, darken-1, lighten-1, darken-1

## The closing sweep

`test/seam-sweep.test.ts` sweeps the four shipped variations. 3,220 seams per depth per va

author: 25778430-eng
body:
Sammy's feedback after trying the live app: it looked too complicated and too much like a website.

## Customers
- Home is the simple list from low-data mode, with no map. The scan button sits in the search bar, and search runs when you press Enter.
- Tabs are Home, Bookings and Account. Map and Scan are gone from the footer.
- No website header on phones.
- Account is grouped like a phone app:
  - Work
  - Settings: Profile, Notifications and Language, each on its own screen
  - Look
  - More: Help, Privacy policy, POPIA and PAIA, Download my data, Terms

## Staff
- Tabs are My bay, Bookings and Account. Home sends staff to My bay unless they choose **Switch to client mode** in Account (saved in a `mode` cookie).
- New `/staff/bookings` page: their own and "anyone" bookings, today and on later days.
- A **Break** button under Call next opens the 10, 15 and 30 minute options.
- Staff can no longer add walk-ins (`/staff/walk-in` removed). Only the shop owner adds them.
- "My chair" is now "My bay".

## Shop owner
- Tabs are Queue, Walk-in and Account. Summary moved into Account.
- Account groups:
  - Shop: Summary, My team, Services and prices, Shop profile, Photos, QR, TV, Job cards
  - Money: Bank account, Payouts, Plan
  - Documents, You, More
- Shop profile (`/vendor/setup`) only has location, open days and hours.
- New `/vendor/services`, `/vendor/photos` and `/vendor/money` pages. Money has the bank account and deposit rules; Basic shops see how to become Verified.
- Each uploaded document has a **View** button.

## Checks
- `tsc`, `next lint`, `next build` and 74 unit tests pass.
- Playwright at phone size, against a local Postgres:
  - customer tabs, Enter-to-search, the scan button and all Account screens
  - staff redirect, the client/staff mode switch and the Break options
  - owner tabs, plus saving the shop profile, bank account and deposit

author: tencur
body:
**In one sentence:** `extract_surface_tracks.py` documents `dust_threshold` (400) in full-resolution voxels and its dust filter converts it for the 4× downsampled labels (400 // 4³ = 6), but `skeletonize_kwargs()` passes the raw 400 to Kimimaro/Brook, which count the downsampled voxels they are given, so every sheet piece in a slab smaller than 400 downsampled voxels (25,600 full-resolution voxels) that the dust filter kept is dropped again by the skeletonizer and gets no tracks; this passes the same converted cutoff.

**One real example:** the CPU backend (Kimimaro) with the shipped settings (downsample 4, `dust_threshold` 400, ribbons 4 thick every 16, vertical slabs 4 thick every 64, `interjoint` paths) on the published PHerc0500P2 surface prediction (volume `20250820143440`, model m7, L0, th0.2; a 128 × 256 × 256 crop at z 3456, y/x 2048), with `z_min`/`z_max` set to the crop.

**Before:** (villa main `4eecd08f`)

```
input: published PHerc0500P2 surface prediction (128, 256, 256), 636549 surface voxels; shipped settings
dust threshold given to the skeletonizer: 400 (prepare_cc_labels cutoff: 6 downsampled voxels)
slabs: 15, slabs without any track: 15
tracks written: 0, track points: 0
```

**After this PR:**

```
input: published PHerc0500P2 surface prediction (128, 256, 256), 636549 surface voxels; shipped settings
dust threshold given to the skeletonizer: 6 (prepare_cc_labels cutoff: 6 downsampled voxels)
slabs: 15, slabs without any track: 3
tracks written: 46, track points: 1306
```

On a crop this small every sheet piece inside a 4-voxel slab is below 400 downsampled voxels, so main loses all of them; on a whole volume the long sheet pieces are far larger, and the ones lost are the smaller fragments.

**In the published spiral datasets:** the track sets at dl.ash2txt.org/datasets/spiral_datasets/ (28-29 Jul) were extracted with downsample 2 and dust 400, before this fix. On 12 ribbons of PHerc0826, main reproduces the published tracks almost exactly (34,657 vs 34,654 tracks, 2,098,179 vs 2,098,181 points); with this fix the same ribbons give 46,054 tracks (+33%) and 2,464,959 points (+17%). The other published sets record the same settings.

**At scroll scale** (same CPU backend and shipped settings, main `39a8cf3a1` vs this branch): on three whole cross-sections of the same PHerc0500P2 prediction, main writes a third to a half of the tracks (965 vs 1,973; 280 vs 879; 1,317 vs 2,707). On a 192 × 2304 × 2304 crop around the umbilicus of PHerc0826's published surface prediction, main writes 193k track points against 445k, and 1,000 tracks of 50+ points against 2,053; near the umbilicus, 22 of 47 slabs get no track on main and none on this branch.

**Proof:** `scripts/realdata/run_rd_c341.sh` runs `rd_c341.py` on main and on this branch (the prediction crop comes from `fetch_data.py`, anonymous S3, ~16 MB).

| Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tencur/villa-pr-evidence/main/C341/screenshot_before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tencur/villa-pr-evidence/main/C341/screenshot_after.png) |

*Terminal output of the real-data proof on main and on this branch (script under Details).*

**Why / where this is useful:** On a small crop of the published PHerc0500P2 surface prediction, extracting surface tracks with the shipped settings gave no tracks at all, because the skeletonizer was given the dust threshold in full-resolution voxels while it counts downsampled ones, so it threw away the sheet pieces the dust filter had just kept. On that 128 x 256 x 256 crop main wrote 0 tracks in 15 slabs; with the same cutoff the dust filter uses, it writes 46. On whole cross-sections main still loses half to two thirds of the tracks, mostly the smaller sheet fragments, and those feed the spiral fit. This section was written by Claude Code under my direction.

- [x] I personally verified that the example and proof above were produced by this PR on the stated data.


## Details

- Cause: `spiral-fitting/extract_surface_tracks.py`: `prepare_cc_labels` max-pools the labels by `downsample_factor` and dusts them at `max(1, dust_threshold // downsample_factor**3)`; `skeletonize_kwargs()` (used by `get_skeleton_tracks` with Kimimaro and passed to Brook by `surface_tracks_gpu.py`) sets `dust_threshold=dust_threshold`. Kimimaro keeps a label only if its voxel count in the array it is given exceeds `dust_threshold`.
- Change: `skeletonize_kwargs()` passes `max(1, dust_threshold // downsample_factor ** 3)`. `geometry()` (the GPU backend's own component filter, already converting) is unchanged.
- Test change: `test_cpu_backend_writes_the_track_format` asserted that some slab of its synthetic volume comes out empty. On that volume main writes 187 tracks with 7 empty slabs and this branch 321 with none: the empty slabs were this bug. The assertion is inverted, with a comment.
- Tests: two new tests in `tests/test_extract_surface_tracks.py` (the cutoff given to the skeletonizer; a 4 × 4 × 144 strip that passes the dust filter gets a track). Main sources: 3 failed, 26 passed, 1 skipped; this branch: 29 passed, 1 skipped (the GPU test). See tests_current.txt.

Reproduction scripts: [tencur/villa-pr-evidence/C341](https://github.com/tencur/villa-pr-evidence/tree/main/C341) (run with [run_proof.sh](https://github.com/tencur/villa-pr-evidence/blob/main/run_proof.sh)).

*Found and written with Claude Code under my direction.*

author: matt-edmondson
body:
Fixes ktsu-dev/Coder#391

## Problem

`CSharpGenerator.GenerateVariableDeclaration` fell back to `DefaultVisibility` (`public`) only for a variable held at file or namespace scope (`heldMember`). A `VariableDeclaration` member of a class or struct with `Visibility.Unspecified` got no modifier, so C# made it private. `new Point { x = 0 }` or `p.x` outside the type then failed with CS0122. C++ and Rust already make the same member public.

## Change

- A new `typeMember` field records the member of a class or struct being written. It is tracked by identity, the same way `heldMember` is, so a local declared in a member's body is unaffected.
- `GenerateVariableDeclaration` applies `SpellVisibility(...) ?? DefaultVisibility` when the variable is a held member or a type member. Locals keep no modifier, and an explicit `Private`/`Protected`/`Internal` is still honoured.

## Tests

- `VisibilityTests.CSharp_WritesAnUnspecifiedTypeVariablePublic`: an unspecified struct variable is `public int x;`, an explicit private one stays `private int hidden;`, and a local in a method stays `int doubled = 0;`.
- `VisibilityTests.CSharp_UnspecifiedTypeVariables_AreReachableFromOutsideTheType`: builds the issue's repro with `dotnet build`.
- `ClassDeclarationTests.CSharp_GeneratesAClass` asserted the old private output (`    int x = 0;`). It now expects `    public int x = 0;`.
- I reverted the generator change: both new tests failed, and the compile test reported `CS0122: 'Point.x' is inaccessible due to its protection level`. With the change restored, the full suite passes (1553/1553).

author: theciege23
body:
## Why
The owner asked whether the guillotine card accounts for best-ball guillotine leagues: "those scores aren't accurate until the last game is played." It didn't.
- **The lineup comes after the games:** in best ball it is picked from the whole roster once the games are played, so a live score is only a floor.
- **The rank switched too early:** the list ranked the field on live points once most teams had any. A team with Sunday-night players read as in the cut every Sunday afternoon.
- **The projection was too narrow:** it priced only the listed starters, never the bench best ball also counts.

## What
- **`lib/core-app/bestBallField.ts` (new):**
  - **The valuation:** every live roster's **projected final**, meaning points already banked plus the best legal lineup its remaining players can still make.
  - **Reuse:** this is `bestBallProjectedFinal`, the matchup screen's model, applied to the whole field instead of two teams.
  - **All-or-nothing:** if any roster can't be valued, the list keeps its ordinary rule and never ranks on a partial field.
- **`readPlayerAvailability` (out/bye/at-risk):** pulled out of `matchupProjections` so the list and the matchup screen share one rule about who is playing. The matchup suites still pass unchanged.
- **`standingIn`:**
  - It ranks on those finals (basis `best_ball`, `provisional` while any playable game isn't final).
  - The live refresh never replaces that rank (`mergeRailMatchup`).
- **The card:** reads "on projected best-ball final · provisional", then "on final best-ball points" once the last game is final. Live Matchup's line says the same.
- **Scope:** read only for best-ball elimination leagues, two on this account today, so ordinary leagues pay nothing.
- **Type fix:** the native guillotine line's `basis` type widened to the standing's own type.

## Verification
- **Valuation (`best-ball-field.test.ts`):**
  - A Sunday-night player is worth his projection, not 0: 38 vs 40 where live points said 28 vs 40.
  - Once the week is final, the totals are the real best-ball scores.
  - One roster that can't be valued makes the whole field unavailable.
- **Wiring through `getRailMatchups`:**
  - the 15 live rosters with their stored players and reserve;
  - the finals become the rank, and the lowest team is named;
  - the fallback when a roster can't be valued;
  - ordinary guillotine leagues never read the best-ball field.
- **Card and merge:** the card's labels, and that the live points rank never replaces a best-ball rank.
- **Positive controls:** four mutations each turned a test red:
  - the roster-key mapping;
  - the best-ball branch in `standingIn`;
  - the merge rule;
  - the provisional flag.
- **Related suites:** 69 files, 654 tests pass. The other failure in that run, `core-home-cards-stream`, came from #3003 and was fixed there. After merging `main`: 6 files, 96 tests.
- **Type check:** the TypeScript ratchet, with a fresh Prisma client, is at 136 against a baseline of 136, no regressions.
- **Guards and lint:** the DB-first boundary check and the ternary ratchet are clean; ESLint reports 0 errors.

body:
Backlog: Portal shell › Backend › BE-01. Spec: [`docs/specs/shell/BE-01-serve-portal-pages.md`](../blob/main/docs/specs/shell/BE-01-serve-portal-pages.md) (sections 1 to 5).

Base: `main`.

### What changed

- `app/api/server/frontend.py`: serves `web/dist/` with the SPA fallback, hashed assets as `immutable`, a plain 404 for missing files with an extension, a JSON 404 for any `/api/...` path, containment inside `dist`, and 503 (dev) or a startup error (prod) when `dist` is missing.
- `app/api/server/security_headers.py`: the three security headers on every response (outermost middleware).
- `app/api/server/main.py`: `create_app(settings, frontend_dir)`. There is no module-level `app` any more, so importing the module never needs `dist`; uvicorn runs `server.main:create_app --factory` (`app/Makefile`, `make dev` and `make serve`).
- `docs/specs/foundation/BE-17-fastapi-project.md` and `docs/BACKEND_GUIDELINES.md`: updated for the factory entry point. This amends the BE-17 spec, approved by the owner.
- `app/api/server/request_log.py`: a `log_route` scope override, so a static file logs by path and fallback or unknown requests log `unmatched`.
- `app/api/tests/`: `test_frontend.py` (new); `conftest.py` sets `PORTAL_ENV=dev` and adds `add_get` (test routes registered after `create_app` land behind the catch-all); `test_request_log.py` uses it.
- `docs/BACKLOG.md`: BE-01 set to Done, and this PR linked in its PRs column.

About 275 changed lines.

### How to test

1. `gh pr checkout <N>`, then `cd app`
2. `make build-web && make serve` (`PORTAL_ENV=prod`)
3. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and follow the links. Expected: pages render, and the only 404s are `/api` ones.

### Tests

`make test-api`: 36 passed (11 new in `test_frontend.py`).

### Verification (spec section 4)

- [x] `/`, `/categorizer`, `/categorizer/abc-123`: 200, HTML, `no-cache`
- [x] `/assets/<built file>`: 200, JavaScript, `immutable`
- [x] `/missing.js`: 404, not HTML
- [x] `GET /api/submissions` and `POST /api/anything`: JSON 404
- [x] `/.env`, `/../.env`, `/%2e%2e/.env`, `/ask_pdf.py`, `/legacy/index.html`: 404, no content

AWS runs the DevOps Agent as a remote MCP server at `https://connect.aidevops.<region>.api.aws/mcp`. It isn't in the MCP registry, so the file carries its own `metadata` and `"selfPublished": true`, the same way `com.amazon.aws--aws-mcp.json` does.

author: zspitzer
body:
[LDEV-6811](https://luceeserver.atlassian.net/browse/LDEV-6811)

`ArrayImpl` drops `Collections.synchronizedList` and owns its storage as a deque: lock-free validated reads (seqlock, as `StampedLock`), one lazy writer lock per CFML operation, skipped for unsynchronized arrays. `ListAsArray` becomes abstract, its old body moves to `ListBackedArray` (user Java lists), and the serialized form is unchanged, so 7.x streams load and 9.0 streams load on 7.x.

## ARM memory ordering

x86 never reorders stores, so neither our laptops nor CI can show an ordering bug. The read and write paths were checked with jcstress on GitHub's `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners as well as x86 (JDK 25), each with a negative control that turns the protection off.

- **`fill()` needed a fence** (`arrayResize`, a set past the end, reusing tombstoned slots): the epoch bump was a release store followed by plain slot stores, which ARM may reorder ahead of it, so a reader holding older bounds returned the new value for the wrong key. Fixed with a `storeStoreFence` after the bump. Without it, arm64 failed in 61 of 146 configs, and in 116 more on a rerun stopped after 2.5 h; with it, 0 on arm64 and x86. x86 never failed either way.
- **Middle `insert`** (in-place shift inside an odd epoch, or growth into a new holder): clean on both CPUs. With the readers' epoch check disabled, the front shift tears on x86 too, which shows the tests can see a torn read.

Harness: [zspitzer/deque-arm-jcstress](https://github.com/zspitzer/deque-arm-jcstress).

## Also in this branch

- `duplicate()` copies through the lock-free `range()`, so copies of a shared array no longer queue behind writers (Wheels duplicates its shared SQL cache array per request).
- `arraySort` throws `ConcurrentModificationException` when the comparator writes to the array during the locked second pass, instead of publishing over the write.

## Tests

- `test/general/ArrayConcurrency.cfc`: readers against a churning queue, bulk readers (`duplicate`, `serializeJson`) against middle insert / delete and growth, parallel append / shift, sort against appends and a writing comparator, a sort holding the lock against `duplicate`. The concurrency specs fail on 9.0 (CME, IOOBE, a torn `duplicate`).
- `test/tickets/LDEV6475.cfc`: synchronized and unsynchronized arrays serialized by Lucee 7.0.2.106 load with values, nulls and `getMetadata().type`.
- `test/functions/GetMetaData.cfc`: synchronized arrays report `synchronized`.
- Full suite: only the bundles that also fail on clean 9.0 here (Windows / environment), plus timing or network flakes.


[LDEV-6811]: https://luceeserver.atlassian.net/browse/LDEV-6811?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
