_Requested by **Stas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01N9S6ZSHXorNUcYCbZQva6f?thread=cmsg_01N9S6ZSHXorNUcYCbZQva6fN7uUUPPmgSFoDr6RSLWDUA)_

## Before

- **Maren:** Stas said she sounded like "a grandma from the jokes", not a military chaplain. Her card asked for exactly that (*Patient and warm*, *Gentle and unhurried*, *a blessing for small things*, *calls the others "my dears"*). Under `--lang ru` the English card was translated word for word, so «мои дорогие» shows up in every full run that has Maren lines (5 of 11 lines in 18-45-48).
- **Ilsa:** Stas called her "slightly cringe". Her card was built only from precision traits. In play that produced numbered interrogations («Первый вопрос: …»), "I am writing your answers down" and her spell count said out loud.
- **Bren:** his card's "right then" stayed in English inside Russian lines, 4 to 5 times per run, or was calqued as «Правильно».

Proposal Stas approved, option 2 with Ilsa: `/mnt/project-files/engine/m7/maren-voice-proposal.md`.

## After

- **Maren:** a field chaplain. Calm, dry and firm, her care shown in deeds; she addresses people by name or calls the party "company". No pet names.
- **Ilsa:** curious and dryly funny. She asks one awkward question at a time and shows the notebook in use instead of talking about it.
- **Bren:** unchanged in English, but his "right then" now has Russian equivalents.
- **New optional card section:** `## Voice in Russian` carries example lines in our own Russian words plus the words the character never uses. It is cut from the card and reaches only a Russian prompt, after the language rule. An English prompt never sees it. Maren, Ilsa and Bren have one; Torva doesn't need one.
- **New rule in the Russian players' language section:** carry the card's voice by meaning; never translate catchphrases or forms of address word for word, and never leave them in English.
- **Unchanged:** contract, engine, DM, and each character's goals and behaviour. Maren still argues for mercy and feeds the hungry.

## How

- `game/src/agents/player.ts`: `RUSSIAN_VOICE` and `promptCard()` cut the section out of the card; `playerPrompt` passes it to `playerLanguage()`.
- `game/src/agents/language.ts`: `playerLanguage(language, voice?)` adds the rule and the voice block.
- Cards `maren.md`, `ilsa.md`, `bren.md`. The Russian examples name no NPC, foe or scene, so the "nothing of what lies ahead" test (Rule 3, AGT-52) still holds; that test caught a first draft that did.
- `scenarios/README.md` documents the optional section.
- Tests: a new test in `player-agent.test.ts` checks that the Russian voice reaches only the Russian prompt, after the rule, and that a card without the section gets no empty block. The existing tests now compare the prompt against `promptCard(card)`.
- Contract unchanged: no request or response handling changes. `check:contract` and `check:ts` (253/253) are green, and `pack:check` is ok. No Rust changed.
- **Check in the next `play:unattended` run:** 0 «мои дорогие» or «добрый человек» from Maren, 0 «Right then» from Bren, no numbered question lists from Ilsa. This PR should land before that run so that it and Stas's `play:demo` use the same build (0043).

body:
## Description
Every Velocity proxy that loaded MinecraftOTEL logged an error during startup, and the proxy dashboards stayed flat. Players were online, but the proxy gauges kept the values from startup, all zero, for days. A proxy that started without backends never showed per-server data at all.

Sampling never actually ran on the proxy: Velocity refused to schedule it under the telemetry service, so only the single sample taken at startup reached the metrics. Sampling now starts under the plugin, so the values follow the proxy.

Two related problems showed up once sampling ran. A backend that was removed kept its last player count on the dashboards, and the registered-server count was not updated when the last backend went away. Per-server series now follow the backends that are currently registered, and the server count is reported on every sample while it is enabled, including 0.

Scope: Velocity only, Paper is unchanged. This also adds the first automated tests to the repository (JUnit, Mockito, OpenTelemetry SDK testing), test scope only.

body:
Os testes dependiam de um banco compartilhado e de uma lista manual de arquivos.
Agora `npm test` na raiz cria um Supabase local exclusivo, aplica o histórico SQL
em ordem numérica, descobre os testes do backend e executa o pytest do agente.
Ao terminar, falhar ou receber Ctrl+C, remove os recursos da própria execução.

Refs #678. Manter como rascunho enquanto os aceites pendentes abaixo são alinhados.

## Alterações

- `scripts/teste-678/preparar.mjs`: adapta as migrations numéricas para a CLI e
  desloca as portas para separar o ambiente de teste do desenvolvimento.
- `scripts/teste-678/executar.mjs`: coordena banco, descoberta e execução dos
  testes, valida o destino local, recusa configurações de destino herdadas e
  verifica a limpeza de containers/volumes. Temporários e cache Python ficam
  sob um UUID por execução.
- `backend/tests/infra/banco-real.test.js`: insere, consulta e remove um cliente
  sintético no banco real local.
- Corrige o replay desde banco vazio: migration 50 preserva a conversão de PK
  para 51/52; 75 declara funcionario_id e 76 cria a FK após funcionarios existir.
  Duas regressões SQL foram adicionadas para essas falhas.
- Adiciona scripts npm, CLI fixada no lockfile, ignores e instalação/uso no README.

## Validação

- Windows: 101 migrations; 65 arquivos de backend, 998 testes passaram; agente
  271 passaram e 1 skip. Comando completo: saída 0 em 103,7 s, com imagens Docker
  já disponíveis. Smoke: 1 teste passou; saída 0 em 59,3 s.
- Falhas deliberadas de arquivo novo do backend e de migration propagaram saída 1.
  URL externa fictícia foi recusada. Usuário confirmou Ctrl+C com saída 130 e
  ausência de containers, volumes, pasta e listener remanescentes.
- Usuário confirmou falha deliberada do agente com saída 1 e nova execução sem
  o defeito com saída 0. Arquivos de defeitos deliberados removidos.
- Porta 55321 reservada por servidor temporário: recusa com saída 1 antes de
  iniciar Supabase; runtime removido e porta liberada ao final do experimento.
- Usuário informou instalação e execução bem-sucedidas em clone local separado
  de caaeead/f596985. Conferidos mesmos commits, status vazio, .venv novo presente
  e .test-runtime ausente. Log e duração dessa rodada não foram fornecidos.
- Regressões SQL falharam com as migrations originais e passaram nas corrigidas.
  Foram executadas manualmente; ainda não fazem parte de npm test.

## Aceites pendentes e limites

- Recuperar ou alinhar os dois arquivos históricos citados na issue e ausentes
  no checkout: apuracoes-ids-invalidos-http.test.js e apuracoes-fs12-prolabore.test.js.
  Usuário não possui os originais. auth.test.js é descoberto, mas contém placeholder.
- Validar o executor no ambiente de CI; workflow e bloqueio de merge pertencem à #681.
- Registrar tempo inicial com download das imagens; os tempos medidos usam cache.
- Teste governamental manual permanece fora do comando automático. As suítes
  antigas com mocks continuam e serão reformadas por área. O teste administrativo
  local da infraestrutura não comprova autenticação, RLS ou isolamento de usuários.
- Frontend, launcher Go e scripts SQL de database/tests não entram neste runner.
- Revisão cruzada com João antes da entrega final; não fechar #678 com estes
  aceites ainda pendentes.

body:
Stage-4 walk finding (lifemodel-653.9.21). The owner's decisions are recorded on the leaf.

- `core.startTask` takes optional `expectedOutputs`; a done task missing any of them ends unsuccessful (`expected_outputs_missing`).
- `core.steerTask` gets a read view `view="file"`: a bounded, read-only, escaped head of a sealed delivered file. Binary content is refused but counts as checked.
- The outcome turn must read the expected files before claiming success. The guard is structural, bounded, and falls back honestly.
- One linked redo (`redoOf`) is allowed, and only from that task's outcome turn. Chains and duplicates are refused by the registry, by SQL guards and by a unique index (migration 035).
- New prompt rules: first-person replies, a plan is not a result, "started" only after acceptance, and the plan is agreed when the request is ambiguous.

Opus review round 1 found no blockers and 4 findings, all fixed. The full check was green locally (6103 tests). Mutation runs prove each fix.

author: fraterunion
body:
**Draft. Do not merge without owner approval.** There is no Prisma migration. Merging redeploys the Railway `api` (code only) and Vercel `gymos-admin`. Nothing here sends email or cancels classes on its own.

These are the two remaining ARES items:

1. Reliable mass email from **fernando@arestrainingclub.com**.
2. Cancelling scheduled classes **across multiple weeks** in one operation.

## A. Email campaigns (Communications)

**Campaign-only sender.** `EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_SENDERS` is JSON keyed by studio slug, and Communications campaigns use it for From and Reply-To. For ARES that gives `From: ARES Training Club <fernando@arestrainingclub.com>` and `Reply-To: fernando@arestrainingclub.com`.
- Password recovery and every other transactional email keep `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`; there's an e2e test for this.
- Studios that aren't listed keep today's behaviour.

**Fail-closed checks.** Each of these blocks confirming and sending, and the admin shows the reason:
- invalid JSON;
- an invalid entry, including a display name that could inject header content;
- a From address outside the verified domain of `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`.

**Paused delivery** (`EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_WORKER=0`). Confirm, retry and resume return 409, so a campaign can never be queued while delivery is paused.

**No surprise sends.** The worker delivers a `SENDING` campaign automatically only within `EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_STALE_AFTER_MINUTES` (default 360) of its last explicit confirm, retry or resume. Older queued campaigns show as **Detenida · requiere reanudar** and need an explicit, audited **Reanudar envío**.

**Admin changes.**
- New `GET communications/status`.
- A banner shows **Envíos activos/pausados**, `De:` and `Responder a:`.
- Sending is disabled while paused or misconfigured.
- Each campaign shows its state and pending count, with one action: confirm, resume or retry failed.

**Kept as-is:** filters, include/exclude, preview fingerprint, confirmation, idempotency keys, history, the unsubscribe link, `List-Unsubscribe` / `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, and suppression.

## B. "Cancelar clases por rango de fechas" (Schedule → •••)

**Endpoints:** `POST schedule-operations/range-cancel/preview` and `POST schedule-operations/range-cancel` (OWNER/ADMIN).

**Scope.**
- Studio-local dates, inclusive on both ends, up to 184 days and 2,000 classes.
- Optional filters by class type and by instructor; foreign IDs are rejected.

**Exact preview.**
- Every class, grouped by week in the admin, with confirmed-booking and waiting-list counts.
- Protected classes are reported and kept: already started or completed, or a future class with an early check-in.

**Execute.**
- Requires `confirm: true`, the preview fingerprint and an idempotency key. An optional reason is stored as `cancelReason`.
- The update runs in one transaction and is conditional: the class must still be `SCHEDULED`, in the future and without attendance.
- It then runs the existing cascade: bookings become `CANCELLED/STUDIO` and waitlist entries become `EXPIRED`.
- A changed range (a new booking, a check-in, a class that started) means **409, and nothing is cancelled**.
- Retries and double submissions replay the first result. An audit row (`SCHEDULE_RANGE_CANCEL`) is written.

**Soft cancel only.** Rows keep their unique slot, so the daily generator cannot recreate them; the e2e test runs the real generator to prove it. Series stay active for other dates.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - campaign sender resolution, including the header-injection and domain rules;
  - Resend request body (`from` display name, `reply_to`, headers, `Idempotency-Key`);
  - delivery paths: configured From/Reply-To, platform default, fail-closed, paused, stale;
  - range date math.
- **E2E: `communications-campaign-sender`.** The real HTTP flow ends in From = Fernando and Reply-To = Fernando. Password recovery keeps no-reply. Paused delivery means 409 and a draft, with PAUSED shown. A stale campaign doesn't send until it's resumed.
- **E2E: `schedule-range-cancel`.** Covers:
  - multi-week ranges;
  - multiple class types and instructors;
  - recurring and one-off classes;
  - bookings and waitlist;
  - protected attendance;
  - past and in-progress classes;
  - regeneration prevention;
  - concurrent duplicate submits;
  - key reuse;
  - stale previews;
  - studio isolation and roles;
  - validation;
  - local-midnight timezone boundaries.
- **E2E: `communications-preview-safety`.** Updated to document the new rule: confirming while paused returns 409.
- **Admin:** `campaignDelivery` and `rangeCancel` presentation specs.
- **Local CI mirror on this head:**
  - API lint, typecheck and build pass;
  - unit tests 1,716/1,716;
  - e2e tests 662/662;
  - admin typecheck, tests and build pass.

## Rehearsal acceptance (synthetic data, `b79e8265` at `4a4571e`)
Evidence: `docs/releases/evidence/ares-pr8-rehearsal-acceptance-20261030.json`.

- **Range cancel:**
  - 4 calendar weeks: 9 classes cancelled, 2 bookings → `CANCELLED/STUDIO`, 1 waitlist entry → `EXPIRED`.
  - 1 early-check-in class kept, with its attendance and booking intact.
  - Local-midnight boundaries handled correctly, and the type and instructor filters are exact.
  - A member gets 403.
  - Two concurrent executes → one result and one replay. A stale fingerprint → 409.
  - Running the generator again recreated nothing (6/6 stay `CANCELLED`).
  - 0 rows deleted; 1 audit row.
- **Campaigns:** status shows paused. The existing QA `SENDING` campaign shows `PAUSED`; it started 21 h ago, so it would be `STALE` and never auto-send. Confirming a draft → 409 and it stays `DRAFT`. 0 emails sent.

## Sender verification
- **DNS:**
  - `resend._domainkey.arestrainingclub.com` DKIM key is present;
  - `send.arestrainingclub.com` has the SES MX and SPF records;
  - DMARC is `p=quarantine` with relaxed alignment;
  - the root MX is Microsoft 365.
- **Resend:** the production key is send-only, so it can't read domain status. One validation send went to Resend's test sink `delivered@resend.dev` with From `ARES Training Club <fernando@arestrainingclub.com>`. Resend accepted it (HTTP 200).
- **Deferred by owner decision:** the real-inbox header check, with one internal recipient, happens at activation step 4.

Rollout plan and activation checklist: `docs/releases/ares-campaign-sender-and-range-cancel-rollout.md`.

author: hanthor
body:
Refs #4154 (RFC 018 tracking issue). SDLC HIVE-6 / TUNA-3 (#4072, ledger #4116).

**Owner decision:** two rings, `:testing` and `:stable`, and no LTS. This RFC turns that into a tag design, a promotion rule and a rollout plan.

**Recommended (option A):**
- The bare `:<flavor>` tag becomes `:stable`. Every existing install, doc and ISO stays on it and now gets soaked images.
- The gated nightly becomes `:<flavor>-testing`.
- Today's ungated candidate tag moves from `-testing` to `-candidate`.

**Promotion:** a new `promote-stable.yml` promotes each cell by digest once its `:testing` image meets all of these:
- it has soaked for at least `soak_days` (default 3);
- no open `release-blocker` issue names the cell;
- the post-publish desktop-contract and lifecycle sweeps are green;
- every `Soak-After:` trailer since the current `:stable` is honoured.

**Rollout:** four phases. Phase 1 only renames the candidate and adds the `-testing` ring. The default users' tag does not change until phase 3, after a week of dry-run.

**Process:** per `RFC-PROCESS.md`, this PR merges after a maintainer comment approves the approach, and ADR 0016 is recorded on merge. The five decisions are listed at the end of the RFC.

Docs only. Labelled `hold`.

body:
Fixes three SSW bars stacked on the same days in the regional swells and storms card (San Diego, Oct 31 – Nov 5).

**Cause.** The detector peaked one long SSW plateau three times. The swell held 3–3.5 ft from Oct 30 to Nov 2 while its period drifted from 13 s to 11 s. `groupEvents` keeps one event per beach in a group, so the three peaks survived grouping as three region events.

**Fix.** After grouping, `regional.ts` joins groups that are the same kind, match in direction and period (the same 45° and 3 s rules `groupEvents` uses) and have overlapping windows. The strongest peak leads, and the window spans every joined peak. `groupEvents` and the detector are unchanged, so alerts, snapshots, Discovery, Week Scout and the story are untouched. The cache key moves to v3.

**Checked against live data.** I replayed San Diego read-only on today's stored forecasts. The three SSW events became one: 13 s, 4 ft, Oct 31 – Nov 5. These stay separate: the 18 s forerunner (Oct 30), the WNW swells (Nov 3–5 and Nov 7–8), the W swell (Nov 5) and the W storm (Nov 6).

**Tests.** Two new tests in `regional.test.ts`:
- a plateau peaked twice joins into one event over both windows;
- two non-overlapping swells from one direction stay apart.

All 174 swell-events tests pass, and lint and typecheck are clean.

**Release.** Only native calls this route, and the card is behind `EXPO_PUBLIC_REGIONAL_SWELLS_ENABLED` (off), so nothing changes for users until the flag-on OTA.

author: f-sharbati
body:
New users previously inherited illustrative plant values, and the live estimate used a simplified AC-capacity climate multiplier. This update starts new accounts empty, offers downloadable sample CSVs, and predicts from total plant capacity, location and imported aggregate production without requiring panel or inverter inventories. Existing passwords, sessions and readings are preserved.

Daily imports are deduplicated per source/date and combined across sources, with incomplete coverage excluded from calibration. A pvlib aggregate geometry model replaces the simplified path for configured plants; next Jalali month and 30 days beginning today disclose weather versus climate coverage. Annual output is an unadjusted diagnostic baseline, not a forced Tehran target or validated accuracy claim.

Login remains password-only, with an eight-character minimum and email-code password recovery. Recovery adds expiring, attempt-limited, single-use codes and revokes sessions only after a valid reset. SMTP credentials remain outside source and images. Project-admin-only Email settings verify fresh SMTP credentials over TLS, store them privately, and show setup/success/failure notifications. Legacy exposed credentials are disabled until fresh setup; ordinary password login and CSV imports remain available.

Validation: 64 backend tests; optimized Next.js/TypeScript build; browser empty-account setup, two-file import, multi-source totals, login and recovery using a local SMTP sink. Real SMTP authentication passed without sending messages. The production database backup clone preserved all users/passwords/sessions/workspaces/imports and 61 owner readings (3930.115 kWh); replay source identities matched. Final container and public acceptance are recorded in deploy/release.json. Independent seasonal forecasting accuracy and Android device acceptance remain unverified. Owner clarification: slide 15 describes an 8% target; slide 17 is the measured comparison.

Closes #3

body:
## Cosa fa

Foto delle serate: l'admin le carica dalla scheda della serata, il sito le mostra nella pagina della serata passata, nella Galleria e in home. Via i riquadri finti "da fornire".

**Admin** (solo admin, `/admin/eventi/[id]/foto`, con un riquadro "Foto" nella scheda): caricamento di molte foto insieme con avanzamento per ognuna e "Riprova" sulla sola fallita; fino a 4 foto in evidenza (se non ne scegli, il sito usa le prime 4); ordine con ← Prima / Dopo →; nascondi; elimina; elimina tutte; credito facoltativo "Foto di …"; spazio occupato; massimo 150 foto per serata.

**Pubblico**: pagina della serata passata con griglia e vista a schermo intero (dita, frecce, tastiera, Esc, senza librerie); Galleria con locandina, foto in evidenza e "Vedi tutte (N)"; home con le foto in evidenza delle ultime serate. Senza foto vere la sezione della home sparisce e la Galleria dice "Le foto arriveranno presto". Le foto si vedono solo se la serata è pubblicata e finita e la foto non è nascosta. Link "Ti riconosci e vuoi togliere una foto? Scrivici".

## Come

- Il browser riduce ogni foto (2000 px + miniatura 600 px, JPEG sempre ridisegnato: niente EXIF né GPS) e la manda **diretta a Supabase Storage** con un indirizzo firmato che il server rilascia solo a un admin; il server poi controlla i file (esistono, < 1,5 MB) e solo allora la foto compare. In sviluppo, senza Supabase, va su disco.
- Dati in una **tabella a parte** (`foto_serate`, più `serate_foto_credito`), non nella riga `archivio_mvp`: le vendite non rallentano e due admin che caricano insieme non si pestano. Accesso solo da `lib/dati/foto.ts` con il controllo del ruolo.
- Spazio: circa 600 KB a foto, 60 foto ≈ 36 MB. Nel piano gratuito (1 GB) entrano circa 16–27 serate.
- Non toccati: porta, pagamenti, intro, `archivio*.ts`, tipo `Evento`, locandine e piantine.

## Da configurare sull'istanza online

1. Applicare `supabase/migrations/20261030000000_foto_serate.sql` (tabelle + bucket pubblico `foto-serate`, solo JPEG/WebP fino a 1,5 MB). Non servono altre regole né variabili nuove.
2. Poi provare un caricamento vero da telefono: **la parte Supabase (indirizzo firmato, elenco dei file, rimozione) non è stata provata contro un progetto vero**, solo la modalità su disco e i test.

## Cose da sapere

- **Una serata oggi non si può eliminare dall'app** (solo toglierla dalla pubblicazione). `eliminaFotoSerata` è pronta e testata; quando arriverà "Elimina serata" dovrà chiamarla. C'è anche il bottone "Elimina tutte le foto della serata".
- Dopo l'eliminazione l'immagine può restare visibile per un po' a chi ha il link diretto (cache dello Storage).
- **Privacy**: l'informativa va completata per le foto e verificata dal consulente prima di pubblicare foto vere (nota nel README).
- **Un test già in main fallisce a quest'ora, non per questa PR**: `tavoli: pagamento online…` in `permessi.test.ts` si aspetta 24 ore di scadenza per le richieste del PR, ma da 24 ore prima di Halloween (seed, 31.10 alle 22:00) la scadenza si accorcia. Si sistema da solo dopo la serata o rendendo il test indipendente dalla data.

## Prove

- `npm run typecheck` e `npm run build` ok. `npm test`: 98 test, 97 ok + quello sopra (87 + 11 nuovi: permessi di staff e PR, in evidenza max 4, nascoste non pubbliche, serate non pubblicate o non finite, eliminazione con file e credito, caricamenti abbandonati).
- Provato nel browser (desktop e 390×844): 10 foto caricate, 4 in evidenza (la quinta rifiutata), una nascosta, una spostata; pagina della serata (9 foto, la nascosta non c'è), Galleria, home, scorrimento con tastiera e con le dita (soglia 50 px, lo scroll verticale non cambia foto), nessuno scorrimento orizzontale; senza foto niente riquadri finti. Non provato: la conferma del browser per "Elimina" (il pannello la scarta da solo; coperto dai test).

## Acid 303 inside Rack 1.0

Draft. Do not merge into #78 or main.

**Source:** #69 `c23b88d2af70c90e38930d7106899144a116d2c5` (stacked on #59 `d4fb97663edcf0c5b2340c7c8d2f31b1f9628bfc`). Those branches were not modified.

**This HEAD:** `0a7fae3fcb2492c528c28888bd132d1cf8910119`.

### Imported
Existing Acid DSP (`AcidEngine`, `AcidGenerator`) and the native `VoxAcid303` module. Canonical `libs/instrument/abi/VoxModuleAbiV2.h` only. The Acid-local ABI pin was not copied.

- `voxModuleEntryV2`, 80 descriptors, `poolIndex` 0–79.

- SOUND page: `instruments/acid/sound.json`, all 80 parameters, waveform stays a continuous knob.
- Pattern: one HOST lane, fields NOTE / OCTAVE / ACCENT / SLIDE / GATE / VELOCITY / TIE. The Rack stores it and `scheduleHostPattern` emits the MIDI. The module does not keep a second pattern.
- Development-signed `VoxAcid303.vins` via `vox_add_vins`. No private key in the tree. Production signing stays the offline release-key procedure.

### Not imported
`AcidParameterBridge`, Acid `PluginProcessor` / `PluginEditor`, APVTS registration, the pinned ABI header, the unsigned `vox.vins/1-input` manifest.

When a loaded package already provides `com.ultimavox.acid`, the built-in Acid descriptor is omitted so the package is the instrument. Tests that construct the built-in provider directly still get Acid.

- `pattern_tests` passed (2125), including the HOST note-lane scheduler.
- `acid_tests` passed (80674, compliance 667).
- `acid_module_tests` passed. Production-shaped prepare is 512 MIDI and 80 parameter changes. The 4096 line in `ACID_RT` is still the artificial cap, not the Rack schedule.
- Linux module `ACID_RT` at 48 kHz / 128: typical p95 33 µs, stress 64+64 p95 53 µs, cap 4096 p95 798 µs. This is the module alone, not Rack+FX.

author: orbit-agent-01
body:
## Task

ORB-20267 — Read explain arm state before truncating condition subjects

### Description

Introduced by ORB-20156 at 0af836eafe5ad1009d5332536c1f2e9b3e19ab4a (delivery #7164), found by frozen review ORB-20254. Severity: low; condition explain can call an already-fired matching subject armed, misleading an operator about whether the next pass will fire. The stored state remains correct.

The new Report::record implementation in crates/orbit-core/src/application/automation/explain/mod.rs:453-467 looks up an individual match's state in tracking.subjects and defaults a missing entry to armed once any state is tracked. However, condition_status at application/automation/condition/status.rs:199-205,248 sorts subjects to put active fires/holds/waits first and then truncates the vector to twenty. This is a display sample, not the complete durable state. Explain's matches independently choose the first twenty natural-ID matches. A genuine fired subject omitted from the tracking sample therefore gets a fabricated armed label and loses its hold values.

Deterministic public-runtime reproduction at the pinned revision: create 21 matching tasks and an enabled condition with max_matches=21; persist a valid current-epoch ConditionState in which the lowest-ID task was baselined fired and the other twenty are fired without baselined=true (as after later edges). The status sample prioritizes the twenty ordinary fired subjects and omits the baselined task. explain_automation returns that lowest-ID task in matches with arm=armed although its durable arm is Fired. The isolated runtime harness prints durable_arm=fired output_arm=armed listed_subjects=20. No worker or clock is launched.

Resolve each displayed match's arm/hold from complete stored subject state, then apply independent output limits. Preserve the 20-item display bounds without treating truncation as an untracked subject.

Duplicate checks: all-status orbit.search `condition explain armed` and `condition explain projection` returned phase-one tasks ORB-19990/ORB-20191/ORB-20193/ORB-20194 and the phase-two delivery, but no finding about this state-projection truncation. Escape: no_test; the culprit's CLI assertion checks one tracked matching subject only, never more than twenty subjects with different display priorities.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Each match returned by condition explain reports its actual durable arm and hold values even when more than twenty subjects are tracked and the tracking sample omits that match.
- A focused public CLI/runtime regression with a baselined low-ID match and twenty higher-priority tracked subjects fails before repair and passes after it; display arrays remain bounded.

## Execution Summary

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

Outcome: success. Condition explain now projects each displayed match from the complete durable ConditionState, sharing the status projection for arm, true_since and hold remaining. Both tracking subjects and matches retain their independent 20-item limits. The isolated CLI regression seeds a current-epoch state with 21 matching fired subjects; the baselined lowest ID is omitted from tracking but returned in matches with fired and its hold values. Before the fix the focused regression failed with armed and missing hold values; after the fix it passed. The existing condition CLI scenarios, including the storm refusal path, passed. Manual QA was not run separately because the regression drives the real CLI and exercises the reported failure path.

Validation passed: make ci-guards; cargo fmt --all -- --check; rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/orbit-cli/tests/task/condition_auto_task_cli.rs; scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo test -p orbit-cli --test task condition_auto_task_cli:: -- --nocapture (3 passed); scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo clippy -p orbit-core --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::disallowed_methods; scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo clippy -p orbit-core --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::disallowed_methods; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo doc --no-deps -p orbit-core; scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo clippy -p orbit-cli --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::disallowed_methods; scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo clippy -p orbit-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::disallowed_methods; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" scripts/build-budget.py -- cargo doc --no-deps -p orbit-cli. Pipeline final validation: not run locally; pipeline owns final validation, with no command list supplied in the task snapshot. No golden surface changed.

Baseline HEAD 0b9c2225acf836d7066438bb836591aa0731ae5d; initial status clean. Reconciled git status and git diff --check: four modified deliverable files only, no untracked or staged changes, no cleanup leftovers. condition/mod.rs is outside the explicit selectors and re-exports the shared subject projection for explain. No docs changes needed; JSON shape and display bounds remain unchanged. No known deviations or remaining risks.

</details>

En el túnel (rama `feat/treasurer`, base local migrada):

author: jet-pang
body:
## 背景

ADR 0052（#417，已合并）复审修订轮（review-151「复审（修订轮）」N3 / N4）。#417 在本修订推送前已合并，故另开此 PR。

## N3（High）：迁移步骤改为「升级前改写」

#417 版本的 runbook 让 aster-api 以 `ASTER_REVALIDATION_ENABLED=false` 部署、先跑 report 重验再 enforce。这不成立：
`PolicyExecutionGate.prefetch/check` 在新 toolchain 下找不到非 advisory 校验行时，会在请求里同步 `typecheckVersion`，
`aster.compile.typecheck=enforce` 下直接 422 `policy_version_invalid` 并写入 invalid 行。关闭启动期重验只是把拦截推迟到第一次执行。

改为：
1. 只读扫描 → 2. 作者把命中版本改写为 Let 并发布（新旧工具链都能编译）→ 3. 常规升级（启动期重验保持开启）。
- 兜底：来不及改完时，升级窗口内临时 `ASTER_COMPILE_TYPECHECK=warn`，report 重验找出命中并改写，清零后恢复 enforce；写明窗口内所有类型错误都只告警。
- 删除「`ASTER_REVALIDATION_ENABLED=false` 可提供缓冲期」的说法，并解释原因；不推荐 `ASTER_COMPILE_GATE=off`。
- ADR §6 同步；合入顺序注明 ts 与 test 已可任意先后合并（ts#269 的往返白名单跳过语料仓中尚不存在的文件）。
- runbook 写明 `has_let_same_name = t` 时须人工确认 Let 在 Set 之前、在同一作用域链上。

## N4（Medium）：扫描不再按 locale 分流

`scripts/ops/adr0052-scan-set-statements.sql` 对每个版本跑 en / de / zh 三条模式（不再按 `locale` 列 JOIN），新增 `pattern_lang` 列。
此前 `zh_CN` 或空 locale 的 zh 策略会被漏扫。

验证（一次性 Postgres 17 容器 `fixadr51-pg151`，用后已删除）：7 条样例中
- en / de 首次声明、locale 为 `zh_CN` 与空串的 zh 首次声明 → 均命中且 `has_let_same_name = f`；
- en 小写 `set` 写回、zh 写回 → `t`；
- 字符串字面量中的 `Set x to` → 不命中；三种语言之间无交叉误报。

## N6（High，终审）：发版门禁

运行一次发版列车 = 升级生产 aster-api（`release-train.yml` 最后一层 dispatch aster-api `deploy.yml` 带 trainId → k3s image-pin PR 验签后自动合并 → ArgoCD 滚动更新；已核对 platform `run-train.sh` 与 aster-api `deploy.yml`）。core#225 已在 core main。runbook 开头新增「发版门禁」，ADR §6 同步：
1. 扫描清零或改写全部发布之前，**不得运行任何发版列车**（含不相关 hotfix 列车）。
2. 必须先发版：先向 k3s `apps/aster-lang/cloud/deployment.yaml`（namespace `aster-cloud`，Deployment / 容器 `aster-api` 的 `env:`）合入 `ASTER_COMPILE_TYPECHECK=warn`（runbook 附 diff 与 `kubectl … jsonpath` 生效确认命令），确认新 pod 已带该变量，再运行列车。
3. 列车后检查重验 invalid 列表，命中清零后向 k3s 提 PR 删除该变量，恢复 enforce。runbook §3 改名为「升级 aster-api（= 运行发版列车）」，回滚一节也注明回滚同样会触发部署。

## 关联

- ADR 0052：#417（已合并）
- aster-cloud/aster-lang-core#225、aster-cloud/aster-lang-locales#112（已合并）
- aster-cloud/aster-lang-ts#269、aster-cloud/aster-lang-test#181（已合并）
- L6：aster-cloud/aster-lang-ts#270

Refs aster-cloud/aster-lang-truffle#151

author: tatskaari
body:
**What this is:** a prologue before the hanged clerk, paced like the start of BG3: you're thrown in on the road, a few fights with a handful of people who make them matter, and a palace guard takes you to the King. Then the night in the palace, and the clerk as before, but now you've met the King, and maybe heard of his grain clerk Wendell before he's found hanged.

Stacked on #679 (the board fights in the story), which the prologue's fights need.

1. **The King's Road** (the afternoon two days before the Assembly). It opens on the cart as the game begins, with no walk. You're riding into Caerwyn on old Barnaby Fitch's cart of three hundred cushions for the Assembly's seats (the King ordered them himself), beside his granddaughter Tansy, nine. A couple of lines, then goblins out of the blackthorn shrieking "Be seen! Be seen!" (**fight 1**, with a second wave up the road behind). Afterwards there's smoke over the toll bridge, and the dead goblins carry new silver heron pennies.
2. **Garrow's Toll Bridge** (dusk, a walk along the road). The one palace patrol on the road this week (Corporal Haskett and her nephew, Guardsman Tob Wren) is pinned behind a hay wain. Garrow the toll-warden shouts about the King's penny through his shutters. **Fight 2** is the goblins' rearguard. After a breather (Garrow's ledger has twelve palace grain wagons crossing his bridge laden: "lost to goblins"? Not on his bridge), the war-boss Grisk comes over the bridge on his worg (**fight 3**). Two Kläggenheim axemen may ride up mid-fight. Then Fitch and Tansy roll up, and Wren takes you to the King.
3. **The King's Thanks** (evening, comes to you in the palace). A short supper on a tray. The King guesses how you take your tea and is delighted about the cushions. He puts the goblins off "until after the Assembly", and may speak fondly of Wendell, whose letter about "irregularities in the Roll" is on his after-the-Assembly pile. You get a purse and a room. Then a night's rest, and the hanged clerk at first light.

Every fight can be lost without the story ending (Fitch drags you onto the cart; the axemen and the patrol see the goblins off and Wren has you carried in). The only way it ends is drawing steel on the King.

## Try it
- **The page preview** (once CI publishes it): https://tatskaari.github.io/kingmaker/pr-preview/pr-681/play/. It needs your OpenRouter key (the fake GM plays every scene with the granary's four replies, so it's only good for the plumbing). New game, any character.
- **A terminal:** `npm run dev`, then `npm run play -- new --session me --build fighter` opens the road. Say a line or two and the goblins come. In the fight, `act --id fight` goes to the board. `npm run play -- go` walks to the bridge after the road. The King comes to you after the bridge.
- **What to look at:**
  - **The pacing:** how quickly the first fight comes (the cue's limit is the third exchange), whether the fights feel like set pieces, and whether the short talk between them carries the emotion (Tansy, Haskett's arm, Wren).
  - **The seeds:** "Be seen!", the heron pennies, Garrow's ledger and the King's mention of Wendell. They should puzzle, not explain: nothing in the prologue says who Longlegs is.
  - **The King's morning:** if the King told you of the letter that first evening, his "He wrote to me" should land differently (its background says he knows you know).

## How it works
- **Three new scenes** (`campaigns/caerwyn/scenes/kings-road`, `toll-bridge`, `kings-thanks`), each a .kmscene the plugin edits. The fights are planned fight events, as the Heron's "Blades out" is. A new map, `maps/kings-road.kmmap`: hedges and the river close each region, so the only ways in and out are the road and the drovers' track, and the riders come up the road. Three places. The King's parlour is a new room on the palace's map, inside its old bounds. Lore notes for the five new people (Fitch, Tansy, Haskett, Wren, Garrow), and the fronts, the grain truth and "Caerwyn now" told of the road. QA truth sheets for the three scenes.
- **A scene that comes to the player** (`summons`, docs/scene-format.md): it opens as soon as the story reaches it rather than waiting in its place. That's the game's first scene as the game begins (the road), or the next as the last ends (the bridge, then the King's thanks). Until now only `next-morning` did that (the King's morning). The plugin's Scene view has it as "Comes to the player".
- **Where a backstory ends** is the campaign's now (`creation.begins`, docs/scenario-format.md), not the code's: Caerwyn's ends on the road, before anyone at court has asked anything of them. The backstory's order-of-events checks follow the new start (they catch "the King sent for me" and "the King's investigator"). The plugin's scenario view has the field. The two backstory goldens are re-recorded from the game (ai/rules/golden/README.md says so).
- **The scenario check** now walks on from the map of every scene it reaches: a summons puts the player on its map. The King's thanks is how the town is reached.
- The hanged clerk has a long rest before it (the night in the palace) and a line of background, and its hook has the King asking at first light. Goblin weapons are in the statblocks.
- **Tests start at the granary, as before.** About 118 tests across 33 files assumed a new game begins in the granary lane. Rather than rewrite each, `shared/scene/testdata/from-the-granary.ts` gives them Caerwyn without its prologue: the clerk first, the old start, the prologue's scenes, places, map, parlour and looks left out. `caerwynPack` uses it unless `prologue: true`, and so do the host, page and e2e tests that read the folder. The prologue has its own story tests (`simulation/src/story/prologue.test.ts`), and `npm run arc` plays the campaign as it is.

## Checks
- `npm run typecheck`; `npm test`: 1183 of 1183, the new prologue tests among them. `npm run screens`: 802 of 802. The campaign check: 9 scenes, 7 places, 5 maps, no problems.
- `npm run arc` on a real stack (the fake model): 20 of 20, the prologue first (the road opens on the cart, the walk to the bridge, the King's thanks coming to the player in the palace, the walk from the palace to the granary) and then the story to The End.
- `npm run e2e`: all 41 steps pass on a real stack. It installs Caerwyn from the granary, as it always played it; the arc plays the prologue.
- The plugin: typecheck, `test:host` (83 of 83), the build, and Playwright (47 of 47).

## What's open
- **No live QA round yet** on real models. The prologue's fights are the board's and #679's, and they haven't been played by personas. That's next, with a pre-approved round of persona games on the three scenes.
- **The map's lead markers are the code's**: a new story scene needs an entry in `shared/map/places.ts` (where it's played, its lead marker, where you come out), so a scene authored in Obsidian doesn't reach the map without code. That's worth making data, the plugin's job.
- **No level-up after the prologue.** The game starts at level 3 as before, and the King's morning is still the only milestone. One option is starting at level 2 and levelling at the clerk.
- **Opening up the city** before the hanged clerk (exploring, new people, side quests) is the next piece, as discussed. The King's thanks ends in the evening, so the city could slot in between it and the morning.

author: babkenmes
body:
## Summary
Bitcoin transfers could emit a positive change output below its script's dust threshold, causing RPC -26 rejections even when the deposit amount was valid. Omit uneconomical change and include its value in the actual fee while preserving the requested deposit amount.

- Estimate signed SegWit/Taproot virtual sizes with actual output scripts, memo length, and change using a single fee-rate snapshot.
- Validate outputs before signing and broadcast; include output values, scripts, dust thresholds, and actual fee/vsize in broadcast failures.
- Fix recipient-address selection in gas estimates and propagate construction/fee errors instead of returning partial transactions or zero fees.
- Keep full-balance Max fee probes separate from funded transaction construction. Unsupported input scripts fail explicitly.

The reported 5,464/5,400-sat amounts are covered by regression tests. The exact rejected session transaction was unavailable, so incident attribution remains unconfirmed. Dust thresholds use Bitcoin Core's default relay policy; custom node policy may differ.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @layerswap/wallet-bitcoin test` — 7 tests passed, including dust boundaries, both reported amounts, full-balance estimation, insufficient funds, and signed virtual-size comparisons.
- `pnpm --filter @layerswap/wallet-bitcoin check:types` — passed.
- ESLint for the Bitcoin adapter source and tests — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

author: paulyhedral
body:
There's no issue for this flake: I found it while running the gate for #357.

## The flake

`knot-mcp-probe` `runner::tests::a_listing_written_to_stderr_is_still_read` failed once during a full `make` run, at **10.02 s against a fixed 10 s runner budget**. It passed on rerun in 0.32 s. Under load, spawning `/bin/sh` and draining both pipes outlasted the test's budget, so a correct runner returned `TimedOut` and the test's `.expect(…)` failed.

That 10 s was the **test's** budget, not production's: the real probe uses `PROBE_TIMEOUT`. But it decided the test's result. Six other subprocess tests in the file used the same fixed 10 s.

## Fix

This is the same idea as #337 (#14): decide by what happened, not by a clock.

- **The decision is now a pure function.** Which stream answers a finished run (stdout, falling back to stderr, or an error with stderr and the exit code) was inline in `CommandRunner::run`. It's now `outcome(label, success, code, stdout, stderr)`. `run` calls it, and behaviour is unchanged: the existing tests all pass unmodified.
- **Each case is tested directly**, with no subprocess and no clock: empty stdout read from stderr (the Gemini case), stdout winning over stderr, a failed run that still listed, a failed run reporting stderr and its code, and a signal-killed run reporting `-1`.
- **The clock no longer decides the subprocess tests.**
  - Tests that check spawning, the working directory, environment, stdin and missing programs now use a named `HANG_GUARD` of 120 s. It's documented as only stopping a stuck test, not as a budget the machine must beat.
  - The stdin test drops its `elapsed < 5s` assertion. A stdin that wasn't closed makes `cat` wait, which already ends as `TimedOut`, so the run exiting is the proof.
  - The two timeout tests keep their 200 ms budget and their elapsed check, because killing the child on time is exactly what they test.

The only non-test change is the behaviour-preserving extraction in `runner.rs`.

## Verification

- **Mutation check:** with a successful run made to ignore stderr, both the subprocess test and the new pure test fail. Restored afterwards.
- **Under load:** the `runner::tests` group passes 30/30 against 8 parallel `/bin/sh` fork-storm loops, the load used for #337. I didn't reproduce the original failure under that storm; it occurred once, during a full parallel workspace test run.
- `cargo clippy -p knot-mcp-probe --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `make` passes locally.
  - The first full `make` run here failed in a **different** crate: `knot-processes` `command::tests::unchecked_run_reports_a_non_zero_exit_as_output`, at 10.01 s. It's the same flake shape, but there the 10 s is the production default timeout, so it needs its own change. I've reported it separately. The rerun was green.

author: kajisho5
body:
## Summary

ECOSYSTEM_ROADMAP step 3: **`VOICE_CLEANUP`**, a typed wrapper of `ffmpeg-skill/audio --voice` (ADR-16).

- **Parameters:** `level` is required and takes `light`, `medium` or `strong`; there is no default, so the caller decides (ADR-3). The other parameter is `audio_stream`, an integer ≥ 0 (default 0). `--voice` exposes nothing else, so no strength, cutoff or other flag was invented. Unknown fields are refused, `filter` among them.
- **Engine shape is detected, not version-gated (ADR-15):** `voice` is added to `FLAGS_USED["audio"]`, and its form is read from the located contract.
  - ffmpeg-skill ≥ 1.13 declares the levels as an enum. The skill passes `--voice <level>`.
  - 0.12.2 … 1.12 declare `voice` as a boolean. The skill passes a bare `--voice`, which runs the same medium chain byte for byte.
  - A level the engine can't run is refused while planning (dry run too) with `TOOL_ERROR` `voice_level_unsupported`, `retryable: false` and `details.available_levels`. It is never swapped for the medium chain.
- **Never sent together with `--denoise`/`--denoise-strength`.** `audio.py` ignores them when `--voice` is set.
- **afftdn limit:** afftdn only accepts `nf` from −80 to −20 dB. The medium and strong chains use a fixed `nf=-25`, so `--voice` can't go out of range. The integration test checks every `afftdn=nf=` value it observes. NOISE_REDUCTION does have this problem: a `strength_db` from 10 up to (not including) 20 fails at run time (FFmpeg 6.1 reports "Numerical result out of range"). That operation is not changed here; it is recorded in docs/STATE.md under PLANNED.
- **Provenance:**
  - `parameters.level`
  - `measurements.voice_cleanup` (`{level, ffmpeg_skill_flag}`, the flag form actually passed)
  - the full filter chain, through ffmpeg-skill's observed command in `tool_commands_observed`
  - the output's operations chain
- **Required capabilities:** every filter any level may use (`highpass`, `deesser`, `afftdn`, `acompressor`, `alimiter`).
- **Capability id:** `audio.voice_cleanup`.
- **Doctor:** reports `checks.ffmpeg_skill.voice_levels`.
- **Docs:** README table, SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, architecture, the ffmpeg-skill measurements of the three chains on 0.12.2 and 2.21.0, testing, STATE, and ADR-16.

**Contract:** adding an operation is breaking for pinning agents. The `tools`, `provides` and `ffmpeg_skill.flags_used.audio` blocks change and `operations/VOICE_CLEANUP` is added. `tests/contract/contract.json` is regenerated. The version is not bumped by hand; the release workflow bumps it from the label (ADR-14).

**video-production-agent impact:** checked with its own `contract_drift`, `contract_breaking_drift` and `check_contract` against the live contract.
- `breaking_drift` is empty. The changed blocks (`tools`, `ffmpeg_skill`, a new operation) are all outside `FATAL_DRIFT_KEYS`.
- If this is released as **0.5.0** (a `feature` label resolves to minor), `check_contract` refuses it: `SUPPORTED_SKILL_VERSIONS` only covers `0.1.`–`0.4.`. That marks `audio-production` MISSING in the agent until the agent adds `"0.5."` and re-pins.
- A 0.4.x release would not be refused.

**Also fixed:** on Windows, a timed-out node could leave its partial intermediate behind. `taskkill` returns before the killed ffmpeg's output handle is released, so the one `unlink` attempt failed silently. `Executor._remove_partial` now retries until the file is gone (deadline 10 s). This was seen as a flaky `test_timeout_is_a_retryable_tool_error` on windows-latest in run 41132339948. The assertion is unchanged, and there is a new unit test for the retry.

author: f4ah6o
body:
## Problem

A held composing TextSession cannot currently adopt a new bounds-only field without replacing the editing owner. That prevents the consumer from preparing a resized scene around the same session and its pending text observation.

## Change

Add an opaque `BoundsProposal`: `prepare_bounds` validates the current target and stages a `TextField::with_bounds` result; `publish_bounds` accepts that candidate only for the exact unchanged session publication. The same captured text target, owner, session ID and delivery watermark remain valid across a bounds-only change, so a previously accepted host record does not need a new epoch or sequence. The field keeps its composition and rollback snapshot. Competing, stale, foreign or reused proposals reject.

This is **only a bounds-only TextSession primitive**. It does not implement a transaction across the Yami runtime, focus, scene and native host, solve accepted-record recovery, or remeasure preview/rollback for scale or font changes. It must not be used as evidence that the Shared Settings P1 is fixed. The new runtime dependency edge is only to gpui's portable `primitives` rectangle.

## Validation

- `moon test text_session --target all --deny-warn`: 38/38 on each of native, JS, Wasm and WasmGC.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_check_contracts.py`: 40/40.
- `moon fmt text_session --check`, `python3 scripts/check_contracts.py`, `git diff --check`: pass.
- No native GUI, scale/font remeasurement, host/scene atomic publication, or live IME execution.

Draft for integration and independent same-HEAD review; depends on #177.

author: rhonda-rodododo
body:
Closes #2333

## What was wrong (measured, not assumed)

A provider's id for a call, recording or message is the key into the provider's CDR, which holds the caller's number. Before this PR:

- `callId` **is** the provider's id (`active_calls.call_id` is the webhook's `CallSid`, `routes/telephony.ts:402`). The logger redacted `callSid`, `parentCallSid` and `recordingSid` only because the key names happen to contain `sid` (`SENSITIVE_KEY_RE`). `callId` passed straight through, as did any interpolated message and any provider error text.
- `audit_log.details` stored `callSid` / `callId` / `recordingSid` as **plaintext JSON for every `system` entry** (`callMissed`, `voicemailReceived`, `providerRecordingDeleteFailed`, …). I reproduced this against real Postgres (see "Verified by breaking it").
- `provider_recordings.last_error` stored the provider's own error text, which names the call and recording it refused.
- `middleware/request-logger.ts` logged `/api/calls/<providerCallId>/answer` at info level, twice per request.

So `ringing.ts:43` (the line in the issue) was actually already printing `"callSid":"[REDACTED]"`; the live leaks were the sites above.

## The fix: a keyed ref, not deletion

`providerRef(id) = "pr_" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(HKDF-SHA256(HMAC_SECRET, info = LABEL_PROVIDER_REF_KEY), id))[0..16]` — `lib/provider-ref.ts`.

**Precedent reused:** `messagingContactHash` / `suppressionHashes` (`lib/messaging-contact-hash.ts`): an HKDF-derived key under a dedicated label, then HMAC. Same shape, its own label (`LABEL_PROVIDER_REF_KEY`, appended at registry index **108**, same five files as #2314's `LABEL_CALL_RECORDING_SEAL`), computed with `@noble/hashes` like `ivr-media-url.ts` so the logger never has to load the native library. Root is `HMAC_SECRET` ("only hashes" role), not a file-only key: the ids it hashes are already plaintext in the database, so a DB reader gains nothing and a log reader has no DB. With no usable `HMAC_SECRET` it fails closed to `pr_unkeyed`, never the id.

Where it applies:

- **Logger** (`lib/logger.ts`): fields `callId callSid parentCallSid legSid recordingSid messageSid callUuid callControlId providerCallId providerMessageId` are written as `<key>Ref`; any Twilio/SignalWire SID (`[A-Z]{2}`+32 hex) inside a message or value is replaced. This is a sink-level backstop, so a new `logger.x({ callSid })` is safe by default. `messageId` is deliberately *not* matched (the Signal queue uses it for its own row ids).
- **Audit** (`services/audit.ts`): `AuditService.log` runs `details` through `withProviderRefs` before the hash chain commits, so every writer (system and user actors) is covered at the one insert.
- **Request log**: the matched route pattern (`/api/calls/:callId/answer`), never the URL. A scanner's URL is not echoed either.
- **Ledger error text** (`provider-recordings.ts`): SIDs scrubbed before `last_error` is stored.

**Debuggability preserved.** The ref is deterministic, so every line about one call carries the same ref. An operator with a failed call's SID from the provider console/CDR runs `docker compose exec app bun scripts/provider-ref.ts <sid>` (or `bun run provider-ref <sid>`) and greps for `pr_…`. Someone holding only our logs, or only the provider's records, cannot make that link without `HMAC_SECRET`. Cost: rotating `HMAC_SECRET` changes every ref, so older logs can no longer be looked up by SID. Documented in PROTOCOL §4.8 and DATA_CLASSIFICATION.

## The audit — every site writing a provider identifier

**Logs (now refs):** `services/ringing.ts:43, 344, 403, 432, 518 (was interpolated into the message), 536`; `routes/telephony.ts:149, 278, 396, 469, 475, 481, 487, 504, 552, 627, 635, 653, 715`; `services/voicemail.ts:52, 65, 92`; `services/call-recordings.ts:137, 227`; `services/call-hangup.ts:43, 48, 56`; `services/call-simulation.ts:65`; `services/calls.ts:99`; `services/provider-recordings.ts:182, 346, 360`; `lib/voip-push.ts:44 (was interpolated)`; `middleware/request-logger.ts` (URL path, 2 lines/request). Provider error bodies that reach logs through `Error.message` (`telephony/telnyx.ts:107,142`, `telephony/adapter.ts:532`, `messaging/sms/twilio.ts:211`, `messaging/whatsapp/*:148,250`) are scrubbed by the SID pattern.

**Audit rows (now refs):** `routes/telephony.ts:433, 499, 557, 630, 702`; `routes/calls.ts:446, 627`; `routes/notes.ts:153`; `routes/simulated-telephony.ts:160, 193, 217`; `services/provider-recordings.ts:187, 291, 369`; `services/hub-shred.ts:111`. No client or server code reads `details.callId`/`callSid` back (grepped `src/`, `apps/worker`, `apps/ios`, `apps/android`).

**Persisted ledger text:** `provider_recordings.last_error` (`services/provider-recordings.ts:357`).

**Metric labels: no provider id is written by any `incCounter`/`observeHistogram`/`setGauge` call site** — all label values are enumerated constants. **One latent exposure, reported not edited** (`routing-metrics` owns `routes/metrics.ts`; the code is `apps/worker/app.ts:109-114`): the `path` label of `llamenos_http_request_duration_seconds` normalises by *shape* (`/\/[0-9a-f-]{8,}(\/|$)/gi`). Twilio `CA…` and UUID ids are hex and collapse; ids that are not pure hex do **not**: Asterisk/ARI unique ids (`1730000000.42`), FreeSWITCH/Telnyx handles with other characters, and `RE…`/`SM…` SIDs. For those, `/api/calls/<id>/answer` becomes a high-cardinality label carrying the id. Fix: use `routePath(c)` from `hono/route` (what the request logger now does).

**Checked and clean:** Caddy (`caddy.j2`: access log off; default log deletes `request>uri`); `sip-bridge/src` (log lines carry no channel/call ids); no `console.*` call in `apps/worker` references an id; incident rows (already id-free, #2353).

## Deliberately left, and why

These need the raw id to function. Each is a named exception, not a silent one:

| Surface | Why raw |
|---|---|
| `active_calls.call_id`, `call_records.call_id`, `call_tokens.call_sid`, `provider_recordings.call_id`/`recording_sid` | Working keys. `recording_sid` is handed back to the provider to delete the recording. |
| Call id in API paths/bodies and relay events | Clients address a call by it. |
| **VoIP push payloads** (`lib/voip-push.ts`: APNs `call-id`, ntfy `call-id`) | The app needs it to answer. **This contradicts the "no provider identifier in a push payload" rule** and reaches Apple/ntfy. It cannot be fixed without separating our call id from the provider's. |
| Object-storage key `call-recordings/{hubId}/{callId}` | Derived from the call id. |
| Callback URLs we mint for the provider (`?callSid=`) | The provider already has it. |
| UUID-shaped ids **inside free text** (Vonage/Plivo/Telnyx error bodies) | Cannot be found by shape (a hub id is a UUID too); only fields named as ids are caught. Residual risk, stated. |

**Follow-up (split, not done here):** give calls our own opaque id and store the provider id as an attribute. It touches the schema, the webhook routes, relay events and the push payloads on three clients; it is what closes the VoIP-push row. I did not file an issue (audit-vs-ship division); the supervisor should.

## Verified by breaking it

`apps/worker/__tests__/integration/provider-id-surfaces.test.ts` (real Postgres, production services) drives voicemail, call-recording, retention-purge/shred/sweep and unaddressable-residue paths, then scans **all stderr/stdout, every `audit_log` row, `provider_recordings.last_error` and `hub_incidents`** for the raw SID, recording SID, message SID and a UUID call id, *and* asserts the ref is present (so the negative cannot pass on an unwritten surface). Plus the audit service, and the request log for hex, UUID and `1730000000.42` ids.

I reverted `audit.ts`, `logger.ts`, `request-logger.ts` and `provider-recordings.ts` to `main` and re-ran: **6/6 fail** — `audit_log` held `"callId":"CA0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"` and the recording SID in plaintext. Restored: 6/6 pass. Unit tests pin the construction against `node:crypto`, fai

body:
For the existing Wing Street test, not a new one.

### Two right answers, one pick

Wings over the fryer with no timer: *temp them before saucing* and *bin them and drop fresh* are both correct. A one-answer question can now mark several answers acceptable — the walker picks one and any marked answer earns full points.

It was failing silently in two ways before: the validator **refused** it outright, and the scoring used an exact set match, so two marked answers would have required selecting both — impossible on a radio, so zero for everyone.

Picking both still scores nothing (it is one answer, not pick-all). Pick-all is untouched. 378 tests pass, including that the old behaviour did not survive, and the old test that asserted the old rule now asserts the new one with the reasoning.

### Save to a file

The editor could load a `.json` but not produce one — a one-way door. An audit in the database could not be handed over, backed up, or copied to another region. Sits next to Load a file.

### Prompts

Drafting and revising did not know about multiple acceptable answers, so asking the AI box for that question would have got a single key back and quietly marked the other right answer wrong.

author: e107help[bot]
body:
### Why

This is the `release/v2.3.x` twin of #6866 by @scottdd, whose commit it carries with their authorship kept.

`MagpieRSS::__construct()` checks the parser `create_parser()` returns with `is_resource()` ([`magpie_rss.php#L110`](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/f49afa356d85e2039f67278d7ba2c5f966a1b23a/e107_handlers/magpie_rss.php#L110)). From PHP 8.0, `xml_parser_create()` returns an `XMLParser` object instead of a resource, so the check fails on every parse. `MagpieRSS::error()` then sets `$rss->ERROR` to `Failed to create an instance of PHP's XML parser.` and writes it to the PHP error log ([`magpie_rss.php#L612-L617`](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/f49afa356d85e2039f67278d7ba2c5f966a1b23a/e107_handlers/magpie_rss.php#L612-L617)), and parsing then carries on and succeeds with the same parser.

### What Changed

- `e107_handlers/magpie_rss.php`: the check accepts a resource (PHP 5.6 to 7.4) or an `XMLParser` instance (PHP 8.0 and later). `instanceof` does not autoload and is false for a class that does not exist, so the check is safe below PHP 8.

The commit is @scottdd's ca28a7f16aec3c744f7aeef27d1d619d9cf6ebda from #6866, cherry-picked with `-x`. It applied without a conflict and nothing in it was changed.

### How It Was Tested

- The whole unit suite passes on this branch under PHP 5.6 and 8.2, and the whole tree parses under PHP 5.6.
- For #6866's review, an RSS 2.0 feed and an Atom feed were parsed with the old and the new check on every PHP release line from 5.6 to 8.5. From 5.6 to 7.4 nothing differs. From 8.0 to 8.5 the old check sets `ERROR` and logs the message once per parse, and the new one does neither. Feed type, channel and items are the same with either.
- No new test, matching #6866 as it stands. The review there offers one. If it lands on #6866, it comes across here too.

### Backwards Compatibility

No BC impact on PHP 5.6 to 7.4, where the check passed before and still does. On PHP 8, a valid feed no longer leaves `$rss->ERROR` set, and the error log no longer gets a line per feed fetch. Rendered output does not change.

Merge after #6866, the two back to back.

Refs #6866

### Checklist

- [x] One issue per PR: the diff is scoped to this change only
- [x] Commit messages explain *why*, not just *what*
- [x] New or changed behavior has test coverage (or explain why not): explained under How It Was Tested
- [x] No unrelated reformatting, renames, or import reordering

author: udaychandra
body:
Spec: `audit-memory-store-workspace-tools`.

## Problem

`FileSystemMemoryBackend` keeps `/memories/` at `<workspace>/.agent/memory`, inside the root the workspace tools read. With `deny MemoryRead(/memories/private/**)`, `Read("./.agent/memory/private/a.md")` still returned the file, because the workspace tools reach it under a different key.

## Change

- **One owner.** `WorkspaceRoot.MEMORY_STORE` replaces `FileSystemMemoryBackend.STORAGE_SUBDIR`.
- **Refused as a target.** `WorkspaceRoot.canonical` throws `path is in the memory store; use MemoryRead: <spelling>` for a target at or below the store, however it was spelled (relative, absolute, through `..`, or through an in-root symlink). This applies with or without a memory backend. The check runs before the parent-directory check, so a path in a store that does not exist yet gets the same refusal. `resolveSafe` is unchanged, so `MemoryFiles` keeps working.
- **Skipped by walks.** `WorkspaceWalk.preVisitDirectory` skips the store with no withheld marker. The check runs before the start-of-walk check, so a direct `WorkspaceWalk.run` started at the store finds nothing as well.
- **Docs and CHANGELOG.** Javadoc, `session/README.md` and the Breaking rows, as the spec lists.

## Worth a look

- **`LS(".agent")` still prints `memory/`.** `LS` lists immediate entries and does not go through `WorkspaceWalk`. The spec's requirement is "no entry inside the store", so this is unchanged; `MemoryStoreIsolationTest` pins that output, and `LS` of the store itself is refused.
- **Two docs beyond the spec's list.** The root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` each state this confinement contract, so each gets one sentence.
- **Rejection reasons carry the tool name.** The session-level text is `Read: path is in the memory store; ...`, from the existing rejection path.
- **The `Grep` refusal test uses the pattern `TOP`.** The spec's `TOPSECRET` would put the secret in the `ToolUse` event's arguments and fail the no-secret assertion on its own. `CanonicalPermissionPathsTest` uses `TOP` too. The walk cases still search for `TOPSECRET`.

## Verification

`mvn -B clean verify javadoc:jar` passed on JDK 25: 7,729 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 66 skipped. PMD, CPD and the coverage gate passed in the same build.

Spec acceptance 4, by hand and reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Drop the `canonical` check | Fails `WorkspaceRootTest` and the `Read`, `Grep` and no-backend cases of `MemoryStoreIsolationTest` |
| Drop the walk skip | Fails the `.agent` `Grep` and `Glob` cases of `MemoryStoreIsolationTest` and both `WorkspaceWalkTest` cases |

The mutation runs used the three directly affected test classes, not the whole suite. One of them still had a test bug at the time, the `Grep` refusal pattern above, which also failed without a mutation; it is fixed in this PR and is not counted in the table.

**Net main-code lines: +11** (+14 / -3, excluding tests, docs and javadoc), against a budget of about +15.

author: themachineqq-spec
body: This branch sits on the video PR, so the same changes apply to photos and videos. The new migration is not applied to the live database. Run `supabase/migrations/20261030180000_perf_thumbs.sql` after the video migration. ## What changed - New uploads write WebP thumbnails at 320 px and 640 px (JPEG if the browser cannot encode WebP), plus a 16 px JPEG blur stored in `blur_data`. - Owners can replace old single JPEG thumbs from **Alte Vorschaubilder erneuern** in Mein Ordner. That re-encodes the current thumb and stores the two sizes. - Thumbnail PUT URLs are signed with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. GET URLs use a signing time rounded to 5 minutes, so the same URL repeats inside that window and stays valid for 10 minutes. - The service worker caches thumbnail responses by object path, ignoring the signature, and keeps at most 180 entries. - The group and folder grids are window-virtualized, with square tiles, prefetch of the next page, and image loads cancelled when a tile leaves the window. - `list_photos` still returns one page and now batch-signs both thumb sizes in that response. New indexes cover `(media_type, captured_at desc, id desc)` and the same with `owner_id`. `photo_months` feeds the month jump. - CI runs `npm run perf` against 20,000 rows (p95 page budget 120 ms) and checks the Gruppe first-load JS stays under 700 KB. ## Numbers Measured on 20,000 photo rows, 40 samples, local Postgres 16. Page time is the SQL keyset query plus local presigning. Before is one thumb URL per tile (24 signs). author: orrybaram
body:
## Summary

Theme recents count what Settings closes on, not every tile clicked:

```diff
 theme.setSelected(name)
   save themeName
-  push name onto recents
 
 <SettingsModal open>
+  useRecentThemesOnClose(open)
+    on open:  note global theme + each project's theme
+    on close: addRecent(each one that changed)
```

`POST /theme` (CLI/MCP) still counts its pick as recent: there is no Settings to close.

Settings › Theme:

```diff
 <ThemeSection>
-  <Input search />
+  <searchRow>
+    <Input search />
+    <sort radiogroup> Name | Color     # localStorage "manor.themeSort"
   <wall listbox>
-    arrow keys  → highlight; Enter selects
+    arrow keys  → highlight + select   # hover still only highlights
```

Color sort: dark themes, then light; within each, greys (dark → light), then tints round the hue wheel. Recent keeps newest-first.

The Settings modal grows from 760px × max 75vh to `min(1040px, 92vw)` × `min(820px, 88vh)`; the wall grows with it.

Keyboard focus ring (`App.css`): the `:not(...)` sat outside `:where()`, giving the rule (0,2,0) specificity, so it beat every component's `outline: none` (23 of them: theme wall, Files drawer, sheets, task detail, inputs). Now the whole selector is inside `:where()`:

```diff
-:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], a, [tabindex]):not(.xterm-helper-textarea, webview):focus-visible {
+:where(:is(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], a, [tabindex]):not(.xterm-helper-textarea, webview):focus-visible) {
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** ring drawn round the whole theme wall while arrowing through it
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orrybaram/manor/3165783429a98db4eadaacc764005f0ab8fae5bd/theme-recents-sort/before-focus-ring.png)
  **After:** no ring on the wall; the picked tile shows the place (arrows selected Night Owl, no Enter)
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orrybaram/manor/3165783429a98db4eadaacc764005f0ab8fae5bd/theme-recents-sort/20-keyboard-picks.png)

- **Recents.** Before: clicking Dracula, Tokyo Night, Manor listed all three. After: browsing Dracula → Tokyo Night shows only Manor (kept on the last close)…
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orrybaram/manor/3165783429a98db4eadaacc764005f0ab8fae5bd/theme-recents-sort/06a-filter-recent-browsing.png)
  …and after closing on Tokyo Night it joins, newest first:
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orrybaram/manor/3165783429a98db4eadaacc764005f0ab8fae5bd/theme-recents-sort/06-filter-recent.png)

- **Sort by color**
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orrybaram/manor/3165783429a98db4eadaacc764005f0ab8fae5bd/theme-recents-sort/21-sort-by-color.png)

- `tests/e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts` passes (2/2): browsing doesn't count as recent; closing does; arrows select without Enter; hover doesn't; wall `outlineStyle` is `none`; sort reorders and is remembered.
- `keyboard-navigation.spec.ts` "focus is visible at every stop" and all of `file-pane.spec.ts` pass. Two keyboard-navigation tests (Shift+F10 context menus, browser-pane shortcuts) fail identically on an untouched `main` build.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes; new unit tests for `keptThemePicks` and color sort. `pnpm test` failures are the pre-existing files only (hook-script, mcp-webview-server, router, workspace-stack-renders, keybinding-commands, paste-image-upload).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No data migration; existing `recentThemes` in settings.json are kept as they are.

**Blast Radius:** app-wide

The focus-ring change applies everywhere: any element whose own CSS sets `outline` now keeps it instead of being overridden. That's the intent for the 23 `outline: none` rules, but a component that set `outline: none` on a real control without its own `:focus-visible` style would lose its keyboard ring (the "focus is visible at every stop" e2e passes). The bigger fixed-height modal leaves short Settings pages with more empty space.

author: pukujan
body:
Refs #144

The `gates` frontend build has failed with `vite: not found` since 2026-10-20. Two changes that day caused it:

- A root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`packages: ["."]`). When `pnpm install` runs in `web/`, it now treats the repo root as the workspace and installs only the root package (25 packages), so web's own dependencies, vite included, never get installed.
- `maplibre-gl` was added to `web/package.json` without updating `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`, so `--frozen-lockfile` would fail even after the first problem is fixed.

The fix:

- The CI frontend step now runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-workspace`, the same flag the root `package.json` scripts already use.
- `web/pnpm-lock.yaml` now includes `maplibre-gl`.

`deploy/deploy.sh` builds from a `git archive` of `web/` in a temp dir, outside the workspace, so the lockfile update alone fixes it.

Checked locally: a clean frozen install plus `pnpm build` in `web/` succeeds.

body:
Pins 1b10904d8fb11e4d775a9eca154305f0b6cd9e22 (UofUEpiBio/epiworld#341).

The stage covers two epiworld changes since 3d-1:
- 3d-2 (UofUEpiBio/epiworld#340, #345) ports the measles models, which these scenarios don't use.
- 3d-1b (UofUEpiBio/epiworld#341) builds networks without `std::map`. It's the fix for the 3d-1 finding, UofUEpiBio/epiworld#339.

The runners are unchanged: the `AdjList` constructor they use kept its signature. Run in the same image as 3d-1 (`9a51e13558f5`), both C++ engines, replicates interleaved. `make container-check` and `make container-smoke` pass; all 1,280 runs ok.

## Rows

Each cell is 0.x, then 1.0. Simulate and build in seconds, peak in MiB.

| Scenario | n | Simulate | Ratio | Build | Ratio | Peak | Ratio | Attack rate |
|---|--:|---|--:|---|--:|---|--:|---|
| 00 | 10,000 | 0.00538, 0.00547 | 1.02 | 0.00149, 0.00131 | 0.88 | 8, 8 | 0.98 | 0.385, 0.385 |
| 00 | 100,000 | 0.00925, 0.00985 | 1.06 | 0.0171, 0.0122 | 0.71 | 38, 33 | 0.85 | 0.060, 0.060 |
| 01 | 10,000 | 0.00248, 0.00249 | 1.00 | 0.00133, 0.00112 | 0.85 | 8, 8 | 0.98 | 0.119, 0.119 |
| 01 | 100,000 | 0.00937, 0.00934 | 1.00 | 0.0133, 0.011 | 0.82 | 43, 41 | 0.94 | 0.014, 0.014 |
| 02 | 10,000 | 0.00236, 0.00245 | 1.04 | 0.00129, 0.00111 | 0.86 | 9, 8 | 0.99 | 0.119, 0.119 |
| 02 | 100,000 | 0.009, 0.00921 | 1.02 | 0.0136, 0.0107 | 0.79 | 44, 41 | 0.94 | 0.014, 0.014 |
| 03 | 1,000,000 | 0.0326, 0.0306 | 0.94 | 0.172, 0.137 | 0.80 | 352, 276 | 0.78 | 0.006, 0.006 |
| 04 | 165,865 | 0.185, 0.175 | 0.95 | 0.0166, 0.015 | 0.90 | 90, 88 | 0.97 | 0.622, 0.622 |

## Against 3d-1 (the 10% rule)

- **Build time and peak memory fell in every row.** The build ratio went from 5.2–9.0 to 0.71–0.90, and the peak ratio from 1.06–2.56 to 0.78–0.99.
- **Attack rates** are the same as 0.x's and as at 3d-1.
- **1,000,000 agents** is no longer noisy: the simulation ratio is 0.94, against 1.58 at 3d-1.
- **The simulation ratio grew by more than 10%** in every scenario up to 165,865 agents: to 1.00–1.06 from 0.69–0.97, and to 0.95 from 0.81 on GeoPops. I profiled it before anything else. The time per step didn't change; page faults moved from the build into the run.
  - **The cause:** the 3d-1 build freed tens of MiB of map nodes that glibc kept, and the run's first allocations reused them.
  - **The measurement:** I built scenario_01's runner at 100,000 agents against three commits (40 interleaved replicates in this image). It simulates in 0.0069 s at 3d-1 (`5811a28`), 0.0070 s after 3d-2 (`b699adb`), and 0.0101 s now.
  - **The fault counts:** inside `run()` it takes 0 minor page faults before #341 and about 3,400 (13 MiB) after. At under a microsecond each, that accounts for the difference.
  - **So:** the 3d-1 ratios below 1 were the same artifact, and the engines now simulate at parity. Build plus simulation at 100,000 agents takes 0.020 s, against 0.104 s at 3d-1. Nothing to fix in epiworld.

The note is under "3d-1b" in `docs/epiworld-v1.md`.

author: eloyleon23
body:
## Problema

En Pinta el Coche y Pinta tu Estancia, en pantalla completa: al girar a horizontal ya no se podía pintar, y al volver a vertical la plantilla se quedaba mal.

## Causa real

Más profunda de lo que parecía: el canvas redimensiona su **propia resolución de dibujo** (atributos `width`/`height`) para que coincida con su tamaño en pantalla — es un elemento "reemplazado" con tamaño intrínseco propio. El arreglo anterior para pantalla completa (CSS `aspect-ratio` + `auto` + `max-width`/`max-height`, la misma técnica que funcionó bien para zonas sin canvas) creaba una **dependencia circular**: el tamaño en pantalla del canvas depende de su resolución interna, que a su vez JS recalcula a partir de ese mismo tamaño en pantalla. Envolver el canvas en más capas de `<div>` no rompía el ciclo, porque cualquier contenedor que se autodimensione a partir de su contenido hereda el tamaño intrínseco del canvas igualmente. Al encogerse una vez (al girar a horizontal), se quedaba pequeño para siempre — y con el ancho/alto del lienzo pasando por 0 en algún punto intermedio, ni dejaba pintar (coordenadas de pintura divididas por un rect en 0) ni la plantilla se recuperaba al volver a vertical.

## Cambios

- El tamaño se calcula ahora a mano en JS (`ajustarCajaProporcion`), a partir del contenedor exterior — que no tiene el problema circular — y se fija como ancho/alto en línea en el div que envuelve el canvas. Es la misma técnica que ya funcionaba para el tablero de Encuentra la Pareja.
- Añadido el aviso al entrar/salir de pantalla completa (`om-pantalla-completa-cambio`): el modo "maximizado" simulado no dispara ningún `resize` de `window` al activarse (no cambia el tamaño de la ventana), así que sin este aviso el lienzo se quedaba con el tamaño de la página normal nada más entrar en pantalla completa en esos navegadores.
- De paso, Quita la Mancha recibe el mismo arreglo, más la comprobación que evita regenerar la suciedad en resizes espurios (que Pinta el Coche y Pinta tu Estancia ya tenían) para que gire sin perder progreso de más.

## Plan de pruebas

- Medido con Playwright, en pantalla completa nativa y simulada, en los 3 juegos: el canvas vuelve exactamente al mismo tamaño y proporción tras un ciclo vertical→horizontal→vertical (antes se quedaba pillado en el tamaño horizontal).
- Pintura verificada funcional en cada paso del ciclo (porcentaje pintado > 0% en las 6 mediciones por juego).
- Regresión completa de los 10 juegos en ambas orientaciones: sin errores de consola ni imágenes rotas.
