author: antoine-le-calloch
body:
DECam alerts do not say whether a detection is a known asteroid. ZTF alerts carry the nearest catalogued object and LSST alerts carry Rubin's own association, but DECam alerts had nothing, so they never got a rock flag and filters could not drop asteroids.

During enrichment, each DECam detection is now compared with the predicted positions of every object in the MPC orbit catalog that BOOM already keeps up to date, as seen from the observatory in Chile. When an object falls within 30 arcseconds, the alert gets a solar system block with its designation, the separation, and its distances and phase angle, and the rock flag is set. The positions are computed without planetary perturbations from the catalog epoch, which is good to a few tens of arcseconds for recent alerts but not for alerts several years old.

author: danipopes
body:
The interpreter carried bookkeeping for one consumer, the step cost that inspectors report: a `step_gas_before` field written in `inspect_step`, a `step_gas_after_charge` marker set by `finish_step_charge` in `call_with` and `create_with` and `Interpreter::step_cost`. This PR deletes all of it from core and leaves `inspect_step` and `inspect_step_end` with the same signatures and the same pc and stack length stores. `inspect_step_end` still sets the remaining gas of an out-of-gas step to 0 before the hook runs, because an out-of-gas frame has burned all its gas.

Each inspector now derives the cost from the gas it records itself. `TracingInspector` records the gas in `step`, takes the difference in `step_end`, and for CALL and CREATE reads the parent's gas in the `call` or `create` hook, which runs after the opcode charged and before the child runs. A call's cost includes the forwarded gas; a create's does not, so the hook adds the message's gas limit back. The JS tracer, `OpcodeGasInspector` and the EIP-3155 tracer in `evm2-eest` follow the same rule. A step that stops out of gas costs the whole remainder it started with, except the reentrancy sentry stop, which costs nothing. That value comes from the stop result and the gas recorded at `step`, never from the counter a failed charge leaves behind, so it does not change whether a failed `spend` wraps the counter or leaves it alone.

The gas the hooks see was already current on every dispatch backend, so this PR adds no store to the message path. Instructions get `&mut Gas` as a split borrow of the interpreter's own gas, not a copy, and tco writes its register back before an inspected instruction. The step cost tests, which pin the call and create costs exactly, pass on tco, packed, single_return and unpacked, and on the default and packed backends in the bench profile (thin LTO, one codegen unit). Reported step costs are unchanged in the inspector tests (struct logs, parity vmTrace, JS tracer, opcode gas) and in the EEST suites. The geth parity harness of #859 merged with this branch reports 0 new differences and 0 stale known entries over its 360 case and fork pairs (5,470 comparisons).

Two points are worth stating. The inspectors read an out-of-gas step from the stop result and the gas recorded at `step`, not from the counter a failed charge leaves behind, so the values come out the same whether a failed `spend` wraps the counter or leaves it unchanged; every inspector test passes with `spend` changed to leave it alone in a local scratch commit. The rule differs only for the reentrancy sentry stop, where `TracingInspector` and `OpcodeGasInspector` report 0 and the JS tracer and the EIP-3155 tracer report the whole remainder; those two values are as on main and the split is deliberate here. The second point is the `before` hook of `call_with` and `create_with`: it now runs before the inspector's `call` or `create` hook, so gas it charges counts toward the step cost, where it was excluded before. Nothing in the repository charges gas there.

`Inspector::step_end` now documents that the remaining gas reads 0 after an out-of-gas stop.

The no-inspector path does not get slower. Callgrind counts of the `evm` bench's measured section, taken one valgrind at a time on same-length base (main) and head checkouts (`cargo bench -p evm2-cli --bench evm`, built for x86-64-v3, all 100 cases in one run per backend). The default backend resolves to tco on the nightly used here.

| default (tco) | Ir | 6,986,205,887 | 6,985,654,403 | -0.008% 🟢 |
| default (tco) | Dr | 1,790,396,551 | 1,790,862,149 | +0.026% 🔴 |
| default (tco) | Dw | 774,898,704 | 774,905,549 | +0.001% 🔴 |
| packed | Ir | 9,402,613,100 | 9,402,146,983 | -0.005% 🟢 |

Instruction counts per case, one run each (default backend / packed):

| Case | Base | Head | Change | Base | Head | Change |

| snailtracer | 499,758,180 | 499,546,119 | -0.042% 🟢 | 745,694,466 | 745,444,037 | -0.034% 🟢 |

author: eserlan
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced chained array method calls (`.flatMap(words).map(w => w.toLowerCase())` and `[...singles].filter().map()`) with imperative `for...of` loops in `packages/generator-engine/src/business-checks.ts`.

🎯 **Why**: When mapping large document text extractions to find known names and single occurrences in `scanForNames` and `findUnintroducedNames`, native array method chaining forced the JavaScript engine to allocate multiple intermediate arrays per operation. This increased garbage collection overhead.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces short-lived array allocations to zero in these hot paths, avoiding unnecessary garbage collection and improving the baseline generator evaluation loop efficiency.

🔬 **Measurement**: Run `bun run --filter generator-engine test` to guarantee functionality remains functionally identical and test executions pass smoothly.

author: devziaus
body:
## What

Every business now stores a timezone, and the console uses that zone for timestamps, the delivery date warning, and the Overdue badge, so two people in different places see the same day. The promised delivery date stays a plain calendar day with no zone attached. Onboarding asks for the zone, and settings lets an owner change it behind a confirmation that explains which orders may newly show as overdue.

## Why

Implements `docs/specs/0008-business-timezone/index.md` (all 12 acceptance criteria, verified live on 2026-10-31).

Before this change, each viewer's browser decided which day it was. A seller in Dhaka and a colleague abroad could disagree about whether a promise was late, and order timestamps read differently on each device. The business row now owns the zone, and the server gets the same day rule as a tested helper for future reports and dashboards.

## Changes

- **Data**: `businesses.timezone` is a text column, not null, defaulting to `Asia/Dhaka`, added by one generated migration (`0006_absurd_hobgoblin.sql`) that backfills every existing business. `orders.delivery_deadline` stays a nullable date with no zone.
- **Contracts**: `TimezoneSchema` trims the value, accepts only an IANA ID the runtime recognizes, and returns the canonical ID, so `asia/dhaka` is stored as `Asia/Dhaka`. Fixed offsets such as `+06:00` and bare abbreviations such as `BST` are rejected because they do not survive daylight saving changes. The profile, update, and draft schemas carry the field; the response schema checks presence only, so a corrupt stored value still reads.
- **API**: the profile and onboarding endpoints return `timezone`, onboarding requires it and rejects an invalid value with 400 without writing, and the draft route accepts it as a field. No new endpoint, permission, or error code, apart from the existing `409 ONBOARDING_COMPLETE` on a skipped draft write.
- **Shared settings**: one `BusinessSettingsProvider` in the root layout holds currency and timezone, loads the profile once per app load and per auth change, and reads a per business cache so the first paint has the right zone. Orders, products, and the shell badge read from it. A malformed cache entry is ignored and removed, and a missing or invalid zone falls back to `Asia/Dhaka` everywhere rather than failing a page.
- **Screens**: onboarding step 3 gains a zone select beside currency, grouped by region and prefilled from the browser zone. Settings gains the same select, and changing it opens a confirmation that says existing order dates do not change but which orders show as overdue may.
- **Dates**: every console timestamp renders in the business zone, the create and edit delivery date warning compares against the business's today, and the Overdue badge appears only for `PENDING`, `CONFIRMED`, `PROCESSING`, or `SHIPPED` with a deadline strictly before that day. The badge is derived at render and never stored.
- **Server helper**: `backend/src/domain/timezone.ts` exposes `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`, `isValidTimeZone`, and `todayInTimeZone`, built from `formatToParts` with a fixed locale so it holds across runtimes and daylight saving changes.
- **Docs and tooling**: the spec with its rationale and verify notes, the review passes, and the project skill set the workflow runs on.

## How to test / verify

- `npm ci`, then `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`.
- `npm run test` without a dev stack: contracts 113, frontend 300, backend 390 (the integration tests there need the local Postgres).
- `RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=true npm run dev` in one terminal and `npm run e2e --workspace @f-commerce/frontend` in another: 42 specs across desktop and mobile. The register rate limiter otherwise blocks new accounts, so keep the flag set locally.
- In the browser, register a new business and walk the wizard: step 3 should prefill your browser zone, the review step should show it beside the currency, and the sidebar badge should read `Asia/Dhaka · BDT` style after you land on the dashboard. Open Settings, change the zone, and expect the confirmation dialog; cancel should revert the select, confirm should save and show `Profile updated`.
- Check that order timestamps and the Overdue badge agree with the business zone rather than the browser zone, for example with the browser set to a zone on a different calendar day.

## Risk & rollout

Moderate but contained. The one migration is additive with a default, so it backfills existing rows and needs no downtime; a rollback would drop the column and lose the chosen zones. All 277 businesses in the local database read a valid zone, and changing a zone alters only how deadlines are compared, never the stored dates or any order status, total, or history.

Residual risks accepted in review: the shared settings load once per app load, so a zone changed in another tab shows up on the next load rather than instantly; and a zone change is not audited in this slice. Standing review nits were cleared across four passes, and the remaining note was a stale test count in the verify notes, now corrected.

## Notes for reviewers

- The backend zone check and the contracts schema share one helper on purpose, so a value the API accepts is a value the frontend accepts. Its input handling is pinned by the contracts corpus at `packages/contracts/src/index.test.ts`.
- A cleared logo used to reach the response as an empty string the contract rejects. It is now normalized to no logo at the repository, the single choke point every read passes through, and pinned from the raw column up through integration, contract, and browser tests.
- The customer profile now uses the shared `formatMoney` like every other screen, which changes displayed amounts there from `$1,200.00` to `1,200 USD`. Worth a look if any report outside the console expected the old form.

author: roodboi
body: Fixes HACK-1346 for the e2e harness on `main`. ## What I found - **The happy path doesn't leak.** I ran all five main Docker scenarios (`cache-prune`, `dependency-cache`, `up-down`, `lifecycle-host-process`, `worktree-parallel-up`). The host had 19 networks before the run and 19 after. - **Killed runs leak.** I sent SIGINT to the runner during `worktree-parallel-up`. It left 2 networks and 4 containers: `e2e-` and `e2e---e2e-parallel`. Nothing runs a `finally` when the process is killed. - **The fallback sweep used the wrong branch name.** `downBestEffort` ran `docker compose -p - down`, but the CLI names branch instances `--` (`resolveLifecycleComposeProjectName`). So if `hack down --branch` failed, the fallback missed the branch instance. - **Nothing failed on a leak.** When a scenario skipped cleanup, the run still passed and the network stayed behind. - **Address pool.** This host's Docker allows 30 IPv4 `/24` pools. Non-e2e Compose projects already use 16 of them, so the 33–34 networks in the issue means the pool was full. P01 needs two networks: primary plus linked worktree. - **P01 isn't on `main`.** `pattern-p01-dependency-bootstrap` and `pattern-fixture.ts` exist only on `next` (#336, #386). Their fixtures get names from `randomProjectName()`, so this PR records ownership there too. Once `next` lands, those scenarios get the leak check and sweep with no further change. ## Change - New `tests/e2e/docker-ownership.ts`: - Every fixture name this process generates is recorded as owned, in memory and in a per-PID journal under `$TMPDIR/hack-e2e-ownership/` (override with `HACK_E2E_OWNERSHIP_DIR`). - Cleanup only touches Compose containers, networks and volumes whose `com.docker.compose.project` label is an owned name or `--`. It removes them by exact ID and never prunes. - It never touches other concurrent e2e runs or unrelated projects. - `runScenarios`: after each Docker scenario, any owned network still present **fails the scenario**. The harness then removes that scenario's owned resources and checks the networks are gone. - `run.ts`: - Prints `fixture networks: before=N after=M left by this run=K` and exits 1 if K > 0. - On SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, removes the run's owned resources before exiting. - At start, reclaims journals left by dead runs (for example after SIGKILL). It skips journals whose process is still alive. - `downBestEffort` now uses `--`. - README "Cleanup guarantees" is updated. ## Proof (real Docker on the shared m5 host, `./dist/hack`) | Case | main's harness | this PR | |---|---|---| | SIGINT during `worktree-parallel-up` | exit 130; **2 networks + 4 containers left** | exit 130; handler removed 4 containers + 2 networks; 0 left | | Mutation: `up-down` skips `hack down` and `downBestEffort` | **exit 0, PASS**, network `e2e-19c60e0e` left | **exit 1, FAIL** "scenario left 1 Docker network(s)…"; sweep removed it | | SIGKILL during `worktree-parallel-up` | n/a | 2 networks + 4 containers left (expected); the next run printed `reclaimed from a dead e2e run: …` and removed all of them | | Full suite (`HACK_E2E_DOCKER=1 HACK_E2E_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1`) | — | 14/14 pass, `fixture networks: before=0 after=0 left by this run=0` | Unit tests: `tests/e2e-docker-ownership.test.ts` (7 tests) use a fake Docker runner. They cover: - ownership boundaries (`e2e-abc1` does not own `e2e-abc12--x`); - that only owned resources are removed, containers then networks then volumes, with no prune; - the leak check, including through `runScenarios`; - journal recovery: dead PID swept, live PID left alone; - `branchComposeProject` matches the CLI's naming. Mutation check: with the leak check disabled, and with branch naming reverted to main's single dash, 2 of the 7 tests fail. All 7 pass with the fix. Gates: `bunx turbo run typecheck check test --force` passes (6/6 tasks, 968 tests, 0 fail). Without `--force`, turbo replays cached results because root `tests/` is outside the package inputs. `bunx ultracite check tests/e2e tests/e2e-docker-ownership.test.ts` is clean. ## P01 `runningConsumersComplete` race (on `next`): not confirmed It lists running `app` containers and then runs `docker exec` on each, so the code does check then act. The only overlapping operation is the first call, during the in-flight linked `hack up`. There, `app` depends on `install` (`service_completed_successfully`), and Compose waits on that dependency before it recreates `app`. The installer is killed, so `up` fails before any `app` container is touched. Every later call runs after `up` has settled. I didn't reproduce it, and I didn't run it here because P01 isn't on `main`. Leaving it with HACK-1296. ## Release signal Only test and harness code changes; no CLI behaviour changes, so no release. @codex review 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

AVM gets Settings of its own, the AVM menu's Settings item, so **Command-Comma** opens it from any AVM window, as in every Mac app. Four categories, in the same Categories toolbar as a machine's Settings (now generic over its categories), with Command-1 to Command-4:

A machine's Settings on the dashboard move from Command-Comma to **Command-Option-Comma**. The README and tester guide say so.
